documents.title: Ludork Documentation
documents.content:
# Ludork Documentation

Ludork combines a visual editor, Blueprint graphs, Lua scripts and an extensible C++20 runtime for map-driven 2D games. Use this manual to configure projects, author maps, Actors, data, animations and user interfaces, and run or package your game.

Downloads and project information are available on the [Ludork website](https://jasonleon01.github.io/Ludork/?lang=en_GB); its footer also links to the [third-party notices](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Choose a learning path

| If you want to… | Start here |
|---|---|
| Make a playable project | [Create Your First Project](<Getting Started/Create Your First Project.md>) |
| Author maps, assets and project data | [Start Page, Workspace and Shortcuts](<Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md>) |
| Configure Actor labels, lights, particles and child Actors | [Actor Components](<Editor User Guide/Actor Components/Overview.md>) |
| Look up what each Palette control does | [UI Controls in the Palette](<Editor User Guide/UI Controls in the Palette.md>) |
| Create material effects and instance parameter overrides | [Materials](<Editor User Guide/Materials.md>) |
| Build GPU particle effects for Actors and UI | [Common Particles](<Editor User Guide/Common Particles.md>) |
| Add timed subtitles to videos | [Video Subtitles](<Editor User Guide/Video Subtitles.md>) |
| Learn Lua | [Lua Basics](<Getting Started/Lua Basics.md>) |
| Write gameplay in Lua or Blueprint | [Lua Runtime and Modules](<Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md>) |
| Add or change native runtime APIs | [Build and Module Layout](<Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md>) |
| Deploy optional remote account storage | [Simple Server](<Simple Server/Deployment and Editor Settings.md>) |
| Preview maps and assets or prepare the native preview host | [PreviewHost](<PreviewHost/Overview.md>) |
| Install or write a trusted editor extension | [Installing and Managing Plug-ins](<Plug-in Development and Installation/Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md>) |
| Find unreferenced project resources | [Official Resource Cleanup](<Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Resource Cleanup.md>) |

## Supported platforms

### Editors

| Platform | Minimum supported version |
|---|---|
| Windows | Windows 10, x64 |
| macOS | Apple Silicon, macOS 13.3 |

### Games

| Platform | Minimum supported version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | Windows 10, x64 | |
| macOS | Apple Silicon, macOS 13.3 | |
| iOS | iOS 16.3, arm64 | C++ Source project required. |
| HarmonyOS | HarmonyOS 6.0.2 / API 22, arm64-v8a | Phones, tablets and 2-in-1 devices. C++ Source project required. |
| Android | Android 7.0 / API 24, arm64-v8a | C++ Source project required. |
| Web | WebGL 2 | C++ Source project required. |

Mobile packages are produced on Apple Silicon macOS. A Standalone project uses the prebuilt runtime for the editor's host platform. See [Run, Debug and Package](<Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for platform tools and signing options.

## Documentation conventions

- Paths are relative to the project root unless a page states otherwise.
- Menu commands and field labels match the English editor interface.

## Product and content licences

Ludork's software licence, third-party notices and Game project asset terms are separate. Review all three before redistributing an editor package or a game made from Game project content.

> **Warning:** Installing a plug-in runs trusted code with the permissions of the editor process. Inspect the source and origin of a plug-in before importing it.

documents.title: Projects and Upgrades
documents.content:
# Projects and Upgrades

## Which project template should I choose?

Choose **Standalone** to build gameplay with Lua, Blueprint, data and assets using the prebuilt runtime without a native compiler. Choose **C++ Source** to modify native services or bindings, or to package for iOS, HarmonyOS, Android or Web. Video playback is an independent template option. See [Template reference](<../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#template-reference>).

## Why is a project template unavailable, and can I create projects offline?

Release editors download templates matching their complete version, including the patch number; if that release or template has not been published, project creation reports it as unavailable. A completed, valid template cache can be reused offline. Development editors use bundled templates and report missing files without downloading replacements. See [Obtaining templates](<../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#obtaining-templates>).

## Will updating Ludork automatically update an existing project?

Updates to the Game project and default templates do not automatically modify projects already created from them; apply any desired changes to each project manually. `Main.proj.version` records the engine compatibility version (`v1.0` for this edition), which is separate from the game's release version and save format. See [Template variants](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Default Template Overview.md#template-variants>) and [Main.proj](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#mainproj>).

documents.title: Gameplay and Scripting
documents.content:
# Gameplay and Scripting

## When should I use Blueprint, Lua or a Script Mixin?

Blueprint graphs define event and execution flow visually. Lua classes provide reusable systems and gameplay types, while Script Mixins attach Lua behaviour directly to a Blueprint class. A Blueprint inheritance chain must consistently use either graph mode or Script Mixin mode. See [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-runtime-and-modules>).

## Can I reload Lua without restarting the game?

For an editor-launched game using loose Lua sources, save your edits and enter `$r` in **Console**. Hot reload updates existing functions while preserving the scene, objects and runtime state. It does not rerun `Entry.lua` or reload JSON, UI assets, metadata, declarations or native code; structural or data changes require a restart. Packed or bytecode-only scripts cannot be hot-reloaded. See [Lua hot reload](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>).

documents.title: Assets and Localisation
documents.content:
# Assets and Localisation

## How do I enable video playback?

Select **Enable video playback (FFmpeg)** when creating the project to add local MOV and MP4 playback for H.264 video and AAC audio (this increases build size). See [FFmpeg option](<../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#ffmpeg-option>) for codec limits, per-platform preparation and distribution requirements.

## Why does an asset reference break after I move or rename a file?

Rename or move assets through the editor, then save. External renames, as well as source-code or dynamic references, must be updated manually; see [Assets](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#assets>) for path requirements.

If an external-change conflict occurs while a move is unsaved, see [Editing and saving](<../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#editing-and-saving>).

## Why do changed translations not appear in the game?

After editing `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx`, run the Official Locale Tools through **Export**, then restart the game. General Data strings are not translated automatically; display them through `LOC`. Lua hot reload preserves loaded language tables. See [Export](<../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md#export>) and [Runtime](<../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md#runtime>).

documents.title: Running Debugging and Publishing
documents.content:
# Running Debugging and Publishing

## Which platforms can I develop on and publish to?

The editor runs on Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS. Games can target those platforms as well as iOS, HarmonyOS, Android and Web. Mobile and Web packaging require a **C++ Source** project; mobile packages are produced on Apple Silicon macOS, and **Standalone** uses the prebuilt runtime for the editor's host platform. See [Supported platforms](<../Ludork Documentation.md#supported-platforms>) for minimum versions and [Packaging](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>) for required tools.

## Why is Play unavailable, and when do I use Construct or Export?

Complete a successful **Export** before the first **Play**. **C++ Source** projects also require a successful Debug build through **Construct** or `tools/build_cpp`. **Construct** compiles native code, **Export** generates UI and locale runtime files and `SceneInit` prepares materials; Lua, UI JSON, game data and localisation edits do not require a native build. Check the first reported error if preparation fails. See [Construct, Export and Play](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#construct-export-and-play>).

## Does Live Debug save changes back to my project?

**Live Debug** edits current runtime instances without modifying project documents or providing Undo/Redo. Enable it before **Play** and use **Individual Window**. Saving the game preserves gameplay state modified by live edits. See [Live Debug](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#live-debug>) for available edits and instance lifetime.

## Why is Confirm disabled in Pack Project?

Hover over the disabled button to view the reason. The entry script must declare a valid static `APP_NAME` (initially supplied through [New Project](<../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#template-reference>)). See [Packaging](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>) for declaration rules and other packaging requirements.

documents.title: Saves and Server
documents.content:
# Saves and Server

## Why do changed game-variable defaults not affect an existing save?

Saved variable declarations provide initial values for new games. Loading a save slot replaces the new instance's variable table with the saved table without merging newly added declarations or migrating existing values. Apply default changes in a new game or implement custom save migration. See [Game variables](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#game-variables>).

## Do I need Ludork Server, and does it provide multiplayer or cloud saves?

Ludork Server is an optional Node.js service with server Lua logic, explicit snapshot proxies, void RPCs and online events. Gameplay code decides when to fetch or refresh data and which business actions to send; the service neither synchronises multiplayer state automatically nor uploads, downloads or replaces local saves. Configuring client integration requires a **C++ Source** project. See [Simple Server](<../Simple Server/Deployment and Editor Settings.md#simple-server-deployment-and-editor-settings>) and [Configuration](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#configuration>).

documents.title: Create Your First Project
documents.content:
# Create Your First Project

Create a Standalone project from a template, open its initial map, export its assets and run it in the editor.

## Create the project

1. On the **Start Page**, select **New Project**.

![Ludork Start page with recent-project and project-creation actions](../../../images/getting-started/start-page.png)

2. Select **Standalone**.
3. Leave **Enable video playback (FFmpeg)** disabled unless the game must play video.
4. Choose an existing destination directory, enter a new project name and fill in the required **APP_NAME** field. Their separate roles are described in [Project Templates](<Project Templates.md#template-reference>).
5. Confirm the destination path and select **Create**. Ludork opens `Main.proj` when creation finishes.

> **Note:** Release editors download the matching template on first use. See [Obtaining templates](<Project Templates.md#obtaining-templates>) for availability, offline reuse and cancellation.

![New Project window with the Standalone template selected](../../../images/getting-started/new-project.png)

## Save and run

1. Select a map in the **Map List**.
2. Select **Export** and resolve any reported errors. **Play** requires a successful export.
3. Select **Play**. Windows supports embedded or individual-window mode; other platforms use an individual window. See [Construct, Export and Play](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#construct-export-and-play>) for window settings and export details.
4. Open **Console** to view runtime output. Project editing is disabled while the game runs unless [Live Debug](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#live-debug>) was enabled before Play.
5. Select the same button, now **Stop**, to end the game and resume editing.

The runtime creates user configuration when none exists for the project's `APP_NAME`; otherwise it reuses the existing settings. See [Game configuration](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>) for its format, location and sharing rules.

documents.title: Project Templates
documents.content:
# Project Templates

Ludork projects start from either the **Standalone** or **C++ Source** template, each with an optional FFmpeg video-playback variant. Use this guide to choose a template, verify platform prerequisites and understand template downloads and layout.

## Template reference

**New Project** presents two template cards, **Standalone** and **C++ Source**, together with an independent **Enable video playback (FFmpeg)** switch.

Enter a project name for the new directory and a separate, required **APP_NAME** for the game. `APP_NAME` identifies the game's [user data directory](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>) and [packaged application](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>); choose a name dedicated to this game. An empty or invalid value keeps **Create** disabled, and renaming the project directory does not change `APP_NAME`.

Project creation substitutes `APP_NAME` into the template's `Scripts/Entry.lua.in` and writes an ordinary, editable `Scripts/Entry.lua` without the `.in` template. Later changes to the application name belong in the static `local APP_NAME` declaration in `Scripts/Entry.lua`.

| Template | Native source | Native compiler required | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standalone | No | No | Authoring Lua, Blueprint, data and assets with the prebuilt runtime. |
| C++ Source | Yes | Yes | Changing native services or bindings, or building for iOS, HarmonyOS, Android or WebGL. |

Each card and FFmpeg combination has its own template. To turn an existing **C++ Source** project into an editable **Standalone** project, use [Pack Project → Standalone project](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#convert-source-to-a-standalone-project>); this creates a separate project that preserves the original export outputs rather than starting from a fresh template.

Before the first Play, run **Construct** and then **Export** for **C++ Source**; **Standalone** needs only **Export**. See [Run, Debug and Package](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for subsequent builds and exports. **C++ Source** templates include a project-root `.clang-format` for native source formatting.

- **Windows:** Selecting **C++ Source** displays **Compiler** and **Get MinGW**. Choose an available compiler before creating the project; without one, **Create** is disabled. Detection prefers MSVC, then Ludork's downloaded MinGW, then any compiler on `PATH` including LLVM Clang, and downloading a compiler refreshes this list without restarting the editor. **Standalone** requires no compiler. See [Windows project compiler](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#windows-project-compiler>) for detection, downloads and later changes.
- **macOS:** **C++ Source** requires a full Xcode installation; Command Line Tools alone do not qualify. **New Project** checks once when the window opens; if Xcode is missing, selecting **C++ Source** shows **Get Xcode** (opening Xcode in the Mac App Store) and disables **Create**. After installing Xcode, close and reopen **New Project** to check again. **Standalone** does not require Xcode.

## Obtaining templates

Development editor packages bundle local templates. If one is missing, **New Project** reports an error without downloading a replacement.

Release editors download templates from the matching GitHub Release. Windows x64 uses ZIP archives; macOS ARM64 uses `tar.gz` archives. Each release publishes eight template assets:

| Template | Windows x64 | macOS ARM64 |
|---|---|---|
| C++ Source | `game-source.zip` | `game-source.tar.gz` |
| C++ Source with FFmpeg | `game-source-ffmpeg.zip` | `game-source-ffmpeg.tar.gz` |
| Standalone | `game-standalone.zip` | `game-standalone.tar.gz` |
| Standalone with FFmpeg | `game-standalone-ffmpeg.zip` | `game-standalone-ffmpeg.tar.gz` |

Templates match the editor's complete version, including its patch number. If the matching release or template has not been published, **New Project** reports that it is unavailable.

All four downloaded variants are cached under `~/Ludork/Templates/v<base-version>/` for validation and offline reuse on Windows and macOS, independently of the installation directory (see [User data directory](<../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#user-data-directory>) for the native path). Bundled development templates are read-only inputs.

**New Project** displays download or copy progress and extraction progress. Selecting **Cancel** or closing the window during creation cancels the operation and deletes the unfinished project and download files; completed, valid cache entries stay cached for later use.

**New Project** always creates the project version matching the editor's `major.minor` version (such as `v1.0` for any `1.0.x` editor) and provides no older-version creation option. Opening supported older projects is handled by the [project-version check](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#mainproj>).

## FFmpeg option

**Enable video playback (FFmpeg)** adds local MOV and MP4 playback for H.264 video and AAC audio, increasing build size. Other codecs, network playback and hardware acceleration are not included.

Windows and macOS use shared FFmpeg libraries, whereas iOS, HarmonyOS, Android and WebGL use static libraries. Distribution requirements, including LGPL relinking materials for static builds, are detailed in `Licenses/FFmpeg/README.md`. On macOS, selecting FFmpeg displays a compatibility notice.

## Template targets

- **Ludork Server:** Configuring [Ludork Server](<../Simple Server/Deployment and Editor Settings.md>) requires **C++ Source**; its Game test-server menu and Pack configuration are hidden in **Standalone**. All templates start with the server disabled and contain no test or production credentials. Converting an existing **C++ Source** project can embed explicitly enabled Release server settings in the resulting **Standalone** runtime.
- **Packaging options:** Script compilation, shader encryption, data encryption, save encryption and **Archive Assets, Data and Scripts (.ldpak)** are packaging options rather than template types. See [Run, Debug and Package](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for complete option behaviour.
- **Excluded generated outputs:** Templates omit UI/locale export outputs (`Scripts/Internal/UI/`, `Scripts/stub/Internal/UI/`, `Scripts/stub/Internal/UIWindows/`, generated locale Lua files and `EditorCache/ProjectExport.json`, all in `.gitignore`), material caches and release `Data/RuntimeSettings.json`/`.ldc`. **C++ Source** also omits `build-web` and `dist`. Run **Export** for UI/locale files; the game [prepares materials at initialisation](<../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#runtime-generation>).
- **Included authored sources:** Templates include UI JSON, authored material graphs under `Data/Materials`, handwritten Controllers and declarations, `Scripts/Source/Locale/Core.lua`, General Data and variable Lua with declarations, native binding declarations and optional `Data/MaterialCombinations.json` for [additional material combinations](<../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#material-combinations>) (combined at initialisation with map combinations).
- **Language-tool declarations:** Templates include `Scripts/stub/**/*.d.lua` for Lua language tools; these declarations are stripped from [game packages](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#loose-and-packed-output>).

Runtime licence texts live in `Licenses` (FFmpeg variants also include `Licenses/FFmpeg`), and asset notices sit beside their assets. Packaging copies available licence texts, but verifying completeness is the distributor's responsibility.

documents.title: Lua Basics
documents.content:
# Lua Basics

Ludork runs Lua 5.5. This guide covers the syntax and runtime behaviour that differ from C; see [Ludork Lua Advanced](<Ludork Lua Advanced.md>) for Ludork's Standard extensions and [SFML Quickstart](<SFML Quickstart.md>) for graphics and geometry types.

## Files, comments and local variables

Lua files use the `.lua` extension, and comments use `--` or `--[[ ... ]]`. Declare local variables with `local`; uninitialised variables evaluate to `nil`.

```lua
-- One line
local playerName = "Hero"
local level, alive, target = 1, true, nil
```

Lua values belong to eight built-in categories: `nil`, booleans, numbers, strings, functions, tables, userdata and threads. `type(value)` returns that category name; application objects represented by tables or userdata report their underlying Lua category.

## Operators

| Kind | Operators |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic | `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `//`, `%`, `^` |
| Comparison | `==`, `~=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` |
| Logic | `and`, `or`, `not` |
| Strings | `..` for concatenation |
| Length | `#value` |

Lua treats only `nil` and `false` as false. Values such as `0`, an empty string (`""`) and an empty table (`{}`) evaluate to `true` in a condition.

## Conditions

```lua
if health <= 0 then
    state = "defeated"
elseif health < maxHealth then
    state = "hurt"
else
    state = "healthy"
end
```

Use explicit `nil` comparisons when absence must be distinguished from `false`, `0` or an empty value.

## Tables

A table acts as an array, dictionary or record. Array indices start at 1.

```lua
local items = { "Key", "Potion" }
local player = {
    name = "Hero",
    hp = 100,
}

items[#items + 1] = "Gem"
player.hp = player.hp - 10
```

Assigning `nil` removes a table key. Keep arrays dense: holes make `#` unreliable, and `ipairs` stops at the first `nil`.

## Loops

```lua
for index, item in ipairs(items) do
    useItem(index, item)
end

for key, value in pairs(player) do
    inspectValue(key, value)
end
```

Use `ipairs` for dense arrays and `pairs` for dictionaries. Numeric loops (`for i = first, last, step do ... end`) include both endpoints when reached by `step`; `while` loops use `while condition do ... end`.

## Functions and methods

Functions are first-class values and may return multiple results. Define instance methods with colon syntax, which passes the receiver as `self`.

```lua
local function clampHealth(value, maximum)
    return math.max(0, math.min(value, maximum))
end

local Character = {}

function Character:setHealth(value)
    self.health = clampHealth(value, self.maxHealth)
end

local value, found = findItem("Key")
```

`object:method(value)` is equivalent to `object.method(object, value)`. Define and call instance methods with colon syntax consistently.

## Modules

A module is a Lua file that returns its public value. Require it by its path beneath `Scripts`, using dots and omitting the `.lua` extension.

```lua
-- Scripts/Source/Score.lua
local Score = {}

function Score.Add(current, amount)
    return current + amount
end

return Score
```

```lua
local Score = require("Source.Score")

local total = Score.Add(10, 5)
```

Project loading order and `require` conventions are documented in [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md>).

## Errors

Use `assert(condition, message)` for required preconditions and `error(message)` for explicit failures. Required project data must fail at its source rather than silently producing partial state.

documents.title: Ludork Lua Advanced
documents.content:
# Ludork Lua Advanced

Ludork's Standard library installs native classes, containers, math and string helpers, configuration parsers and cooperative async APIs before `Scripts/Entry.lua` runs, without `require`. Its declarations live in `Scripts/stub/Standard.d.lua` and `Scripts/stub/Class.d.lua`; `Engine`, `GlobalCore`, `GlobalFunctions` and LuaSF have separate bindings.

## Ludork classes

Create a plain definition table without a metatable, add defaults and methods, then return `class(definition, ...)`. The definition must not already be finalised, every base must be a finalised Ludork class or a registered native type and duplicate bases are rejected. Base order determines the C3 method-resolution order (MRO) used to search inherited members.

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")

local Actor = Engine.Actor

local Pickup = {}

Pickup.count = 1
Pickup.sound = ""

function Pickup:init(texture, tag)
    Actor.init(self, texture, tag)
    self._collected = false
end

return class(Pickup, Actor)
```

### Defaults and instance state

Editable or inheritable defaults belong on the definition table before finalisation, including metadata fields, component defaults, `default*` spawn values and Blueprint-overridable identifiers.

`init` applies constructor arguments and creates per-instance state. Copy mutable class defaults whenever each instance must own an independent value:

```lua
local RouteFollower = {}

RouteFollower.speed = 96.0
RouteFollower.defaultRoute = {}

function RouteFollower:init()
    self._route = deepcopy(self.defaultRoute)
    self._routeIndex = 1
end

return class(RouteFollower)
```

> **Important:** Do not initialise a public default only inside `init`. Subclasses and Blueprint discovery read defaults from the class table.

An explicit `nil` restored from Blueprint, Component or General Data is stored as an own field that overrides inherited defaults; inheritance, `copy` and `deepcopy` preserve it. Assigning `nil` in Lua clears that override and resumes inheritance lookup. Native properties and Lua getters and setters follow their normal lookup and dispatch rules.

### Construction, lifecycle and inheritance

- **Construction:** `Type.new(...)` constructs an instance and calls `init`. Finalised classes are also callable; follow the convention of neighbouring modules. A class without `init` accepts no arguments unless a single native root defines its constructor contract. Invoke required native-base initialisers explicitly.
- **Native property deferral:** Before a native root is constructed, typed assignments to its properties are stored on the composite and applied during native-base initialisation. Native property access targets that root; script getters and setters resolve from script classes, and setter errors propagate to the caller.
- **Lifecycle and disposal:** Lifecycle methods such as `onCreate`, `onTick` and `onDestroy` run only when their owning runtime contract calls them. `instance:dispose()` runs the resolved implementation at most once, releases native ownership and instance fields, and is not repeated by garbage collection.
- **Super calls and multiple inheritance:** Inside a method, `super()` resolves the next implementation from the defining class; use `super(ClassName, self)` when an indirect callback makes ownership ambiguous. Multiple inheritance is supported, and declared base order must stay stable.
- **Script Mixins:** [Script Mixins](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Script Mixins/Runtime Contract.md>) use lifecycle callbacks instead of `init`.

### Class utilities

| API | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Class.isInstance(value, target)` | Test a raw Lua type or an instance against a class's complete MRO. |
| `Class.isSubclass(value, target)` | Test a class against its complete MRO. |
| `Class.type(value)` | Return its Ludork class or native fallback type. |
| `Class.hasOwnField(value, key)` | Test whether a field is stored directly. |
| `Class.getMro(value)` | Return a detached MRO array. |
| `Class.getParameterNames(callable)` | Return declared parameter names without `self`. |
| `Class.constructNamed(type, values)` | Match named values to `init` parameters and construct. |
| `Class.super(cls?, self?)` / `super(...)` | Resolve the next implementation in the active MRO. |
| `Class.monitor` / `Class.unmonitor` | Add or remove a named subscription to a field. |
| `Class.MISSING` | Sentinel used when a monitored field had no previous value. |

Use `Class.monitor(target, name, callback, params?, notifyEqualWrites?, identifier?)` to subscribe to writes on a table or userdata field without invoking `callback` immediately, and `Class.unmonitor(target, name, identifier?)` to remove that subscription:

- **Identifiers and ordering:** `identifier` defaults to `""`. Registering again with the same identifier replaces that subscription in place; subscriptions with distinct identifiers run in registration order. `Class.unmonitor` removes only the named subscription and ignores missing ones.
- **Value filtering and arguments:** Monitored fields reject `nil` assignments and notify only when their visible value changes unless `notifyEqualWrites` is `true`. A previously missing or explicit `nil` value reports `Class.MISSING`. Each callback receives `(oldValue, newValue, ...)`, followed by the entries of `params`.
- **Re-entrancy and errors:** Re-entrant assignments take effect while each subscription suppresses its own recursion. Callback errors stop dispatch and propagate without rolling back the assignment.
- **Snapshot dispatch and teardown:** Dispatch iterates a subscription snapshot: removing or replacing a subscription before its turn skips the old callback, and newly registered callbacks start on subsequent assignments. Removing the last subscription restores ordinary field storage and the table's original metatable.

### Type checks

Use `Class.isInstance` for every type check. Its target may be a finalised Ludork or registered native class, or an exact Lua type name: `nil`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `function`, `userdata`, `thread` or `table`.

```lua
if Class.isInstance(value, "string") then
    print(string.upper(value))
end

local isActor = Class.isInstance(actor, Actor)
local isNativeVector = Class.isInstance(position, sf.Vector2f)
local isInteger = Class.isInstance(value, "number") and math.type(value) == "integer"
```

String targets preserve Lua `type` semantics: native containers are userdata, and callable tables are reported as tables. Unknown names return `false`; targets that are neither strings nor tables raise argument errors. Call `math.type` only after a number check, use `Class.type` only when the resolved type value is needed and never compare a Lua `type` result with `==` or `~=`.

## Project truth values and copies

Ludork's `bool(value)` extends [Lua truth values](<Lua Basics.md#operators>): `0`, empty strings, empty tables and empty native containers also count as `false`. Use explicit `nil` comparisons when absence is a distinct protocol value.

| API | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `copy(value)` | Shallow-copy tables and supported native values. |
| `deepcopy(value)` | Recursively copy keys and values while preserving aliases and cycles. |
| `asizeof(value)` | Estimate the memory owned by a Lua or native value graph, in bytes. |

For known bound value types, call `value:copy()` or `value:deepcopy()` directly (for example `position:copy()`, `rect:copy()` or `colour:copy()`) to produce independent values. Global `copy` and `deepcopy` handle Lua tables and dynamic graphs, delegating supported bound values to the same LuaGlue entry points. Resources without a value-copy policy are returned by reference rather than copied.

For monitored tables, `copy` and `deepcopy` copy the current logical field values and preserve the original metatable without the monitoring proxy or subscriptions. The copied values can be saved normally; subscriptions belong to live instances and must be registered again after loading.

## Native containers

`list`, `tuple` and `dict` are native containers. They do not replace the Lua tables required by JSON, metadata, Blueprint values or Core bindings.

```lua
local route = list("north", nil, "east")
local position = tuple(4, 7)
local visited = dict {
    [position] = true,
}
```

| Type | Main operations |
|---|---|
| `list` | `append`, `extend`, `insert`, `pop`, `remove`, `clear`, `index`, `count`, `contains`, `reverse`, `sort`, `copy`, `unpack`, `toTable` |
| `tuple` | `index`, `count`, `contains`, `unpack`, `toTable` |
| `dict` | `get`, `setdefault`, `update`, `pop`, `remove`, `clear`, `contains`, `keys`, `values`, `items`, `copy`, `toTable` |

- **Construction and indexing:** `list(...)` and `tuple(...)` store arguments in 1-based slots; a single table, `list` or `tuple` argument is shallow-copied as a sequence. `dict(mapping?)` copies a mapping. Tuples reject `nil`, whereas lists and dictionaries preserve `nil` slots and values. Negative sequence indices are invalid, and list writes and inserts must target an existing slot or `#value + 1`.
- **Iteration and lookup:** Native `ipairs` visits `nil` list slots, `dict` iteration preserves insertion order and structural mutation during iteration raises an error. `dict:get(key, default)` uses `default` only when the key is missing; `dict:contains(key)` distinguishes absence from a stored `nil`. Method names take precedence over same-named string keys on `dict`, so read them with `value:get("get")` or `dict.get(value, "get")`.
- **Mutation and snapshots:** Remove dictionary entries with `remove` or `pop` rather than `dictionary[key] = nil`. `remove` returns whether it found the key; `pop` raises on a missing key unless given a default. `list:pop()` removes the last slot by default, `list:remove` raises when its value is absent and `list:sort(compare?)` is stable. `dict:keys()` and `dict:values()` return insertion-ordered `list` snapshots; `dict:items()` is a lazy iterator.
- **Equality and tuple keys:** Lists and dictionaries compare structurally, including cyclic graphs. Tuples act as immutable native-dictionary keys: booleans, finite numbers, strings and nested tuples compare by value, whereas mutable or reference values compare by identity. `nil` and non-finite numeric tuple keys are invalid. Ordinary Lua tables hash tuple userdata by identity.

### Conversion boundaries

`toTable` recursively converts native containers while preserving aliases and cycles. Converted lists and tuples preserve JSON-array shape when empty or nested, `nil` list slots and dictionary values become `cjson.null`, and tuple keys become compact strings such as `(1,2)` (failing on collision with an existing string key). JSON encoders, metadata, Blueprint values and Core bindings do not perform this conversion automatically.

Use record arrays instead when key identity must be reconstructed after loading.

## Math extensions

Standard adds these functions to Lua's `math` library. Except for `isFinite`, arguments must be finite Lua numbers (convert numeric strings explicitly with `tonumber`). Invalid ranges, arithmetic overflow and integer results outside the Lua integer range raise errors. `gcd` and `lcm` require Lua integers, and `round` and `trunc` preserve integer inputs exactly.

`lerp`, `inverseLerp` and `remap` support reversed intervals and extrapolation without clamping.

| API | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `math.isFinite(value)` | Return `true` for finite Lua numbers, `false` otherwise. |
| `math.clamp(value, min, max)` | Return a float constrained to `[min, max]`. Require `min <= max`. |
| `math.lerp(a, b, t)` | Linearly interpolate from `a` to `b` by `t`. |
| `math.round(value)` | Round to the nearest integer, choosing the even integer at exact halves. |
| `math.trunc(value)` | Truncate towards zero and return an integer, unlike the exact conversion in `math.tointeger`. |
| `math.isNearZero(value, epsilon=0.1)` | Test `abs(value) < epsilon`. Require `epsilon >= 0`. |
| `math.gcd(a, b)` | Return the non-negative greatest common divisor. `gcd(0, 0)` is `0`. |
| `math.lcm(a, b)` | Return the non-negative least common multiple, or `0` if either argument is `0`. |
| `math.sign(value)` | Return the integer `-1`, `0` or `1`. Both signed zeros return `0`. |
| `math.inverseLerp(a, b, value)` | Return `(value - a) / (b - a)`. Require `a ~= b`. |
| `math.remap(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax)` | Map proportionally from the input interval to the output interval. Require `inMin ~= inMax`. |
| `math.smoothstep(edge0, edge1, value)` | Clamp the normalised position `t` to `[0, 1]`, then return `t²(3 − 2t)`. Require `edge0 < edge1`. |
| `math.moveTowards(current, target, maxDelta)` | Move by at most `maxDelta` without passing the target. Require `maxDelta >= 0`. |

## String and table extensions

Standard adds these helpers to Lua's existing libraries:

| API | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `string.pformat` | Format `{}` positional fields or `{name}` fields from a final mapping table. `{{` and `}}` escape braces. |
| `string.contains`, `string.startsWith`, `string.endsWith` | Test string contents or boundaries. |
| `string.isEmpty`, `string.isBlank` | Test empty or whitespace-only text. |
| `string.strip`, `string.stripLeading`, `string.stripTrailing` | Remove Unicode whitespace. |
| `string.replace`, `string.split` | Replace or split text. |
| `string.utf8Length`, `string.utf8Slice` | Measure or slice by UTF-8 codepoints. |
| `string.graphemeLength` | Count Unicode grapheme clusters (user-perceived characters). |
| `string.stripUnicode` | Trim Unicode `White_Space` from both ends. |
| `table.contains`, `table.index` | Search a dense Lua array using Lua equality, stopping at the first `nil` slot. |
| `table.orderedStringKeys` | Return preferred keys first, then remaining string keys sorted. |

## Platform, configuration and files

`PLATFORM` is the lowercase target name (`win32`, `darwin`, `ios`, `android`, `ohos`, `web` or the CMake system name). `LUDORK_MOBILE` and `LUDORK_DESKTOP` expose the runtime host category: on HarmonyOS, phones and tablets report mobile and 2-in-1 devices report desktop. Do not infer the platform from paths or environment variables.

`configparser.ConfigParser()` provides `read`, `write`, `has_section`, `add_section`, `get`, `getfloat`, `getint`, `getboolean` and `set`. `read(path)` and `write(path)` select XML plist for a `.plist` extension (case-insensitive) on macOS only; all other paths, including explicit `.ini` files on macOS, use INI. Use [the game configuration path API](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#configuration>) for the platform's default game configuration file.

Configuration plists contain one root dictionary whose keys name sections, and each section is a dictionary of keys and string values (including numbers and booleans written as text):

```xml
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Main</key>
    <dict>
      <key>scale</key><string>1.25</string>
      <key>verticalsync</key><string>true</string>
    </dict>
  </dict>
</plist>
```

- **Plist restrictions:** Binary plists and non-string values (`<integer>`, `<real>`, `<true/>`, arrays or nested dictionaries) are unsupported, and keys that differ only in case within one section are rejected. Empty sections and strings, Unicode text and interior whitespace are preserved; XML characters such as `&` and `<` are escaped on write.
- **Case sensitivity and conversion:** Section names are case-sensitive; keys are case-insensitive while preserving the last spelling passed to `set`. Values are stored as strings and converted on read by `getfloat`, `getint` and `getboolean` (`1`/`yes`/`true`/`on` are `true`; `0`/`no`/`false`/`off` are `false`, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace). Missing values or failed conversions return the fallback or `nil`.
- **Merging and read errors:** Repeated successful reads merge into existing sections and preserve unrelated keys. `read` returns `false` if the file is absent (INI also returns `false` on open failure); an unreadable, malformed or unsupported existing plist raises an error and leaves existing sections unchanged.
- **Write atomicity:** `write` serialises before opening the destination so serialisation failures leave the existing file intact; file-write errors raise.

`locale.getdefaultlocale()` returns the host locale pair.

Filesystem extensions:

| API | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `os.getcwd`, `os.listdir` | Read the current directory, or sorted direct entry names relative to that directory. |
| `os.createDirectories` | Create a UTF-8 directory path and any missing parents; existing directories are accepted. |
| `os.removeFile` | Remove the file at a UTF-8 path. Missing files and failures raise. Does not replace `os.remove`. |
| `os.path.join`, `os.path.splitext`, `os.path.basename`, `os.path.dirname`, `os.path.abspath` | Build or inspect paths. |
| `os.path.isdir`, `os.path.isfile` | Test existing directory or file paths. Missing paths return `false`; inspection errors propagate. |
| `os.path.getmtime` | Return a file modification timestamp. |

`os.listdir`, `os.path.isdir`, `os.path.isfile` and `io.open` access only the real filesystem; `/Game/Assets/...` paths work only with Ludork resource APIs. For packed Data, `os.path.getmtime("Data/...")` returns the timestamp of the containing `.ldpak` file; other filesystem APIs do not expose archive entries.

Binary-safe codec globals:

| API | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `zlib.compress`, `zlib.decompress` | Compress data to zlib, or decompress zlib or gzip data. |
| `base64.encode`, `base64.decode` | Encode or decode Base64. Decoding accepts whitespace and valid padding, and rejects malformed data. |

## Cooperative tasks and file batches

`asyncio.create_task(callback, ...)` schedules a cooperative task and returns its handle. Inside a task, call `asyncio.sleep(seconds)` for a delay or `asyncio.await(operation)` to wait for an asynchronous result while the game loop continues. If a task raises a Lua runtime error, the engine ends the task, logs its Lua stack trace and keeps running other tasks.

Use `asyncio.create_required_task(callback, ...)` for work that must succeed for the game to run. It takes the same arguments and returns the same handle type, but an unhandled Lua error in a required task ends the game session.

For example, while a `SceneMap` is active, these configured tutorials run in sequence:

```lua
local Scene = require("GlobalFunctions.Scene")

local task = asyncio.create_task(function ()
    asyncio.await(Scene.ShowTutorial("Map01Menu"))
    asyncio.await(Scene.ShowTutorial("Map01Dialogue"))
    asyncio.await(Scene.ShowMessage("Guide", "Ready to continue."))
end)
```

`await` returns the operation's final result; if the operation is cancelled, the task ends without executing the next statement. Call `asyncio.cancel_task(task)` to stop only that task while the shared operation and its other waiters stay active. Task completion and cancellation execute Lua `__close` cleanup.

See [AsyncOperation](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Events and Module Root.md#asyncoperation>) for the operation API and [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md#asynchronous-operation-updates>) for custom-entry initialisation.

For larger reads, `asyncio.start_file_batch(specs)` reads independent files concurrently and delivers them in manifest order. `asyncio.file_worker_count()` returns the process's default parallel file-read limit based on available logical processors; a batch uses at most that many workers and at most one per file (WebGL uses one cooperative worker).

- **Specifications:** Give each specification a unique `category` and a `root`. For a directory scan, set `suffix` (and optionally `excludeSuffix` or `recursive = true`); for a single file, set `file` to a relative path under `root` without scan options. Logical `Data/...` roots read packaged data—including the encrypted equivalent of a `.json` file—while other roots use the physical filesystem. A missing required input fails the job.
- **Polling and cancellation:** `asyncio.poll_file_batch(job, maxItems?, waitForItem?)` returns progress, ordered items and any structured failure, defaulting to one item with no wait. Pass a positive `maxItems` and `true` to wait for the next ordered item or a terminal state, or pass `0` to inspect progress without collecting items; use non-blocking polls during frame updates. Call `asyncio.cancel_file_batch(job)` to cancel the job.
- **Job states:** Match `state` against the `asyncio` constants `FILE_BATCH_SCANNING` (`"scanning"`), `FILE_BATCH_RUNNING` (`"running"`), `FILE_BATCH_COMPLETED` (`"completed"`), `FILE_BATCH_CANCELLING` (`"cancelling"`), `FILE_BATCH_CANCELLED` (`"cancelled"`) and `FILE_BATCH_FAILED` (`"failed"`). Completed, cancelled and failed are terminal job states; delivered data conversions follow their own stepping contract below.
- **Worker decoding (`parseData = true`):** Selected filenames or suffixes must end in `.json` or `.ldc`. Workers decode JSON or binary LDC (reporting decode failures with `operation = "parse"`), and polling returns a `FileBatchDataConversion` whose `contentBytes` gives the decoded payload byte count before conversion into Lua values.
- **Incremental conversion:** Advance a `FileBatchDataConversion` on the Lua logic thread with `asyncio.step_file_batch_data(conversion, maxNodes, maxMilliseconds)` using positive budgets. It returns `completed, processed, data` (delivering `data` once on completion). Matching `Engine.loadData`, arrays carry their logical length in `n`, root null becomes `nil`, null array slots are absent keys and null object fields keep `cjson.null`.
- **Conversion lifetime:** Call `asyncio.clear_file_batch_data` to release a conversion idempotently; cancellation, garbage collection and shutdown also invalidate it. Conversions cannot cross Lua VMs or threads.
- **Raw bytes (`parseData` omitted or `false`):** `item.content` contains the original file bytes, including the LDC header and encoded payload. Pass them to `Engine.decodeData` when needed (Blueprint caches keep these bytes for deferred decoding).

## Timing and memory diagnostics

`perfCounter()` returns a monotonic high-resolution timestamp in seconds. `processMemoryMB()` returns current process memory in MiB; use `asizeof` to measure an owned value graph rather than process-wide memory.

documents.content:
# SFML Quickstart

SFML supplies Ludork's graphics, audio, window, input and geometry types. LuaSF exposes it as the global `sf` table, available to project scripts without `require`.

## Official documentation

Use the [SFML 3.1.0 API reference](<https://www.sfml-dev.org/documentation/3.1.0/>) for member details and the [3.1 tutorials](<https://www.sfml-dev.org/tutorials/3.1/>) for graphics and audio concepts. Ludork vendors **SFML 3.1.0**; SFML 2 uses a different constructor style.

## What Ludork provides and what SFML provides

Use `sf` for graphics values and resources; use `Engine`, `GlobalCore` and `GlobalFunctions` for maps, Actors, Blueprints, Scenes, UI and project data. The runtime owns the window, frame loop and UI tree, so project drawing normally uses Engine controls and Scenes rather than a separate `sf.RenderWindow`.

## The sf table

`sf` contains classes, enums and helper functions:

| `sf` group | Members |
|---|---|
| Vector and matrix | `sf.Vector2i`, `sf.Vector2u`, `sf.Vector2f`, `sf.Vector2b`, `sf.Vector3i`, `sf.Vector3u`, `sf.Vector3f`, `sf.Vector3b`, `sf.Vector4i`, `sf.Vector4f`, `sf.Vector4b`, `sf.Mat3`, `sf.Mat4`, and the GLSL aliases `sf.Vec2`, `sf.Vec3`, `sf.Vec4`, `sf.Ivec2`, `sf.Ivec3`, `sf.Ivec4`, `sf.Bvec2`, `sf.Bvec3`, `sf.Bvec4` |
| Geometry | `sf.Color`, `sf.IntRect`, `sf.FloatRect`, `sf.Angle`, `sf.Time`, `sf.Transform` |
| Graphics | `sf.Texture`, `sf.Image`, `sf.Font`, `sf.Text`, `sf.Shader`, `sf.RenderStates`, `sf.RenderTarget`, `sf.RenderTexture`, `sf.RenderWindow`, `sf.VertexArray`, `sf.VertexBuffer`, `sf.Vertex`, `sf.Shape`, `sf.CircleShape`, `sf.ConvexShape`, `sf.RectangleShape`, `sf.Sprite`, `sf.View` |
| Audio | `sf.SoundBuffer`, `sf.Sound`, `sf.Music`, `sf.SoundStream`, `sf.SoundSource`, `sf.Listener`, `sf.SoundRecorder`, `sf.SoundChannel`, `sf.PlaybackDevice` |
| Window and input | `sf.Keyboard`, `sf.Mouse`, `sf.Joystick`, `sf.Touch`, `sf.Sensor`, `sf.Clipboard`, `sf.Cursor`, `sf.VideoMode`, `sf.Event` and its `sf.Event_*` variants |
| System | `sf.Clock`, `sf.sleep`, `sf.Version`, `sf.InputStream`, `sf.FileInputStream`, `sf.MemoryInputStream` |
| Network | `sf.IpAddress`, `sf.Dns`, `sf.Http`, `sf.Ftp`, `sf.Sftp`, `sf.TcpSocket`, `sf.TcpListener`, `sf.UdpSocket`, `sf.SocketSelector`, `sf.Packet` |

Helpers sit directly on `sf`: `sf.seconds`, `sf.milliseconds` and `sf.microseconds` build an `sf.Time`, while `sf.degrees` and `sf.radians` build an `sf.Angle`. Named blend modes such as `sf.BlendAlpha` and `sf.BlendAdd` are also fields on `sf`.

## Value types

Geometry values are native userdata, distinct from Lua tables and Standard containers.

Construct them with `new`:

```lua
local cell = sf.Vector2i.new(4, 7)
local speed = sf.Vector2f.new(1.5, -2.5)
local limit = sf.Vector2u.new(640, 480)
local tint = sf.Color.new(255, 255, 255, 128)
local area = sf.IntRect.new(0, 0, 32, 32)
```

`x` and `y` are readable and writable fields, and `Vector3*` and `Vector4*` add `z` and `w`:

```lua
local position = sf.Vector2i.new(0, 0)
position.x = position.x + 1
position.y = 4

local amount = sf.Vector3f.new(1.0, 0.5, 0.0)
local offset = sf.Vector4f.new(0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0)
```

Two-dimensional vectors support arithmetic:

```lua
local start = sf.Vector2f.new(64.0, 64.0)
local step = sf.Vector2f.new(16.0, 0.0)

local moved = start + step * 2.0   -- Vector2f(96, 64)
local isSame = moved == sf.Vector2f.new(96.0, 64.0) -- true
```

- **Operators:** 2D vectors support `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `==`, plus `*` and `/` with a scalar number. Ordering comparisons such as `<` are not defined, and vector-by-vector multiplication is a method rather than an operator.
- **Methods:** All three `Vector2` types provide `lengthSquared`, `perpendicular`, `dot`, `cross`, `componentWiseMul`, `componentWiseDiv` and `unpack` (returning the components as separate values). `sf.Vector2f` adds `length`, `normalized`, `angle`, `angleTo`, `rotatedBy` and `projectedOnto`, which work in `sf.Angle` rather than degrees.

`sf.Vector2f.new` also accepts a length and an `sf.Angle`, constructing the vector from polar coordinates:

```lua
local forward = sf.Vector2f.new(1.0, sf.degrees(90)) -- Vector2f(0, 1)
```

### Colour, rectangles and time

`sf.Color` holds `r`, `g`, `b` and `a` in the range 0–255. The four-argument constructor takes red, green, blue and alpha, and shorter forms use defaults for omitted components:

```lua
local solid = sf.Color.new(32, 96, 160)
local veil = sf.Color.new(0, 0, 0, 160)
```

Predefined colours are fields on `sf.Color`: `Black`, `White`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Yellow`, `Cyan`, `Magenta` and `Transparent`. `toInteger` returns the packed 32-bit value. `sf.Color` defines no operators, so it cannot be added or compared directly; read and compare its components instead.

`sf.IntRect.new` and `sf.FloatRect.new` take a position and a size, or four numbers. The last two numbers are width and height, not the bottom-right corner:

```lua
local tile = sf.IntRect.new(sf.Vector2i.new(0, 0), sf.Vector2i.new(32, 32))
local same = sf.IntRect.new(0, 0, 32, 32)
local sub = sf.IntRect.new(32, 0, 32, 32)

local origin = tile.position      -- Vector2i(0, 0)
local height = tile.size.y        -- 32
local inside = tile.contains(sf.Vector2i.new(16, 16)) -- true
local overlap = tile.findIntersection(sub) -- an sf.IntRect, or nil, when the rectangles do not overlap
```

`sf.Angle` represents a rotation rather than a raw number, so pass values through `sf.degrees` or `sf.radians`:

```lua
local facing = sf.degrees(90)
local radians = sf.radians(math.pi / 2)

local degrees = facing.asDegrees()
local wrapped = sf.degrees(450).wrapSigned().asDegrees() -- 90
```

`wrapSigned` normalises to `[-180°, 180°)` and `wrapUnsigned` to `[0°, 360°)`; unwrapped angles are also valid. `sf.Angle.new()` and `sf.Angle.Zero` are both zero.

`sf.Time` represents a duration constructed with `sf.seconds`, `sf.milliseconds` or `sf.microseconds`:

```lua
local cooldown = sf.seconds(0.75)

local milliseconds = cooldown.asMilliseconds() -- 750
```

`sf.Time.new()` is zero, and `sf.sleep` pauses the calling thread for the given duration.

## Object types

Graphics objects mirror the SFML inheritance hierarchy in Lua:

```text
sf.Drawable
sf.Transformable
sf.Shape : sf.Drawable, sf.Transformable
sf.CircleShape, sf.ConvexShape, sf.RectangleShape : sf.Shape
sf.Sprite : sf.Drawable, sf.Transformable
sf.Text : sf.Drawable, sf.Transformable
```

Every `sf.Transformable` exposes `setPosition` and `getPosition` (`sf.Vector2f`), `setRotation` and `getRotation` (`sf.Angle`), `setScale` and `getScale`, `setOrigin` and `getOrigin` (`sf.Vector2f`), plus `move`, `rotate`, `scale` and `getTransform`.

```lua
local cell = sf.RectangleShape.new(sf.Vector2f.new(32.0, 32.0))

cell:setPosition(sf.Vector2f.new(64.0, 64.0))
cell:setOrigin(sf.Vector2f.new(16.0, 16.0))
cell:setRotation(sf.degrees(45))
cell:setScale(sf.Vector2f.new(2.0, 2.0))
cell:move(sf.Vector2f.new(8.0, 0.0))

local bounds = cell:getGlobalBounds()
```

`sf.RectangleShape.new` takes a size, `sf.CircleShape.new` takes a radius and a point count, `sf.ConvexShape.new` takes a point count and `sf.Text.new` takes a font, a string and a character size. Shapes also provide `setFillColor` and `setOutlineColor` (`sf.Color`), and `setOutlineThickness` (number).

The abstract base classes (`sf.Drawable`, `sf.Shape`, `sf.RenderTarget`, `sf.InputStream`, `sf.SoundSource`, `sf.SoundStream`, `sf.SoundRecorder`, `sf.SoundFileReader`, `sf.SoundFileWriter` and `sf.Socket`) exist as tables without `new` and cannot be constructed directly. Construct a concrete subclass instead and treat the base class as the parameter or return type.

`sf.Drawable` is the one base that Lua can implement directly: `sf.LuaDrawable.new(drawCallback)` creates a drawable whose `draw` runs in Lua.

Events follow this pattern in reverse: payload types such as `sf.Event_Closed` and `sf.Event_Resized` are constructible, while `sf.Event.new` requires one as its argument. Project code normally receives events rather than constructing them.

## Using SFML in a project

Positions, sizes and rectangles cross the Engine API as `sf` values, so converting between cell coordinates and world positions uses ordinary vector arithmetic:

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")
local Player = require("GlobalFunctions.Player")

local CELL_SIZE = Engine.GetCellSize()

local function cellToWorld(cellX, cellY)
    return sf.Vector2f.new(cellX * CELL_SIZE, cellY * CELL_SIZE)
end

local player = Player.GetPlayer()
if player ~= nil then
    local position = player:getPosition()
    local cell = sf.Vector2i.new(
        math.floor(position.x / CELL_SIZE),
        math.floor(position.y / CELL_SIZE)
    )
end
```

Check the declared type before passing a value: an API expecting `sf.Vector2f` rejects `sf.Vector2i`, a Standard `tuple` or a plain table without converting between them.

JSON and metadata store pure data whereas `sf` values are native userdata, so conversion is explicit. The Game project's save codec writes an `sf.Vector2i` as `{ x, y }` and rebuilds it on load, and its record normaliser turns `sf.Vector2i`, `sf.Vector3i`, `sf.IntRect`, `sf.FloatRect` and `sf.Color` into numeric arrays. Store raw components for data destinations and reconstruct the `sf` value where it is used.

## Where to read more

`Scripts/stub/LuaSF.d.lua` provides the complete Lua declarations and SFML comments indexed by EmmyLua for completion and hover. Member names and parameter order closely follow the official SFML C++ reference linked above.

# Start Page, Workspace and Shortcuts

Navigate the Ludork editor workspace, manage global preferences and user data, browse project files and use keyboard shortcuts, save workflows and diagnostic tools.

## Start page

The Start page offers **New Project**, **Open Project** and up to three recently opened projects. It shares the list with the **Recent** desktop menu. A successfully opened project moves to the top, and unavailable files drop out of the list.

Drag and drop an existing `.proj` file anywhere onto the Start page to open it (if multiple files are dropped, the first existing `.proj` is opened and the rest are ignored). Projects with an unsupported version cannot be opened; see [Main.proj](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#mainproj>).

On macOS, right-click Ludork in the Dock or click its menu bar icon. On Windows, right-click its notification area icon. Choose **New Window** for another Start page, or **Open Project…** or **Recent** to open another project alongside the current one. Opening a `.proj` file from Finder or File Explorer has the same effect. If the project is already open, Ludork brings its window forward. Inside a project window, **File → Open Project** switches the project in that window after you resolve any unsaved changes.

**Close Window** closes that project and stops its running game. By default Ludork stays running after its last window closes. Launching Ludork again, clicking its Dock icon or left-clicking its Windows notification area icon brings back the last active window, or opens a Start page if all windows have closed.

Choose **Quit Ludork** to exit the application. Each project with unsaved changes prompts before any project window closes. Cancelling a prompt or a failed save keeps the windows open. To exit automatically when the last window closes, clear **Keep Running After Closing the Last Window** in the desktop menu. Clearing it while all windows are closed exits Ludork immediately.

## Main workspace

| Area | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Left panel** | **Map List** for ordinary maps and composite worlds. |
| **Centre panel** | Map canvas with layer tabs above it. Tile and Actor mode controls sit beside the canvas (hidden for world maps). |
| **Right panel** | Tile palette in Tile mode, or **World Outliner** and **Actor Info** in Actor mode. |
| **Bottom strip** | **File Explorer** tabs and **Console**. |
| **Toolbar** | **Construct → Export → Play** / **Stop** (Standalone projects hide **Construct**). See [Run, Debug and Package](<Run Debug and Package.md>). |

Resource windows display a loading indicator while opening; if loading fails, click **Retry**. Clicking a task completion notification returns you to the project or result window that produced it.

## Online documentation

Press `F1` to open the online manual inside the editor. Development editors open `trunk` (`/Ludork/docs/trunk/`); release editors open the frozen major.minor snapshot matching their version (for example, `1.0.7` opens `/Ludork/docs/v1.0/`).

The manual starts in the active editor language, with language and version selectors available in the sidebar. **About** and third-party notices load online from the same version, while **About** displays the installed package version.

Embedded pages hide website navigation: internal documentation links stay inside the window, whereas the homepage, downloads and external links open in the system browser. An internet connection is required, and failed loads offer **Retry**. Windows requires Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (offering an install link if missing); macOS uses the system WKWebView.

## Global editor preferences

Preferences shared across all projects are stored in `~/Ludork/Ludork.plist` on macOS (XML plist; see [Platform, configuration and files](<../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md#platform-configuration-and-files>)) and `~/Ludork/Ludork.ini` on other platforms. macOS never reads or migrates an existing `Ludork.ini`; if the plist is absent, defaults apply.

| Area | Saved preferences |
|---|---|
| **Main window** | Normal position and size, maximised state, map-list and inspector widths, lower-area height, Actor outliner/inspector split and world-map child-list width. |
| **File Explorer** | Initial icon/list view, content zoom, source-list expansion for new workspaces and preferred external open target. |
| **Tool windows** | Position, normal size and maximised state per window type. |
| **Tool content** | Adjustable split widths or proportions, UI Timeline and system-control category expansion, and particle configuration section expansion. |

- **Defaults and recovery:** File Explorer defaults to icon view, `100%` zoom, a collapsed source list and the system file manager. Saved project tabs use their own display preferences independently. Missing or invalid values fall back to defaults. An unreadable or malformed plist is reported and never overwritten by saves — repair it and restart before saving preferences again.
- **Scope and monitors:** Project browsing and map selection live in `Main.proj`; global preferences never modify project files or restore search text, input drafts, layer selection or canvas view state. Window layouts adapt to connected monitors, restoring the latest non-minimised geometry per window type. For project-specific display preferences, see [Viewport options](<../PreviewHost/Map and World Previews.md#viewport-options>).

## User data directory

Windows and macOS editors store persistent data under `~/Ludork` (`C:\Users\<user>\Ludork` on Windows, `/Users/<user>/Ludork` on macOS) across installed, portable and repository runs.

| Data | Path beneath `~/Ludork` |
|---|---|
| Preferences, recent projects and window layouts | `Ludork.plist` (macOS) or `Ludork.ini` (other platforms) |
| Global and project plug-ins, registrations and retained data | `Plugins/` and `plugins.json` |
| Downloaded project templates (all four variants) | `Templates/v<base-version>/` |
| Signing profile indexes | `macos-signing.json`, `ios-signing.json`, `harmony-signing.json`, `android-signing.json` |
| Local server test settings | `.localserver/<project-directory-name>/test.json` |
| Project Console logs | `Log/<project-key>/Ludork.log` |
| Windows embedded-browser data | `WebView2/` |

Plug-in discovery also reads the working directory's registry and sources, giving working-directory IDs priority over user copies while keeping retained plug-in data in `~/Ludork` (see [Global and project storage](<../Plug-in Development and Installation/Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#global-and-project-storage>)).

Project files, build outputs and `EditorCache` stay inside each project, game runtime configs and saves keep their own directories, passwords live in the OS credential store, and macOS manages its WebKit cache separately.

> **Warning:** On Windows, MSI and EXE uninstallers select **Delete user data** by default, deleting the verified initiating user's entire `~/Ludork` directory — including all plug-ins, registrations, preferences, logs, template caches, browser data and signing indexes.
>
> Quit Ludork and back up needed files before uninstalling, or clear the option to keep your data. Projects outside `~/Ludork` (such as `~/LudorkProjects`) and other users' data are never deleted. Removing the macOS application leaves `~/Ludork` intact.

| Uninstaller | Flag | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows MSI** | `REMOVE_USER_DATA=0` (keep) / `1` (delete, default) | Runs only on explicit full uninstall after the removal transaction commits (never during repair or major upgrade). Deletion errors are reported and may require manual cleanup. Service accounts and sessions whose initiating user cannot be verified must pass `REMOVE_USER_DATA=0`. |
| **Windows EXE** | `/REMOVEUSERDATA=0` (keep) / `1` (delete, default) | Honoured in interactive and silent removal while keeping the Windows uninstall entry. If another administrator supplies UAC credentials, no interactive desktop exists, or the initiating user cannot be confirmed, user data is preserved and manual cleanup is requested rather than substituting the administrator's or desktop user's directory. |

If manual cleanup is required, sign in as the intended user, back up anything needed and delete only that user's `~/Ludork` directory.

### Moving existing editor data

Apart from the working-directory plug-in scan, legacy storage locations are not read or migrated automatically (Windows previously stored data in the installation directory and repository runs could use the working directory or repository; macOS previously kept settings and signing indexes in `~/Library/Application Support/Ludork`, while published plug-ins and template caches already used `~/Ludork`).

1. Quit Ludork and back up needed files **before uninstalling an older version**.
2. Install the new version. To keep existing plug-ins, clear the EXE installer's **Install Official Plug-ins** option or pass `INSTALL_OFFICIAL_PLUGINS=0` to MSI (restoring plug-ins before an install with that option enabled overwrites them).
3. Restore preferences in the [current platform format](#global-editor-preferences), signing indexes, template caches and local server settings into `~/Ludork`, backing up any existing destination files first. Restore `Plugins` and `plugins.json` together from the same backup.

System credential-store entries and project files do not need to move.

## Global shortcuts

The primary modifier is `Ctrl` on Windows and `Command` on macOS.

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl/Command+N` | New Project |
| `Ctrl/Command+O` | Open Project |
| `Ctrl/Command+S` | Save |
| `Ctrl/Command+Z` | Undo |
| `Ctrl/Command+Shift+Z` or `Ctrl/Command+Y` | Redo |
| `Ctrl/Command+W` | Close the current project window |
| `Command+Q` (macOS) | Quit Ludork |
| `Ctrl/Command+1` | Tile mode |
| `Ctrl/Command+2` | Actor mode |
| `F1` | Ludork Documentation |
| `F3` | Game Config |
| `F4` | System Config |
| `F5` | Animation Overview |
| `F6` | Common Particle Overview |
| `F7` | Tilesets Data |
| `F8` | Common Functions |
| `F9` | Game Variables |
| `F10` | General Data |

- **Context-specific `F2` rename:** Renames the selected event tab (Blueprint editor), Common Function (Common Functions window), file (File Explorer on Windows/Linux; unavailable on macOS) or time tag (animation editor). Windows do not display an `F2` hint.
- **Dialog keys:** Single-button hint and error dialogs close with `Enter`, `Return`, `Space` or `Escape`. Confirmation dialogs confirm with `Enter`, `Return` or `Space`, and cancel with `Escape`.

## Editing and saving

Displayed field defaults are written only when edited. Clearable file fields list **Clear** first in every directory and file filter (select and click **Open**, press `Enter` or double-click to clear; **Cancel** or `Escape` keeps the previous value). Save dialogs, multi-file imports and required-file selectors omit **Clear**.

### Saving and progress locks

- **Global Save:** Managed edits and asset renames or moves stay in memory until Save (**Discard** restores saved paths). Every Save button and `Ctrl/Command+S` writes all modified documents (including unopened ones); Construct, Export, Play and Pack invoke the same save flow. Successful saves show no dialog; failures report only failed items and their errors. Normal Save validates changed Blueprints, whereas forced save can retain unfinished graphs. [Game Config](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>) writes immediately on confirmation.
- **Operation locks:** Save, deletion, file transfers, renames, Undo and Redo temporarily disable editing, project switching and window closing. Longer operations (including pre-deletion reference checks) display a non-cancellable animated progress dialog showing stage, current file and completed count, yielding to any confirmation prompt. If project or external files change during validation, the editor asks you to retry.
- **Unsaved markers:** Modified documents show `*` in File Explorer, window titles and resource selectors. Closing a resource window preserves unsaved changes until the project closes. Closing or replacing a project lists unsaved files with **Save**, **Discard** and **Cancel**; a save failure keeps modified markers and prevents closing.

### Undo, Redo and pending moves

- **Per-file history:** Undo and Redo operate on the active file (up to `100` steps). Windows displaying the same file share data and history across close and reopen. Continuous text or numeric input in one field merges into a single step (ended by changing control or view, automatic updates, Save, Undo or Redo); buttons, checkboxes and selections are individual steps.
- **Reference barriers:** Undo cannot restore references to deleted resources or unavailable/renamed asset paths or General Data member IDs (rejected steps leave document and history unchanged). Automatic reference updates insert a marked Undo barrier in every updated target file (including unopened files): later edits stay undoable, but Undo stops at the barrier and identifies its source. Undoing or redoing the source rename updates targets against current content and places a new barrier, preserving unrelated edits. Save preserves history and barriers.
- **Pending asset paths:** Select a file or folder in File Explorer to Undo or Redo its path change (undoing a folder move preserves later independent child changes). Save pending moves before copying, deleting, importing, creating or writing files at their source or destination paths; further renames and moves remain allowed.
- **External-change conflicts:** **Keep memory** accepts disk contents while keeping pending paths, updated references and Undo/Redo (fails without partial changes if a source is missing or destination is occupied). **Use disk** cancels affected pending moves and restores recognised references to saved paths while preserving unrelated edits, but does not restore missing files or clear their references.

## File explorer and reference tree

**File Explorer** browses `Assets` and `Data` through the source list and breadcrumbs (Up stops at the selected root).

### Tabs, navigation and layout

- **Multiple tabs:** Click **＋** beside **Console** or choose **View → New File Explorer Tab**. The first **File Explorer** tab stays permanently open; extra tabs are numbered and show **×**. New tabs inherit the most recently active File Explorer's directory and display preferences with empty search, history and selection; closing an active extra tab focuses the tab to its left.
- **History and Locate:** Navigate each tab's history via **Back** / **Forward**, `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right` or mouse side buttons (restoring search, expanded folders, selection, scroll and display preferences; navigating after Back clears forward history; refreshing, changing selection/search or switching tabs adds no entry).
  - Resource **Locate** targets the most recently active File Explorer even while Console is active. Reopening restores tabs, directories, display preferences and active tab per [Main.proj](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#mainproj>); search, history, selection and scroll are session-only.
- **Views and zoom:** List view expands/collapses folders in place (double-click enters; `Right` expands or selects first child; `Left` collapses or selects parent; expansion lasts for the session), whereas icon view and search results are flat. Zoom `50%–200%` with `Ctrl/Command+wheel` or the bottom-right slider, and press `F5` to refresh external changes.
- **Search:** Matches filenames case-insensitively in the current directory and subdirectories (including unsaved resources, excluding symlink folders). Clearing the box, changing directories or locating exits search.
- **Media previews:** Image and video files show supported thumbnails (see [Actor previews](<../PreviewHost/UI Actor Particle and Subtitle Previews.md>) for Blueprint JSON). Press `Space` on an image, audio or video file (or use a file selector's right-hand pane) to preview locally starting paused, with playback, seek and volume controls (`Escape` closes). Preview relies on system codecs (Windows needs Edge WebView2 Runtime), requires no FFmpeg option or native build, and reports unsupported or damaged files.

### File operations, deletion and reference tree

- **Context menus and drag-and-drop:** Right-click an entry for item actions or empty space for the current directory menu. File Explorer tabs share copied and cut files within the same project. Pasting or dropping targets a folder directly, a file's containing folder, or the current directory on empty space (including expanded folders and search results); `Ctrl/Command+V` uses the selected entry or current directory if none or multiple are selected.
  - Drag any selected entry to move the group (clicking and releasing without dragging selects just that entry; folders cannot move into themselves or descendants). Right-click and choose **Show in File Explorer** (Windows) or **Show in Finder** (macOS) to reveal the right-clicked entry only (disabled for unsaved entries; never saves pending changes).
- **Duplicating and move conflicts:** Duplicate a folder in place with `Ctrl/Command+C` followed by `Ctrl/Command+V` (conflicts append `_copy`, `_copy2`, placed before file extensions; copied folders appear once complete). A cut or drag causing duplicate destinations or name collisions rejects the entire move (leaving the cut clipboard ready after fixing conflicts). On disk error during a move, the editor attempts rollback, reporting any unreturned file and keeping remaining items on the cut clipboard.
- **Reference tree and creation:** The reference tree shows outgoing and incoming references. Create, rename and move managed resources in the editor so recognised references update automatically (update arbitrary strings and source code manually). Creating or copying a managed resource leaves it unsaved without a creation Undo step; renames appear immediately and Global Save commits paths and references together. [Fixed resource directories](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#fixed-resource-directories>) enforce additional path restrictions.
- **Pre-deletion checks:** Remove recognised references and save referring files before deleting. For `Assets` files and folders, File Explorer checks both current and last saved project data (including nested folder contents) and blocks the entire selection if referenced, listing each asset, referring file and field (delete referring files first rather than together).
- **Recycling and recovery:** Confirmed deletions move saved files to the Windows Recycle Bin or macOS Trash (keeping items that fail to recycle while already-recycled items stay deleted). Recycling preserves the last saved disk path and content, discarding unsaved edits; never-saved resources disappear without a recoverable copy. Deleted resources leave managed documents/lists so Save does not recreate them; Editor Undo cannot undo resource deletion (restore via Trash/Recycle Bin and reopen the project; in-document item deletions use document Undo).

### Opening in external editors

The open menu at the upper right always offers the system file manager (opening the active directory) and remembers your selection as the preferred target, falling back to the system file manager when unavailable on another project or machine without overwriting the preference.

It lists installed VS Code and Cursor, plus installed CLion and Windows Visual Studio 2022 for C++ Source projects. VS Code, Cursor and CLion open the project root regardless of the current File Explorer path. When `.idea` or `.vs` is absent, opening CLion or Visual Studio prompts (**Initialise IDE Environment**) before running the project's environment generator (cancelling leaves the project unchanged); Visual Studio opens the generated root `Main.sln`.

## Console and performance monitor

**Console** collects plug-in, build and runtime output and accepts input only while a compatible runtime connection is active. Open **Edit → Development Tools and Settings → Performance Monitor** to view live frame, logic and memory samples while the game runs.

Console output writes to `~/Ludork/Log/<project-key>/Ludork.log`, keyed by the project's absolute path so identically named projects in different folders stay separated. Each new session archives the previous log with its modification timestamp; moving or renaming a project starts a new log directory while previous logs stay on disk.

### World-streaming samples

When profiling a composite world, Performance Monitor includes an optional `worldStreaming` snapshot (omitted for ordinary maps and unprofiled ticks):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queueDepth` | Child regions waiting in the streaming queue. |
| `reading` | Regions currently in `Reading`. |
| `prepared` | Loaded regions in `Prepared`. |
| `active` | Regions in `Active`. |
| `dormant` | Loaded regions in `Dormant`. |
| `cacheBytes` | Conservative estimate for the non-Active region cache (not an exact process, Lua, native or GPU memory total). |
| `publishMilliseconds` | Time spent converting and publishing regions during the logic tick. |
| `visibleTileChunks` | Unique 32×32-cell `TileLayer` chunks submitted by visible child layers in the latest draw. |
| `activeActors` | Actors currently present in the world's Active update/render batches. |

![Console output after a Game project run](../../../images/editor/console-output.png)

![Performance Monitor waiting for runtime telemetry](../../../images/editor/console-performance.png)

*The monitor waits until a compatible runtime telemetry session connects.*
