documents.content:
# Project Settings and Asset Layout

A Ludork project stores editor and packaging settings in `Main.proj`, runtime preferences in its [game configuration](#game-configuration), raw resources in `Assets`, editor-authored JSON in `Data` and runtime Lua code in `Scripts`. C++ Source projects also include the native sources described in [Build and Module Layout](<../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md>).

All editor-written project JSON (`Main.proj`, `Data` documents and export records) uses UTF-8 without a byte order mark (BOM) and LF line endings on every platform, preventing platform-specific line-ending diffs.

## Main.proj

`Main.proj` defines project compatibility, native build flags, packaging defaults and project-scoped workspace state. For example, the Game project enables C++ and FFmpeg and defaults to an individual run window:

```json
{
  "version": "v1.0",
  "Cpp": true,
  "ffmpeg": true,
  "IndividualWindow": true,
  "packaging": {
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "dev": false
  },
  "editor": {
    "fileExplorer": {
      "tabs": [
        {
          "number": 1,
          "path": "Assets",
          "iconView": true,
          "zoom": 100,
          "sourcesExpanded": false
        }
      ],
      "activeTabNumber": 1
    }
  }
}
```

| Key | Purpose and rules |
|---|---|
| `version` | Required engine compatibility version (`v<major>.<minor>`, e.g. `"v1.0"` from editor `1.0.7`). This edition supports `v1.0`; missing, malformed or unsupported values block opening. Opening a supported older project neither migrates contents nor rewrites `version`. |
| `Cpp`, `ffmpeg` | Enable C++ Source mode and FFmpeg support; match the template selected at project creation. |
| `compiler` | Optional Windows C++ Source compiler selector. Absent means MSVC; MinGW stores the absolute path to `g++.exe` (e.g. `"C:\\Tools\\mingw64\\bin\\g++.exe"`); LLVM Clang stores the absolute path to `clang-cl.exe` (e.g. `"C:\\Program Files\\LLVM\\bin\\clang-cl.exe"`). Selecting MSVC removes this field. |
| `packaging.version`, `packaging.dev` | Store the game's base release version (default `"1.0.0"`) and internal dev-package flag (default `false`), independent of top-level `version`. Managed via Pack Options or overridden per CLI run; see [Release version and internal packages](<Run Debug and Package.md#release-version-and-internal-packages>). |
| `editor.fileExplorer` | Saves `tabs` (ordered entries with `number`, relative `path`, `iconView`, `zoom` `50–200` and `sourcesExpanded`) and `activeTabNumber`. Tab 1 always exists and cannot close. Defaults to `Assets` with [global initial display preferences](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#global-editor-preferences>). |
| `lastOpenedMapKey` | Stores the last selected map key (including world maps and child maps) and saves immediately on selection change without saving map data. Missing or invalid values pick the first entry (none if empty). Live Debug map changes do not overwrite it. |
| `editor.mapList.expanded` | Lists keys of expanded Map List parent rows (e.g. `["World_01", "Map_02"]`). Toggling rows does not mark the project modified; the state saves with the project and restores on open. Missing keys are ignored and an empty list omits the entry. |

Preserve unknown keys as editor-owned state. Editor appearance and window layouts are stored globally rather than in `Main.proj` (see [Global editor preferences](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#global-editor-preferences>)).

- **Machine-specific Windows compiler:** Construct, Preview and Windows packaging require the exact configured `compiler` and report an error instead of falling back to another toolchain. After moving a project to another machine, select a local compiler via [Change project compiler](<Run Debug and Package.md#windows-project-compiler>) so required build cleanup runs; do not edit `compiler` by hand while old native outputs exist. General templates and converted Standalone projects omit this field.
- **File Explorer path recovery:** Saved paths must stay beneath `Assets` or `Data`. If a saved folder no longer exists, reopening falls back to its nearest existing parent in the same root; invalid, absolute, symlinked or out-of-root paths fall back to `Assets`. Search text, navigation history, selection and scroll position are not written to `Main.proj`. See [File explorer and reference tree](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#file-explorer-and-reference-tree>).

## Game configuration

Open **Game → Game Config** (`F3`) to edit the game's language, display and audio settings. **Confirm** writes immediately outside document Undo and unsaved changes; **Cancel** keeps previous values. A write error leaves the dialog open.

- **Format:** macOS stores settings in XML `Main.plist`; other platforms (including iOS) use `Main.ini` with identical sections, keys and defaults. macOS never reads or migrates an existing `Main.ini`; when `Main.plist` is absent, defaults apply and `Main.ini` is untouched. An unreadable or malformed plist is reported and cannot be overwritten with defaults — repair it before saving. See [Platform, configuration and files](<../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md#platform-configuration-and-files>).
- **Languages:** Populated from exported `Scripts/Source/Locale/*.lua` (excluding `Core.lua`) each time the dialog opens, keeping the currently configured language selectable even if its export is missing. Export workbook changes before choosing a newly added language.
- **Scale row:** Always shown in the editor; the in-game Config window shows it only when `Display.isDisplayScaleConfigurable()` reports host support.

### User data locations

| Platform | User data root (`Main.plist`/`Main.ini`, `Save/`, runtime caches) |
|---|---|
| Windows, macOS, Linux | `~/<APP_NAME>` (`C:\Users\<user>\<APP_NAME>` on Windows, `/Users/<user>/<APP_NAME>` on macOS) across Play, IDE runs, direct runs and packaged builds. |
| iOS | `~/Library/Application Support/<APP_NAME>` |
| Android, HarmonyOS | `<APP_NAME>` beneath the app-private user-data root |
| WebGL | Virtual `/UserData/<APP_NAME>` persisted in IndexedDB per browser profile and site origin (scheme, host and port). |

On WebGL, the host restores `/UserData/<APP_NAME>` before `Entry` runs, and built-in config/save writes synchronise IndexedDB so refreshes retain completed writes. Clearing site data, changing origin or using private browsing can remove or isolate storage; `APP_NAME` never grants cross-origin access.

`APP_NAME` is configured during [project creation](<../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#template-reference>) and stored statically in `Scripts/Entry.lua`. Projects sharing an `APP_NAME` share configuration, saves and caches for the current user; changing it points to a new directory without migrating old files.

Project-local configs and `Save/` are never read or written. Use the [runtime path APIs](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#configuration>) to resolve paths, and see [Game Settings Reference](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Game Settings Reference.md>) for keys, defaults and timing.

## System Config

Open **Database → System Config** (`F4`) to edit JSON configuration files under `Data/Configs` (objects with `type: "system"` or no `type`, keyed by extensionless relative paths). Select **Audio**, **System** or **Gameplay** on the left to display its fields on the right.

![System Config with a configuration list on the left and the selected form on the right](../../../images/editor/system-config.png)

*Select **System** to configure title, dimensions and startup settings, or **Audio** for music and sound resources.*

**Gameplay** edits shared gameplay settings using a **Use default** checkbox on every row:

- **Enabled (default for new data):** Hides the value editor and writes `null` to `value` so the game uses the Lua script default. Re-checking **Use default** clears a saved override.
- **Disabled:** Reads the saved Lua source (save script edits first) to populate the current script default and create an override. Existing overrides do not track later script changes; toggle **Use default** on and off to re-read. If the default cannot be read, the row stays on **Use default** and shows the reason.
- **Field inputs:** Enums use drop-downs, text/numbers accept typed input, and booleans use checkboxes. Clearing a numeric input restores **Use default**, whereas an empty string, `false` and numeric `0` are explicit values (enter positive values for save-slot count and tutorial shrink duration).

See the [shared Gameplay configuration reference](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#shared-gameplay-configuration>) for supported keys and defaults. Save and restart the game to apply changes. Switching entries preserves unsaved edits (marked with `*` in the list and title). Global Save (`Ctrl/Command+S`) writes changes; Undo/Redo applies per selected configuration.

## Fixed resource directories

The editor protects the following project directories — including all files and subdirectories inside them — for runtime configuration and built-in resources:

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Data/Configs` | Game configuration (startup, audio and gameplay settings) |
| `Assets/Shaders/Global` | Built-in rendering shaders |
| `Data/Curves/Global` | Shared animation and effect curves |
| `Data/Materials/Global` | Shared materials such as `Standard.json` |
| `Data/TextConfigs/Global` | Shared text styles |

You can edit, save and copy resources inside these directories, but File Explorer blocks renaming (including case-only renames), moving or deleting any protected entry or ancestor containing one. Selecting a protected entry with other items blocks the entire operation and reports the protected path.

## Assets

Authoring files live in the physical `Assets` directory. Stored references must use exact-case `/Game/Assets/...` paths with `/` separators and file extensions on every platform (paths like `Assets/...`, category-relative paths, native absolute paths and traversal segments are invalid).

`PathVars` marks a field as a validated `/Game/Assets/...` reference unless `PathRoot` selects `"Project"` files or `"Data"` documents; config `base` sets only the picker root. Direct LuaSF file constructors and standard physical filesystem calls use native paths.

Resource resolution rejects symbolic links, broken links, reparse points and inaccessible paths anywhere from the target up to its resource root. Path conversion and picker roots may name files or directories not yet created, provided existing ancestors pass those checks.

Keep conventional top-level subdirectories so pickers filter accurately: `Tilesets`, `Autotiles`, `Characters`, `Animations`, `Particles`, `Icons`, `Fonts`, `Musics`, `Sounds`, `Voices`, `Shaders`, `Panoramas`, `Transitions`, `System` and `Videos`. Packaging with `.ldpak` archives the entire `Assets` tree into `Assets.ldpak` (including files directly in `Assets`) without changing logical paths.

Rename or move files and folders inside `Assets` through the editor so recognised references update automatically; external renames, handwritten source strings and dynamic paths require manual updates. See [Editing and saving](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#editing-and-saving>).

## Data and Scripts

`Data` holds editor-authored JSON and the localisation workbook:

| Location | Reference format and purpose |
|---|---|
| `Data/Materials` | Full `Data/Materials/...json` paths; see [Materials](<Materials.md>). |
| `Data/Subtitles` | Full `Data/Subtitles/...json` paths; see [Video Subtitles](<Video Subtitles.md>). |
| `Data/Particles` | Extensionless relative keys such as `Combat/Hit`; see [Common Particles](<Common Particles.md>). |
| `Data/UI` | Extensionless relative asset keys; see [UI Asset Editor](<UI Asset Editor.md>). |
| `Data/TextConfigs` | Shared text styles and rich-text tags (ordinary UI text styles live on their UI nodes). |
| `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx` | Localisation workbook managed by [Official Locale Tools](<../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Locale Tools.md>). |

`Scripts` stores runtime Lua, metadata and type declarations. See [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md>), [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>) and [General Data and Text Config](<General Data and Text Config.md>) for module layout and generated outputs.

> **Important:** Do not hand-edit `Engine_meta.lua`, `GlobalCore_meta.lua`, `GlobalFunctions_meta.lua` or generated Core/LuaSF declarations. Keep `Data` and `Scripts` as loose directories while authoring; packaging removes `Scripts/stub` and rejects misplaced `.d.lua` files (see [Loose and packed output](<Run Debug and Package.md#loose-and-packed-output>)).

### Runtime resource lookup

Logical `/Game/Assets/...`, `/Game/Data/...` and `/Game/Scripts/...` paths, relative `Data/...` references and Lua module names resolve in strict priority order:

1. **User data directory:** Beneath `Engine.getUserDataPath()` (set by `Engine.setAppName` in default Entry; the Entry script itself loads from the game root). The user root need not contain all three trees.
2. **Game root or `.ldpak` archive:** The packaged game's loose directory or archive entry.

For example, `/Game/Assets/System/icon.png` loads `<user-data>/Assets/System/icon.png` if present, otherwise the game's `Assets/System/icon.png` or `Assets.ldpak` entry. Absolute physical Data paths use their explicit location.

- **Source beats format:** A user `.ldc` overrides a game `.json`, a user `.luac` overrides a game `.lua`, and encrypted shader variants follow the same rule. Each API's normal format rules apply within each source; exact-path JSON reads never fall back to encrypted files.
- **Errors and enumeration:** Missing files fall through to the next source, whereas unreadable, damaged or invalid files report their error immediately. Data directory enumeration merges both sources, deduplicates and gives user entries priority (including file/directory conflicts).
- **Downloaded updates:** Games can write updates to physical user-data paths; new files take effect on the next read or first `require`, while already loaded modules and cached resources keep their live caches (no live replacement or startup rerun). Logical `/Game/...` paths are read-only; write files using explicit physical user-data paths. Native `io.open` and direct LuaSF constructors do not use `/Game` resolution. See [Entry and module order](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md#entry-and-module-order>).

### Map and world-map assets

An ordinary map is `Data/Maps/<Name>.json`. A composite world is a folder `Data/Maps/<WorldFolder>/` containing one `_world.json` manifest and direct child-map `.json` files (deeper nesting is disallowed; non-JSON regular files such as `.DS_Store` are ignored).

Editor [Map List order](<Tilesets Autotiles and Maps.md#map-list-and-composite-worlds>) is stored in `Data/Maps/_info.json` and `Data/Maps/<WorldFolder>/_info.json` as `{"order": ["Map_01", {"Map_02": ["Map_03"]}, "World_01"]}`, where strings name file stems or world folders and single-key objects nest rows visually. The runtime ignores `_info.json`, [packaging](<Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>) excludes it, and `_info` is reserved as a map or world name.

The folder name is the world's path identity, while `_world.json` stores its display `worldName` and serves as the world's identity in selectors and saves (hidden in the Map List). Each child stores its editable `mapName` (staying valid if moved out of the world) and uses its filename as its path and placement identity.

```json
{
  "type": "worldMap",
  "worldName": "{WORLD_01}",
  "width": 256,
  "height": 192,
  "fog": {
    "enabled": false,
    "colour": [255, 255, 255, 255],
    "density": 0.5,
    "scale": 256,
    "velocity": [15, 15],
    "turbulence": 0.5,
    "seed": 0
  },
  "panorama": "",
  "layerOrder": ["floor", "default"],
  "placements": [
    {
      "map": "Map_01.json",
      "rect": [0, 0, 64, 64]
    }
  ]
}
```

- **Coordinates and bounds:** `width`, `height` and `[x, y, width, height]` placement rects use zero-based cells. Each rect must match its child's size and fit inside the world, and each child may be placed at most once. Touching placements and uncovered holes are valid. Temporary overlaps are allowed during editing, but Save rejects overlapping placements.
- **Manifest ownership:** `worldName` must be non-empty. `layerOrder` is derived from placed children (contradictory cycles are rejected). The manifest owns world display name, size, composition, global fog and global panorama; audio, filters and ambient light belong to each child map.
- **Fog format:** Ordinary maps and worlds use the same procedural `fog` object (no fog image asset required); configure it via [Fog](<Tilesets Autotiles and Maps.md#fog>).

> **Note:** Renaming or moving maps updates recognised map-file settings and destinations in `GotoMap` and `RecordTelepoint` Blueprint nodes. Update arbitrary strings and dynamically constructed paths manually.

# Tilesets, Autotiles and Maps

Author tilesets, autotiles, ordinary maps and composite worlds, then paint tile layers and place interactive Actors and lights.

## Tilesets and autotiles

Open **Database → Tilesets Data** (`F7`) to configure tilesets (**Tilesets Data** tab) and animated or connected autotiles (**AutoTiles** tab). Store source images under `Assets/Tilesets` or `Assets/Autotiles`, and their JSON definitions in the corresponding `Data` subdirectory.

Select a definition, edit its display `name`, and use the browse button beside **File Name** to pick its source image. The map palette displays `name` on tabs while the JSON filename acts as the internal key: editing `name` preserves references, whereas renaming the key updates every affected map's `layerTileset` (including unopened maps) under the shared [save and Undo rules](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#editing-and-saving>).

![Tilesets Data tab showing per-tile passability](../../../images/editor/tilesets-data.png)

*In Passable mode, circles mark passable tiles and crosses mark blocked tiles.*

![AutoTiles tab showing whole-asset passability](../../../images/editor/auto-tile.png)

*Autotile properties apply to the entire asset rather than individual displayed cells.*

### Editing tile properties

| Mode | Ordinary tileset (per tile) | Autotile (whole asset) |
|---|---|---|
| **Passable** | Left-click toggles tile passability. | Toggles whole-asset passability. |
| **Material** | Left-click selects a [material resource](<Materials.md>); clearing removes the sparse entry and restores default rendering. | Assigns one [material resource](<Materials.md>) to the asset. |
| **Dir4** | Left-click toggles passability on the edge nearest the click. | Not applicable. |

In an ordinary tileset, `Shift+left-drag` copies the pressed source tile's property across every crossed cell in a single Undo step (boolean in **Passable**, resource reference in **Material**, all four edges in **Dir4**). Autotiles do not support this batch brush.

> **Note:** Modifying a tileset after maps are authored can change how existing tile indices render. Moving a tileset or editing arbitrary gameplay strings does not rewrite hardcoded string paths automatically.

### Map layer order

Map JSON requires a `layerOrder` string array defining the authoritative draw and Actor-processing sequence, while `layers` and `actors` are dictionaries keyed by those names and kept in sync by the editor. Loading ordinary maps and streamed child maps rejects missing or duplicate layer references, layers absent from `layerOrder`, and Actor groups whose layer is absent from `layerOrder`. Loading never infers order from JSON key order.

![Map editor with layer tabs above the canvas and a tile palette on the right](../../../images/editor/tile-layers.png)

*Select a layer tab above the canvas to paint from the tile palette; eye icons toggle layer visibility.*

## Map list and composite worlds

The **Map List** displays ordinary maps and composite worlds. A world row shows `worldName` from `_world.json` and expands to list direct child maps by their editable `mapName` (`_world.json` stays hidden).

Use **World Map Properties** to change `worldName` and **Rename World Map** to rename the folder and runtime paths. Each child stores its own **Map Name** so it stays usable standalone; select a world to open its composition panel and use context menus to create each asset type.

### Ordering, nesting and moving maps

- **Visual order (`_info.json`):** The Map List reflects `Data/Maps/_info.json` (top level) and each world's `_info.json` (children). Nesting is purely organisational with no runtime effect. Drag a row to the top or bottom edge of another row to reorder, or onto its centre to nest beneath it (nested rows move with their parent). Worlds stay at the top level and cannot be nested. Unlisted maps appear last in filename order; stale entries are dropped. Reordering marks the project modified (not part of Undo/Redo).
- **Moving into or out of a world:** Dragging an ordinary map onto a world (or among its rows) moves that map and its nested children into the world folder; dragging a child to the top level or another world moves it out. Moved maps arrive unplaced, and leaving a world removes any placement.
  - Moving updates recognised references and inserts an Undo barrier. Moves are rejected on destination name collision, Actor tag conflict in the destination world, or active references to a map moving into a world (unplaced children cannot be runtime destinations).
- **Create, copy, rename and delete:** Use the Map List (not File Explorer, which preserves `Data/Maps` hierarchy) to create, delete or move maps between top level and worlds. Copying a child assigns fresh Actor map tags without placing the copy.
  - Renaming updates recognised references (see [Project Settings and Asset Layout](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md>)); automatic reference, placement and layer-order updates insert Undo barriers across separate world and child histories. Deleting a world recycles its entire saved directory (manifest, children and other files); see [resource deletion and recovery](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#file-explorer-and-reference-tree>).

### Composing a world

![World composition panel with child-map thumbnails and placed maps](../../../images/editor/world-map.png)

*Child-map thumbnails display placement coordinates alongside the combined canvas preview.*

- **Placing and removing:** Drag an unplaced child onto the world canvas to place it, drag a placed child to reposition it, and press `Delete` / `Backspace` (or use its context menu) to unplace it. Each placement edit is one Undo/Redo step.
- **Overlaps and bounds:** Temporary overlaps are permitted while arranging or resizing a child map, but Save fails until all overlaps are resolved. Bounds and layer-order violations are rejected immediately during editing, and resizing cannot push a child outside the world. Remove a child's placement and save before deleting its file. Actor tags must be unique across the world, and non-JSON regular files are ignored.
- **Click priority:** The selected placement draws above overlapping siblings within each layer and takes click priority so you can drag it free; otherwise the last placement takes priority. You can also drag an obscured child from the child-map list onto the canvas.
- **Navigation:** Scroll or pan the canvas, and zoom with `Ctrl+wheel` (Windows/Linux) or `Command+wheel`/pinch (macOS). See [Map and World Previews](<../PreviewHost/Map and World Previews.md>).

### New map defaults and map properties

Creating an ordinary map or world child pre-fills **Map Properties** (dimensions, ambient light, BGM/BGS and filters, fog parameters and panorama) as independent copies from the most recently modified map, assigning fresh filename and map-name defaults.

Current-session edits (including unsaved edits and Undo/Redo) take priority over file modification time, whereas opening or saving alone does not alter edit order. With no existing maps, standard defaults apply.

- **Ambient Light:** Click the swatch button (displaying ARGB and a checkerboard for transparency) to choose a colour.
- **Audio and Panorama:** Click the browse button beside BGM, BGS or **Panorama** (conventionally in `Assets/Panoramas`) to select a file, or choose **Clear** to remove it, then confirm. World Map Properties configures a global panorama the same way. See [Panorama rendering](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Resources Audio Video and Effects.md#shaders-fog-and-transitions>).

## Fog

**Map Properties** and **World Map Properties** share identical **Fog** settings (enable fog to reveal controls). The GPU generates the noise pattern procedurally in world coordinates with no asset image required, so panning and zooming do not pin fog to the screen. Worlds can combine global fog with child-region fog seamlessly across region boundaries.

| Setting | Meaning | Standard default |
|---|---|---|
| **Enabled** | Whether the map renders fog. | Off |
| **Colour** | RGBA tint and alpha. | White, fully opaque |
| **Density** | Fog coverage (`0–1`). | `0.5` |
| **Scale** | Pattern size in map pixels (smaller values produce smaller cloud patches). | `256` |
| **Velocity X / Y** | Drift speed in map pixels per second. | `15` / `15` |
| **Turbulence** | Pattern variation (`0–1`). | `0.5` |
| **Seed** | Non-negative integer choosing a repeatable pattern. | `0` |

Density controls coverage and colour alpha controls opacity; black fog darkens the scene while preserving density variation. For example, the supplied `Map_02` uses black `(0, 0, 0, 128)` with Density `0.5`, Scale `128`, Velocity `[15, 15]` and Turbulence `0.8`.

See [Viewport options](<../PreviewHost/Map and World Previews.md#viewport-options>) for preview controls and [Map and world-map assets](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#map-and-world-map-assets>) for the JSON schema.

## Layers and painting

Tile mode supports creating, renaming, reordering, copying, pasting and deleting layers, and assigning a [layer material](<Materials.md#create-and-assign>). Selecting a tileset tab immediately switches the active layer's tileset, reinterpreting existing tile indices against it.

- **Visibility:** Each layer tab shows its name on the left and a visibility toggle on the right. Visibility is saved map data; hidden layers do not render and are read-only. **Overview** displays all visible layers at full brightness; selecting a single layer dims the others without altering draw order.
- **Brush selection:** Select a tile, multi-tile region or autotile in the palette. Clicking a single selected ordinary tile again clears selection; with nothing selected, the brush erases. Zooming and panning never modify map data.

| Gesture | Painting action |
|---|---|
| `Left-drag` | Paint continuously (multi-tile selections place the full pattern at each position). |
| `Shift+left-drag` | Fill the outlined rectangle, repeating multi-tile patterns from the top-left corner and clipping to bounds. |
| `Shift+left-click` | Paint a single cell. |
| `Right-click` | Sample the clicked cell. |
| `Alt+left-click` (`Option+left-click` on macOS) | Flood-fill the 4-connected region matching the clicked cell's tile and autotile values (works with multi-tile patterns, autotiles and erase). |

Each brush stroke, rectangle or flood-fill is one Undo step. Saving during a stroke starts a new Undo step for subsequent painting; Undo or Redo ends the active stroke until the mouse button is pressed again.

## Lights and Actors

Use Actor mode to place Blueprint instances, move them and edit exposed attributes (instance overrides never alter Blueprint defaults). Attach lights via `lightComp` and edit them in **Actor Info**; see [Light Component](<Actor Components/Light.md>) for Blueprint defaults and fields.

![Actor mode with the World Outliner and material parameter overrides in Actor Info](../../../images/editor/actor-mode.png)

*Selecting an instance in **World Outliner** exposes its overrides in **Actor Info**, such as overriding the `Poison` material's `lightBlock` parameter.*

### Selecting and editing Actors

Project editing supports single or multiple Actor selection on the active layer of an ordinary map or independently opened world child (Live Debug supports single selection only).

| Location and gesture | Selection behaviour |
|---|---|
| **World Outliner:** plain click | Replace selection with that Actor. |
| **World Outliner:** `Ctrl-click` (`Command-click` on macOS) | Toggle that Actor. |
| **World Outliner:** `Shift-click` | Select range from the selection anchor (`Ctrl/Command+Shift` adds the range). |
| **World Outliner:** click another layer's Actor or layer row | Switch layers and select that Actor, or clear selection on a layer row. |
| **Map:** plain click on a selected Actor | Keep group selection ready to drag. |
| **Map:** plain click on an unselected Actor | Replace selection with that Actor. |
| **Map:** `Shift-click` / `Ctrl/Command-click` | Add / toggle that Actor. |

- **Gesture thresholds:** Map modifier clicks apply on release; moving at least `4` device-independent screen pixels on either axis starts a drag and cancels the click. Modifier drags must begin on an already-selected Actor or the entire gesture is ignored. With multiple Actors selected, a plain click on empty map space clears the selection without placing an instance; otherwise normal placement applies. Switching maps or leaving Actor mode clears selection.
- **Multi-selection in Actor Info:** Displays only properties common to all selected Actors with compatible types and editing rules (including common children of structures, components, lists and dictionaries). Values reflect inherited defaults and overrides, showing **multiple choices** where values differ. Editing one sub-field (such as a vector's X) updates only that sub-field across the group. Dependent properties are editable only when their condition holds for every selected Actor.
- **Multi-selection restrictions:** Tag is read-only; Blueprint displays a shared reference (with Open/Locate) or **multiple choices**; container add/remove and type-switching controls are disabled. Resetting a property or all overrides restores each Actor's own defaults for common editable fields while preserving others. Batch edits apply atomically or fail without partial changes.

### Moving and transforming Actors

| Gesture | Transform effect |
|---|---|
| `Left-drag` selected Actor | Move group by the same grid delta; stops at map edges preserving relative offsets (rejected if the group cannot fit). |
| `Ctrl+left-drag` (`Command+left-drag` on macOS) | Adjust `defaultTranslation` continuously in map pixels without changing grid cells. |
| `Alt/Option+left-drag` | Adjust each Actor's `defaultOrigin` in local coordinates (accounting for rotation and scale; image moves opposite the drag; unavailable if a scale axis is zero). Takes precedence over `Ctrl/Command`. |
| `Ctrl/Command+wheel` or `Command+pinch` (macOS) | Scale `defaultScale` (preserving axis ratios and signs, including zero axes; `×1.1` per wheel unit, continuous on pinch). Zooms the map if no eligible editable selection exists; unmodified pinch always zooms. |
| `Alt/Option+wheel` or `Option+pinch` (macOS) | Adjust `defaultRotation` around each Actor's origin (`+15°` per wheel unit, `+18°` per `0.1` pinch; positive/outward = clockwise, negative/inward = counterclockwise). Takes precedence over `Ctrl/Command`; falls back to viewport behaviour without an eligible selection. |

These transform shortcuts do not apply in Live Debug. A complete group drag, batch edit, reset, delete or paste is one Undo step; consecutive wheel or pinch adjustments to the same property and selection merge into one step until selection, map, layer or mode changes, or the project is saved.

### Copying and deleting Actors

Copy or delete the selection from the World Outliner or map context menu, or press `Ctrl/Command+C` and `Delete`/`Backspace`. Right-clicking a selected Actor preserves the group; right-clicking an unselected Actor selects it alone first.

Paste via the map context menu or `Ctrl/Command+V` at the pointer's grid cell. The primary Actor anchors to that cell while other copied Actors keep their relative offsets. Paste targets the active layer, preserves instance overrides, generates unique tags for the map or world, and selects the pasted group. If any target cell is out of bounds, occupied or self-colliding, the entire paste fails without changing the map.

See [Actor and layer assistance](<../PreviewHost/Map and World Previews.md#actor-and-layer-assistance>) for invisible Actors, layer dimming and light-range overlays.

### Light offset and occlusion

- **Emitter position:** `LightComponent.lightOffset` is measured from the centre of the Actor's local bounds and follows the full Actor transform (rotation and scale). For a wall-mounted torch, place the offset at the flame on the room side of the wall because the renderer does not shift emitters into nearby passable cells.
- **Light blocking (`Surface.LightBlock`):** Material opacity in `[0, 1]` applied per `CellSize` of penetration (`0` = fully transmissive, `1` = fully opaque, intermediate values compound by physical path length — e.g. `0.5` transmits roughly `0.707`, `0.5` and `0.25` through half, one and two cells respectively).
- **Self-occlusion:** An emitting Actor is excluded from dynamic occluders for its own light only — it occludes other lights, while tiles and other Actors at the same position occlude normally. Separate walls and torches into distinct Actors so excluding the torch does not exclude the wall.

### Map tags in a world

Creating or pasting an Actor inside a world child prefixes its default tag with `<child-file-stem>.` and enforces uniqueness across the entire world. Renaming a child or world does not rewrite existing or custom tags. Copying a child rewrites copied tags to `<new-child-stem>.<old-tag-body>` and updates their matching `BPClassVarChanged` keys.

## Map targets

The `startMap` file field and the Blueprint Transfer picker share the same map tree:

- **World selection:** Stores `<WorldFolder>/_world.json` with world-cell coordinates.
- **Placed child selection:** Stores `<WorldFolder>/<ChildFile>.json` with child-local coordinates converted to world coordinates at runtime.
- **Unplaced children:** Visible in the tree but cannot be selected as runtime destinations.

## Live Debug

With **Individual Window** Play and [Live Debug](<Run Debug and Package.md#live-debug>) enabled, the map panel follows the player's current ordinary map or world child; see that section for allowed operations and save boundaries.

documents.content:
# Materials

Author 2D materials in a visual node graph to control sprite colour, alpha, local emission, scene lighting response, light blocking, reflection strength and vertex displacement. Actors, `CharacterView` controls, tiles, autotiles and tile layers reference material assets beneath `Data/Materials`.

Actors default to `Data/Materials/Global/Standard.json`, while `CharacterView` controls, tiles and autotiles with an empty material use the built-in default (source texture with scene lighting, and no emission, reflection, light blocking or displacement). Effect examples and `Surfaces` presets live outside `Global`.

## Create and assign

Create a material via **New Material** in File Explorer or the **File** menu under `Data/Materials`, or double-click an existing `.json` asset to open it. In an Actor Blueprint, the material field also offers creation when set to `Standard`; use the open action beside the field to edit the active material. Materials are shared project resources.

The material editor opens on the **Preview** tab with the parameter list on the left, selected parameter details beneath it, and **Preview** / **Node Graph** tabs on the right (drag dividers to resize). Switching tabs preserves selections, graph zoom and pan, preview settings and playback time. Editing a parameter default updates every instance that does not override that parameter.

- **Assignment paths:** Set `material` to a full `Data/Materials/...json` path. Recognised material and texture references participate in reference checks, renames and deletion guards under the shared [save and Undo rules](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#editing-and-saving>); maintain dynamically constructed script paths manually.
- **Inheritance:** Child Blueprints and map instances inherit their parent's material unless overridden. Selecting **Clear** or explicit `Standard` overrides an inherited material (such as `Rainbow`) back to `Standard`; removing the override restores inheritance. The Actor field, parameter list and previews reflect the effective material.
- **Parameter overrides (`materialParameters`):** On Actors and `CharacterView` controls, check a parameter to override it or uncheck it to use the resource default. Switching an Actor between **Clear** and explicit `Standard` keeps overrides such as `lightBlock`; switching to a different material clears previous overrides in the same edit. A child Blueprint that switches material writes an empty override dictionary to block inherited parameters from the prior material; resetting the full instance restores inheritance.
- **Tiles, autotiles and layers:** Tilesets save assigned materials in a sparse `materials` object keyed by zero-based tile indices (e.g. `{"7": "Data/Materials/Water.json"}`), removing the key when cleared. Autotiles store a single `material` field. Tile layers evaluate the tile or autotile material first and the layer material second; Actors on the layer use their own material.

## Exposed parameters

The left parameter list shows display names and types, with stable IDs and groups in tooltips. Right-click an entry or the background and choose **Add Parameter**, then provide a non-empty unique stable ID and a type (`float`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color`, `bool` or `texture`). Delete entries from the context menu or with `Delete` (creation and deletion support Undo/Redo).

Edit the selected parameter's default value, display name, group and optional numeric range below the list:

- **IDs and types** are read-only after creation; editing the display name preserves the ID referenced by graph nodes and saved overrides.
- **Values and bounds:** Vectors use numeric arrays (numeric ranges apply per component with `min ≤ max`); colours use four channels in `[0, 1]`; textures use canonical `/Game/Assets/...` paths and accept PNG (`.png`) and JPEG (`.jpg`, `.jpeg`).
- **Deleted references:** Deleting a parameter used in the graph produces a diagnostic until affected Parameter nodes are reconnected or removed. Instance panels let you delete overrides whose IDs no longer exist.

## Edit the graph

Open **Node Graph** and right-click the canvas background to open **Add Node**, choose a category and node type, drag headers to move nodes, and drag between ports to connect values. Material-wide settings, including maximum vertex displacement, live in the initially collapsed **Rendering** section below the parameter pane.

![Crystallize material node graph with parameters on the left and connected nodes on the right](../../../images/editor/material-editor-nodegraph.png)

*Click **View Generated Shader** above the canvas to inspect the compiled vertex and fragment GLSL.*

### Editing and navigation

- **Inputs and constants:** Edit unconnected literal inputs directly below their pins and node properties inside the node (connected inputs hide value controls). Declared defaults display without writing an override; implicit and inherited inputs show **Default input** or **Pass-through**. Right-click an unconnected input pin for **Set Constant** or **Reset Input**.
- **Disconnecting links:** Right-click an input pin to disconnect its link, or an output pin to disconnect all outgoing links. A node's context menu also provides **Disconnect All Inputs** and **Disconnect All Outputs** (each batch action is one Undo step; unavailable actions are disabled). Disconnected inputs return to their default or pass-through behaviour without keeping pre-connection constants.
- **Selection, copy and pan:** Right-click a node to delete it (right-clicking a node inside a multi-selection preserves the group; right-clicking another node selects it first). The `Surface` output cannot be deleted. Right-drag pans the canvas without opening a menu on release. Copy/Paste assigns new node IDs while preserving internal links; standard Undo/Redo and focused control input apply.
- **macOS trackpad and zoom:** Two-finger scroll pans horizontally and vertically; pinch or `Command+wheel` zooms around the pointer (`10%–1000%`). Scrolling over a node's value control adjusts that control.
- **Constrained node properties:** Parameter pickers display names while saving stable IDs; numeric nodes offer supported scalar/vector dimensions; Compose offers `2`, `3` or `4` components; Swizzle offers an output-length selector and component drop-downs (`X/R`, `Y/G`, `Z/B`, `W/A`). The compiler validates that selected channels exist in the input and flags invalid saved values until fixed. Numeric fields enforce declared bounds without adding artificial limits to unrestricted values.

### Surface channels and data flow

Material graphs are pure data-flow graphs with one protected `Surface` output and no gameplay events or Blueprint execution.

The native runtime's node registry supplies available nodes (surface inputs, exposed parameters, time, positions, sprite/texture sampling, arithmetic, vector composition, swizzles and degree-based `HueShift`). For example, connect `SurfaceInput.BaseColor` and a `float` Parameter to `HueShift`, then link `Value` to `Surface.BaseColor`.

| Surface input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BaseColor`, `Alpha` | RGB colour and transparency. |
| `Emission` | Local RGB emission independent of scene illumination (use a Light component to illuminate surrounding objects). |
| `LightingWeight` | Blend between unlit colour and scene lighting. |
| `LightBlock` | Light opacity per `CellSize` of penetration; see [light occlusion](<Tilesets Autotiles and Maps.md#lights-and-actors>). |
| `ReflectionStrength` | Contribution to the map reflection surface. |
| `VertexOffset` | Additional local vertex displacement in pixels. |

Unconnected channels pass through the incoming surface; an unconnected `VertexOffset` applies zero displacement, allowing layer materials to modify a single channel without replacing tile channels. Set `rendering.maxVertexOffset` to non-negative `[x, y]` bounds enclosing every possible displacement (including parameter ranges) for culling and preview framing. Texture sampling is fragment-only; invalid stage connections report compiler diagnostics.

## Preview and diagnose

On **Preview**, pick a **Preview Texture** and set integer frame bounds (`X`, `Y ≥ 0`; `Width`, `Height ≥ 1`), then adjust ambient light and the optional point light to inspect lighting and emission. These preview settings are temporary. The preview — along with Actor, map and UI previews — reads unsaved material snapshots directly.

![Crystallize material preview with parameter controls and frame and lighting settings](../../../images/editor/material-editor-preview.png)

*Adjust the preview frame rectangle, ambient light and optional point light in **Preview Settings**.*

Compilation diagnostics appear below the right-hand tabs and highlight the offending node when identifiable; click an error to jump to **Node Graph** and focus it. **View Generated Shader** displays the generated vertex and fragment GLSL. Graphs compile to GLSL through the native compiler and do not accept raw shader source; normal maps, graph inheritance and subgraphs are not supported.

## Material combinations

Map tile-plus-layer combinations are discovered automatically during game initialisation. Open **Game → Material Combinations** only to register additional combinations used dynamically by scripts (such as assigning layer materials or building maps at runtime). Switching an Actor or UI control between individual materials, or modifying parameters, requires no extra entry.

| List | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Material** | All materials under `Data/Materials`, with **Default Material** first (evaluated before the layer). |
| **Layer** | The same materials without an empty/default entry. |
| **Existing Combinations** | Additional saved combinations only (`Material + Layer`); auto-detected map combinations are omitted. |

Entries display paths relative to `Data/Materials` without `.json` (keeping subdirectories, e.g. `Surfaces/Water`). Select one entry from **Material** and **Layer**, then click **Add** (disabled until both are chosen and while that ordered pair already exists; `A + B` and `B + A` are distinct, and a material may combine with itself). Select a saved entry to enable **Delete**.

Each addition or deletion saves immediately (opening or selecting writes nothing; failed saves show an error and preserve the list). Missing saved references are flagged and stay removable; runtime preparation reports missing references with their source location.

The editor manages `Data/MaterialCombinations.json` automatically (do not edit by hand), creating it on the first addition and deleting it when empty. Each `additionalCombinations` item stores full `Data/Materials/...json` paths in `material` (empty string for default) and `layer`. Templates and game packages include this file; updates take effect on the next material-cache preparation.

## Runtime generation

Save material changes before running the game. During `SceneInit`, the native material compiler generates GLSL shaders and metadata under `<user-data>/Assets/Shaders/MaterialGenerated` (independent of editor **Export**). Desktop previews compile unsaved snapshots in memory with the same compiler without writing the runtime cache.

- **Discovered programs:** Preparation compiles every individual material (plus the built-in default) and the deduplicated, path-sorted union of [additional combinations](#material-combinations) and map usage. Source reads follow [user-directory resource priority](<Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#runtime-resource-lookup>).
- **Map scanning:** Preparation recursively scans all ordinary maps under `Data/Maps` (including world-map children) regardless of startup map or visibility. Each layer with a material is paired with the base materials of tiles and autotiles placed on that layer (unassigned tiles use default; unused tileset entries are skipped). Scripts are not scanned or executed.
- **Cache layout:** `Data/Materials/Surfaces/Water.json` maps to `Assets/Shaders/MaterialGenerated/Materials/Surfaces/Water/`, and the built-in default maps to `Assets/Shaders/MaterialGenerated/Builtin/Default/`.

| Entry | Contents |
|---|---|
| `resource.json` | Parameter declarations, defaults and `maxVertexOffset`. |
| `single/` | Base material without a layer. |
| `layers/<relative path without .json>/` | Base material combined with the specified layer material. |

Every program directory contains `vertex.vert`, `color.frag`, `surface.frag`, `transmission.frag`, `source.frag` and `program.json` metadata (conflicting output mappings are rejected). Logical filenames map to encrypted shader suffixes and `.ldc` metadata when enabled by [packaging encryption settings](<Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>).

- **Cache validation:** Reused only when input content, generator version, encryption settings and generated-file hashes match; changed, missing or damaged files regenerate. Replacements build and verify atomically before publication (no partial output on failure or cancellation), pruning obsolete combinations and plaintext/encrypted forms on success.
- **Cache storage:** Always stored as loose files (even with `.ldpak`), excluded from templates and packages, and safe to delete while the game is stopped (recreated on next launch).
- **Initialisation order:** The default [initialisation scene](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Default Template Overview.md#entry-and-modules>) finishes material preparation before creating shaders or material-dependent UI/graphics; custom initialisation scenes must do the same. See [Material cache preparation](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Maps and Materials.md#material-cache-preparation>). Drawing binds prepared runtime files and parameters directly.

## File format

Material JSON is fixed at version `1`:

```json
{
  "type": "material",
  "version": 1,
  "parameters": [],
  "graph": {
    "nodes": [{"id": "surface", "type": "Surface", "inputs": {}, "properties": {}}],
    "output": "surface"
  },
  "rendering": {"maxVertexOffset": [0, 0]},
  "editor": {"positions": {"surface": [400, 200]}}
}
```

Node inputs hold either literals or links (`{"node": "tint", "port": "Value"}`). Node positions and `editor.view` (zoom and offset; a continuous pan/zoom shares one Undo step) are saved as editor data.

Parameter entries store `id`, `type`, `default` and optional `displayName`, `group`, `min` and `max`; instance dictionaries store only ID-to-value overrides. Materials and referenced textures are included in normal packaging (including encrypted Data and `.ldpak`).

documents.title: Blueprints Common Functions and Actors
documents.path: docs/en_GB/Editor User Guide/Blueprints Common Functions and Actors.md
documents.content:
# Blueprints, Common Functions and Actors

Create reusable Blueprint classes beneath `Data/Blueprints`, define typed attributes and components, place Actor instances on maps and author visual event graphs.

## Create a Blueprint

Choose **Game → New Blueprint** (or create one from File Explorer), pick a parent class deriving from `BPBase`, and choose a path under `Data/Blueprints`. Parent defaults and events resolve through the full inheritance chain. A new graph-mode Blueprint initialises each inherited event with an `Event → Parent` node chain including parameter links.

A Blueprint key is its case-preserving path relative to `Data/Blueprints` using `/` separators without `.json` (for example `Actors/Guard`), corresponding to the class reference `Data.Blueprints.Actors.Guard`. Key inputs accept an optional `.json` suffix and normalise backslashes and surrounding whitespace. In full class references, every dot separates a module segment (`Data.Blueprints.Actors.json` maps to key `Actors/json`).

## Class and instance values

Class attributes supply defaults for every instance, while map Actors may override individual fields. Metadata-declared components appear as structured fields, and fields listed in `InvalidVars` are hidden from ordinary editing.

The Blueprint editor resolves attributes and components across the entire inheritance chain, giving child overrides precedence over ancestor defaults (see [Actor Components](<Actor Components/Overview.md>)). When a Blueprint's `ID` selects a General Data member, its `attributes` display read-only — edit those values in General Data.

In both the Blueprint editor and **Actor Info**, ordinary variables sit inside grey dashed frames beneath the component list, grouped by the class, Script Mixin or Blueprint that first declared them. Hover over a group heading to view its full class reference; inherited fields stay in their declaring group even when overridden.

### Add a typed attribute

Click **Add Attribute**, enter a name, pick a type and set its initial value. For `enum`, choose an `Enums.*` module in **kind** and select a key (lists and dictionaries also support enum items or values); file fields can restrict the picker with a base directory.

- **Storage and inheritance:** New fields save declarations in `attrDefs` and initial values in `attrs`. Naming an inherited field with no local value locks the type to the inherited declaration and adds an `attrs` override only. Child Blueprints inherit both type and default and cannot redeclare inherited fields; removing an override restores the inherited default. Deleting a locally declared field removes both its declaration and value, and is blocked while any descendant or map Actor override depends on it.
- **Validation:** Every saved attribute must be declared in metadata, an active Script Mixin or inherited/local `attrDefs`. Invalid declarations block loading and saving (reporting Blueprint and attribute). Parent changes and field deletions cannot leave descendants or map overrides incompatible; **Save Invalid Blueprint** permits unfinished graphs but never bypasses attribute errors. See [Blueprint attribute declarations](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Metadata Schema and Decorators.md#blueprint-attribute-declarations>).

## Actor placement and Actor Info

Select an Actor Blueprint (deriving from `Engine.Actor`) in any **File Explorer** tab to arm it for placement, then click an empty cell on an editable layer in Actor mode to place an instance (double-click the file to open its editor). Selecting a single placed Actor on the map also arms its Blueprint for placement. Press `Escape` with the map focused to cancel placement. See [Actor previews](<../PreviewHost/UI Actor Particle and Subtitle Previews.md#actor-previews>).

- **Placement persistence:** Switching tabs, navigating history, refreshing, locating resources or selecting non-Actor files does not alter the armed Blueprint. Armed Blueprints follow editor renames, moves and Undo/Redo; deleting the Blueprint or changing its class to a non-Actor cancels placement.
- **Locate Blueprint:** Right-click a map Actor in Actor mode and select **Locate Blueprint** to highlight its file in the most recently active [File Explorer](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#file-explorer-and-reference-tree>) (disabled on empty space or Actors lacking a project Blueprint).
- **Actor Info:** Displays the selected Actor's Blueprint reference (with **Open** and **Locate**), grid position `X`/`Y`, tag and exposed fields. Continuous focused position or text edits merge into one Undo step. Click the reset button beside a field to clear its override, or **Reset All** to clear all class-field overrides and restore Blueprint defaults. On hidden layers, **Actor Info** stays inspectable (including Blueprint navigation) while tag, position, reset actions and class fields are read-only.
- **Undo and deletion:** Placing and deleting map instances uses map Undo. Deleting a Blueprint file follows [resource deletion and recovery](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#file-explorer-and-reference-tree>): if an instance was deleted and saved before its Blueprint was deleted, map Undo cannot restore it while the Blueprint is missing. Editing Blueprint fields (including Undo/Redo) refreshes Actor visuals from current inherited defaults.

## Graph mode

Enabling **Script Mixin** hides the right-hand graph and preview pane so variables use the full width; disabling it restores the pane and prior column widths immediately while preserving graph data across mode inheritance, Undo/Redo and reloads.

Each graph begins at a red **Event** entry node — connect its execution pin to define the start node (unconnected entries appear translucent with a notice; Blueprints fall back to inherited implementations, whereas Common Function and General Data graphs do not run). See [Execution Flow, Events and Variables](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#events>).

### Events, Parent nodes and drag-to-connect

- **Adding local events:** Click **New Event** to create a local graph (listing inherited events without a local graph; existing local graphs — even empty ones — cannot be added twice). When the parent chain defines the event, the new graph starts with a brown **Parent: Event Name** node wired to the entry and its parameters in one Undo step. Viewing an inherited event tab alone does not create an override or modify saved data.
- **Node actions:** Parent nodes are editable and available only in graph-mode class Blueprints (add via the node picker, or move, copy and delete normally). Right-click a node to disconnect all inputs/outputs, copy or delete it; right-click empty canvas to add, paste or organise nodes. New, pasted and duplicated nodes appear at the pointer (or viewport centre if outside), preserving relative layout and internal links.
- **Drag-to-connect picker:** In any editable Blueprint, Common Function or General Data graph, drag an execution or parameter output pin onto empty canvas to open a pin-filtered picker (execution pins list nodes with execution inputs; parameter pins list nodes with at least one [compatible typed input](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#typed-connections>), filtered by the pin rather than Blueprint class; the right-click picker keeps **Context Sensitive**).
- **Auto-connection rules:** Selecting a node from the dragged picker creates and wires it in one Undo step. Exact parameter type matches take priority over compatible matches (breaking ties by declaration order), and new execution links replace prior ones from that output. Cancelling changes nothing; dropping directly on an input pin connects existing nodes.

### Plain text parameter inputs

Right-click an editable node in any Blueprint, Common Function or General Data graph and choose **Convert to Plain Text Inputs** to edit all unconnected parameters as text boxes (connected inputs keep normal pins); choose **Restore Typed Inputs** to switch back.

- **Type conversion:** String and file inputs preserve text; numbers and booleans parse as literals; containers, vectors and composites use JSON syntax (including `$type`/`$value` for unions); object and function pins keep expression semantics (literal parameters do not gain expression evaluation). See [Metadata Schema and Decorators](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Metadata Schema and Decorators.md>).
- **Validation and scope:** Invalid text stays visible as an unsaved draft with an error without overwriting the last valid value and must be fixed before restoring typed inputs or saving (**Save Invalid Blueprint** cannot bypass draft errors; save errors name graph and parameter). Input mode and drafts persist across graph switches within the open window only, clear when closed, are never written to project files or copied, and new/copied nodes default to typed inputs.

### Graph shortcuts

For editor-wide shortcuts and primary modifiers, see [Global shortcuts](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#global-shortcuts>).

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl/Command+N` | Open the node picker at the pointer |
| `Ctrl/Command+A` | Select all editable nodes in the active graph |
| `Ctrl/Command+C` | Copy selected nodes and internal links |
| `Ctrl/Command+V` | Paste at the pointer |
| `Ctrl/Command+D` | Duplicate selection at the pointer |
| `Arrow keys` | Nudge selected editable nodes by one graph unit |
| `Delete` | Delete selected editable nodes |
| `Ctrl+drag` on empty canvas | Box-select enclosed nodes on release |

The virtual entry node is auto-positioned and excluded from select-all, nudging, duplication and deletion (Parent call nodes are editable). Shortcuts yield to focused input fields and mutating actions are disabled in read-only graphs. General Data member graphs expose only the type's events, have no class attributes and disallow latent nodes (see [General Data and Text Config](<General Data and Text Config.md>)).

## Inheritance

A child Blueprint inherits fields, components and behaviour from its parent. Changing a saved parent path can alter inherited fields, events and component compatibility, so verify affected children and map instances carefully. Every Blueprint in an inheritance chain must use either graph mode or Script Mixin mode consistently; see [Script Mixin Authoring Workflow](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Script Mixins/Authoring Workflow.md>).

documents.title: Overview
documents.content:
# Actor Components

Attach optional presentation or child-Actor behaviour to an Actor by configuring components as class defaults in a Blueprint or overriding them on individual map instances.

| Component | Field | Available on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Billboard](<Billboard.md>) | `billboardComp` | `Engine.Actor` and derived classes | Stack of images and text above the Actor |
| [Light](<Light.md>) | `lightComp` | `Engine.Actor` and derived classes | Dynamic light following the Actor's transform |
| [Emitter](<Emitter.md>) | `emitterComp` | `Engine.Actor` and derived classes | Common Particle effect attached to the Actor |
| [ChildActor](<ChildActor.md>) | `childActorComp` | Default Gameplay `Source.MapActors.Enemy` and derived classes | Child Actor (used for the enemy damage readout) |

Available components come from the selected class's metadata and inheritance chain. For example, `childActorComp` is declared on `Enemy`, not native `Engine.Actor`; adding a component never introduces a new field onto an arbitrary class.

## Configuration

1. Open an Actor Blueprint to edit class defaults, or select a placed Actor and open **Actor Info** for instance overrides.
2. In **Components**, click **+** to add an available optional component, or double-click an existing component to edit its fields.
3. Save the edited Blueprint or map document.

Child Blueprints inherit omitted values and override ancestor defaults when explicitly configured; unset optional components without ancestor defaults are omitted from new Blueprint JSON. Map instance overrides take precedence over Blueprint defaults — use a field's reset button in **Actor Info** to inherit again, or **Reset All** to clear every class-field override on that instance.

**Related guides and APIs:** [Blueprints, Common Functions and Actors](<../Blueprints Common Functions and Actors.md>) · [Engine Actor and Component APIs](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Gameplay Types.md#component>) · [Default Gameplay: Actors, Enemies, Items and Equipment](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Actors Enemies Items and Equipment.md>)

documents.title: Billboard
documents.content:
# Billboard Component

Display a vertical stack of images and text — such as a name plate or interaction prompt — above an Actor when the player moves within range.

`Engine.Actor` and its derived classes expose `billboardComp` as an optional `Engine.BillboardComponent`. Manage it using the shared [component workflow](<Overview.md#configuration>).

## Configuration

1. Add or open `billboardComp` under **Components**.
2. Set `showRange` to the maximum player-to-Actor distance in map logical pixels (default `128`).
3. Use **+** and **-** in `items` to add or remove top-to-bottom entries, and click **...** beside an entry summary to edit it.
4. Choose `text` to configure text content, font size (default `12`) and colour, or `image` to select a picture via `path` (corresponding to the runtime API's `image` field). Switching item kinds preserves hidden fields.
5. Save the Blueprint or map.

**API reference:** [BillboardComponent and BillboardItem](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Gameplay Types.md#billboardcomponent>)

documents.title: Light
documents.content:
# Light Component

Attach a dynamic point light to an Actor — such as a carried lantern or wall torch — so its emitter follows the Actor's transform.

`Engine.Actor` and its derived classes expose `lightComp` as an optional `Engine.LightComponent`. Author map lighting through Actor components and edit per-instance overrides in **Actor Info**.

## Configuration

1. Add or open `lightComp` via the [component workflow](<Overview.md#configuration>).
2. Set `lightColour` and a positive `lightRadius` (defaults: white light, radius `16`).
3. Set `lightOffset` from the centre of the Actor's local bounds to the light source (default `[0, 0]`, transformed with Actor rotation and scale). For wall torches, use a separate torch Actor and position `lightOffset` on the room side of the wall.
4. Edit per-instance values in **Actor Info** and save the Blueprint or map. Inspect lighting and range overlays via [Actor and layer assistance](<../../PreviewHost/Map and World Previews.md#actor-and-layer-assistance>).

**Related guides and APIs:** [LightComponent](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Gameplay Types.md#lightcomponent>) · [Map light editing](<../Tilesets Autotiles and Maps.md#lights-and-actors>)

documents.title: Emitter
documents.content:
# Emitter Component

Attach a GPU Common Particle effect — such as flames, auras or sparks — directly to an Actor. Author particle tracks, textures and lifetime curves in [Common Particles](<../Common Particles.md>).

`Engine.Actor` and its derived classes expose `emitterComp` as an optional `Engine.EmitterComponent`. For effects inside UI layouts, use [Engine.EmitterView](<../UI Controls in the Palette.md#engineemitterview>) instead.

## Configuration

1. Create and preview a Common Particle asset under `Data/Particles`.
2. Add or open `emitterComp` via the [component workflow](<Overview.md#configuration>).
3. Choose `resource` from the live `Enums.Particle` string enum (extensionless key such as `Combat/Hit`; empty disables the effect).
4. Set `anchor` to a normalised point within the Actor's local bounds (default `[0.5, 0.5]`) and tune `offset`, `rotation` and `scale` relative to the Actor.
5. Leave `beforeActor` set to `false` to draw immediately after the owner, or enable `true` to draw immediately before it. Ordinary maps and composite worlds preserve their Actor-list and layer order; this option does not add Y sorting.
6. Save the Blueprint or map.

**API reference:** [EmitterComponent](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Time Rendering and Particles.md#emittercomponent>)

documents.title: ChildActor
documents.content:
# ChildActor Component

Spawn a child Actor from a class reference and position it relative to its owning Actor. Default Gameplay uses this component to display the enemy damage readout.

`Source.MapActors.Enemy` declares `childActorComp` (`Source.Components.ChildActorComponent`), making it available to Enemy Blueprints and their descendants; native `Engine.Actor` does not declare this field.

## Configuration

1. Open an Enemy Blueprint or select an Enemy map instance, then open `childActorComp` under **Components** (see [Actor Components](<Overview.md#configuration>)).
2. Set `className` to the full Actor class reference (Enemy defaults to `Source.MapActors.EnemyDamageText`; Blueprint children use paths such as `Data.Blueprints.Actors.Guard`). Leaving `className` empty spawns no child.
3. Set `relativePosition` to the child's local offset from the owner (default `[0, 0]`).
4. Save the Blueprint or map.

**API references:** [ChildActorComponent](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Source Classes/ChildActorComponent.md>) · [Enemy](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Source Classes/Enemy.md>) · [EnemyDamageText](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Source Classes/EnemyDamageText.md>)

documents.title: General Data and Text Config
documents.path: docs/en_GB/Editor User Guide/General Data and Text Config.md
documents.content:
# General Data and Text Config

Author structured project databases under `Data/General`, declare shared runtime Game Variables and configure reusable rich-text styles in Text Config.

General Data suits enemies, items, equipment, player presets, states and other records shared across maps and Blueprints. Each JSON file defines one type schema and its named members; its Form, Table and member ability-graph windows share a single document and Undo/Redo history.

## Type structure

| Key | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `params` | Ordered field definitions with `type`, `defaultValue`, optional `comment`, and recursive schemas for enums and containers. |
| `members` | Named records storing values for every schema field. |
| `events` | Optional ordered event names; each member can define an independent graph per event. |

### Supported types and enums

Supported types include strings, booleans, integers, floats, files, lists, dictionaries, `sf.Vector2f/i/u`, `sf.Vector3f/i/u`, `sf.Color`, `sf.IntRect` and `any` (preserves heterogeneous JSON literal types without evaluating strings). Enum, tuple and union composition follows [Metadata Schema and Decorators](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Metadata Schema and Decorators.md>); choose a union branch before entering its value.

New and edited fields write complete recursive `type` objects — such as `{ "list": "int" }` or `{ "dict": "int", "key": { "enum": "Enums.GeneralData.Item", "valueType": "string" } }` — while legacy `"type": "list"` + `itemType` and `"type": "dict"` + `valueType` remain readable.

- **Adding or editing enum fields:** In **Add Field** / **Edit Field**, choose `enum`, pick its module in **kind**, choose an inferred or explicit scalar value type (managed project enums use `string`; empty source enums require an explicit scalar type) and set a default. Dictionaries select key and value types independently. Selectors write directly to `type` without saving separate `kind` or `reference` fields.
- **Built-in managed enums:** Reference Item keys with `{ "enum": "Enums.GeneralData.Item", "valueType": "string" }`, type keys with `Enums.GeneralDataKey`, animations with `Enums.Animation` and particles with `Enums.Particle` (including inside lists, dictionary keys/values, tuples and unions). Selectors reflect unsaved additions, renames and deletions.
- **Enum rules:** String enum pickers include **— None —** (`""`), retain unknown non-empty values (validation checks scalar type rather than option membership), preserve literal whitespace and quotes in IDs, and allow empty managed collections. Enum-keyed dictionary rows stay pending until a non-empty unique key is selected so no placeholder key is saved. Enum declarations count as dependencies even when unused by any member.
- **Rejected legacy and invalid schemas:** Loading fails on missing subtypes, missing or unknown non-underscore member fields, type mismatches, `linkedType`, the old `GeneralDataVars` decorator and the old `reference` protocol.
- **Field comments:** Enter optional plain English tooltips in **Comment** (omitted when empty; shown on hover over Form labels and Table headers; not locale keys or member data).

### Renaming types and member IDs

- **Type renames:** Update recognised module paths across editable JSON (including self-references and modules reassigned due to identifier collisions). Lua metadata dependencies appear in the reference tree but must be updated manually. Remove and save all dependencies before deleting a referenced type.
- **Member ID renames (`Change ID`):** Update typed member references across defaults, Blueprint and map fields, graph parameters and containers (including dictionary keys). Inherited values update at their declaring definition without creating child or map overrides. Animation and particle renames similarly update typed scalar references. Dictionary key collisions reject the entire rename. Undo/Redo follows [Editing and saving](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#editing-and-saving>); update arbitrary strings and Lua/C++ source manually.

## Authoring workflow

1. Open **Database → General Data** (`F10`).
2. Select a type, or right-click the type-tab strip to create one.
3. Define fields before creating many members (right-click a Form field name to edit its definition).
4. Add members and enter values. Right-click a member in the list or Table to change its ID, duplicate it, delete it or open its ability graph.
5. Manage events from the type tab's context menu, then open member graphs via **Edit Ability Graph**. Renaming or deleting an event updates all member graphs.
6. Inspect references before renaming or deleting types or members, then save.

- **Generated Lua modules:** Saving generates `Enums.GeneralDataKey`, each `Enums.GeneralData.<TypeName>` (e.g. `require("Enums.GeneralData.Item")` exposes `Item.EnemyBook`), `Enums.Animation`, `Enums.Particle` and `Source.Configs.GeneralDataTypes` (with its LuaLS declaration). Do not edit these generated files by hand; type renames and deletions update generated modules while preserving handwritten files. Use `GeneralDataTypes.Create(typeName, memberID, memberData)` to restore a typed member record.
- **Schema edits:** Renaming a field preserves member values; changing only the default leaves existing members unchanged. Changing a field's type or a container's item/key/value type asks for confirmation and resets every existing member's field to the new default. Removing a field does not automatically update scripts that read it.
- **Member graphs:** Support only declared type events and synchronous nodes, with no inheritance, Parent or `self` node; use global nodes and `GameplayEventData`. Runtime code activates member graphs explicitly (see [General Data event execution](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#events>)).

## Search and views

Search filters case-insensitively across member IDs and direct scalar fields (strings, numbers, booleans), excluding containers and graphs. Each type remembers its search query, selection and Form/Table mode while the window stays open.

- **Form view:** Edits one member completely.
- **Table view:** Lists IDs and fields in declaration order with horizontal scrolling and inline editing for booleans, numbers and strings; click **Edit** on structured cells to jump to Form view. Editing follows the shared [Undo rules](<Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#editing-and-saving>).

![General Data editor](../../../images/editor/general-data.png)

## Game Variable Manager

Open **Database → Game Variables** (`F9`) to declare mutable runtime variables shared across Blueprints and the active game instance. Filter names case-insensitively with the search box, click **New Variable** to add a declaration, select an entry to edit its type, initial value and editor-only remark, or click **Delete Variable** to remove it after confirmation. Keep variable names stable once referenced by graphs, maps or scripts.

![Game Variable Manager with a selected integer variable](../../../images/editor/game-variables.png)

| Manager type | Written metadata type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `bool`, `int`, `float`, `string` | `bool`, `int`, `float`, `string` | Scalar defaults |
| `list` | `any[]` | Ordinary Lua table (not Standard native `list`) |
| `dict` | `Dict[string, any]` | Ordinary Lua table (not Standard native `dict`) |

Changing an existing variable's type clears its initial value and resets it to the new type's empty default. Saving generates `Scripts/Source/Configs/GameVariables.lua` (initial values) and `GameVariables_meta.lua` (declarations) together; edit declarations through the manager only (opening the window alone writes nothing).

Blueprint fields and node pins marked with `InstVar` display a searchable variable selector (type-filtered selectors, such as conditional doors in the Game project, show compatible variables only), and paired `InstVarValue` fields automatically adapt their editor to the selected variable's type.

> **Important:** Schema and Game Variable edits cannot automatically repair scripts, graphs, save files or hardcoded string references. General Data and generated variable declarations are project definition data, not stores for mutable play-session state.

## Text Config

Style ordinary UI text directly on its UI node; use **Game → New Text Config** for reusable shared styles or named rich-text tags.

![Text Config editor](../../../images/editor/text-config.png)

Localised display keys such as `{ITEM_NAME}` resolve at presentation time rather than load time; see [Game Localisation Workflow](<../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>). For the Game project's built-in database schemas, see [General Data Reference](<General Data Reference/Overview.md>).

documents.title: Animations and Curves
documents.content:
# Animations and Curves

Author frame-based 2D animations under `Data/Animations` and scalar interpolation curves under `Data/Curves` for combat effects, UI transitions and particle tracks.

## Animations

Open **Database → Animation Overview** (`F5`) to browse project animations, or choose **Game → New Animation** to create a JSON asset under `Data/Animations`. The editor exposes frame timing, visual tracks, audio segments and event time tags.

Store source images under `Assets/Animations` (or another asset subdirectory); non-empty image and sound fields save canonical `/Game/Assets/...` paths.

![Animation editor showing frame timing and preview controls](../../../images/editor/animation.png)

### Exporting MP4 locally

Save the animation before exporting. From the repository root, run `tools\animation_to_mp4.bat` (Windows) or `sh tools/animation_to_mp4.sh` (macOS) to export all `Game/Data/Animations` JSON files to `Game/EditorCache/AnimationMp4`. This requires a rebuilt Toolchain with Pillow and a standalone FFmpeg binary supporting `libx264` and AAC; see [tool setup and options](https://github.com/JasonLeon01/Ludork/blob/main/tools/README.md#animation-mp4-export).

```bat
tools\animation_to_mp4.bat Game --input Game/Data/Animations/attack.json --output Game/EditorCache/attack.mp4
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--input`, `--output` | Target a single JSON file or a directory (directories scan recursively and preserve subdirectory structure). |
| `--size 512x512` | Fix an even-sized canvas and crop overflowing content without rescaling (by default the canvas auto-fits all sampled frames around the animation origin). |
| `--background "#202020"` | Set an opaque background colour (defaults to black). |
| `--mute` | Omit audio without shortening the timeline. |
| `--overwrite` | Replace existing output files only after export succeeds. |

Exports preserve frame rate, track order, position/rotation/scale interpolation, horizontal flips and sound timing/trimming. Each clip plays one pass up to the last image or sound segment (rounded up to whole frames; only the background shows after visual tracks end). Time tags are not encoded as video events, and inputs must be saved source JSON with loose assets rather than compressed caches or `.ldpak` archives.

## Curves

Choose **Game → New Curve** to create a curve under `Data/Curves`. Each curve defines a name, default value, pre-/post-infinity behaviour and ordered keys (time, value, interpolation and arrive/leave tangents).

Add, drag and delete keys in the curve editor while keeping key times ordered; avoid duplicate timestamps unless the chosen interpolation explicitly supports discontinuities.

![Curve editor showing ordered keys and interpolation](../../../images/editor/curve.png)

## Referencing data

Metadata-driven selectors reference animation and curve keys from Blueprints and General Data. Because renaming a JSON file changes its path-derived logical key, inspect the reference tree before renaming.
