documents.content:
# Class

Defines player class presets, including their display metadata, available equipment slot names and initially equipped items.

**Source:** `Data/General/Class.json` · **Member events:** None

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `""` | Display name of this class. |
| `desc` | `string` | `""` | Display description of this class. |
| `slot` | `Dict[string, string]` | `{}` | Equipment slot names mapped to the equipment ID initially equipped in each slot (an empty string leaves the slot unequipped). |

documents.title: Enemy
documents.content:
# Enemy

Defines enemy combat statistics, defeat rewards, item drops, special ability parameters and attack animation.

**Source:** `Data/General/Enemy.json` · **Member events:** None (Gameplay Abilities handle defeat behaviour)

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `"NEW ENEMY"` | Display name of this enemy. |
| `desc` | `string` | `"NEW ENEMY DESC"` | Display description of this enemy. |
| `MAXHP` | `int` | `0` | Maximum HP. |
| `ATK` | `int` | `0` | Attack value. |
| `DEF` | `int` | `0` | Defence value. |
| `EXP` | `int` | `0` | Experience granted on defeat. |
| `GOLD` | `int` | `0` | Gold granted on defeat. |
| `drops` | `Dict[string, sf.Vector2i]` | `{}` | Item Blueprint class paths mapped to map-cell offsets from the defeated enemy. |
| `special` | `{ dict = "any", key = { enum = "Enums.GeneralData.Special", valueType = "string" } }` | `{}` | `Special` member IDs mapped to their typed parameters. |
| `ANIMATION_KEY` | `{ enum = "Enums.Animation", valueType = "string" }` | `""` | Attack animation key. |

## Editing notes

- **Special trait parameters (`special`):**
  - **Presence-only traits** (`Compete`, `Hard`, `Magic`, `First`, `Flank`, `Blockade`): store `""` — the key's presence enables the trait.
  - **`Vampire`:** Finite non-negative number.
  - **`Reborn`:** Non-empty Blueprint class path.
  - **`FixDmg`:** Either a finite non-negative number or a non-empty expression string. Only the string form substitutes `{m<attribute>}` (player) and `{e<attribute>}` (enemy) placeholders before `Engine.Eval`; no other special value is evaluated.
- **Enemy drops (`drops`):** Every key must be a Blueprint class path whose Actor derives from `Source.MapActors.Item`. Its `sf.Vector2i` offset adds to the defeated enemy's map coordinates. The spawned Actor's tag derives from the Blueprint path and absolute target cell; if an identical tag already exists, that drop is skipped with a warning rather than spawning a suffixed duplicate.

documents.title: Equip
documents.content:
# Equip

Defines equippable items, the `Class` slot each item occupies, its passive attribute bonuses and optional equip/unequip ability graphs.

**Source:** `Data/General/Equip.json` · **Member events:** `onEquip`, `onUnequip`

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `""` | Display name of this equipment. |
| `desc` | `string` | `""` | Display description of this equipment. |
| `icon` | `file` | `""` | Canonical logical icon path (picker root: `/Game/Assets/Icons`). |
| `slot` | `string` | `""` | `Class` slot key occupied by this equipment. |
| `attrPlus` | `Dict[string, int]` | `{}` | Attribute names mapped to integer modifiers applied while equipped. |

documents.title: Item
documents.content:
# Item

Defines inventory items, their usability, shop pricing, icon presentation and drop/use ability graphs.

**Source:** `Data/General/Item.json` · **Member events:** `onDrop`, `onUse`

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `""` | Display name of this item. |
| `desc` | `string` | `""` | Display description of this item. |
| `usable` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the item can be activated from the inventory to trigger `onUse`. |
| `price` | `int` | `0` | Shop buy price. Selling grants `floor(price / 2)` gold; items whose sell price is `0` are not listed for sale. |
| `icon` | `file` | `""` | Canonical logical icon path (picker root: `/Game/Assets/Icons`). |
| `cost` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the inventory displays this item's stack count. |

## Editing notes

- **`onUse`:** Activated by the inventory with the Player as `GameplayEventData.target`. Place state-removal nodes here because they act on the Player.
- **`onDrop`:** Activated once by enemy drops with the spawned Item Actor as `GameplayEventData.target`. The `Item` schema declares no `onGet` event.

documents.title: Player
documents.content:
# Player

Defines playable character presets, referencing a `Class` member and setting starting combat attributes, progression stats and attack animation.

**Source:** `Data/General/Player.json` · **Member events:** None

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `""` | Display name of this player preset. |
| `desc` | `string` | `""` | Display description of this player preset. |
| `CLASS` | `{ enum = "Enums.GeneralData.Class", valueType = "string" }` | `""` | `Class` member ID defining equipment slots and initial equipment. |
| `MAXHP` | `int` | `1000` | Starting maximum HP. |
| `HP` | `int` | `1000` | Starting current HP. |
| `ATK` | `int` | `10` | Starting attack value. |
| `DEF` | `int` | `10` | Starting defence value. |
| `EXP` | `int` | `0` | Starting experience. |
| `GOLD` | `int` | `0` | Starting gold. |
| `LEVEL` | `int` | `1` | Starting level. |
| `ANIMATION_KEY` | `{ enum = "Enums.Animation", valueType = "string" }` | `""` | Attack animation key. |

## Editing notes

In the Game project, the `Bravor` member sets `MAXHP = 2000` and `HP = 1000`. At runtime, the selected member is copied into `PlayerAttributeSet`; the `BP_Actor_Braver.json` Blueprint stores only the member `ID`.

documents.title: Special
documents.content:
# Special

Defines presentation metadata (display name, description template and icon) for enemy special traits whose runtime parameters are configured in `Enemy.special`.

**Source:** `Data/General/Special.json` · **Member events:** None

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `""` | Display name of this special trait. |
| `desc` | `string` | `""` | Display description (may include one `{value}` placeholder). |
| `icon` | `file` | `""` | Canonical logical icon path (picker root: `/Game/Assets/Icons`). |

## Editing notes

`Special` records supply UI presentation only; trait parameters live in `Enemy.special` (presence-only traits store `""`). When displaying `FixDmg`, the Enemy Book localises expression tokens before substituting `{value}` into `desc`.

documents.title: State
documents.content:
# State

Defines persistent status effects, their stackability and their step- or hook-triggered ability graphs.

**Source:** `Data/General/State.json` · **Member events:** `onWalk`, `onHookTriggered`

## Schema

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | `""` | Display name of this state. |
| `desc` | `string` | `""` | Display description of this state. |
| `icon` | `file` | `""` | Canonical logical icon path (picker root: `/Game/Assets/Icons`). |
| `stackable` | `bool` | `false` | Whether reapplying this state increments the existing stack count. |

## Editing notes

Applying a State creates an Infinite Gameplay Effect and grants its event abilities:

- **`onWalk`:** Listens for `Event.Movement.Step`.
- **`onHookTriggered`:** Triggered explicitly by `Event.State.Trigger.<stateID>` or via `GlobalFunctions.Gameplay.SendEvent` in a gameplay graph. Applying or stacking the State does not emit `onHookTriggered`.

documents.title: Lua Runtime and Modules
documents.path: docs/en_GB/Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md
documents.content:
# Lua Runtime and Modules

Ludork runs Lua 5.5 with Standard extensions, LuaSF and project-native modules. This page covers project scripting architecture, module boundaries, hot reload, error handling and workspace declarations.

New to Lua? Start with [Lua Basics](<../Getting Started/Lua Basics.md>), then read [Ludork Lua Advanced](<../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md>) for Ludork language additions (`class`, `bool`, `list`, `dict`, copying, filesystem helpers and `asyncio`).

| Model | Best suited to | Primary source |
|---|---|---|
| Blueprint graph | Visual event and execution flow | `Data/Blueprints/*.json` |
| Lua class | Reusable systems and gameplay types | `Scripts/**/*.lua` |
| Script Mixin | Lua behaviour attached directly to a Blueprint class | `Scripts/Mixins/**/*.lua` plus same-name `_meta.lua` |
| Declarative UI | JSON assets and generated typed View trees | `Data/UI/**/*.json`, generated `Scripts/Internal/UI/**/*.lua` and matching stubs |
| UI behaviour | Handwritten foundations and business Controllers | `Scripts/Internal/UIBase`; private Controllers inside window modules; independent row and Scene `Controller.lua` modules |

> **Important:** A Blueprint inheritance chain uses either graph mode or Script Mixin mode; do not switch modes within one chain.

## Entry and module order

Native startup runs the script passed as the first command-line argument, or `Scripts/Entry.lua` when no argument is supplied. Startup does not read a project-local configuration or `script` setting to choose the entry file.

Load the root native modules in the order below, finish direct `require` calls, then declare local aliases:

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")
Engine.setAppName("MyGame")

local GlobalCore = require("GlobalCore")
local GlobalFunctions = require("GlobalFunctions")
local Logging = require("Global.Utils.Logging")

local Input = Engine.Input
local System = GlobalCore.System
local ManagerFunctions = GlobalFunctions.Manager
```

### Module boundaries and loading rules

- **Native vs. Lua `GlobalFunctions`**: The native `GlobalFunctions` module exposes `Components`, `UI`, `NodeGraph` and `Manager`. Lua Blueprint function libraries under `Scripts/GlobalFunctions` are separate modules loaded by full path (such as `require("GlobalFunctions.Math")`) and are not members of the native root table.
- **Blueprint function library restrictions**: Modules under `Scripts/GlobalFunctions` must not call `require` at module scope (including for native modules); resolve dependencies inside functions on first use so libraries load without cycles. Their paths and exported names must not collide with C++ `GlobalFunctions` bindings. Run `ludork-check global-functions <repository-root>` to validate these rules statically; it also flags malformed strings, long comments and numeric literals with file, line and column.
- **No aggregators or ad-hoc lazy imports**: Load project modules by their full dotted path and do not add directory-level `init.lua` aggregators. Outside Blueprint function libraries, use direct top-level `require` calls; defer a `require` only to break a genuine dependency cycle or at an explicit first-use boundary (such as an optional window's factory) whose lifecycle is owned by the enclosing scene or feature.
- **Layer dependency direction**: Static dependencies flow from root native modules through `Scripts/Global` to `Scripts/Source`. `Global` implementations and declarations must not require `Source` or reference its types (including via project-aware `GlobalFunctions` libraries); the native root `GlobalFunctions` is a lower-layer API, while `Scripts/Internal` and `Scripts/GlobalFunctions` may depend on `Source`.
- **Injecting project behaviour into Global**: Generic infrastructure may resolve opaque module names supplied by data, but must not hard-code higher-layer business modules. Inject project callbacks and class objects at startup via [`Global.Data.InitializeRuntime(options)`](<Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#data-services>).
- **Shared constants**: Native resource suffixes are exposed through `Engine.ResourceFileConstants`; map identities and Gameplay tags live in `Source.Configs.MapConstants` and `Source.Configs.GameplayConstants`. Public enums live in `Enums.*`.
- **Classes and encapsulation**: Keep each reusable class in its own module that returns the class. A window module may define a private Controller and export the UI through `Ui.DefineWindow` (see [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>)); utility modules may group related helpers. Access private members only through `self` or same-instance `super(..., self)` dispatch — use public getters, commands or data for all other objects, including chained and dynamic access.

### Script and Data storage boundaries

- **Script root layout**: The game root uses one script storage form: loose `Scripts/` during development or a root `Scripts.ldpak` in a packed release. Mixed, missing or invalid layouts fail startup. Once `Entry` calls `Engine.setAppName`, loose files in the user data directory override either layout per [runtime resource lookup](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#runtime-resource-lookup>).
- **Module resolution and Lua loaders**: Every Lua state exposes project modules through `package.preload` and a dynamic searcher without shadowing native modules. New user-directory modules load on first `require`; modules already cached in `package.loaded` do not re-execute merely because their file changed. Script Mixins load fresh on every execution, and audio states use the same effective script sources. `loadfile` and `dofile` accept `/Game/Scripts/...` with standard return, error and environment semantics alongside ordinary physical paths. General filesystem APIs do not expose script archive contents.
- **Data lookup**: Loose and packed `Data` resolve through logical `Data/...` and `/Game/Data/...` paths. `Engine.loadData` and `Engine.dataExists` fall back from a missing `.json` path to a binary `.ldc` alternative within each source, giving user data priority over root data. JSON platform APIs read only the exact path. This is a read-only runtime boundary, not a general archive filesystem.

## Enum modules

Each public enum lives in its own module under `Scripts/Enums`, keeping its constants, EmmyLua annotations and API documentation together in the source file without a mirrored stub. A handwritten enum declares a local table of string keys and scalar literals and returns it, with no dependencies, functions or class construction:

```lua
-- Scripts/Enums/StairDirection.lua
---@enum Enums.StairDirection
local StairDirection = {
    None = "None",
    Up = "Up",
    Down = "Down",
}

return StairDirection
```

Load an enum with `local StairDirection = require("Enums.StairDirection")` and read `StairDirection.Up`. Blueprint metadata references it via `type = { enum = "Enums.StairDirection" }`; see [Enum schemas](<Blueprint Scripting/Metadata Schema and Decorators.md#enum-schemas>).

| Game enum module | Values or purpose |
|---|---|
| `Enums.StairDirection` | `None`, `Up`, `Down` (stored as the same strings) |
| `Enums.BattleResultCode` | `WIN = 1`, `CANNOT_DAMAGE = 2`, `LETHAL_COUNTER_DAMAGE = 3` |
| `Enums.CriticalResultCode` | `VALUE = 1`, `NOT_NEEDED = 2`, `UNKNOWN = 3` |
| `Enums.DamageHintLevel` | `NONE = 0`, `BATTLE = 1`, `MAP = 2` |
| `Enums.WindowTransitionProfile` | `DEFAULT = "Default"`, `MENU = "Menu"` |
| `Enums.ShopMode` | `BUY = "buy"`, `SELL = "sell"` |
| `Enums.EventKey` | `LocaleChanged`, `AbilitySystemChanged`, `PlayerChanged` event names |
| `Enums.AbilitySystemChangeKind` | `Attribute`, `State` payload kinds |
| `Enums.PlayerChangeKind` | `Inventory`, `Name`, `Map` payload kinds |
| `Enums.MovementLatentOutput` | `STARTED = 0`, `FINISHED = 1` execution output indices |
| `Enums.CombatResolutionCode` | Intermediate [combat resolution results](<Source Classes/Gameplay.md#motabattleability>) |
| `Enums.MovementResultCode` | [Movement-hazard query and commit results](<Source Classes/Gameplay.md#movementspecials-and-movement-danger>) |
| `Enums.PlayerNameValidationError` | [Player name validation errors](<Source Classes/Player.md#lua-runtime-api>) |
| `Enums.SaveLoadMode`, `Enums.SaveLoadCloseReason` | [Save/load window mode and close reason](<Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>) |
| `Enums.WorldActorState` | World Actor lifecycle labels: `NEVER_ACTIVE = "NeverActive"`, `ACTIVE = "Active"`, `DORMANT = "Dormant"` |
| `Enums.WorldPublishPhase` | Region publication labels: `CONVERT = "convert"`, `BUILD = "build"`, `INDEX = "index"`, `FINALISE = "finalise"` |

Native builds generate `Enums.Engine.*`, `Enums.GlobalCore.*`, `Enums.GlobalFunctions.*` and `Enums.sf.*`. Saving project data generates `Enums.GeneralDataKey`, one `Enums.GeneralData.<TypeName>` module per data type, `Enums.Animation` and `Enums.Particle`. The editor resolves these project-managed string enums directly from the current catalogue (including unsaved edits), while runtime `require` loads the generated modules. Treat the owning native declarations or database records as the source of truth: edit those sources and regenerate rather than editing generated enum files directly.

## Native modules and values

Standard globals such as `os.createDirectories`, `os.removeFile`, `zlib` and `base64` are host-installed and require no `require`. The host also sets the `SAVE_AS_LDC` default from `LUDORK_SAVE_AS_LDC`; see [Saves](<Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>) for project overrides. `LudorkRuntime` is a native library rather than a Lua module — Core bindings load only through `Engine`, `GlobalCore` and `GlobalFunctions`, with no `Runtime` or `CoreSystem` alias.

LuaSF registers the global `sf`. Pass exact native values such as `sf.Vector2i.new(...)`, `sf.Vector2f.new(...)` and `sf.Color.new(...)` whenever an API expects them; native containers and plain Lua tables do not implicitly convert to SFML vectors.

## Asynchronous operation updates

The default `Scripts/Entry.lua` calls `GlobalFunctions.NodeGraph.initLatent()` to drive asynchronous operation updates. Custom entry scripts must also call it, even for script-only gameplay. See [Cooperative tasks and file batches](<../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md#cooperative-tasks-and-file-batches>) and [Execution Flow, Events and Variables](<Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md>).

## Session lifetime

The main thread and all coroutines within one Lua VM share a single native session. Captured callbacks and opaque handles survive coroutine yields, cannot cross VMs, and become invalid when the session shuts down. See [Session and module lifetime](<../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md#session-and-module-lifetime>) for native host integration.

## Live Debug

Live Debug edits Actor state inside an editor-launched game, including Actors spawned at runtime. Edits are transient and are neither saved to project data nor reapplied when instances rebuild. See [Live Debug](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#live-debug>) for the editor controls.

## Lua hot reload

In an editor-launched Debug or Release game running from loose `Scripts/` sources, save your edits and enter `$r` in the Console. On the next Console update (between gameplay callbacks), the runtime updates loaded project modules and used Script Mixins while keeping the active scene, live objects and Lua VM intact. Packed or compiled-only scripts do not support hot reload.

### What updates and what requires a restart

- **Updated in place**: Existing named functions are replaced while preserving module and class identities, instance fields, module data, constants, defaults and captured non-function values. Cached references to matched functions (including native callbacks) redirect to the new functions, and ordinary global accesses may be added or removed.
- **Unchanged until recreated**: Existing anonymous callbacks and suspended coroutine frames keep their original bodies (though calls to matched helpers update). Constructors and lifecycle callbacks do not rerun. Existing [audio processors](<Default Gameplay/Resources Audio Video and Effects.md#audio>) keep their code until a new playback starts.
- **Requires a restart**: Changing class defaults, deleting a loaded module or used Script Mixin, changing export names, class bases, field-vs-function kinds, native callback members, incompatible captured state, or using an unmatchable custom `_ENV`.
- **Scope and exclusions**: The runtime compiles all effective Lua sources (including user-directory overrides) before applying changes. `Entry` is checked but not rerun, and new or unloaded modules load on demand via `require`. Metadata, declarations, JSON data, UI assets and native code are excluded.

> **Warning:** Syntax, compatibility or candidate-execution failures leave existing definitions intact and log an error in the Console, but external side effects from candidate execution cannot be rolled back. Restart the game after any error that may have modified native resources or shared objects. Keep module top levels restricted to definitions and dependencies, and place resource creation and subscriptions in explicit startup or lifecycle functions (see [Entry and modules](<Default Gameplay/Default Template Overview.md#entry-and-modules>)).

## Logging and errors

Log runtime diagnostics through `Global.Utils.Logging`: `debug` for diagnostic detail, `info` for major stages, `warning` for recoverable data issues and `error` for unrecoverable failures. Logging never raises an exception; call `error` or `assert` when execution must stop.

- **Scheduled callback isolation**: When a scheduled Scene input/frame callback, Actor frame callback or UI input/frame/animation-completion callback raises a Lua error, the engine aborts that invocation and prints the callback name and Lua stack trace to the Console. Synchronous calls inside the failing callback unwind with it, while state changes made before the error stay applied. Other scheduled callbacks continue, and repeating callbacks can run on their next turn. A failing mouse-button-down callback leaves the input unconsumed.
- **Fatal startup errors and async tasks**: An error escaping the entry script or required initialisation aborts launch. See [Cooperative tasks and file batches](<../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md#cooperative-tasks-and-file-batches>) and [Scene timers](<Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Scenes and System.md#scene-timers>) for their error rules.
- **Runtime providers**: Engine providers register explicitly during [startup](<Default Gameplay/Default Template Overview.md#entry-and-modules>), never as a side effect of `require`. Missing or duplicate providers, stopped sessions and invalid return counts or types raise errors; returning zero values differs from returning one `nil`.

## Runtime, declarations and metadata

Lua files are divided by ownership:

- **`.lua` runtime modules**: Contain runtime behaviour and implementation-only annotations. Short pure constant tables and simple configuration tables keep their public annotations and documentation directly in the source file (like pure-data enums), without mirrored stubs. This exception does not apply to short modules with business methods or lifecycle behaviour.
- **`Scripts/stub/**/*.d.lua` declarations**: Contain all other public documentation and LuaLS declarations, with no runtime side effects or `require` calls. Type-only declarations with no runtime implementation live here even when short. Native API enum types live in their owning declarations, such as `Engine.d.lua` and `LuaSF.d.lua`.
- **`*_meta.lua` metadata**: Contain pure editor metadata and never execute as gameplay scripts.

A requireable declaration mirrors its runtime module's path and begins with `---@meta <module.path>` (for example, `Global/Pool.d.lua` declares `---@meta Global.Pool`). Global-only declarations (`Standard.d.lua`, `Class.d.lua`, `LuaSF.d.lua`) and declaration-only `Scripts/stub/Source/Configs/EventChangePayload.d.lua` use a bare `---@meta`. Source-owned declarations omit `---@meta`. The language server reads declarations directly from the workspace without runtime `require`.

The EmmyLua workspace configures `Scripts/stub` as its workspace root and library. In `.emmyrc.json`, `workspace.moduleMap` maps `Scripts/Enums` modules to `Enums.*` and maps the exact source-owned modules (`Global.WorldMapConstants`, `Source.Configs.HotKey`, `Source.Configs.Tutorial`, `Source.Configs.MapConstants` and `Source.Configs.GameplayConstants`) directly to their runtime import paths, while all other public imports resolve to their stub declarations:

```json
"moduleMap": [
    {
        "pattern": "^Scripts[.]Enums[.](.*)$",
        "replace": "Enums.$1"
    },
    {
        "pattern": "^Scripts[.](Global[.]WorldMapConstants|Source[.]Configs[.](HotKey|Tutorial|MapConstants|GameplayConstants))$",
        "replace": "$1"
    }
]
```

See [Project Templates](<../Getting Started/Project Templates.md>) for which declarations templates and game packages ship.

Standalone and C++ Source templates include the Windows VS Code launch configuration `Ludork: EmmyLua Attach (Windows)` for attaching `tangzx.emmylua`'s `emmylua_attach` debugger to a running `Main.exe` (Windows only). C++ Source templates also include native `cppvsdbg` and `lldb` launch and attach configurations.

# Script Mixins Overview

A Script Mixin attaches Lua behaviour directly to a Blueprint class, keeping the Blueprint's authored defaults and inheritance hierarchy while implementing event logic in Lua.

| [Authoring Workflow](<Authoring Workflow.md>) | Creating the script and metadata pair, attaching it to a Blueprint and configuring inheritance. |
| [Runtime Contract](<Runtime Contract.md>) | Table and member rules, defaults, parent calls and hot reload. |
| [Game Examples](<Game Mixins.md>) | Consumable and door mixins provided in Default Gameplay. |
| [Metadata](<Metadata.md>) | Declaring editable Blueprint fields for a Script Mixin. |

documents.content:
# Script Mixin Authoring Workflow

Use a Script Mixin to implement a Blueprint class's event behaviour in a Lua table instead of a visual graph.

Graph mode and Script Mixin mode are mutually exclusive within one Blueprint inheritance chain. The first Script Mixin Blueprint in the chain provides the script; descendants may inherit it or supply another compatible mixin, but cannot switch back to graph mode.

A Script Mixin Blueprint may omit `graph` because its events execute from Lua. If a `graph` field is present, it must be a structurally valid graph object even though the runtime does not execute it. Graph-mode Blueprints must always store a `graph` object.

## Create and attach a Script Mixin

1. Create or open a Blueprint whose parent provides the lifecycle events and native members the mixin needs.
2. Enable **Script Mixin** on the first Blueprint in the chain.
3. With **Script Path** empty and editable, click **+** beside **...**, choose a directory under `Scripts/Mixins`, and enter a file name (such as `Doors/KeyDoor.lua`). The editor appends `.lua` if omitted.
4. Save to generate the script and its same-named `_meta.lua` companion. The editor selects the new script automatically and hides **+**. To attach an existing script instead, click **...**. Stored paths are relative to `Scripts/Mixins`.
5. Implement the generated event methods and add any editable defaults and metadata fields, then refresh or reopen the Blueprint and save.

- **Naming and file safety**: Script names must start with an ASCII letter or underscore, contain only ASCII letters, digits and underscores, and avoid Lua keywords. Creation never overwrites existing files, and undo/redo restores the selection without deleting created files.
- **Generated template**: The generated script includes every event declared on the resolved Actor type (including inherited events with their most-derived signature), forwarding parameters to `super()` and returning its results. Ordinary methods and `init` are omitted. The companion metadata file declares only the matching type with an empty `attrs` table.

## File pair

`scriptPath` points to an existing `.lua` file relative to `Scripts/Mixins` using forward slashes. Empty segments, `.`, `..`, drive prefixes, absolute roots and `_meta.lua` suffixes are invalid.

```text
Scripts/
└── Mixins/
    └── Doors/
        ├── KeyDoor.lua
        └── KeyDoor_meta.lua
```

The metadata file declares editable fields for the editor and never supplies runtime methods. The runtime script owns behaviour and must not load its metadata companion.

You can also create both files manually following the [Table rules](<Runtime Contract.md#table-rules>) and [Script Mixin Metadata](<Metadata.md>). An empty `attrs` table is valid.

## Inherited scripts

A child Blueprint may omit `scriptPath` to inherit its parent's mixin, or supply another path to layer a compatible child mixin over inherited members. Before replacing a script, verify that field and function kinds match the inherited class and remove any stale saved attributes that no longer belong to the resolved schema.

documents.content:
# Script Mixin Runtime Contract

At runtime, Ludork loads a Script Mixin as `Mixins.<path-with-dots>` and requires it to return a plain Lua table with no metatable. This contract defines generated class members, instance defaults, reserved names, parent calls and hot reload.

## Table rules

- Every table key must be a string.
- Function entries become methods on the generated Blueprint class.
- Non-function values are deep-copied into class and instance defaults.
- An inherited member cannot change kind between field and function.
- Saved Blueprint attributes cannot replace a mixin method.

The following member names are reserved:

```text
__*  init  new  scriptMixin  scriptPath
_GENERATED_CLASS  _graph  _hasImplementationOwner
```

> **Note:** Because `init` is reserved, a Script Mixin cannot declare a constructor. Initialise private instance state in the owning type's lifecycle callback (such as `onCreate`) and release subscriptions or resources in the matching teardown callback.

## Parent method calls

Call `super()` inside a mixin method to continue the Blueprint and native inheritance chain:

```lua
local Door = {}

function Door:onCollision(other)
    if self.opening then
        return
    end
    super().onCollision(other)
    self:openDoor()
    self.opening = true
end

return Door
```

The parent class must supply every native property and method the mixin accesses; referencing a missing member raises an error.

## Hot reload

[Lua hot reload](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>) applies to active Script Mixins: `$r` updates compatible methods without rerunning lifecycle callbacks or overwriting defaults and live instance state. Structural changes require a restart.

Lua compilation and `.ldpak` packaging preserve mixin module paths and fresh-load behaviour. See [Run, Debug and Package](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for packaging options.

# Game Script Mixins

Default Gameplay includes the Script Mixin examples below. Each requires the listed parent capability, its companion `_meta.lua` file and the referenced project data or configuration.

| Script | Parent capability | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `Consumables/Bottle.lua` | Collidable Actor | Detects the Player, restores `HP`, plays a configured sound and destroys the pickup. |
| `Consumables/Gem.lua` | Collidable Actor | Adds a value to a direct Player attribute or matching component field. |
| `Doors/Door.lua` | `DoorBase` | Opens on collision and guards against repeated opening. |
| `Doors/KeyDoor.lua` | Script Mixin door Blueprint | Requires and consumes a configured General Data item before calling the parent collision method. |
| `Doors/ConditionDoor.lua` | `DoorBase` | Enables polling only when a game variable is configured, and opens the door once it reaches the threshold. |

For end-to-end setup walkthroughs, see [Consumables](<../Default Gameplay/Recipes/Consumables.md>) and [Doors](<../Default Gameplay/Recipes/Doors.md>).

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md
documents.content:
# Execution Flow, Events and Variables

Blueprints define class defaults and visual event graphs in `Data/Blueprints`, while Common Functions provide reusable graphs shared across Blueprints. See [Blueprints, Common Functions and Actors](<../../Editor User Guide/Blueprints Common Functions and Actors.md>) for editor usage. Script Mixin Blueprints define their events in [Lua](<../Script Mixins/Authoring Workflow.md>) and do not execute graphs.

## Events

An event is declared with `type = "event"`. Its Event entry node exposes ordered parameter outputs and a single execution output.

- **Local execution and fallback**: The execution connection selects the first node to run. If it is unconnected, the local graph does not execute; a class Blueprint then searches its parent chain for an implementation, skipping empty ancestor graphs. Common Functions and General Data graphs have no inherited-event fallback.
- **General Data member graphs**: General Data graphs run as synchronous abilities rather than inherited Blueprint events. `Source.Gameplay.GeneralDataGraphAbility` activates the selected graph with `GameplayEventData` as its owner. A `null` start node returns `NoGraph`. Latent nodes are invalid inside General Data graphs, and runtime errors propagate to the caller.

## Parent event calls

New graph-mode Blueprints and newly added local event graphs initialise with an `Event → Parent` connection whenever an ancestor declares the same event, with initial data links forwarding each event parameter to the matching Parent input. A parent Blueprint's custom event without a metadata signature has no parameter inputs. Existing graphs are not populated automatically, and Script Mixin graphs are inactive.

A Parent node has one execution input, one execution output, typed data inputs matching the event parameters, and no receiver or return-data pins. It resolves the event implementation above the class that owns the current graph.

- **Argument resolution**: Each input supplies its connected value or unconnected default. The argument array follows `SUPER` length and fallback rules: missing or `nil` arguments can fall back to the caller's event context.
- **`nil` holes and overrides**: A `nil` input does not clear the original event argument, and values after a `nil` hole are subject to the same array-length boundary. Non-nil arguments within that boundary — including `false` — override the corresponding event values.

[GlobalFunctions.Utils.SUPER](<../Node Functions/Utils.md>) invokes a parent event from Lua or Blueprints via `SUPER(obj, params)`. Ordinary instance methods use the `self` input described under [Instance method receivers](<#instance-method-receivers>).

## Common Functions

Common Functions share the caller's local context and graph owner, including across nested calls. `SELF` and default instance receivers therefore refer to that same owner.

## Execution semantics

Node metadata and graph links govern how execution flows through a graph:

- **`Pure = true`**: Removes execution input and output pins. Having return values does not imply purity.
- **`ExecSplit`**: Maps named execution outputs to runtime return values.
- **`Latent`**: Returns an `Engine.AsyncOperation`, suspends the graph and resumes along declared state outputs.
- **Re-entry suppression**: Every Blueprint event drops repeated triggers for the same graph instance and event key while latent nodes from the current execution are pending. Once all latent work resolves, new triggers are accepted. Different graph instances and event keys execute independently.
- **`LoopNode`**: Declares loop-body and completion execution outputs.
- **Pin cardinality**: Data links connect compatible typed pins, and execution links connect flow pins. Each execution output accepts one connection; execution inputs accept multiple. Data outputs accept multiple connections; each data input accepts one.

Runtime event queries and execution operate on native `Engine.Graph` userdata. Raw `GraphData` supports definition-time event inspection only, and local execution contexts hold per-invocation state rather than executable graphs. When constructing a graph without a parent class, pass the read-only string `Engine.Graph.NO_PARENT_CLASS` (`"NOT_WRITTEN"`) as `Graph.new`'s `parentClassName`; the `parent` parameter supplies the graph owner independently.

### Cancelling latent execution

Call `operation:cancel()` or `Engine.latentManager:cancel(operation)` to cancel waiting event executions — including pending nodes and loops — without running downstream outputs or completion callbacks. See [AsyncOperation](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Events and Module Root.md#asyncoperation>) for the shared Lua and Blueprint operation contract.

## Instance method receivers

Every instance-method node exposes a typed `self` input, including methods inherited by the current Blueprint. An explicit connection or entered value selects the receiver; if neither is set, the declared `"self"` default resolves to the graph owner. Connected `nil` values, incompatible receivers and missing owners raise an error before the method runs.

- **Parameter layout**: Short method names, `self.method` and fully qualified paths share one parameter order and pass the receiver once. Saved `params` place the receiver at index `0`: a stored `"self"` selects the owner, while an unset entry uses the declared default. Parameter links use the same zero-based indices. Static functions and event payloads have no receiver slot.
- **General Data graphs**: In General Data graphs, the owner is `GameplayEventData`. Connect its `target` (or another object) to `self` when calling an Actor method.

## Typed connections

The graph validator checks data pin connections against the declared types:

- **Unions**: A value connects to a union when at least one branch accepts its type. A union output connects only when the target accepts every branch.
- **Containers**: Lists, dictionaries and tuples apply compatibility rules recursively.
- **Inheritance**: Derived types connect to their declared bases.
- **Numbers and vectors**: `int` connects to `float`, whereas `float` to `int` and conversions between distinct SFML vector types are rejected.
- **`any`**: Allows dynamic connections whose actual runtime values are checked on invocation.
- **Enums**: Enum pins preserve their enum schema but check compatibility using the module's underlying `string`, `bool`, `int` or `float` type. They connect to compatible scalar pins and other compatible enums, including inside containers and unions. Integer enums connect to `float` inputs; `float` enums cannot connect to `int` inputs. Values do not need to match a current named choice.

> **Note:** Incompatible connections appear in red after loading or pasting a graph, with a tooltip explaining the mismatch. Fix them before performing a normal save.

## Defaults and references

New inputs start with their declared default or a valid literal for their type; object and function inputs without either stay unset. Saved literals must match the declared type, even when the pin is connected. Invalid literals appear as errors and block normal saving, and connected values are checked at runtime. See [Functions and events](<Metadata Schema and Decorators.md#functions-and-events>) for metadata default and return declarations.

An enum selector displays keys and saves the underlying scalar value, rereading the enum file whenever the selector opens or regains focus. An unknown saved value stays preserved with an informational message, whereas a value of the wrong scalar type is invalid. Plain-text inputs expect the scalar value, not the displayed key. See [Enum schemas](<Metadata Schema and Decorators.md#enum-schemas>) for module and metadata examples.

## Class attributes

A Blueprint stores attribute values in `attrs` and declares newly introduced variables in a sibling `attrDefs` object with an explicit `type`; **Add Attribute** writes both. Inherited metadata, Script Mixin and ancestor Blueprint fields already carry declarations, so a child Blueprint overrides only the value in `attrs`. Field access nodes and Actor Info use that inherited type, including enum identity and nested container types.

> **Important:** Missing declarations, incompatible values and duplicate declarations fail both editor and runtime loads. Neither global save nor **Save Invalid Blueprint** bypasses class schema validation.

Map Actor overrides validate against the same resolved class schema. See [Blueprint attribute declarations](<Metadata Schema and Decorators.md#blueprint-attribute-declarations>) for JSON examples.

## Class definitions and session lifetime

`ClassDict` instances within one Lua VM share resolved classes, definition tables and compiled graph templates. Changes to JSON class definitions or graph templates require a restart; [Lua hot reload](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>) updates only compatible script functions.

`ClassDict:getData(path)` — also exposed as `Global.Data.GetClassData(path)` in Default Gameplay — uses the same resolution path as `get` and returns the resolver's JSON definition table. Unknown paths raise an error, and Lua module classes without a JSON definition return `nil`. Repeated reads within one VM return the same table, so use `copy` or `deepcopy` when you need an independent copy.

Mutating that returned table affects subsequent definition reads, but does not rebuild generated classes, instance-default records or compiled templates; new instances and executable-event queries use the previously generated results.

documents.content:
# Metadata Schema and Decorators

`_METADATA` is the pure-data schema that describes Blueprint fields, function signatures, editor controls and execution protocols for Lua and C++ types. Every metadata file must return a pure-data table named `_METADATA`.

```lua
local _METADATA = {
    SoundFilter = {
        moduleReturn = true,
        attrs = {
            "volume",
        },
        volume = {
            type = "float",
            default = 1.0,
        },
        apply = {
            type = "function",
            parameters = {
                "self",
                "source",
                self = { "Source.SoundFilter", "SoundFilter" },
                source = { "Engine", "SoundSource" },
            },
            default = { [1] = "self" },
            ["return"] = {},
            Pure = false,
        },
    },
}

return _METADATA
```

## Types and fields

Every type table lists its editable fields in an ordered `attrs` array; table key order is not significant. Each field requires a `type` and displays an ordinary value only when the Blueprint already stores one or metadata provides a `default`.

- **Primitives**: `bool`, `int`, `float`, `string`, `function`, `event`, `any` and `Pair`.
- **SFML and Core types**: SFML values use the `sf.` prefix. Core and Lua types use `{ "Module", "Type" }`, with `[]` on the second item for arrays.
- **Recursive containers**: `T[]` is a variable-length list, `Dict[string, T]` is a string-keyed dictionary and `Tuple[T1, T2, ...]` is a fixed-length heterogeneous array (for example `Dict[string, Tuple[string, any]]`, `Dict[string, int[]]` or `int[][]`).
- **Component and composite controls**: `component = true` marks component fields. Composite controls are selected from their real type (vectors, colour, rectangles and `Pair`, where `Pair` is a two-component numeric control rather than a heterogeneous `Tuple`). `RectRangeVars` adds texture-range selection to `sf.IntRect`.

The capitalised `Dict[...]` and `Tuple[...]` tokens describe metadata schemas, not constructors for Standard's lower-case runtime `dict` and `tuple` containers. Metadata defaults must be JSON-convertible pure data using plain Lua tables rather than native `list`, `tuple` or `dict` values. Runtime pins that accept native containers must declare their qualified type (such as `{ "_G", "list" }`) or include it in a union; `T[]` pins accept Lua arrays and require an explicit conversion node for a native `list`.

The declared schema always governs serialisation shape, even for empty containers: `Dict` serialises as a JSON object, while lists and `Tuple` serialise as JSON arrays. Use an explicit recursive type whenever a shape is known. Runtime calls must supply the declared types; see [Runtime Value Boundaries](<../../Native C++ Development/Runtime Value Boundaries.md>) for conversion rules.

### Value literals and unset inputs

- A `string` field preserves literal text verbatim, including `"nil"`. Strings nested inside saved containers stay literal.
- Whole-value expressions evaluate once, so `nil` in an `any` expression yields Lua `nil`.
- Unset node inputs save as JSON `null` and fall back to the declared default when present. JSON-value editors accept `null` directly; clearing a function expression leaves it unset.
- An `any` input is edited as text: on focus loss, text that parses as a JSON literal (such as a number) saves as that literal, while other text saves as an expression string.

### Plain-text node inputs

**Convert to Plain Text Inputs** bypasses editor selectors and numeric controls while enforcing the same schema:

| Schema type | Accepted plain-text input |
|---|---|
| `string`, `file` | Preserves all text verbatim, including whitespace, blank input and `null`. |
| `int` | Signed 64-bit integer with no fractional part. Blank input is unset. |
| `float`, `double`, `number` | Finite number using `.` as the decimal separator. Blank input is unset. |
| `bool` | `true` or `false`. Blank input is unset. |
| Vectors, `Pair` | Valid JSON component array (e.g. `[1, 2]`). Blank input is unset. |
| `sf.Color` | JSON array of four integers in `0..255`. Blank input is unset. |
| `sf.FloatRect` | JSON array of four numbers. Blank input is unset. |
| `sf.IntRect` | Nested JSON array, such as `[[0, 0, 32, 32]]`. Blank input is unset. |
| Containers and unions | Valid JSON; unions use the declared `$type`/`$value` wrapper, including inside containers. Blank input is unset. |
| `any` | Standard JSON-or-expression conversion, preserving blank text and quoted JSON strings; enter `null` to leave unset. |
| Functions, events, objects | Standard runtime expression and object-reference semantics. |

Invalid plain text is kept as an editor-session draft and never saved as a parameter value. It blocks saving and returning to typed inputs until fixed. Plain-text mode and drafts are window-local and do not modify metadata or Blueprint JSON.

## Blueprint attribute declarations

A Blueprint JSON document stores attribute values in `attrs` and declares fields introduced by that Blueprint in the sibling `attrDefs` object. Omit `attrDefs` when the Blueprint introduces no new fields. Each entry requires `type` using the same primitive, qualified, enum or recursive schema as metadata; `file` fields may also declare `base` to constrain the asset selector while storing a complete `/Game/Assets/...` path.

```json
{
  "attrDefs": {
    "rewardCount": { "type": "int" },
    "stairChoice": { "type": { "enum": "Enums.StairDirection" } },
    "offsets": { "type": { "list": "sf.Vector2i" } },
    "icon": { "type": "file", "base": "Images" }
  },
  "attrs": {
    "rewardCount": 3,
    "stairChoice": "Up",
    "offsets": [[0, 1]],
    "icon": ""
  }
}
```

An `attrDefs` entry contains only `type` and optional file `base`; values and initial defaults belong in `attrs`. A declaration may omit a value, and both editor and runtime preserve its declared type rather than inferring one from the value.

- **Inheritance**: Resolve declarations from Lua/native metadata, the active Script Mixin and ancestor Blueprints before adding local `attrDefs`. A child inherits both type and default: it may override the value in `attrs`, but must not repeat or alter an inherited declaration in `attrDefs`. Local names must not collide with existing fields, methods or reserved runtime names (for example, `speed` or a Mixin's `needKeyCount` is a value override, not a new declaration).
- **Strict validation**: Every saved attribute and nested typed record member must be declared and match its schema. Unknown fields, missing definitions, invalid schemas and conflicting declarations fail loading with the Blueprint path and field name; neither editor nor runtime infers missing declarations or converts legacy untyped shapes.
- **Other graph assets**: Map `BPClassVarChanged` entries store values only and validate against the Actor class's inherited schema. Graph-only Common Functions and General Data member graphs have no class declarations.

## Enum schemas

An enum schema references one module under `Scripts/Enums` whose source holds a literal scalar table and its EmmyLua annotation (see [Enum modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#enum-modules>)). Reference it by its `require` path in any field, parameter, return or nested container/union schema:

```lua
stairDirection = {
    type = { enum = "Enums.StairDirection" },
    default = "None",
}
```

### Source module and scalar-type rules

- **Allowed syntax**: An enum module may return a literal table directly or assign one local literal table and return that variable. Comments, annotations, optional semicolons and one pair of parentheses around a scalar literal are allowed. Function calls (including `require`), calculations, table mutations, other returned variables and extra statements are rejected.
- **Keys and value categories**: Keys must be non-empty strings, and all values must share one category: strings, booleans or finite numbers. Without `valueType`, an all-integer table resolves to `int`, while any floating-point literal (including `1.0`) resolves to `float`.
- **Explicit `valueType`**: Optional `valueType` (`"string"`, `"bool"`, `"int"` or `"float"`, e.g. `{ enum = "Enums.GeneralData.Item", valueType = "string" }`) allows empty enum tables and fixes the scalar type in advance. Non-empty constants must match it (integer literals are accepted for explicit `float`). An empty module without `valueType`, an incompatible constant, an unknown schema property or a missing module fails validation, including inside nested containers. `valueType` constrains only the scalar type, not membership in the current option list.

### Selector, defaults and live resolution

The editor selector lists keys in declaration order and saves the underlying scalar value directly — not the key name or a Lua expression — without requiring `Meta.DropBox`. Equal values display the first matching key. Values absent from the current table stay saved with an unknown-value message and are valid if their scalar type matches; enums do not impose runtime membership checks.

- **Defaults**: An explicit `default` takes priority as the scalar value. Without one, new node inputs and container items use the first option, or the scalar type's default (`""`, `false` or `0`) when the enum is empty. An attribute without a default stays schema-only until a value is saved. String enum selectors include **— None —** (storing `""`), while unknown non-empty values stay visible and preserved.
- **Ordinary enums**: The editor rereads the source file whenever the field displays or the selector opens (including after regaining window focus) without executing gameplay modules.
- **Project-managed enums**: The editor resolves four `valueType = "string"` enums directly from the live project catalogue (including unsaved edits), before source generation:

| Managed enum | Selects |
|---|---|
| `Enums.GeneralDataKey` | General Data type keys |
| `Enums.GeneralData.<TypeName>` | Members of a General Data type |
| `Enums.Animation` | Animation keys |
| `Enums.Particle` | Particle keys |

A deleted managed module fails validation even if an old generated file exists on disk. An invalid enum reports its module path and preserves the current value.

### Enum-keyed dictionaries and plain text

Dictionary schemas can declare a string enum key independently of their value schema:

```lua
type = {
    dict = "int",
    key = { enum = "Enums.GeneralData.Item", valueType = "string" },
}
```

- Omitting `key` uses ordinary string keys. An explicit `key` must be `"string"` or an enum declaring `valueType = "string"`; numeric, boolean, container and untyped enum keys are rejected.
- Values use their own recursive schema, and JSON serialises as an object with the selected scalar strings as keys.
- Adding an enum-keyed row waits for a non-empty unique key before updating saved data; duplicate keys are rejected. `DictKeyMeta` refines unrelated key controls without replacing the declared key type.
- **Plain-text mode and connections**: **Convert to Plain Text Inputs** edits the underlying scalar value (for example, enter the number for an integer enum). The schema preserves enum identity, including inside a union's `$type` descriptor, while the stored value is the scalar. [Typed connections](<Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#typed-connections>) check compatibility using that underlying scalar type.

Native enums and marked constant maps generate equivalent modules such as `Enums.Engine.Direction`, `Enums.GlobalCore.WeatherType` and `Enums.sf.Keyboard.Scan`; see [Generated enum modules](<../../Native C++ Development/Generated Metadata and Stubs.md#generated-enum-modules>).

## Union schemas and stored literals

A union declares its allowed branches as `{ union = { T1, T2 } }` (displayed as `Union[T1, T2]`) and composes with `{ list = T }`, `{ dict = T }` and `{ tuple = { T1, T2 } }` — the structured forms of `T[]`, `Dict[string, T]` and `Tuple[...]`.

A declared default chooses the initial branch and value. Otherwise, a new node selects the first branch that has a valid literal default; branches without one stay unset. Switching branches resets the value to the new branch's default.

```lua
type = { union = { "sf.Vector2f", "sf.Vector2u", "nil" } },
default = { ["$type"] = "sf.Vector2u", ["$value"] = { 64, 32 } },
```

This saves in JSON as `{ "$type": "sf.Vector2u", "$value": [64, 32] }`. `$type` identifies the branch using its qualified name or recursive container schema (such as `{ "list": "sf.Vector2u" }`), distinguishing types with identical JSON shapes.

Explicit `nil` serialises as `{ "$type": "nil", "$value": null }` in JSON and `{ ["$type"] = "nil" }` in Lua metadata, distinct from an unset value (which falls back to defaults). Use the `$type`/`$value` wrapper only where a schema declares a union, including nested unions. Runtime calls receive the unwrapped value; invalid values report the affected field or parameter.

## Inheritance

`bases` is an ordered array of direct metadata bases written as `{ "Module", "Type" }`. List only bases that participate in editor field inheritance. Script Mixin metadata cannot declare `bases`.

When a Lua module returns its class directly, set `moduleReturn = true` in that class's metadata table and keep exactly one type in the metadata file. Class selectors and new Blueprint parents then use the module path (such as `Source.MapActors.Enemy`). A class exposed as a named member omits `moduleReturn` and uses its full reference (such as `Engine.Actor`). Metadata type references — including `bases`, fields and node pins — always use the explicit `{ "Module", "Type" }` pair (for example `{ "Source.MapActors.Enemy", "Enemy" }`).

## Functions and events

`parameters` and `["return"]` combine an ordered name array with name-to-type entries. The optional `default` array aligns by index with `parameters`. `Pure` is explicit, while `ExecSplit`, `Latent`, `LoopNode` and `type = "event"` declare the graph runtime execution protocol.

- **Instance methods**: Every ordinary instance method declares `"self"` as its first parameter with the owning class's explicit `{ "Module", "Type" }` reference and `default[1] = "self"` (for example `{ "Source.Scenes.SceneMap", "Scene" }`). Its receiver pin is visible in every Blueprint context; see [Instance method receivers](<Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#instance-method-receivers>). Include the receiver slot when indexing defaults and saved parameters. Static functions and events omit `"self"`. Lua colon-call signatures and native method declarations keep their normal argument lists.
- **Pin ordering and returns**: The array part sets pin order and string keys set pin types. A `nil` slot in `default` means no default. A `nil` type named in `["return"]` creates an output pin, whereas an empty `["return"] = {}` declares no outputs. Only `Pure = true` removes execution pins.
- **Unset defaults**: Use `defaultUnset = { "parameterName" }` when a parameter's initial value must stay `nil` instead of receiving an editor-generated literal (for example, `Scene.recordActorPosition` sets `defaultUnset = { "position" }` so it defaults to the Actor's current position). Names in `defaultUnset` are unaffected by receiver index shifts.

A static function declares only its own arguments:

```lua
calculate = {
    type = "function",
    parameters = {
        "value",
        "clamp",
        value = "float",
        clamp = "bool",
    },
    default = {
        nil,
        true,
    },
    ["return"] = {
        "result",
        result = "float",
    },
    Pure = true,
}
```

## Execution declarations

- **`ExecSplit`**: Orders execution outputs and maps them to runtime return values, e.g. `ExecSplit = { "success", "fail", success = true, fail = false }`.
- **`Latent = true`**: Marks graph suspension. Ordered `LatentStates` maps resume outputs to stage values, and the return type must be `{ "Engine", "AsyncOperation" }`. See [Execution semantics](<Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#execution-semantics>).
- **`Loop = true`**: Marks a loop node; `LoopNode = "ForEach"` or `"ForLoop"` selects the runtime iteration protocol.
- **`type = "event"`**: Creates an event entry node using the same parameter/return format. Without an explicit `ExecSplit`, the event receives `ExecSplit = { "default", default = "nil" }` (the string `"nil"` is the metadata token for the default branch).

> **Important:** Execution declarations are contracts with the graph runtime. The Lua or C++ implementation must return the declared split values, resume the declared latent states or drive the declared loop protocol.

## Editor names and decorators

Editor labels for types, fields, functions, events, pins and Blueprint variables are derived automatically from their identifiers (for example, `textureRect` displays as **Texture Rect**). Metadata keys, runtime member names and saved Blueprint names stay unchanged.

Do not declare `DisplayName`, `DisplayDesc`, `VariableDisplayNames`, `VariableDisplayDescs`, `ParameterDisplayNames` or `ParameterDisplayDescs` on ordinary members; the editor never evaluates `LOC(...)` or other expressions to derive schema labels or descriptions. The sole exception is operator nodes such as `ADD` and `IADD`, which may declare a literal `Meta.DisplayName` (such as `+` or `+=`) without `LOC(...)` and without a default `DisplayDesc`.

`Meta` supplies editor semantics that cannot be inferred from the declared type: `DropBox`, `PathVars`, `PathRoot`, `PathFilter`, `ProgressVars`, `SliderVars`, `RangeVars`, `MoveRouteVars`, `Transfer`, `BlueprintClassVars`, `CommonFunctionVars`, `ConfigVars`, `InstVar`, `InstVarValue`, `DictKeyMeta`, `ItemMeta`, `InvalidVars` and `RectRangeVars`. Preserve decorator names and ordered data directly; do not wrap them in invented `fields`, `nodes` or `events` containers.

### Resource and data path selectors

| Decorator | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `PathVars` | Selector root. For game resources, supply a full logical root such as `/Game/Assets/Sounds`; the field stores the full logical path. |
| `PathRoot = "Project"` | Selects project files such as Script Mixins. |
| `PathRoot = "Data"` | Selects files under a project-relative `PathVars` directory (such as `Data/Subtitles`) and stores the full `Data/...` path. References must stay inside the selector directory without traversal segments. |
| `PathFilter` | File pattern filter, e.g. `PathFilter = "*.json"`. |

Function metadata targets a named parameter by table mapping, such as `PathRoot = { subtitleFileName = "Data" }`.

### Game-variable selectors (`InstVar` and `InstVarValue`)

- **`InstVar`**: Marks a string field or parameter as a game-variable name, replacing text input with a searchable selector populated from current declarations (including unsaved edits). Set `InstVar = true` for all types, `InstVar = { types = { "int", "float" } }` to restrict to listed metadata types, or `InstVar = { "valueName" }` in function metadata to target named parameters.
- **`InstVarValue`**: Links a field or parameter to the selected variable's type so it adopts that type's editor control. Specify the sibling field name as a string (e.g. `InstVarValue = "openConditionName"`) or a parameter map in function metadata (e.g. `InstVarValue = { value = "valueName" }`). This affects editor controls only; runtime reads and writes use the actual game-variable table.

```lua
openConditionName = {
    type = "string",
    Meta = {
        InstVar = {
            types = {
                "int",
                "float",
            },
        },
    },
}
openConditionVal = {
    type = "int",
    Meta = {
        InstVarValue = "openConditionName",
    },
}
```

### Container and control decorators

Container decorators refine controls at the immediate container layer without altering the schema or JSON shape:

- **`DictKeyMeta`**: Applies decorators to each string key.
- **`ItemMeta`**: Applies decorators to each immediate list item or dictionary value. When the item is a `Tuple`, `ItemMeta.TupleMeta` maps 1-based tuple positions to per-slot decorators.
- **`DropBox`**: Provides ordered literal drop-down choices when no shared enum module exists; prefer an enum schema whenever choices belong to one.
- **`"$dictKey"`**: Inside a dictionary value's `TupleMeta`, `InstVarValue = "$dictKey"` resolves to that row's dictionary key. It is reserved and has no meaning outside that row.
- **`InvalidVars`**: Lists fields hidden from the Blueprint property editor and serialiser.
- **`RectRangeVars`**: Associates an `sf.IntRect` with the texture/range field needed by the image-region selector.

```lua
afterBattleVarChanges = {
    type = "Dict[string, Tuple[string, any]]",
    default = {},
    Meta = {
        DictKeyMeta = {
            InstVar = {
                types = { "int", "float" },
            },
        },
        ItemMeta = {
            TupleMeta = {
                [1] = {
                    DropBox = { "=", "+", "-", "*", "/", "//", "%", "**" },
                },
                [2] = {
                    InstVarValue = "$dictKey",
                },
            },
        },
    },
}
```

This field stores as a JSON object whose values are two-element JSON arrays. The key selector lists declared `int` and `float` game variables, tuple element 1 offers an operator drop-down, and element 2 uses the selected variable's numeric editor. These decorators constrain authoring only; the runtime game-variable table does not enforce the declared type.

## Safety rules

Metadata must be pure data: functions, userdata, threads, cycles, non-finite numbers and side effects are forbidden, and defaults must be JSON-convertible. Metadata strings are never evaluated to produce labels; runtime localisation and localised option values are separate concerns.

Core metadata is generated from `BIND_*` annotations — never edit generated Core metadata by hand. See [Generated Metadata and Stubs](<../../Native C++ Development/Generated Metadata and Stubs.md>).

# Declarative UI Authoring Workflow

Declarative UI generates typed Lua Views from JSON assets while keeping business logic in handwritten Controllers. Use the [UI Asset Editor](<../../Editor User Guide/UI Asset Editor.md>) for visual layout.

| Layer | Owns |
|---|---|
| JSON View | Hierarchy, asset-local node names, static control properties, Slots, animation timelines and design-only preview data |
| Generated Lua View | Complete typed control and child-View tree, asset identity, mounting and owned-object lifetime |
| Lua Controller | Model access, callbacks, localised and formatted text, state refresh and dynamic composition |
| Window UI | Native window and input state, its generated View and its private Controller |
| Native control | Rendering, measurement, hit testing, focus and primitive interaction state |
| `UIManager` | Mounting and removing prepared root controls |

> **Important:** Never store Controller functions, expressions, event handlers or `LOC(...)` calls inside a UI asset. Author fixed positions, dimensions, spacing and text styles in JSON; Controllers read prepared controls only when dynamic content requires measurement or resizing.

## File layout

UI assets live under `Data/UI`:

```text
Data/UI/
├── Inventory.json
└── Parts/
    ├── Inventory/ItemRow.json
    └── Shared/KeyPrompt.json
```

Place complete screens, windows, HUDs and overlays directly under `Data/UI`. Place sub-parts owned by one UI under `Parts/<Owner>` and reusable shared parts under `Parts/Shared`. Do not organise directories purely by control type.

Generated Lua Views mirror the asset tree. Everything under `Scripts/Internal/UI`, `Scripts/stub/Internal/UI` and `Scripts/stub/Internal/UIWindows` is generator-owned — do not edit generated files by hand:

```text
Scripts/Internal/UI/
├── Inventory.lua
└── Parts/
    ├── Inventory/ItemRow.lua
    └── Shared/KeyPrompt.lua
```

- **Handwritten UI modules**: Shared foundations live in `Scripts/Internal/UIBase`. Window modules (such as `Scripts/Source/Windows/WindowInventory.lua`) define a private Controller and export the UI class via `Ui.DefineWindow`. Independent row and Scene Controllers live in dedicated `Controller.lua` modules (such as `Source.Windows.WindowInventory.ItemRow.Controller` and `Source.Scenes.SceneTitle.Controller`).
- **Window declarations**: A window's handwritten stub declares only the private Controller using bare `---@meta`; the generator derives the public window declaration under `Scripts/stub/Internal/UIWindows`. Numeric constants outside plain decimal syntax (such as `1e3` or `0x20`) require an explicit `---@field NAME type` annotation on the Controller. See [Declare business members once](<Controller Examples.md#declare-business-members-once>).
- **Generator parsing rules**: The declaration generator resolves top-level `local Name = require(...)` calls from quoted or long-bracket Lua string literals (decoding valid UTF-8 module names) and expects one final `return Ui.DefineWindow(...)`. Malformed strings, long comments or numeric literals report the file, line and column.

## Create the UI and add its behaviour

1. Author the JSON asset in the UI Asset Editor and give every node accessed from Lua a stable name.
2. Enable **Exposed** if other UI assets need to nest it from the Project Palette.
3. Save the asset and click **Export** to generate its View, then `require` that View from your window module.
4. Define a local Controller and return `Ui.DefineWindow(ViewClass, Controller, nativeBase?)`. Place business setup in `init`, native callbacks in `bind`, and state updates in `watch` or `refresh`.
5. Configure initial host behaviour with `windowOptions`, bind authored child panes with `createChild`, and populate variable-length rows with collections. See [Declarative UI Runtime Contract](<Runtime Contract.md>) and [Declarative UI Controller Examples](<Controller Examples.md>).
6. Maintain the private Controller stub and regenerate. Create, mount and dispose of the window from its owner, using [first-use construction](<Runtime Contract.md#create-optional-windows-on-first-use>) for optional popups.

> **Note:** Assets backed by `WindowBase` or `WindowSelectable` nest `Parts/Shared/WindowChrome` and `Parts/Shared/WindowPauseMark` as nodes named `WindowChrome` and `WindowPauseMark`. Their Slots position the chrome over the frame and the pause mark at the bottom content edge; the window base binds return-button, gamepad-hint and pause-mark behaviour automatically.

## Regenerate after asset changes

After moving an asset or renaming nodes, update handwritten `require` paths and node references, then click **Export**. To regenerate UI Views and declarations without a full export, run:

```bash
ludork-assets ui-assets generate <project-root>
```

Ordinary Save and Construct do not regenerate UI code; export before launching or packaging from the command line (see [Run, Debug and Package](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>)).

Generation enforces strict file safety:
- Output paths occupied by handwritten Lua files or symbolic links are rejected; only obsolete files carrying the generator marker are removed.
- Updated Views, declarations and case-only directory renames install as one atomic batch. Any installation failure rolls back applied changes (and reports paths if rollback itself fails). A case-only directory rename fails if the directory contains handwritten files.

## Authoring constraints and conventions

- **Screen structure**: Give each visible screen one top-level asset and nest owner-specific sub-panes from `Parts/<TopLevelName>/`. Nested parts require `palette.exposed = true`; runtime-only helpers need not be exposed.
- **Dynamic content and localisation**: Localise tab labels and populate dynamic collections before display; fixed controls and rows stay the instances constructed from JSON. Reserve literal JSON `text` for permanent, language-independent symbols, and use design-only preview fields for placeholders (see [UI previews](<../../PreviewHost/UI Actor Particle and Subtitle Previews.md#ui-previews>)).
- **Animated characters**: Use [`Engine.CharacterView`](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Layout and Image Controls.md#characterview>) for frame-animated characters and enemies. Provide preview defaults in JSON and call `setCharacter` at runtime with the real Actor visual.
