documents.content:
# Windows, Menus, Input and Controls

This page covers Default Gameplay's windows, HUD shortcuts, transition animations, localisation refreshes, Floor Teleporter previews and input/focus behaviour. To build custom UI assets and Controllers, see [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>).

## Windows and menus

Default windows follow the [Declarative UI Runtime Contract](<../Declarative UI/Runtime Contract.md>): each screen owns one top-level asset with nested sub-panes, sibling input hosts reuse nested lists and scroll boxes, menus keep stable command keys separate from display text, and overflowing lists use [`Engine.ScrollBox`](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Layout and Image Controls.md#scrollbox>).

- **Eager vs. lazy construction**: Map entry creates the player HUD and Region Title immediately. The title's Save/Load and Config windows and all optional map windows (Menu, Item, Equip, shops, Shop Records, Save/Load, Config, Enemy Book, Encyclopedia, Floor Teleporter, Player Name and Message) use separate [`LazyWindow` handles](<../Declarative UI/Runtime Contract.md#create-optional-windows-on-first-use>) and construct on first display (Message constructs on the first message or choice). Opening Menu does not instantiate unused sub-windows.
- **In-game menu**: Lists **Items**, **Equipments**, **Files**, **Config** and **Return to Title**. `WindowMenu.new(player, windows, onExit)` runs `onExit` after the closing animation while the scene owns destination routing and assigns one stacking layer to the menu and its sub-windows. Opening **Config** overlays the menu and deactivates the command list; closing returns focus to the menu.
- **Templates and preview placeholders**: Default assets include `#TAB` and `#ITEM` preview children. Enemy Book and Encyclopedia use [`CharacterView`](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Layout and Image Controls.md#characterview>) with authored cell sizes while Controllers measure localised labels and special tags. The title's `WindowCommand` binds rows in `Parts/Title/CommandWindow` (placed by `Title`) following the [title scene's platform rules](<New Game Title and Scene Flow.md#new-game-title-and-scene-flow>).

### Window transitions

Top-level window transitions interpolate linearly (default `0.2` seconds), while internal panes and tabs switch immediately. Input locks during playback, close callbacks run after `FadeOut` hides the root, and initialisation/disposal hide immediately. Related `FadeOut` transitions may run in parallel; using an inventory item triggers its callback once the item window hides, and an open menu then closes and restores movement once no blocking window is open.

| UI | Timeline behaviour |
|---|---|
| Default windows and Config | `FadeIn`: centre Scale `0.5` to `1` plus colour; `FadeOut`: colour only. |
| Title command | `FadeIn`: local Y `80` to `0` plus colour. Opening Config or Save/Load leaves it visible. |
| Map Menu | `FadeIn`/`FadeOut`: local X `-192` to `0` and back, plus colour. |
| Item and Equip | Menu animations only. Save/Load supports both default and Menu pairs; Config always uses default. |
| Message | `Panel` colour only. |
| Game Over | Colour-only `FadeIn` (`0.5` s) and `FadeOut` (`1` s). Scene switching waits for `FadeOut`, which holds its transparent final frame until disposal. |
| Region Title | `Display` holds colour for `1` s, then fades over `1` s. |

Pass `Enums.WindowTransitionProfile.DEFAULT` (`"Default"`) or `.MENU` (`"Menu"`) when opening Item, Equip or Save/Load windows.

### Selection, chrome, touch and localisation

- **Selection and scroll**: Focusing a selectable list (on open, pane switch or return to parent) scrolls the active selection into view without moving the mouse cursor. Starting a new open session on Menu, Item, Equip, shops, Config or Enemy Book resets selectors to `0` (or `nil` if empty) and scrolls to the top; focus switches and in-place refreshes within a session keep the selection.
- **Touch and Web lists**: On mobile and Web, tapping an unselected row selects it without confirming, tapping the selected row confirms it, and dragging scrolls without confirming (applies to title commands, Save/Load slots and all selectable windows; Web also supports mouse selection — see [Web input](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Input and Services.md#web-input>)). On the title screen, open Config or Save/Load windows prevent the underlying command window from receiving any part of the same touch gesture.
- **Window return button**: `Parts/Shared/WindowChrome` places a `16 × 16` return button on the top-left border (outside `Content`). `WindowBase` binds it for windows setting `windowOptions.returnButton = true` and implementing `Controller:onReturn()`, playing System `CancelSE` once (other Cancel sources must not duplicate it). Multi-pane windows show it only on the active interactive pane; hidden, inactive or suppressed windows hide it.
- **Gamepad hints and pause mark**: `WindowChrome` also places an `Engine.GamepadHintBar` on the bottom border, displaying up to three `Engine.GamepadHint` entries when a gamepad is connected (`setGamepadHints`, `setGamepadHintEnabled`, `getGamepadHintCount`, `isGamepadConnected`, `setOnGamepadHintTriggered`; see [GamepadHintBar](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Interactive and Declarative UI Controls.md#gamepadhintbar>)). `Parts/Shared/WindowPauseMark` defines pause-mark bounds while `WindowBase` drives its animation and visibility.
- **Static vs. dynamic rows**: Static command rows store `localeKey` and dynamic rows store literal `text` (never both), letting language switches refresh controls in place without losing callbacks or cursor state.
- **Live locale refreshes**: `SceneMap` owns one `LocaleChanged` subscription for long-lived map windows. Active dialogue keeps its raw speaker, message/choices, explicit `localeArgs` and snapshots of node-local and instance variables so template localisation and string `localeArgs` rerun in place; Item/Equip details, shops, attribute shops, Enemy Book, `WindowEnemyEncyclopedia`, `WindowFloorTeleporter`, title commands, Menu, Save/Load tabs and visible Region Titles refresh in place while preserving selection, mode, focus and previews. Hidden windows refresh on next open; Config, save-slot and HUD controllers manage their own subscriptions.

### Shops and dialogue

- **Item shops**: Load `Enums.ShopMode` (`BUY = "buy"`, `SELL = "sell"`) for `WindowShop:setMode(mode)`. The two-column item list stays focused while **Q**/**E**, **LB**/**RB**, mouse or touch switches tabs (resetting cursor and scroll; transactions preserve valid selections). Cells show icons and owned counts; details show localised name, description, `Price` label and right-aligned price. Selling pays `floor(price / 2)` GOLD and hides zero-price items. Buy-only shops hide tabs and centre remaining panes. Cancel closes the shop, restores movement and blocks map input for one frame.
- **Attribute shops**: Expose snapshots via `getOffers()` and validate purchases via `purchaseAttribute(key)`. A scalar price reference is shared across offers, whereas an array assigns per-offer prices; each purchase increments its price.
- **Dialogue (`WindowMessage`)**: Uses a full-screen Canvas and transparent `FunctionalImage` to consume one click/tap for plain-message confirmation; choice mode (up to four options without a ScrollBox) disables that layer so blank-space clicks cannot pick a choice. `SceneMap` blocks map input only while dialogue is active. Dialogue, tutorial and window APIs return `Engine.AsyncOperation` (see [Lua waiting and results](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#lua-waiting-and-results>)).

### Floor Teleporter and static previews

- **Eligibility and single-map mode**: Lists maps in the current region that have recorded telepoints (maps without a region have none). With zero eligible maps, it plays the buzzer and refuses to open even when the player owns the item (without locking movement, taking focus or building previews). With one map, it opens directly on its first telepoint (requiring explicit confirmation; Cancel closes).
- **Multi-map mode**: With multiple maps, it opens the floor list with the current map selected and scrolled into view (or the first entry if absent), toggling the left pane between floor and telepoint lists (telepoints start at entry 1; Cancel returns to floors). Opening resolves the initial mode and selection before rendering its single preview.
- **Scrolling and naming**: Long map and telepoint names use [ListView child scrolling](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Layout and Image Controls.md#listview>) inside fixed selection rectangles without shifting the right-side preview. A composite-world manifest appears as one floor with children at world offsets. Labels resolve recorded tags via `LOC` (falling back to localised `POINT` numbers for blank/auto tags, or the raw tag if untranslated).
- **Discovery and stair pairing**: Set each stair Blueprint's `stairDirection` for opposite-direction matching; telepoints record on stair transfers or `Teleporter:goToMap` even before acquiring the Teleporter item (opening the window or approaching stairs does not record). See [Teleporter](<../Source Classes/Teleporter.md>) and [Saves](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>).
- **Preview rendering**: Previews update on keyboard, mouse or touch focus at fixed scale, clamped to map/manifest bounds and centring axes smaller than the viewport. They render from [static Actor display records](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#static-actor-display-data>) with material time fixed at `0`, excluding gameplay-script-only visuals.
- **Preview persistence and cache invalidation**: Destroyed tags and their children are filtered out before creating records or textures; added, moved and terrain edits plus declarative `childActorComp` children restore without running callbacks, and ordinary maps honour region hiding. `ConditionalActor` visibility evaluates against live variables without subscriptions (variable edits invalidate cached textures, and reopening clears preview models, textures and class templates).

### Player HUD shortcuts

The player HUD mounts a native `WrapBox` `8` logical pixels below the keys, flowing available shortcut buttons left to right without empty slots and wrapping when width runs out:

1. **Enemy Book** (when the player owns `Item.EnemyBook`; uses the item's icon).
2. **Floor Teleporter** (when the player owns `Item.Teleport`; uses the item's icon).
3. **Visited shops** (when `GameInstance` has at least one shop record; uses `Assets/System/mting-495.png` and obeys [Visited shops](<#visited-shops>) opening rules, including Teleporter ownership).

Icons are `32 × 32` with an `8`-pixel gap; mobile and Web expand each button's hit area to `40 × 40` via the [touch-hit bounds API](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Runtime Values and Functional Controls.md#touch-capture>) without scaling the image. Buttons never take keyboard focus or replace hotkeys.

- **Binding and event-driven refreshes**: `Source.Windows.HUDPlayerAttr.new(instance, openMenuCallback?, shortcutCallbacks?)` binds to `GameInstance` (with optional `enemyBook`, `floorTeleporter` and `shopRecords` callbacks wired by `SceneMap`). Call `setInstance(instance)` after loading or switching the primary player. Shortcuts rebuild only initially, on rebind, on `PlayerChanged` inventory events for the current player, and on [shop-record changes](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>) for the current instance (never polled per frame).
- **HUD event subscriptions**: Subscribes to `LocaleChanged`, `AbilitySystemChanged` and `PlayerChanged` (`Enums.EventKey`), ignores events whose `owner` is another battler, and updates only changed controls. Payloads use `Enums.AbilitySystemChangeKind` (`Attribute`, `State`) or `Enums.PlayerChangeKind` (`Inventory`, `Name`, `Map`) under `Source.Configs.EventChangePayload`. Owned subscriptions and callbacks release with the HUD.

### Visited shops

- **Opening**: Releasing **V** opens `WindowShopRecords` when shop recording is enabled, the player owns the Teleporter item, at least one shop is recorded and the scene allows opening a window.
- **List display**: Shows records across all regions as single-column rows displaying localised `mapName` (or `worldName`), a space and the localised recorded tag, with in-row scrolling for long text. Reopening resets selection to row 1 and top scroll; language switches update labels without resetting selection or scroll.
- **Recording**: Both item and attribute shops record successful openings when opened from an Actor with a map identity (see [Shop Actors](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#shop-actors>) and [Saves](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>)).
- **Remote execution**: Confirming a row closes the list and runs that shop's complete `onCollision` event with the current player as `other` while keeping the player on the current map. The shop Actor constructs independently from its saved map placement (`BPClassVarChanged` and world coordinates) without loading the target map scene, mutating shared class defaults or running `onCreate` — shop graphs must rely on configured fields and live game variables rather than target-map attachment or `onCreate` state. Dialogue, conditions and post-shop logic execute normally.
- **Closing and missing records**: Closing the shop returns directly to map play without reopening the list, and cancelling the list restores movement. A missing map or tag plays the buzzer while leaving the list and saved record intact (delete obsolete entries with `removeShop`). Remote openings never re-record the shop under the player's current map.

### Map introduction

`Map_01` places an invisible `BP_MapIntroduction` Actor that runs introductory guides in order after the map transition, then records and destroys itself.

- **Configuration**: `Source.Configs.Tutorial` maps tutorial keys to `{ rect: sf.IntRect, text: string }` using fixed logical screen coordinates (update rectangles if UI layout changes). `BP_MapIntroduction` passes its ordered keys through `ForEach` to `ShowTutorial`; the scene component renders whatever keys are requested without hard-coding map names or tags (see [Tutorials](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#tutorials>)).
- **Presentation**: The spotlight contracts to `rect` over `0.25` seconds while blocking input, dimming the rest of the screen (including HUD and margins) with a `40%`-opaque grey curtain, flashes the border once, and then enables [confirmation](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Input and Services.md#inputcapture>). Explanations render in size-12 outlined localised text (refreshing on language change), wrapping to screen width first, anchoring left-aligned at the bottom-middle of `rect`, shifting left to stay inside the right edge, and flipping above top-middle if space below is insufficient.

### Player name window

The NPC beside `Map_01`'s starting point opens `WindowPlayerName` and pauses map input until closed. Use **Tab** / **Shift+Tab** and directional keys to switch between the text input and **Confirm** (which stays visible across all devices).

- **Mouse and touch**: Activate the input or **Confirm** directly; submitting the mobile/Web system input dialog updates the draft without closing the window.
- **Keyboard**: **Enter** / **Space** applies the name when **Confirm** has focus, or starts editing otherwise. **Escape** exits editing first, and a second press discards the draft and closes the window.
- **Gamepad**: **A** starts editing (even while **Confirm** is focused). Holding **X** for one second (`gamepadButton = "X"`, `gamepadLongPress = true` on the button asset, without populating `GamepadHintBar`; see [Button](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Runtime Values and Functional Controls.md#button>)) applies the name regardless of focus. **B** (or the return button) exits editing on first press and discards/closes on the second.
- **Validation and HUD**: Invalid names disable **Confirm** (see [Source.MapActors.Player](<../Source Classes/Player.md>)). The HUD displays the confirmed name above the player's level, truncated to fit.

### Region-aware map previews

When `GameMap.HideDisconnectedRegions` is enabled, Enemy Book filters out Actors hidden by the player's current region before grouping and deduplicating. Floor Teleporter previews apply the same visibility mask using the player's cell on the current floor and the selected destination cell on other floors; changing destination regions or terrain invalidates the preview cache. Region hiding is visual only and never modifies telepoint records or destinations (see [Disconnected regions](<../Global and Core Modules/Global APIs/GameMap.md#disconnected-regions>)).

## Input

Runtime input comes from the C++ input service rather than editor state (embedded Windows play forwards compatible input over the runtime protocol; standalone builds read the native window directly).

- **Hotkeys**: `Source.Configs.HotKey` binds native keys to a `Scene`, a `Filter` and optional `FunctionWhenPressed` / `FunctionWhenReleased` callbacks receiving the scene instance.
- **Keyboard and gamepad actions**: Physical **Enter** and **Space** map to Confirm and **Escape** maps to Cancel (press and release are edge events). Controllers use logical buttons `Engine.JoystickButton.getA()` through `getShare()`, where **A**/**Cross** is Confirm and **B**/**Circle** is Cancel (see [Engine: Input and Services](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Input and Services.md>)).
- **Directional input**: Movement and menu navigation read only left-stick `X`/`Y` and D-pad `PovX`/`PovY` (right-stick and trigger axes cannot steal direction). Horizontal wins whenever `|X| >= |Y|` (exact 45-degree input resolves horizontally), and vertical wins otherwise, for both stepped navigation and held movement.
- **Mobile and HarmonyOS gestures**: On Android and HarmonyOS, the system Back button/gesture emits one Cancel/Escape pulse instead of closing or backgrounding the app — separate from HarmonyOS external-keyboard forwarding (which emits SFML scancode edges, resolvable logical-key edges and modifier state) and separate from two-finger touch (a right-click cancellation gesture). Both system Back and two-finger touch reach the focused window's `onReturn()`, though only two-finger touch emits right-mouse input.
- **Window cancellation**: `WindowSelectable` owns default Cancel-key and right-click closing; derived windows pass unhandled input up to it so each edge triggers one `CancelSE` and one close transition.

## Focus and navigation

Define an explicit focus order for keyboard and controller navigation, and ensure disabled or hidden controls never stay focused.

## Configuration controls

- **Config tabs and navigation**: Opens on **Graphics** with row 1 focused. **Q**/**E**, **LB**/**RB**, mouse hover and touch tap switch tabs with `CursorSE`. Each tab keeps its cursor and scroll within an open session and across locale refreshes; reopening resets all tabs. See [Game Settings Reference](<Game Settings Reference.md>) for option meanings.
- **DropBox controls**: Switching tabs collapses an open DropBox silently; Cancel and the return button collapse it first and close Config on the next press. An expanded DropBox overlays rows, scrolls internally when height-limited, captures input until closed and uses preview-then-confirm on mobile/Web touch (see [Interactive and Declarative UI Controls](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Interactive and Declarative UI Controls.md>)).
- **Mobile and Web Sliders**: Tapping a Slider sets its value on release. Once dragging passes the drag threshold, horizontal drags belong to the Slider while vertical or tied drags scroll the Config list (when overflowing), keeping gesture ownership locked until release.
- **Save/Load window**: Shares one slot list across Load and Save tabs, preserving cursor, scroll and detail when switching tabs. Reopening defaults to Load on the newest save (or slot `0` if none exists), whereas map hotkey **S** opens in Save mode. Cancel closes the window; title load-only mode hides the tabs and centres the remaining panes.

For low-level UI and input APIs, start with [GlobalFunctions.Container](<../Node Functions/Container.md>). For text localisation keys, see [Game Localisation Workflow](<../../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>).

# Resources, Audio, Video and Effects

This page covers Default Gameplay's logical resource paths, animation caches, map audio and DSP effects, 2D materials, procedural fog, panoramas, composite-world environments and FFmpeg video playback.

## Resource paths

Stored assets use exact-case `/Game/Assets/...` paths with `/` separators and file extensions. Generic resource managers require this full path, whereas category helpers such as `loadCharacter("actors/Hero.png")` and `playSE("cursor.ogg")` accept category-relative paths and prepend their own prefix.

The runtime reads both loose files and `.ldpak` archives through the same logical paths, including streaming and seeking for music and video. Standard Lua filesystem APIs and LuaSF file constructors do not resolve paths inside archives.

## Animation caches

Animation sources live in `Data/Animations`. `Engine.getAnimationCacheRoot()` resolves and creates `Cache/Animations` under `Engine.getUserDataPath()` for both loose and archived data, following the [application user-data location](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>) in every launch mode.

- **Build and invalidation**: Startup generates missing `.anim.json`/`.anim.ldc` caches and rebuilds them whenever source definitions or referenced frame assets change, preserving relative paths under `Data/Animations`. Caches are disposable and omitted from templates and player packages.
- **Binary format**: Sources decode through `Engine.decodeData` and caches write through `Engine.saveData`. `.anim.ldc` stores direct binary data without intermediate JSON; delete legacy compressed-JSON caches so startup regenerates them.
- **Modules**: `Source.Utils.AnimationCache` handles key extraction, frame-asset discovery and staleness checks for `SceneInit`; `Global.Data.LoadAnimations()` loads prepared caches.

## Audio

Music, sound effects and voices each have separate enable switches and volumes in the [game configuration](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>). Play gameplay audio through the [GlobalFunctions Manager helpers](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalFunctions.md#manager>).

### Map BGM and BGS (`Global.Audio.MapAudio`)

`Global.Audio.MapAudio` manages map BGM/BGS playback and filters using `Global.Audio.MapAudioState` for source reuse and fades. Custom scenes construct an instance with `MapAudio.new()`, trigger tracks via `playMapAudio(mapData, transitionSeconds?)`, advance fades in `onTick(deltaTime)` and halt playback with `stopMapAudio()`.

User music enable and volume settings apply immediately during fades, and updating a track's filter volume preserves fade progress. Requesting the already-playing file reuses its source, reapplies the filter and cancels any active fade. See [Script operations and lifetime](<../Source Classes/SceneMap.md#script-operations-and-lifetime>) for scene-stack returns.

### Lua DSP audio effects

`Source.Utils.AudioEffects` defines the case-sensitive DSP presets used by the gameplay Manager and Blueprint audio nodes:

| Preset | Default parameters |
|---|---|
| `Echo` | `0.3` s delay, `0.5` decay |
| `Distortion` | `2.0` drive, `0.7` threshold |
| `Underwater` | `0.7` depth, `0.3` bubble |
| `BehindWall` | `900` Hz cutoff, `0.35` transmission |

- **Selecting a preset**: `GlobalFunctions.Audio.SetEffect(audioType, effect)` resolves `effect` via `AudioEffects.Get` and stores the attacher independently for `Sound`, `Voice` or `Music` (both parameters appear as drop-downs in metadata). Selecting an effect does not instantiate a processor or alter playing sources; each subsequent source invokes the attacher in an isolated audio Lua state with a fresh processor. Pass the literal string `"nil"` to clear future playback; any other unknown name raises an error immediately.
- **Registry ownership**: `Source.Utils.AudioEffects` is the sole preset registry — adding or renaming presets also requires updating `SetEffect`'s metadata drop-down. The project attacher passes `"Source.Utils.AudioEffects"`, `"Get"` and the preset name to [`AudioEffectControl.attachLuaProcessor`](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Resource Managers.md#audiomanager>); replacing the registry module requires updating that call. Effect selection is separate from `SoundFilter` and `MusicFilter`.
- **Sample rate, hot reload and tail draining**: Non-empty presets capture the active playback device's sample rate on source creation (active sources keep their coefficients across device rerouting; start a new Manager playback to adopt the new rate or pick up [hot-reloaded](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>) audio code). Presets do not chain or mix. `Echo` drains its buffered tail after natural end of stream, whereas an explicit Manager stop, dialogue skip or shutdown discards the tail. Direct `sf.SoundSource:setEffectProcessor` calls bypass Manager isolation, EOS handling and cancellation.
- **Dialogue voice lifetime**: `GlobalFunctions.Scene.ShowVoiceMessageByTag` and `ShowVoiceMessage` track the Voice handle started by that call and stop it when dialogue ends before `FinishedDialogue` resumes downstream nodes (so a subsequent `SetEffect` applies to the next Voice). Leaving or destroying a map scene also stops the active global Voice; ordinary message nodes leave Voice playback untouched.

## Shaders, fog and transitions

### 2D materials and shaders

Actors and tile layers render through Ludork's 2D material system. `SceneInit` generates material shaders and runtime metadata in the user data directory before gameplay, followed by a separate [platform shader cache](<../../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md#mrb-rendering>) preparation stage; see [Runtime generation](<../../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#runtime-generation>) for cache validation and ownership.

- **Material combinations**: Startup prepares all individual materials and scans saved maps for tile/layer combinations. If runtime scripts construct maps or swap layer materials into new combinations, register them in [Game → Material Combinations](<../../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#material-combinations>) before preparation. Actor and UI material switches and parameter edits need no extra entry.
- **Sharing and evaluation**: Material resources and compiled programs are shared while per-instance parameters stay independent. Character effects are standard `Data/Materials` graphs (for example, hue shifts use a HueShift node and parameter). Alpha, light blocking and vertex displacement evaluate from the same graph, so a dissolved silhouette updates its shadow mask automatically. Emission composites within each surface without illuminating neighbours or bypassing foreground occlusion.
- **Built-in pipelines and platform support**: Built-in weather and fog use cross-platform shader pipelines whose load and compile errors propagate. World entry prewarms the shared renderer for the current viewport and repeats after regional geometry changes. HarmonyOS compiles programs on first normal draw once render state and uniforms are bound. Shader availability depends on the target runtime GPU — a working editor preview does not guarantee target hardware support.
- **Particles**: Attach GPU [Common Particle](<../../Editor User Guide/Common Particles.md>) emitters to Actor Components and UI; Default Gameplay's code-driven particles work alongside them.

### Enemy defeat shatter effect

Default Gameplay's project-wide defeat shatter effect is toggled by `Enemy.DefeatShatterEffectEnabled` in [Shared Gameplay configuration](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#shared-gameplay-configuration>) rather than per Enemy Blueprint. Its shader snapshots the enemy and scatters world-space logical-pixel fragments radially outwards over ~`0.65` seconds. Because the enemy is already recorded and destroyed, the effect is visual only and never blocks movement, collision or light. When disabled or when `sf.Shader.isAvailable()` is `false`, defeated enemies disappear immediately.

### Procedural fog and panoramas

- **GPU fog**: Generated procedurally from world coordinates, absolute time and a deterministic seed using four noise layers (no fog texture). Density controls coverage, colour alpha scales patch opacity without adding a flat veil, and smaller scales create finer patches (including for black fog). Map data stores `enabled`, `colour`, `density`, `scale`, `velocity`, `turbulence` and `seed` (see [FogController](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Map and Fog.md#fogcontroller>)). Fog composites after materials and lighting, before foreground weather and particles, responds to scene light, and resets per map session.
- **Map panorama**: Optional canonical `/Game/Assets/...` string on `panorama` (missing, `nil` or blank disables it). The texture Cover-scales to `GameMap.MapViewRect` preserving aspect ratio and crops overflow by the Camera origin as a fraction of `(mapPixels - viewPixels)` per axis (`0.5` when an axis cannot scroll). Transparent tiles and canvas margins show the panorama tinted by ambient light only, while point lights apply to opaque tiles. A missing panorama texture fails loading.

### Composite-world environment

- **Fog and panorama**: A world manifest may set global fog (covering the whole world, including holes) and a global panorama (scrolling across total world bounds). Child fog clips to its placement, samples the same world coordinates and time, composites after global fog in stable placement order (blending continuously across matching neighbours), and disappears on child eviction until reload. A child's `panorama` applies only when loaded as a standalone map.
- **Audio and ambient light**: World manifests cannot define BGM, BGS, audio filters or ambient light — these follow the child map under the player, with `0.5`-second fades for audio and subsequent ambient-light transitions. Holes have no map audio and use white ambient light while keeping world fog and panorama active.
- **World lighting**: Lights operate in world coordinates, so Actor `LightComponent` lights illuminate and cast shadows across child boundaries. Tile light masks clip to their placements, and holes contribute neither surfaces nor blockers. See [PreviewHost: Map and World Previews](<../../PreviewHost/Map and World Previews.md>) for editor preview controls.

## Video

Video playback requires an FFmpeg-enabled project or template. Store videos under `Assets/Videos` and reference them as `/Game/Assets/Videos/...` (loose files and `Assets.ldpak` entries share the same seekable playback contract). See [FFmpeg option](<../../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#ffmpeg-option>) for build and packaging details.

- **Android**: Supports MOV, H.264/AAC, `swscale` and `swresample`; excludes network streams, JNI, MediaCodec and hardware acceleration.
- **WebGL**: Uses the same FFmpeg software decoder, resource paths, mute, skip and subtitles without relying on browser HTML codecs. Audio obeys [browser startup policy](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#webgl>), focus loss pauses the video clock, and decoding runs on the main thread (so smooth resolution depends on the device).

Play videos with `GlobalFunctions.Video.PlayVideo(videoFileName, mute, skipable, subtitleFileName?)`, where the optional fourth argument is a project-relative `Data/Subtitles/...json` path (omitted or `""` plays without subtitles):

```lua
local Video = require("GlobalFunctions.Video")
Video.PlayVideo("/Game/Assets/Videos/intro.mp4", false, true, "Data/Subtitles/intro.json")
```

[Subtitle files](<../../Editor User Guide/Video Subtitles.md>) define `type: "subtitle"` and a `sections` array with start/end times (seconds) plus either a shared string array or a language-keyed dictionary. Dictionary entries select the active game language, falling back to `en_GB` only if the key is absent (an explicit empty array suppresses subtitles). Subtitles track the video clock and render centred at the bottom of the viewport in white with a black outline using the default font.

# Runtime Data, Configuration and Saves

This page documents Default Gameplay's configuration files, data-service bootstrap contract, runtime state and persistence model, composite-world save records and `.json`/`.ldc` save formats.

## Configuration

`Data/Configs` stores project configuration JSON, while mutable user preferences live in the [platform game configuration](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>). Use the configuration APIs and editor controls so unknown sections and keys survive round trips.

> **Note:** Optional [remote account dictionaries](<../../Simple Server/Native Client API.md>) are an independent service and do not automatically upload, download or overwrite local saves; gameplay code explicitly chooses what to read and write.

### Paths, constants and keys

- **Config resource vs. data references**: Resource-valued `file` fields store complete `/Game/Assets/...` paths (`base` and `ext` constrain only the editor selector). In `System.json`, `startPlayerBlueprint` is relative to `Data/Blueprints` (`root = "Data"`, resolving to `Data.Blueprints.*`) and `startRegion` names the starting region; both apply to new games only, as saves keep their stored player class and region.
- **Engine constants and Lua config modules**: Grid cell size is compiled into the engine (`32` by default; read with `Engine.GetCellSize()`, not configured in `System.json`). Lua config modules live under `Scripts/Source/Configs` (`Source.Configs.*`). `Source.Locale.Core.DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` (`en_GB`) is the shared initial and fallback language (also used by `Source.Configs.Main`), `Source.Configs.MapConstants.WORLD_MANIFEST_FILE` is `"_world.json"`, and data readers/saves use suffixes from `Engine.ResourceFileConstants`.
- **Initial data keys**: Keys are paths relative to their category directory using `/` separators with only the final extension stripped, preserving internal dots (e.g. `folder.v1/item.v2.json` becomes `folder.v1/item.v2`). Animation keys strip the full `.anim.json` cache suffix.
- **User-data directories**: `Engine.getUserDataPath(appNameOverride?)`, `Engine.getMainConfigPath(appNameOverride?)` and `Engine.getSavePath(appNameOverride?)` resolve the user-data root, config file and `Save/` directory after `Entry` calls `Engine.setAppName(APP_NAME)`. Passing `appNameOverride` queries another application name without altering the active one. All launch modes obey the same [directory rules](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>); `LUDORK_EDITOR` does not redirect them.
- **Loading user config**: `Source.Configs.Main.LoadOrCreate()` returns the user configuration path and `ConfigParser`, creating platform defaults if absent and raising an error on unreadable or malformed plist files rather than overwriting them. Entry script selection is independent of user preferences (see [Entry and module order](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#entry-and-module-order>)).
- **Android paths**: Android mirrors immutable runtime assets into `filesDir/ludork/runtime/<runtime-hash>` before native startup and writes mutable configuration and saves to `filesDir/ludork/user-data/<APP_NAME>` without modifying the runtime directory or requiring external-storage permission.

### Shared Gameplay configuration

`Data/Configs/Gameplay.json` stores project-wide overrides for shared script defaults. Edit them in [Database → System Config → Gameplay](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#system-config>).

| Key | Type | Script default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enemyDamageHintLevel` | `Enums.DamageHintLevel` | `BATTLE` (`1`) | Sets `EnemyDamageText.EnemyDamageHintLevel`: `NONE` (`0`) hides expected-damage hints, `BATTLE` shows enemy readouts, and `MAP` (`2`) also shows movement-danger cell totals. Owning the required Item gates hints; actual damage particles are unaffected. |
| `enemyDefeatShatterEffectEnabled` | boolean | `true` | Sets `Enemy.DefeatShatterEffectEnabled`, toggling the [enemy-defeat shatter effect](<Resources Audio Video and Effects.md#shaders-fog-and-transitions>). |
| `hideDisconnectedRegions` | boolean | `false` | Sets `GameMap.HideDisconnectedRegions`, enabling the [tile mask for disconnected regions](<../Global and Core Modules/Global APIs/GameMap.md#disconnected-regions>) on newly constructed ordinary maps. |
| `enableShopRecord` | boolean | `true` | Sets `GameInstance.EnableShopRecord`. Disabling stops new shop records and the [visited-shop shortcut](<Windows Menus Input and Controls.md#visited-shops>) without deleting saved records. |
| `maxSaveSlots` | positive integer | `100` | Sets `WindowSaveSlot.MAX_SAVE_SLOTS` for the slot list and quick-save, quick-load and latest-slot queries. Lowering it hides higher slots without deleting their files. |
| `tutorialShrinkDuration` | finite positive number (seconds) | `0.25` | Sets `WindowTutorial.SHRINK_DURATION`, the tutorial mask contraction time. |

- **JSON override schema**: Fields use string `type` values (`"int"`, `"float"`, `"bool"`), `nullable: true` to permit script defaults, and `enum: "Enums.DamageHintLevel"` for enum choices. Overrides store under `value` with no separate `useDefault` flag; new Gameplay files default every override to `null`.
- **`null` vs. concrete overrides**: `null` selects **Use default** (leaving the script default active without assigning `nil`), whereas explicit `false` and `0` are concrete overrides (`0` selects `NONE` for damage hints, but fails validation for positive numeric fields). Actor and map defaults (such as movement speed or `GameMap.MapViewRect`) stay on their class or Blueprint properties.
- **`scriptDefault` source reference**: Every nullable field requires `scriptDefault: { module, field }` pointing to a Lua file under `Scripts` and a `table.field` assignment (such as `Controller.MAX_SAVE_SLOTS`). The editor parses one unconditional top-level assignment of scalar literals, imported enum members or simple scalar arithmetic without executing Lua; missing files or unsupported expressions keep **Use default** selected and report an error.
- **Startup application and runtime overrides**: `Source.System.Init()` calls `Source.Configs.Gameplay.Apply()`, which validates every value and fails startup on invalid types, enum values or ranges. JSON edits take effect after saving and restarting (not via Lua hot reload). Scripts can toggle `GameInstance.EnableShopRecord` directly at runtime without erasing recorded shops.

## Data services

`Global.Data` owns shared data loading, resource queries, Blueprint classes and graphs, Actor construction and static previews; require it directly. `Source.Data` owns project startup, default General Data queries (such as `GetGeneralPlayerData` and `GetGeneralItemData`) and `CreateGeneralAttributeSet(typeName, memberID)`.

`Source.Data.InitializeRuntime()` invokes `Global.Data.InitializeRuntime(options)` once per Lua session (a second call raises an error; requiring either module never initialises it). Custom projects must pass all four `Global.Data.RuntimeOptions` fields from startup:

| Required option | Type and purpose |
|---|---|
| `configResolver` | `(configName: string, settingName: string) -> string`; resolves config references for empty string overrides. |
| `nodeModuleCandidates` | `(prefix: string) -> string[]`; extra node module paths in search order (the unprefixed path is tried first). |
| `conditionalActorBase` | `Class.ClassType<Engine.Actor>`; Actor base whose subclasses expose `conditionVariable`, `conditionOperator` and `conditionValue` in previews. |
| `childActorComponentBase` | `Class.ClassType<Engine.Component>`; component base whose subclasses supply `className` and `relativePosition` through `childActorComp` in previews. |

Pass finalised class objects (not module-name strings or instances) satisfying `Class.isSubclass` against `Engine.Actor` and `Engine.Component`. Default Gameplay supplies `Source.System.GetConfigValue`, the ordered `Source.` and `Global.` node candidates, `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor` and `Source.Components.ChildActorComponent`, keeping `Global` independent of `Source`. Configuration provider registration is handled separately by `Source.System.InstallRuntimeProviders()`.

## Runtime state

Keep static definitions in Blueprint, Config and General Data files, and mutable session state on `GameInstance`, Actors and components — avoid writing transient state back to source JSON.

- `Global.Data.GetClassData(path)` returns the shared session definition; see [Class definitions and session lifetime](<../Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#class-definitions-and-session-lifetime>).
- Construct General Data Attribute Sets with `Source.Configs.GeneralDataTypes.Create`, using type keys from `Enums.GeneralDataKey` and member keys from `Enums.GeneralData.<TypeName>` (e.g. `Enums.GeneralData.Item`). The editor resolves these from live data and regenerates their Lua modules alongside `Enums.Animation` and `Enums.Particle` on save; see [General Data and Text Config](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data and Text Config.md>).

### Static Actor display data

`Global.Data.GetActorPreviewData(classPath, classVarChanges?)` returns `Global.Data.ActorPreviewData` (or `nil` for an empty path; invalid paths and non-`Engine.Actor` classes raise an error):

- **Resolution**: Merges inherited Blueprint and Script Mixin defaults, then applies declared display and condition overrides using typed conversion. Unknown overrides fail; unrelated gameplay values and `BlueprintOnly` overrides are skipped.
- **Returned record**: Contains texture and material paths, first-frame `rect`, `translation`, rotation (degrees), `scale`, `origin`, `visible`, `materialParameters`, condition fields and optional recursive `child` with `childOffset` (from declarative `childActorComp`; cycles raise an error). Every call returns independent copies of tables and mutable `sf` vectors/rectangles so shared templates cannot be mutated.
- **No gameplay side effects**: Extraction neither constructs gameplay Actors, instantiates graphs, loads textures, runs component/lifecycle callbacks nor initialises combat state. Call `Global.Data.ClearActorPreviewCache()` to discard cached class display templates without affecting shared class definitions (clearing the floor-preview cache calls it automatically).

### Players

- **Party storage and order**: `GameInstance` keeps ordered keys in `_playerKeys` and objects in `_players`, keyed by the non-empty, unique Player General Data key (`Player.ID`). `getPlayers()` returns the live dictionary; `getPlayerKeys()` returns the live order (its first key is the primary player returned by `getPlayer()`). `getPlayerByIndex()` resolves 0-based indices; `setPlayer(playerKey)` and `setPlayerByClass(playerClass)` promote an existing member to primary; `addPlayerByClass(playerClass, mapPath, position)` appends a member with its required map/cell; `removePlayerByClass` also removes that key's stored map.
- **Player serialisation**: Saves mirror `playerKeys` and `players` (every key must match exactly one entry with the same restored `Player.ID`), plus a required `customName` string alongside `attr` (`""` selects the localised General Data default; non-empty values must be pre-trimmed and satisfy [Source.MapActors.Player](<../Source Classes/Player.md>)).
- **Persisted attributes and inventory**: Each Player saves finite numeric Attribute Set Base values under `attr` via `getNumericAttributeBases()` (matching the generated `int`/`float` schema; missing keys in older saves keep the initial Base, derived Current values are not saved, and non-numeric fields rebuild from Player General Data), along with inventory/equipment counts, equipped IDs and State stacks.
- **Load rebuild order**: Loading restores Base values first, then Item abilities, equipment Effects and State Effects without running initial-equipment or member graphs. Handles, derived Current values, transient Effects, ability specs and tags are not saved — custom persistent additions require their own record and rebuild logic.

### Game variables

Initial game variables load from generated `Scripts/Source/Configs/GameVariables.lua` (save edits in the [Game Variable Manager](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data and Text Config.md#game-variable-manager>) before launching). List and dictionary initial values are ordinary Lua tables rather than Standard containers, and empty tables round-tripped through JSON may not preserve array-vs-object shape.

- **New game vs. save load**: `GameInstance:init` deep-copies the generated map so each new game starts independently (Default Gameplay declares `MTExample = 0` and `ShopPrice = 20`; runtime code can add dynamic keys, though only editor-declared keys appear in `InstVar` selectors). Loading a save replaces the variable table wholesale — generated initial values apply to new games only, and adding, removing or retyping a declaration does not migrate existing saves (retyping resets only the project initial value).
- **Monitored fields**: Snapshots capture logical values while `deepcopy` strips monitor proxies and subscriptions so `ConditionalActor` listeners stay local to the live session. On load, `onCreate` resubscribes and recomputes visibility without extra save fields.

### Map Actor identity

- **Map tags**: Map JSON `tag` becomes the Actor's map-persistence tag read by `Actor:getMapTag()` — `GameMap:getActorByTag` and `GameInstance` persistence use only this tag, keeping `Actor.tag` independent. Untagged Actors are not persisted, and map paths normalise via `Global.Utils.MapPath.Normalise`.
- **Added and destroyed pairs**: Runtime-spawned Actors that must survive map rebuilds save as added-Actor records with generated placement tags; destroying them writes a destroyed record that suppresses the addition (`Reborn` enemies use this same mechanism instead of reusing the original tag).
- **Composite-world tags**: World runtime tags use `<child-file-stem>.runtime_default_<N>` inside placements and `<world-directory>.runtime_default_<N>` in holes; all tags stay reserved for the world's lifetime and conflicts raise errors. Editor tags are unique world-wide and survive map renames.
- **Typed overrides**: Map `BPClassVarChanged` and persisted `classVarChanges` store values only for declared class fields resolved from metadata, Script Mixins and `attrDefs`. Unknown names or schema mismatches fail loading; enum overrides store scalar values, and vectors/records apply typed conversion.

### Composite-world persistence

- **Manifest identity**: The primary player's `map` entry stores the `_world.json` manifest path even when entry targeted a child map. Player, added, moved and destroyed records use manifest identity, world coordinates and global tags; conflicting added or moved records fail loading.
- **Restoring Actors**: Added Actors spawn at `actorPositions[tag]` if present (otherwise their original position); destroyed tags are skipped. Placement Actors restore with their child without distant child I/O, while hole Actors can restore immediately.
- **Moved roots (`worldMovedActors`)**: Required in a save whenever any player's stored map is a world manifest. Tracks authored roots that left their definition child (identity, owner, layer overrides, world position), rebuilding them only at their current owner; returning home or destroying removes the record. Moved snapshots preserve reconstruction identity, `classVarChanges`, layer and position, but not arbitrary Lua fields or timer progress (persist those separately or recover elapsed time in `onWorldWake`).
- **Suppression and terrain**: Destroying a tag removes its moved record and suppresses authored, added, resident and in-progress instances without loading absent children (tags stay reserved; invalid records/collisions fail). Terrain edits store child paths and local coordinates, applying when that child builds and updating only its live layer (holes cannot own terrain edits).

## Saves

The Default Gameplay save schema is version `1` (numeric `1`). `SaveCodec` accepts only the current structure and version, rejecting incompatible saves without migration. Schema versions are independent of application versions and the packaging dev checkbox: use `vN-dev` while developing a breaking format change and freeze it as `vN` before release.

> **Note:** [Live Debug](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#live-debug>) never edits project files or save schemas, though saving during a debug session persists gameplay state altered by live edits.

### Save data collections

- **`telepoints`**: Maps normalised map paths (manifest paths + world coordinates for worlds) to ordered `{ position = {x, y}, tag = "raw tag" }` records (`sf.Vector2u` at runtime; unlocalised string tags). `GameInstance:recordTelepoint(mapPath, position, tag)` preserves the first entry per `(map, position)`; `getTelepoints(mapPath)` returns records, `getVisitedMapPaths()` returns sorted paths (copy), and `getTelepointsForMap(key)` matches ignoring extensions (copy).
- **`triggeredTutorials`**: Unique tutorial keys in display-start order (`list<string>` at runtime, JSON array in saves preserving `[]`). Loading validates the native reader's `n` count against array elements and rejects holes or invalid keys. `hasTriggeredTutorial(key)` queries history and `recordTriggeredTutorial(key)` appends once when mask contraction starts (not while queued). Legacy v1 saves missing this field load as empty.
- **`shops` record format**: Shared array of `[mapPath, mapTag]` pairs using normalised map/manifest paths and `Actor:getMapTag()`. Entries are unique by full pair in first-visit order, saving empty as `[]` (legacy v1 saves missing `shops` load empty).
- **`shops` API and events**: `GameInstance:getShops()` returns a copy; `recordShop(mapPath, tag)` adds a pair while `GameInstance.EnableShopRecord` is enabled (successful shop open records without requiring a purchase; see [Visited shops](<Windows Menus Input and Controls.md#visited-shops>)); `removeShop(mapPath, tag)` removes even when recording is disabled. Both return whether the list changed, publishing `Enums.EventKey.ShopRecordsChanged` (`Source.Configs.ShopRecordsChangePayload`, `{ instance = self }`) only on real changes so subscribers can match `instance`. Revisiting a removed shop can record it again.
- **`map`**: Object keyed by `playerKeys` where every member has one non-empty normalised map path (extra keys fail loading). `GameInstance:getCurrentMapPath()` returns the primary player's map or `nil`; `applyMapInfo` writes it; `restoreFromData(data)` applies a validated save.

### Save format, encryption and UI contract

- **Format selection (`SAVE_AS_LDC`)**: `false` (default) writes plain `.json`; `true` writes compressed, obfuscated binary `.ldc`. **Encrypt save contents** sets the native default for C++ Source packages. Any project (including Standalone) can override it by setting `SAVE_AS_LDC = true` or `false` at the top of `Scripts/Entry.lua` before all `require` calls; `Source.Save` captures the setting on first load and ignores later writes.
- **LDC codec and encryption**: `Source.Save` reads and writes through `Engine.saveData` and `Engine.loadData`, decoding `.ldc` directly into runtime data without intermediate JSON (legacy compressed-JSON `.ldc` saves are unsupported). Save encryption is independent of project JSON encryption, though Pack Options groups both under **Encrypt game data**.
- **Loading and previews**: `GetSavePath(slot)` returns the 1-based slot path for the active format. Previews load asynchronously without constructing gameplay objects; confirming a load invokes `Save.LoadGame(filePath)`.
- **Save/Load window**: `open` accepts `initialMode` as `Enums.SaveLoadMode.LOAD` (`"load"`, default) or `.SAVE` (`"save"`; load-only windows stay in load mode). `onClose(reason)` receives `Enums.SaveLoadCloseReason.CANCEL` (`"cancel"`), `.SAVED` (`"saved"`) or `.LOADED` (`"loaded"`) after closing. The window shows loading, empty and failed states, preselects the most recently modified slot (or slot 1 when none exists), and focuses it after the open animation. New screenshots preserve aspect ratio up to `224 × 168` pixels (larger existing screenshots stay readable).

> **Important:** Changing `SAVE_AS_LDC` does not rename or migrate existing slots — choose the format before release or write a migration. Save-version upgrades, atomic writes, backups, cloud synchronisation and custom tuple-key record formats are project responsibilities.

## Native containers at data boundaries

Convert Standard `list`, `tuple` and `dict` values to ordinary Lua tables before writing JSON or LDC:

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")
Engine.saveData("slot.ldc", payload:toTable())
```

Decoding either format produces plain Lua tables: arrays carry logical length in `n`, root `null` and `null` array slots become `nil`, and `null` object fields keep `cjson.null`. See [Ludork Lua Advanced](<../../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md>) for tuple-key strings, `cjson.null` handling and record-array reconstruction; never persist an internal tuple hash.

documents.content:
# Game Settings Reference

**Game Config** edits the supported keys in the `Main` section of the [platform game configuration](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>). This page documents every key, default, quality preset and platform display constraint used by Default Gameplay.

## Supported keys

| Key | Type | Default and meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | Game catalogue key (see [Game Localisation Workflow](<../../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>)). |
| `scale` | float | Display-scale preference; default `0` selects Fullscreen on configurable displays. |
| `maxrenderscale` | float | Maximum internal render scale; default `2.0`. Unlimited (`0`) removes the cap. |
| `lightingrenderscale` | discrete float | Direct-light render scale: `0.5`, `0.75` or `1.0` (default `1.0`; invalid values fall back to `1.0`). |
| `framerate` | integer | Target frame rate; default `60`. Unlimited (`0`) removes the cap. |
| `antialiasinglevel` | non-negative integer | Requested SFML multisample anti-aliasing level; default `8`. |
| `verticalsync` | boolean | Enables or disables vertical synchronisation. |
| `musicon`, `soundon`, `voiceon` | boolean | Per-channel audio enable toggles. |
| `musicvolume`, `soundvolume`, `voicevolume` | float | Per-channel volume clamped to `0`–`100`. |

The editor preserves unknown sections and keys. Invalid values for supported keys fall back to safe defaults in their respective readers, though you should fix the source file rather than relying on fallbacks. Saving writes changed settings; new user configurations and missing keys default to the **High** quality preset (`2`, `60`, `8`, `1`) and `scale = 0` without overwriting existing values.

> **Note:** Only keys handled by your runtime readers take effect; adding custom keys to the configuration file requires matching runtime code.

Project and tooling flags live in `Main.proj` rather than mutable user preferences: `Cpp` selects C++ Source behaviour, `ffmpeg` enables video packaging, `IndividualWindow` stores the preferred editor launch mode, and `packaging.version` / `packaging.dev` configure releases (see [Release version and internal packages](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#release-version-and-internal-packages>)).

## Display scale, render limits and frame rate

- **Scale (`scale`)**: Applies immediately on configurable displays. Desktop windows and HarmonyOS tablets in free-window mode use positive values for fixed window sizes and `0` for fullscreen; other mobile displays and WebGL omit **Scale** (including Fullscreen), while **Render Limit** is available. A newly created config writes `scale = 0`, whereas a missing key uses `0` in memory only. Negative or non-finite values resolve to `1`. See [Display](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Scenes and System.md#display>) for runtime APIs.
- **Desktop and HarmonyOS 2-in-1 scale filtering**: Startup filters the positive presets (`1`, `1.25`, `1.5`, `1.75`, `2`, `3`, `4`) against the primary display work area, and opening Config rechecks the current display. Fullscreen (`0`) and fitting non-preset values stay available; an over-limit value clamps down to the highest fitting preset (or Fullscreen if none fits) and does not raise automatically on a larger display. A failed size query leaves choices and the current value unchanged.
- **HarmonyOS tablet free-window limits**: Free-window mode uses the smaller of the display's available area and the Stage maximum. That maximum is sampled at native host initialisation, when enabling free-window mode and on returning to the foreground — moving windows across displays while staying in the foreground does not resample it. HarmonyOS 2-in-1 follows ordinary desktop display queries.
- **Render Limit (`maxrenderscale`)**: Caps the internal Graphics canvas and dependent render targets immediately on all platforms without changing window dimensions, logical game size or `scale`. Measured in physical drawable pixels relative to logical game size (including Retina density); on macOS, `scale` controls window size in Cocoa points while Unlimited renders at full drawable resolution. Config offers `0.5`, `0.75`, `1`, `1.5`, `2`, `3`, `4` and Unlimited (`0`), preserves any other finite non-negative value, and resolves negative or non-finite values to `2`.
- **Lighting Render Scale (`lightingrenderscale`)**: Adjusts direct-light resolution starting on the next map frame without resizing the window or canvas; values below `1.0` smoothly upsample. Missing, non-finite or unsupported values resolve to `1.0`. See [Graphics](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Scenes and System.md#graphics>).
- **Frame Rate (`framerate`)**: Offers `30`, `60`, `90`, `120` and Unlimited (`0`). Unlimited disables active frame-rate capping while preserving **Vertical Sync**. Fixed updates step at `1/60` second when Unlimited, or `1/framerate` for positive frame rates.
- **Anti-aliasing (`antialiasinglevel`)**: Requests a multisample level (SFML selects the closest supported context; `0` disables anti-aliasing, and negative or out-of-range values fall back to the SFML default). Because anti-aliasing applies at context creation, changing it saves immediately and takes effect after display reinitialisation (normally on the next launch).

## Quality presets

Config derives the displayed **Quality Preset** from `(maxrenderscale, framerate, antialiasinglevel, lightingrenderscale)` in the order below:

| Preset | `(maxrenderscale, framerate, antialiasinglevel, lightingrenderscale)` |
|---|---|
| Low | `(0.75, 30, 0, 0.5)` |
| Medium | `(1, 60, 2, 0.75)` |
| High | `(2, 60, 8, 1)` |
| Extra High | `(3, 90, 8, 1)` |
| Original | `(0 (Unlimited), 120, 8, 1)` |

If the active values match no preset, Config appends and selects **Custom** (selecting Custom applies no changes); once values match a preset again, Config selects it and removes **Custom**. Presets are derived dynamically — no preset key is saved, and `scale` and `verticalsync` do not participate.

documents.title: Troubleshooting
documents.content:
# Troubleshooting

Use this guide to diagnose common project, Blueprint, launch, asset, localisation and packaging failures in Default Gameplay projects. For native C++ crashes, binding-generation failures or plug-in load errors, consult the corresponding Native C++ Development or Plug-in Development pages.

## The project will not open

Validate JSON syntax in `Main.proj` and every loaded file under `Data`. Confirm that all paths stay within the project root, and restore any missing project directories rather than opening a partial package.

## A Blueprint will not save

Save errors point to invalid parents, inheritance cycles, nodes, links, pins or defaults. Script Mixin Blueprints additionally require a valid relative `scriptPath`, a script returning a plain table and a matching `_meta.lua` file; see [Script Mixin Authoring Workflow](<../Script Mixins/Authoring Workflow.md>).

## The game will not start

Inspect the Console starting from the first reported error:

- **Build and export order**: **Play** checks **Construct** (when required) before **Export**. Export validation failures, plug-in errors and failing before-Run hooks all block launch.
- **Scripts and modules**: Verify generated UI and locale files, native modules, the [startup script](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#entry-and-module-order>), Core module load order and runtime protocol diagnostics.
- **Material cache failures**: If `SceneInit` halts during material preparation, inspect its first generation or cache error. The runtime cache lives under the game's user data directory; see [Runtime generation](<../../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#runtime-generation>).

## A node is missing

Verify that the metadata file is pure data, returns `_METADATA`, declares the member with `type = "function"` or `type = "event"`, and lives outside `Scripts/Mixins`. For C++ bindings, rebuild so bindgen regenerates metadata.

## An asset or data reference is broken

Use the reference tree to find the invalid key or path. See [Assets](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#assets>) for rename and path rules, and [Type structure](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data and Text Config.md#type-structure>) for typed General Data references.

## Localised text is missing

Confirm that language-file IDs, the active language and `LOC` format arguments match the project text. See [Game Localisation Workflow](<../../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>) for workbook and export configuration.

## Packaged behaviour differs

- **Runtime environment and paths**: Verify packaged assets, scripts, native modules, FFmpeg variant and the [writable game configuration location](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>). Never infer the platform from path separators; read the injected `PLATFORM` global instead.
- **Android packaging**: Requires a C++ Source project, a local Android Studio installation and its required tools. Packaging errors list missing prerequisites; see [Run, Debug and Package](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for expected paths and versions.
- **Android signing**: Confirm that the JKS or PKCS12 keystore path is absolute and readable, the key alias exists, and both passwords are correct. Fix stale saved values in the dialog and re-enter unsaved passwords. Failed runs publish neither unsigned intermediates nor partial APKs. Reuse the same signing key for all updates to an installed app.

documents.title: Consumables
documents.content:
# Consumables

Create collision-driven healing bottles and stat-boosting gems using Default Gameplay's Script Mixins. This workflow requires a Blueprint derived from `ConditionalActor` with collision enabled, a matching numeric field in the generated Player Attribute Set and a valid Audio configuration fallback.

## Configure a consumable Blueprint

1. Create a Blueprint derived from `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor.ConditionalActor`, enable collision and enable **Script Mixin**.
2. Attach `Consumables/Bottle.lua` (healing) or `Consumables/Gem.lua` (attribute boost).
3. Configure `HP_plus` for a healing bottle, or `ATTR_key` and `plus` for a gem.
4. Choose a pickup sound in `getSE`, or leave it at its default to use `Audio.getSE` from the Audio configuration.

On collision, the shared pickup flow locates the Player, applies an Instant Add Effect (`Bottle` modifies `HP`; `Gem` modifies the `int` or `float` Player attribute named by `ATTR_key`), records the pickup as destroyed and destroys the Actor.

## Default template examples

- **`BP_Bottle_200.json`**: Derives directly from `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor.ConditionalActor`, enables `scriptMixin`, attaches `Consumables/Bottle.lua`, enables collision, sets `HP_plus = 200` and assigns the potion texture.
- **`BP_Gem_1_1.json`**: Attaches `Consumables/Gem.lua`, sets `ATTR_key = "ATK"` and `plus = 1`, and assigns the gem texture.
- Both Blueprints keep `getSE` at its metadata default so runtime pickup resolves `Audio.getSE`.

> **Note:** These template mixins rely on their declared parent capabilities, metadata fields and General Data or configuration keys; adapt or replace them if your project uses a custom inventory or attribute model.

documents.title: Doors
documents.content:
# Doors

Create map doors that open with an inventory key or when a named game variable reaches a threshold. Both workflows build on `Source.MapActors.DoorBase.DoorBase` with a door sprite sheet and matching Item or Game Variable identifiers.

`DoorBase` inherits `tickable = false` and activates ticks only while opening or reversing. Once the opening animation finishes, `DoorBase` records its map-placement tag as destroyed (if non-empty) so rebuilt maps and loaded saves keep the door open.

## Key door

1. Create a shared base door Blueprint derived from `Source.MapActors.DoorBase.DoorBase` and configure its texture, source rectangle, collision and opening defaults.
2. Derive a colour-specific door Blueprint — for example, Default Gameplay's `BP_Door_Y.json` inherits `BP_Door_General` and sets `needKeyID = "KEY_Y"`.
3. In `onCollision`, return early if the door is already opening and check `MeetPlayer`.
4. Read `needKeyID`, call `GetItemCount` and verify the count is at least `1`.
5. On success, invoke the parent collision flow via `SUPER` and remove one key. Leave the failure branch unconnected or attach custom feedback.

The configured `needKeyID` must match both the Item General Data member and its pickup Blueprint (such as `KEY_Y` and `BP_Item_Key_Y.json`).

## Conditional door

Attach `Mixins/Doors/ConditionDoor.lua` to a `DoorBase` Blueprint to poll `openConditionName` against `openConditionVal`:

- Leaving `openConditionName` empty disables polling; naming an uninitialised variable treats its starting value as `0`. Reaching `openConditionVal` calls `openDoor`.
- `openConditionName` uses a numeric `InstVar` selector listing `int` and `float` entries from the Game Variable Manager, and `openConditionVal` uses `InstVarValue` to match that variable's numeric control. Default Gameplay provides `MTExample = 0` for testing this workflow.

> **Note:** Doors do not perform scene transfers — use `Teleporter` for map-to-map travel. Renaming a key or game variable requires updating every stored door reference manually.

documents.title: Enemies
documents.content:
# Enemies

Create an enemy whose physical Actor Blueprint and General Data combat statistics stay decoupled and independently reusable. Ensure the referenced Item Blueprint paths, special-effect IDs and animation keys exist before linking them.

## Create an enemy Blueprint and data record

1. Add a member to Enemy General Data with its combat stats, rewards, drops, special effects and animation key.
2. Create or derive an Enemy Blueprint from `Source.MapActors.Enemy` (or a compatible subclass) and set `ID` to that member key.
3. Configure movement, collision and presentation defaults on the Blueprint.
4. Implement custom defeat sequences in the Enemy Actor's `onDefeat` event or a subclass-granted Gameplay Ability. Enemy General Data has no member events, and fixed settlement waits for `onDefeat` to finish.

Place reusable combat algorithms in Gameplay Abilities, Gameplay Effects or shared Lua modules.

## Default template examples

- **`BP_Enemy_Slime.json`**: Derives from `Source.MapActors.Enemy` and sets `ID = "Slime"`, resolving `Slime` in `Data/General/Enemy.json`. The Blueprint owns physical and visual defaults (texture, source rectangle, material speed), while General Data owns `MAXHP`, `ATK`, `DEF`, `EXP`, `GOLD`, `drops`, `special` and `ANIMATION_KEY`.
- **Drops and defeat shatter**: Map `drops` keys to Item Blueprint paths with `sf.Vector2i` cell offsets (see [Enemies](<../Actors Enemies Items and Equipment.md#enemies>) for drop activation, persistence and settlement order). Toggle the project-wide [enemy-defeat shatter effect](<../Resources Audio Video and Effects.md#shaders-fog-and-transitions>) in [System Config → Gameplay](<../../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#system-config>).
- **Reborn replacement (`GhostSoldier`)**: Sets `special.Reborn = "Data.Blueprints.Enemies.BP_Enemy_Skeleton_01"`. On defeat, settlement spawns the replacement on the same cell and layer with a fresh map-placement tag so it persists across map rebuilds and saves.

> **Important:** Unknown enemy IDs and missing referenced records raise explicit runtime errors; the engine never synthesises fallback combat definitions.

documents.title: Equipment and Items
documents.path: docs/en_GB/Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Recipes/Equipment and Items.md
documents.content:
# Equipment and Items

Create Item and Equipment General Data entries alongside `Source.MapActors.Item` and `Source.MapActors.Equip` Blueprints with stable inventory IDs, matching Class slots and focused member graphs.

## Author items and equipment

- **Item activation and stacking**: Set `usable` on Item General Data to enable inventory use, and `cost` to display stack counts. The `onUse` graph decides whether to consume the item.
- **Item member graphs**: Put inventory activation logic in `onUse` and enemy drop logic in `onDrop` (see [Items](<../Actors Enemies Items and Equipment.md#items>) for `GameplayEventData.target` and `self` pin rules).
- **Equipment slots and stats**: Match each Equip record's `slot` to the active Class slot dictionary. Put static stat bonuses in `attrPlus` and reserve `onEquip` / `onUnequip` graphs for custom side effects.
- **Icons**: Store item and equipment icons under `Assets/Icons` and select them through the resource picker.

## Default template examples

- **Equipment (`BP_Equip_Sword_A.json`)**: Derives from `Source.MapActors.Equip` and sets `ID = "Sword_A"` to link its Equip record. See [Equipment](<../Actors Enemies Items and Equipment.md#equipment>) for the execution order of `attrPlus`, `onEquip` and `onUnequip`.
- **Item (`BP_Item_Key_Y.json`)**: Derives from `Source.MapActors.Item` and sets `ID = "KEY_Y"`, matching both the Item database record and the yellow door's `needKeyID`.
- **Ability ownership and save loading**: Owning an item grants its `onUse` ability and removing the last copy revokes it; `Player:activateItem` targets that Player. [Save loading](<../Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#players>) restores saved abilities and Effects without replaying `onUse`, `onDrop`, `onEquip` or `onUnequip` graphs.

> **Important:** Renaming a General Data member does not update stored Blueprint or map references automatically. Class slot mismatches and unknown record IDs raise explicit data errors.

documents.title: Overview
documents.content:
# Node Functions Overview

This chapter lists the Lua Blueprint node libraries under `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/`, with their inputs, outputs, execution semantics and editor metadata.

## Modules

| Module | Responsibility | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `GlobalFunctions.Container` | Loop constructs and dictionary and list operations available as Blueprint nodes. | [Container.md](<Container.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.GameMap` | Actor lookup nodes. | [GameMap.md](<GameMap.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Math` | Scalar, vector, rectangle, angle, random and operator nodes. | [Math.md](<Math.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Mota` | Monster handbook, region and floor-transport nodes. | [Mota.md](<Mota.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Movement` | Nodes that toggle movement, assign a movement route and start automatic pathing. | [Movement.md](<Movement.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Player` | Nodes that read and change Player state, inventory and equipment. | [Player.md](<Player.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Save` | Save, load and save-path nodes. | [Save.md](<Save.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Scene` | Map transfer, dialogue, window, camera, terrain and persistence-record nodes. | [Scene.md](<Scene.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Gameplay` | Nodes that read a gameplay event context and apply attributes, States and events. | [Gameplay.md](<Gameplay.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.String` | Conversion, search, case and substring nodes for string values. | [String.md](<String.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Audio` | Nodes editing the shared `SoundFilter` and `MusicFilter` and playing audio; playback applies filters only when `applyFilter` is `true`. | [Audio.md](<Audio.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Utils` | General-purpose nodes for flow control, local and game variables, attributes, animation helpers, the event bus and common functions. | [Utils.md](<Utils.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Video` | The `PlayVideo` node; its `mute`, `skipable` and `subtitleFileName` arguments are optional. | [Video.md](<Video.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Weather` | The `SetWeather` and `ClearWeather` nodes; the selector displays `NONE`, `RAIN`, `STORM` or `SNOW` and stores its `Enums.GlobalCore.WeatherType` value. | [Weather.md](<Weather.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.ScreenEffects` | Screen flash, tone and shake nodes, paired with stop or clear nodes. | [ScreenEffects.md](<ScreenEffects.md>) |
| `GlobalFunctions.Transition` | Freeze and transition-wait nodes returning `Engine.AsyncOperation`, shared by Blueprint execution and Lua `asyncio.await`. | [Transition.md](<Transition.md>) |

## Looking up a node

Choose a module by its purpose above, then look up the node's identifier. For example, the `+` node is `Math.ADD`.

The function tables on these pages use four columns:

- **`Function`** — the metadata identifier of the Blueprint node function.
- **`Parameters`** — ordered input pins as `name: type`, followed by `= value` when metadata declares a default, or `—` when the node takes no parameters.
- **`Returns`** — output pins as `name: type` (or bare `type` for unnamed return values), or `—` when the node produces no data output.
- **`Notes`** — execution flags (`Pure.`, `Latent.`, `Loop.`), named execution branches, editor metadata (drop-downs, path pickers, selectors, display names) and behaviour summaries. Non-pure, non-latent, non-loop nodes use a single default execution output unless branches are listed. See [Execution declarations](<../Blueprint Scripting/Metadata Schema and Decorators.md#execution-declarations>) for execution rules.

## Relationship to the GlobalFunctions Lua API

The native `GlobalFunctions` root exposes Lua APIs in `Components`, `Manager`, `NodeGraph` and `UI`; its empty metadata declares no Blueprint nodes. See [GlobalFunctions Lua API](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalFunctions.md>).

The node libraries here load separately, for example `require("GlobalFunctions.Math")`, and are not members of that root table. Their loading and dependency rules are covered in [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#entry-and-module-order>).

documents.title: Container
documents.content:
# GlobalFunctions.Container

`GlobalFunctions.Container` provides Blueprint loop constructs alongside dictionary and list creation, lookup, mutation and table-conversion nodes.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Container_meta.lua`

## Container

### Functions and events

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ForLoop` | `firstIndex: int = 0`, `lastIndex: int = 0`, `step: int = 1` | `index: int` | Loop (`ForLoop`). Branches: `LoopBody` (`__loop_body__`), `Completed` (`__loop_completed__`). |
| `ForEach` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]` | `element: any`, `index: int` | Loop (`ForEach`). Branches: `LoopBody` (`__loop_body__`), `Completed` (`__loop_completed__`). |
| `CreateDict` | — | `value: any` | Pure. Creates an empty dictionary. |
| `DictGet` | `dict_: any`, `key: any` | `value: any` | Pure. Reads the value stored at `key`. |
| `DictAdd` | `dict_: any`, `key: any`, `value: any` | — | Inserts or updates `key` with `value`. |
| `DictRemove` | `dict_: any`, `key: any` | — | Removes `key` from the dictionary. |
| `DictClear` | `dict_: any` | — | Removes all entries from the dictionary. |
| `DictContains` | `dict_: any`, `key: any` | `value: bool` | Pure. Returns whether `key` exists in the dictionary. |
| `TableToDict` | `table_: any` | `value: _G.dict` | Pure. Converts a Lua table to `_G.dict`. |
| `DictToTable` | `dict_: _G.dict` | `value: any` | Pure. Converts a `_G.dict` to a Lua table. |
| `CreateList` | — | `value: any[]` | Pure. Creates an empty list. |
| `ListGet` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list, _G.tuple]`, `index: int = 0` | `value: any` | Pure. Reads the element at `index`. |
| `ListAppend` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]`, `value: any` | — | Appends `value` to the end of the list. |
| `ListExtend` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]`, `values: Union[any[], _G.list, _G.tuple]` | — | Appends all elements from `values` to the list. |
| `ListRemove` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]`, `index: int = 0` | — | Removes the element at `index`. |
| `ListFind` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]`, `value: any` | `index: int` | Pure. Finds the index of `value` in the list. |
| `ListClear` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]` | — | Removes all elements from the list. |
| `ListContains` | `list_: Union[any[], _G.list]`, `value: any` | `value: bool` | Pure. Returns whether `value` is present in the list. |
| `TableToList` | `table_: any[]` | `value: _G.list` | Pure. Converts a Lua table to `_G.list`. |
| `ListToTable` | `list_: _G.list` | `value: any[]` | Pure. Converts a `_G.list` to a Lua table. |

documents.content:
# GlobalFunctions.Math

`GlobalFunctions.Math` provides pure scalar, vector, rectangle, angle, random and operator Blueprint nodes, together with compound-assignment execution nodes. For scalar math behaviour, see [Math extensions](<../../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md#math-extensions>).

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Math_meta.lua`

## Math

### Functions and events

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
