# GlobalFunctions.Movement

`GlobalFunctions.Movement` provides Blueprint nodes that toggle Actor movement, assign explicit movement routes and start automatic pathfinding.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Movement_meta.lua`

Route and pathfinding functions return `Engine.AsyncOperation`. They emit `Enums.MovementLatentOutput.STARTED` (`0`) and complete with `FINISHED` (`1`), matching the Blueprint `Started` / `Finished` branches. Route replacement and cancellation follow [Actor.setRoute](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Gameplay Types.md#routes-and-operation-lifetime>).

## Movement

### Functions and events

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SetMoveEnabledByTag` | `tag: string`, `enabled: bool = true` | — | Enables or disables movement on the Actor matching `tag`. |

| `SetAutoPathToDestination` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `destination: sf.Vector2i = sf.Vector2i(0, 0)` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branches: `Started` (`0`), `Finished` (`1`). Pathfinds `actor` to `destination`. |
| `SetAutoPathToDestinationByTag` | `tag: string`, `destination: sf.Vector2i = sf.Vector2i(0, 0)` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branches: `Started` (`0`), `Finished` (`1`). Pathfinds the Actor matching `tag` to `destination`. |

# GlobalFunctions.Scene

`GlobalFunctions.Scene` provides Blueprint nodes for map transfers, timers, tutorials, dialogue and shop windows, camera control, terrain editing, dynamic Actor spawning and persistence records.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Scene_meta.lua`

## Scene

### Functions and events

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GotoMap` | `mapPath: string = ""`, `blockTransition: bool = false`, `position: sf.Vector2i` | — | Transfers to `position` on `mapPath`. `Transfer` metadata links `position` to `mapPath`. |
| `GameOver` | — | — | Triggers the Game Over sequence. |
| `AddTimer` | `interval: float`, `blocking: bool = false` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `TimeUp` (`true`). Waits for `interval` seconds. |
| `ShowEnemyBook` | — | — | Opens the monster handbook window when permitted. |
| `ShowTutorial` | `key: string` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `Finished` (`true`). Displays the configured tutorial for `key`. |
| `ShowMessageByTag` | `name: string`, `message: string`, `refActorTag: string = ""` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `FinishedDialogue` (`true`). Displays a dialogue message positioned relative to the Actor matching `refActorTag`. |

| `ShowVoiceMessage` | `name: string`, `message: string`, `voiceFileName: string`, `refActor: Engine.Actor`, `minDistance: float = 64` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `FinishedDialogue` (`true`). Path (`voiceFileName`): `/Game/Assets/Voices`. |

| `ShowRefSelection` | `name: string = ""`, `options: string[] = {}`, `refActor: Engine.Actor`, `allowCancel: bool = true` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branches: `Selected0` (`0`), `Selected1` (`1`), `Selected2` (`2`), `Selected3` (`3`), `Cancelled` (`-1`). |
| `LockCamera` | — | — | Locks the scene camera. |
| `UnlockCamera` | — | — | Unlocks the scene camera. |

| `CreateActorFromBPPath` | `bpPath: string = ""`, `layerName: string = "default"`, `position: sf.Vector2i`, `tag: string = ""`, `emitCreateEvent: bool = true` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | Blueprint class picker on `bpPath` (`BlueprintClassVars`). Spawns an Actor on `layerName`. |
| `CreateActorFromBPPathWithDefaults` | `bpPath: string = ""`, `defaults: any = {}`, `layerName: string = "default"`, `position: sf.Vector2i`, `tag: string = ""`, `emitCreateEvent: bool = true` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | Blueprint class picker on `bpPath` (`BlueprintClassVars`). Spawns an Actor with overridden defaults. |
| `DestroyTerrain` | `layerName: string`, `position: sf.Vector2i`, `tileID: any` | — | Destroys a terrain tile on `layerName` at `position`. |
| `DestroyTerrainList` | `layerName: string`, `positions: sf.Vector2i[] = {}`, `tileID: any` | — | Destroys terrain tiles on `layerName` at each position in `positions`. |

| `RecordAddedActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records `actor` as added in map persistence. |
| `SelfRecordAdded` | — | — | Records the current graph owner Actor as added in map persistence. |
| `RecordActorPosition` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records `actor`'s current position in map persistence. |
| `SelfRecordActorPosition` | — | — | Records the current graph owner Actor's position in map persistence. |
| `RecordDestroyedActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records `actor` as destroyed in map persistence without destroying it. |
| `SelfRecordDestroyed` | — | — | Records the current graph owner Actor as destroyed in map persistence. |
| `RecordAndDestroyActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records `actor` as destroyed and destroys it. |
| `SelfRecordAndDestroy` | — | — | Records the current graph owner Actor as destroyed and destroys it. |
| `OpenPlayerName` | — | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `Closed` (`true`). Opens the player rename window. |
| `OpenShop` | `items: string[] = {}`, `canSell: bool = true`, `actor: Engine.Actor = nil` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `Closed` (`true`). Opens an item shop window. |
| `OpenAttrShop` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `shopName: string = ""`, `shopDescription: string = ""`, `abilities: any = {}`, `price: any = 0`, `priceIncrement: int = 1`, `moneyName: string = "GOLD"` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `Closed` (`true`). Opens an attribute shop window for `actor`. |
| `OpenAttrShopByTag` | `actorTag: string = ""`, `shopName: string = ""`, `shopDescription: string = ""`, `abilities: any = {}`, `price: any = 0`, `priceIncrement: int = 1`, `moneyName: string = "GOLD"` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `Closed` (`true`). Opens an attribute shop window for the Actor matching `actorTag`. |

### Lua waiting and results

Latent functions return `Engine.AsyncOperation`; see [Lua asynchronous tasks](<../../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md>) for sequential waiting. Tutorials, messages, timers and window-close operations complete with `true`. Selections return a zero-based index or `-1` when the player cancels; that cancellation follows the Blueprint `Cancelled` output rather than cancelling the operation.

Messages and windows complete after their closing animation. A new message or selection cancels the previous dialogue operation; reopening a shop replaces its operation, whereas repeated requests made while the player-name window is open share one operation. Voice playback stops when its dialogue completes or is cancelled. Scene and map cleanup follows [SceneMap](<../Source Classes/SceneMap.md#script-operations-and-lifetime>).

### Shop Actors

`OpenShop(items, canSell, actor?)` uses its optional Actor to identify a shop visit. When omitted in a Blueprint, it uses the current graph owner if that owner is an Actor. Direct Lua callers supply the shop Actor as the third argument to record the opening. `OpenAttrShop` uses its `actor` argument, and `OpenAttrShopByTag` resolves that Actor on the current map. An Actor without a map identity does not create a record. These nodes complete with `Closed`; see [Visited shops](<../Default Gameplay/Windows Menus Input and Controls.md#visited-shops>) for recording and remote-access behaviour.

### GotoMap world destinations

`GotoMap` accepts ordinary maps, world manifests and placed children. Manifest positions are world coordinates, and child positions are local. `GotoMap` fails on unplaced children, invalid data and out-of-range positions. World entry waits for a complete target viewport. `blockTransition` skips only the visual mask, not the readiness checks.

### ShowEnemyBook

`ShowEnemyBook()` opens the current-map monster handbook when the player owns it and the scene allows an overlay to open.

### Tutorials

`ShowTutorial(key)` displays the configured guide and completes with `true` after confirmation. Pending requests for the same key share an operation, even if the key has already been recorded; otherwise, recorded keys complete immediately. Different keys queue in order, and unknown keys raise an error.

When a request reaches the front of the queue, empty localised text (`""`) skips presentation and recording and completes through `Finished`. Recording rules are described under [Saves](<../Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>).

Blueprints choose tutorial keys and their order; see [Map introduction](<../Default Gameplay/Windows Menus Input and Controls.md#map-introduction>) for the `Map_01` configuration.

### OpenPlayerName

`OpenPlayerName()` opens the rename window of the primary Player. `Closed` resumes after the closing animation, whether the rename is confirmed or cancelled.

# GlobalFunctions.Gameplay

`GlobalFunctions.Gameplay` provides Blueprint nodes for reading a General Data gameplay event context and modifying Battler attributes, States, Effects and gameplay events.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Gameplay_meta.lua`

## Gameplay

### Functions

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetContext` | — | `context: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | Pure. Returns the current gameplay event context. |
| `GetSource` | — | `source: any` | Pure. Returns the event context's instigator/source. |
| `GetTarget` | — | `target: any` | Pure. Returns the event context's target. |
| `GetEventTag` | — | `eventTag: string` | Pure. Returns the active gameplay event tag. |
| `GetPayload` | — | `payload: any` | Pure. Returns the event context's payload table. |
| `HasTag` | `target: Source.Battler`, `tag: string` | `value: bool` | Pure. Checks whether `target` has the specified gameplay tag. |
| `GetNumericAttribute` | `target: Source.Battler`, `attribute: string` | `value: any` | Pure. Dynamic numeric pin. Reads a numeric attribute from `target`. |
| `SetNumericAttributeBase` | `target: Source.Battler`, `attribute: string`, `value: any` | — | Dynamic numeric pin. Writes the attribute's Base value on `target`. |
| `ApplyAttributeDelta` | `target: Source.Battler`, `attribute: string`, `magnitude: any` | — | Dynamic numeric pin. Applies an Instant Add modifier to `target`. |
| `ApplyState` | `target: Source.Battler`, `stateID: string`, `stacks: int = 1` | `handle: int` | `Enums.GeneralData.State` string enum selector. Applies or stacks a State on `target`. |
| `RemoveState` | `target: Source.Battler`, `stateID: string` | — | Execution branches: `Success`, `Failed`. `Enums.GeneralData.State` string enum selector. |
| `ReduceState` | `target: Source.Battler`, `stateID: string`, `stacks: int = 1` | — | Execution branches: `Success`, `Failed`. `Enums.GeneralData.State` string enum selector. |
| `RemovePlayerState` | `stateID: string` | — | `Enums.GeneralData.State` string enum selector. Removes the State from the context's target. |
| `ReducePlayerState` | `stateID: string`, `stacks: int = 1` | — | `Enums.GeneralData.State` string enum selector. Reduces the State stacks on the context's target. |
| `SendEvent` | `target: Source.Battler`, `eventTag: string`, `payload: any = {}` | `results: any` | Sends a synchronous gameplay event to `target`. |
| `ApplyEffect` | `target: Source.Battler`, `effect: any`, `stacks: int = 1`, `sourceKey: any` | `handle: int` | Applies a `GlobalCore.GameplayEffect` to `target`. |

The context accessors and the context-bound mutation nodes require a General Data graph owned by `GameplayEventData`. Using them in an ordinary Actor graph is an error. `RemovePlayerState` and `ReducePlayerState` act on that context's target and use a single execution output when no State exists.

Dynamic attribute pins are typed `any`, but the Ability System requires a finite number of the selected schema type. `SetNumericAttributeBase` writes Base; `ApplyAttributeDelta` applies an Instant Add modifier.

`SendEvent` runs synchronously, preserves the instigator and targets the supplied Battler. `ApplyEffect` accepts a `GameplayEffect`; Instant Effects return no persistent handle and cannot grant tags or abilities.

# GlobalFunctions.Audio

`GlobalFunctions.Audio` provides Blueprint nodes for sound and music playback, channel audio effects and filter configuration. `SoundFilter` and `MusicFilter` hold the shared filters edited by `EditSoundFilter` and `EditMusicFilter`; playback applies them only when `applyFilter` is `true`.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Audio_meta.lua`

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EditSoundFilter` | `attr: string`, `value: any` | — | Sets a field on the shared `SoundFilter`. `attr` drop-down: sound filter attributes (listed below). |
| `EditMusicFilter` | `attr: string`, `value: any` | — | Sets a field on the shared `MusicFilter`. `attr` drop-down: music filter attributes (listed below). |
| `SetEffect` | `audioType: string`, `effect: string` | — | Applies an effect preset to an audio channel. `audioType` drop-down: `Sound`, `Voice`, `Music`. `effect` drop-down: `nil`, `Echo`, `Distortion`, `Underwater`, `BehindWall`. |
| `PlaySound` | `soundFileName: string`, `applyFilter: bool = false` | — | Plays a sound effect, applying `SoundFilter` when `applyFilter` is `true`. Path (`soundFileName`): `/Game/Assets/Sounds`. |
| `PlayMusic` | `musicFileName: string`, `applyFilter: bool = false` | — | Plays background music on the active Scene, applying `MusicFilter` when `applyFilter` is `true`. Path (`musicFileName`): `/Game/Assets/Musics`. |
| `SetBgmFilter` | `attr: string`, `value: any` | — | Updates a filter property on the active `SceneMap` BGM. `attr` drop-down: music filter attributes (listed below). |
| `SetBgsFilter` | `attr: string`, `value: any` | — | Updates a filter property on the active `SceneMap` BGS. `attr` drop-down: sound filter attributes (listed below). |

Filter `attr` drop-down keys:

- **Sound and BGS filters** (`EditSoundFilter`, `SetBgsFilter`): `loop`, `offset`, `pitch`, `pan`, `volume`, `spatial`, `position`, `direction`, `cone`, `velocity`, `dopplerFactor`, `directionalAttenuationFactor`, `relativeToListener`, `minDistance`, `maxDistance`, `minGain`, `maxGain`, `attenuation`.
- **Music and BGM filters** (`EditMusicFilter`, `SetBgmFilter`): all sound filter keys above plus `loopPoint`.

# GlobalFunctions.Utils

`GlobalFunctions.Utils` provides general-purpose Blueprint nodes for flow control, local and game variables, party management, attributes, animations, the event bus and common functions.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Utils_meta.lua`

`RunCommonFunction` shares the caller's local context and graph owner, including nested calls. `SELF` returns that owner, which is also the default for unconnected instance-method receivers inside the Common Function.

`SUPER(obj, params)` calls the parent implementation of the current Blueprint event. See [Parent event calls](<../Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#parent-event-calls>) for inheritance, parameter-array and `nil` fallback rules.

## Utils

### Functions and events

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IF` | `condition: bool = false` | `int` | Execution branches: `TRUE` (`0`), `FALSE` (`1`). |
| `SetLocalValue` | `valueName: string`, `value: any` | — | Sets a node-local variable in the current graph context. |
| `GetLocalValue` | `valueName: string`, `default: any` | `value: any` | Pure. Reads a node-local variable, returning `default` if unset. |

| `GetGameVariableRef` | `valueName: string`, `default: any` | `value: any` | Pure. Returns a mutable reference to a game variable. `InstVar` on `valueName`; `InstVarValue` binds `default` to `valueName`. |
| `AddPlayerByClass` | `playerClass: string = ""`, `mapPath: string = ""`, `position: sf.Vector2i` | — | Blueprint class picker on `playerClass` (`BlueprintClassVars`); `Transfer` links `position` to `mapPath`. |
| `SetPlayerByClass` | `playerClass: string = ""` | — | Blueprint class picker on `playerClass` (`BlueprintClassVars`). Switches the primary Player. |

| `AddAnim` | `animName: string`, `position: sf.Vector2f = sf.Vector2f(0, 0)`, `rotation: float = 0`, `scale: sf.Vector2f = sf.Vector2f(1, 1)` | — | `Enums.Animation` selector. Spawns an animation at `position`. |
| `AddAnimOn` | `animName: string`, `actorTag: string`, `rotation: float = 0`, `scale: sf.Vector2f = sf.Vector2f(1, 1)` | — | `Enums.Animation` selector. Spawns an animation centred on the Actor matching `actorTag`. |

| `SUPER` | `obj: any`, `params: any[] = {}` | `value: bool` | Invokes the parent Blueprint event implementation on `obj`. |
| `SELF` | — | `value: any` | Pure. Returns the current graph owner. |
| `GetAttrRef` | `obj: any`, `attrName: string` | `value: any` | Pure. Returns a mutable reference to a component field or object attribute. |
| `GetAttr` | `obj: any`, `attrName: string` | `value: any` | Pure. Reads a component field or object attribute. |
| `SetAttr` | `obj: any`, `attrName: string`, `value: any` | — | Writes a component field or object attribute. |
| `GetScene` | — | `value: GlobalCore.SceneBase` | Pure. Returns the active Scene from `SceneManager`. |
| `IsValidValue` | `value: any` | `value: bool` | Pure. Returns `true` when `value` is not `nil`. |
| `ToShortNumber` | `value: any = 0` | `value: any` | Pure. Formats a number using compact short notation. |
| `RunCommonFunction` | `commonFunctionName: string = ""` | `any` | Common Function picker on `commonFunctionName` (`CommonFunctionVars`). |
| `RegisterEventBus` | `key: string`, `obj: any`, `functionName: string` | — | Registers an object method on the event bus under `key`. |
| `RegisterEventBusEvent` | `key: string`, `obj: any`, `eventName: string` | — | Registers a Blueprint event on the event bus under `key`. |
| `UnregisterEventBus` | `key: string` | `value: bool` | Unregisters all handlers for `key` from the event bus. |
| `UnregisterEventBusEvent` | `key: string`, `obj: any` | `value: bool` | Unregisters `obj`'s event handler for `key` from the event bus. |
| `TriggerEventBus` | `key: string`, `kwargs: any = {}` | — | Triggers all event-bus handlers registered under `key`. |
| `TriggerBlueprintEvent` | `obj: any`, `eventName: string` | — | Triggers the named Blueprint event on `obj`. |
| `BackToTitle` | — | — | Returns to the title Scene. |
| `Print` | `message: any = ""` | — | Logs `message` to the console output. |
| `EXEC` | `script: string = ""` | — | Executes a Lua script string. |
| `GetSelfAttr` | `attrName: string` | `value: any` | Pure. Reads a component field or attribute on the current graph owner. |
| `SetSelfAttr` | `attrName: string`, `value: any` | — | Writes a component field or attribute on the current graph owner. |
| `IfPlayerOverlaps` | — | `value: bool` | Pure. Returns whether the Player overlaps the current Actor. |
| `IfGameVar` | `varName: string = ""`, `op: string = "=="`, `value: any` | `bool` | Execution branches: `TRUE` (`true`), `FALSE` (`false`). `op` drop-down: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`. `InstVar` on `varName`; `InstVarValue` binds `value` to `varName`. |

`AddPlayerByClass` stores the new member's map and cell without changing the primary player. `SetPlayerByClass` moves that class to `playerKeys[1]`, rebinds Scene UI and loads the stored map.

`GetAttr` and a read through `GetAttrRef` both return the component field value when it is non-nil; otherwise they read the object's attribute. Both preserve `false`, `0` and empty strings, and both raise an error when no non-nil value exists. Reading an Actor's `tag` returns its string value, which can connect directly to the `refActorTag` input of dialogue nodes.

# GlobalFunctions.Weather

`GlobalFunctions.Weather` provides Blueprint nodes for activating and clearing scene weather effects.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/GlobalFunctions/Weather_meta.lua`

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SetWeather` | `weatherType: Enums.GlobalCore.WeatherType`, `power: int = 40`, `maxCount: int = 80` | — | Activates a weather effect. `Enums.GlobalCore.WeatherType` selector. |
| `ClearWeather` | — | — | Clears the active weather effect. |

The selector displays `NONE`, `RAIN`, `STORM` and `SNOW` from the generated `Enums.GlobalCore.WeatherType` module and stores their numeric values `0`, `1`, `2` and `3`. Lua callers pass the enum value directly:

```lua
local WeatherType = require("Enums.GlobalCore.WeatherType")
local Weather = require("GlobalFunctions.Weather")

Weather.SetWeather(WeatherType.STORM, 30, 50)
```

The node forwards the value to `GlobalCore.WeatherController.setWeather`; names and localised labels are not runtime arguments. Blueprint JSON stores the example above as `[2, 30, 50]`.

documents.title: Battler
documents.content:
# Source.Battler

`Battler` is the Lua gameplay base class of `Enemy` and `Player`. Each concrete subclass constructs a generated Attribute Set from General Data and owns an Ability System Component for attributes, abilities, effects and tags.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/Source/Battler_meta.lua`

## Runtime state

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | `GlobalCore.AttributeSet` | — | Live generated Attribute Set; concrete subclasses narrow this to Enemy or Player. |
| `_abilitySystemComponent` | `GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent` | — | Private owner of attributes, abilities, effects and tags. |

## Runtime API

Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.Battler`).

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `init` | `attributes: GlobalCore.AttributeSet` | — | Requires an Attribute Set and creates its Ability System Component. |
| `getAbilitySystemComponent` | — | `GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent` | Returns the live Ability System Component. |
| `getAttr` | `name: string`, `base?: bool = false` | `number` | Returns numeric Current, or Base when `base` is `true`. |
| `setAttr` | `name: string`, `value: number` | — | Sets numeric Base through the Ability System and recalculates Current. |
| `addAttr` | `name: string`, `delta: number` | — | Adds `delta` to numeric Base; negative values subtract. |
| `playAttackAnimationAt` | `scene`, `targetPosition` | `GlobalCore.Animation?` | Plays `attributes.ANIMATION_KEY` at the target and returns the animation, or `nil` when the key is empty. Callers can read its visual duration and time tags. |

Use `getAttr`, `setAttr` and `addAttr` for individual numeric attributes. `addAttr` reads Base, so active modifiers stay separate. These methods enforce native validation: unknown attributes, non-finite values and generated `int` or `float` schema mismatches fail. Read other fields directly from `attributes`, and use the Ability System for batch writes, persistence, Effects and listeners.

# Source.MapActors.DoorBase

`DoorBase` is a conditionally visible map Actor for animated doors, declaring collision, opening interval, gate sound and state properties alongside latent open and close methods.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/Source/MapActors/DoorBase_meta.lua`

## DoorBase

**Inherits:** `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor` (see [Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor](<ConditionalActor.md>) for inherited visibility conditions).

`openDoor()` and `closeDoor()` return `Engine.AsyncOperation`. Animation start emits `Enums.MovementLatentOutput.STARTED` (`0`); completion returns `FINISHED` (`1`), matching the Blueprint `Started` / `Finished` branches.

Repeated requests in the same direction share the pending operation; a request in the opposite direction cancels it. Opening an already-open door or closing an already-closed door completes immediately. Normal opening completes before the door destroys itself; other destruction cancels an unfinished operation.

### Properties

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collisionEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | — |
| `openInterval` | `float` | `0.05` | Frame interval for the door animation. |
| `gateSE` | `string` | `""` | Path: `/Game/Assets/Sounds`; config fallback: `Audio.gateSE`. |
| `opening` | `bool` | `false` | — |
| `closing` | `bool` | `false` | — |

### Functions and events

Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.MapActors.DoorBase`), which Blueprint nodes expose as the first target pin.

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openDoor` | — | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branches: `Started` (`0`), `Finished` (`1`). Opens the door and destroys it after normal completion. |
| `closeDoor` | — | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branches: `Started` (`0`), `Finished` (`1`). Closes the door. |
| `onTick` | `deltaTime: float` | — | Event. Default execution output. |

# Source.MapActors.Enemy

`Enemy` is a conditionally visible Battler Actor bound to an Enemy General Data entry. It declares a damage-text child component, animation flags and post-battle variable changes, and exposes the `onCollision` and `onDefeat` events.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/Source/MapActors/Enemy_meta.lua`

**Inherits:** `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor`, `Source.Battler` (see [Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor](<ConditionalActor.md>) for inherited visibility conditions).

The Blueprint editor synthesises a read-only `attributes` preview of `Source.Configs.GeneralDataTypes.EnemyAttributeSet`. The preview is not serialised into the Blueprint JSON.

## Properties

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` | `string` | `"FILL_IT_BY_YOURSELF"` | `Enums.GeneralData.Enemy` enum selector. |
| `childActorComp` | `Source.Components.ChildActorComponent` | Damage-text child | Component. |
| `collisionEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | — |
| `animatable` | `bool` | `true` | — |
| `animateWithoutMoving` | `bool` | `true` | — |
| `afterBattleVarChanges` | `Dict[string, Tuple[string, any]]` | `{}` | Numeric game-variable selector and fixed operator selector. |

The shared runtime setting `DefeatShatterEffectEnabled` is controlled by `enemyDefeatShatterEffectEnabled` in [Gameplay configuration](<../Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#shared-gameplay-configuration>). The `attributes` field holds the generated Enemy Attribute Set.

`Enemy` inherits the `Engine.Actor` default `tickable = false`.

## Functions and events

Events omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.MapActors.Enemy`).

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onCollision` | `other: Engine.Actor[]` | — | Event. Default execution output. |
| `onDefeat` | — | — | Event. Default execution output. |

`init(texture?, rect?, tag?)` constructs the Attribute Set, the Ability System, the Mota ability and the configured special Effects. Collision prevalidates combat and required settlement before committing counter damage. On a loss, the prepared Game Over Effect is applied after the animations.

After a win animation, the Actor Blueprint's `onDefeat` hook runs before mandatory destruction, Reborn/drops, rewards and States. These values come from the prepared snapshot, and `afterBattleVarChanges` is evaluated after the hook. Enemy General Data has no `onDefeat` member graph.

documents.title: Gameplay
documents.content:
# Source Gameplay API

`Source.Gameplay` provides the Default Gameplay Scene contract, abilities, Effects, combat rules, movement-hazard helpers and generated General Data Attribute Sets built on `GlobalCore`.

## GameplayScene

**Module:** `Source.Gameplay.GameplayScene`  
**Inherits:** `GlobalCore.SceneBase`

`SceneMap` implements this contract, and Actors reach it through their owning map. Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.Gameplay.GameplayScene`).

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getGameMap` | — | `Global.GameMap` | Returns the scene's loaded map. |
| `getGameInstance` | — | `Source.GameInstance` | Returns the game instance that owns variables and persistence state. |
| `recordAddedActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records an added Actor in persistence state. |
| `recordDestroyedActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records a destroyed Actor in persistence state. |
| `recordActorPosition` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `position` | — | Records the Actor's map position. |
| `requestFloorStep` | `teleporter`, `step: int` | `bool` | Accepts one adjacent-floor request; `step` must be `1` or `-1`. Arrival selects the nearest visible, surviving stair of the opposite direction. |
| `requestMapTransfer` | `teleporter`, `mapPath: string`, `position: sf.Vector2i`, `record?: bool = true` | `bool` | Accepts one transfer to the specified tile without searching for a stair; optionally records each endpoint on its own map. |
| `requestGameOver` | `player`, `delay: number` | — | Waits for a finite non-negative animation delay and navigates without applying damage or Effects. |

Combat and movement hazards require a `GameplayScene` before they change state. Unavailable or rejected Teleporter requests preserve movement and records. Game Over uses the longest remaining animation duration. Duplicate requests are ignored, and replacing the scene, map or player cancels pending navigation.

## GeneralDataGraphAbility

**Module:** `Source.Gameplay.GeneralDataGraphAbility`  
**Inherits:** `GlobalCore.GameplayAbility`

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generalType` | `string` | — | General Data type key. |
| `memberID` | `string` | — | General Data member identifier. |
| `graphEvent` | `string` | — | Member graph event name. |

Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.Gameplay.GeneralDataGraphAbility`).

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `init` | `generalType: string`, `memberID: string`, `graphEvent: string`, `triggerTags?` | — | Creates ability ID `GeneralData.<type>.<member>.<event>`. |
| `calculate` | `abilitySystem: GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent`, `eventData: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Returns `ExecutableGraph` with graph data or successful `NoGraph`. |
| `activate` | `abilitySystem: GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent`, `eventData: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Builds and synchronously executes the selected event; returns `GraphExecuted` or `NoGraph`. |

The graph parent and the `eventData` argument are the same `GameplayEventData`. Its payload receives the three fields above and, for State graphs, `activeEffect`. Execution uses `Engine.BPBase.ExecuteGraph`. General Data graphs have no Actor dispatch or inheritance, cannot be latent and propagate errors.

## Effects

**Module:** `Source.Gameplay.Effects`

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateInstantModifierSpec` | `effectID: string`, `attribute: string`, `operation`, `magnitude: number`, `eventData?: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `GlobalCore.GameplayEffectSpec` | Creates, without applying, one Instant modifier spec. |
| `ApplyInstantModifier` | `target`, `effectID: string`, `attribute: string`, `operation`, `magnitude: number`, `eventData?: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | — | Applies one Instant modifier. |
| `CreateEquipmentEffect` | `equipID: string`, `slot: string`, `attrPlus` | `GlobalCore.GameplayEffect` | Creates an Infinite equipment effect and an `Equipment.Slot.<slot>` tag. |
| `CreateStateEffect` | `stateID: string` | `GlobalCore.GameplayEffect` | Creates an Infinite state effect, tag and granted state abilities. |
| `CreateStateSpec` | `stateID: string`, `stacks?: int`, `eventData?: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `GlobalCore.GameplayEffectSpec` | Creates, without applying, a State spec with a positive stack count. |
| `ApplyState` | `target`, `stateID: string`, `stacks?: int`, `eventData?: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `int` | Applies or stacks the State effect and returns its handle. |
| `RemoveState` | `target`, `stateID: string` | `bool` | Removes the complete State effect. |
| `ReduceState` | `target`, `stateID: string`, `stacks?: int` | `bool` | Removes only the requested stacks when supported. |
| `ClearStates` | `target` | — | Removes every effect whose ID begins with `State.`. |
| `GetStateStacks` | `target` | `table<string, int>` | Returns State ID to stack count. |
| `GetStateIDs` | `target` | `string[]` | Returns active State IDs in stable order. |
| `FindActiveEffectHandle` | `abilitySystem: GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent`, `effectID: string` | `int?` | Returns the first matching active handle. |

Equipment uses `attrPlus` in stable attribute order. Weak applies `-1 ATK` and `-1 DEF` per stack, with a minimum of `0`. Poisoned grants its damage ability. States may grant `onWalk` and `onHookTriggered` graph abilities.

## MotaBattleAbility

**Module:** `Source.Gameplay.MotaBattleAbility`  
**Inherits:** `GlobalCore.GameplayAbility`  
**Ability ID:** `Ability.Combat.MotaBattle`

Load these constant modules directly with `require`; `MotaBattleAbility` returns their scalar values in `result.code`.

| Enum | Members |
|---|---|
| `Enums.BattleResultCode` | `WIN = 1`, `CANNOT_DAMAGE = 2`, `LETHAL_COUNTER_DAMAGE = 3` |
| `Enums.CriticalResultCode` | `VALUE = 1`, `NOT_NEEDED = 2`, `UNKNOWN = 3` |

Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.Gameplay.MotaBattleAbility`).

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calculate` | `abilitySystem: GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent`, `eventData: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Produces an `Enums.BattleResultCode` code and prevalidated damage/Game Over specs without mutation. |
| `activate` | `abilitySystem: GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent`, `eventData: GlobalCore.GameplayEventData` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Calculates and optionally commits when `eventData.payload.commit` is `true`. |
| `CalculateDamagePerRound` | `attacker`, `defender` | `damage: number`, `details: table` | Static. Runs the attack, defence, damage, hit-count and incoming-damage event pipeline. |
| `CommitResult` | `result: GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | — | Static. Applies the prevalidated counter-damage Effect exactly once. |
| `CalculateCriticalValue` | `enemy`, `player` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Static. Returns an `Enums.CriticalResultCode` code. |

The owner is the enemy, and `eventData.target` is the player. Calculation validates without applying counter-damage or Game Over Specs. Its battle result data includes per-round damage, counter rounds, Vampire healing, first-strike and fixed damage, both Battlers, prepared Specs and `committed`. `CommitResult` applies the combined damage once, and the Enemy handles Game Over after the animation. Critical calculation includes Vampire healing and uses the same round-count threshold regardless of First, but ignores FixDmg expressions.

Combat resolution passes return strings from `Enums.CombatResolutionCode`: `ATTACK = "AttackResolved"`, `DEFENSE = "DefenseResolved"`, `HIT_COUNT = "HitCountResolved"`, `DAMAGE = "DamageResolved"`, `INCOMING_DAMAGE = "IncomingDamageResolved"` and `BATTLE_RULES = "BattleRulesResolved"`. These intermediate results are separate from the final `Enums.BattleResultCode` outcome.

## GameplayConstants

**Module:** `Source.Configs.GameplayConstants`

This module owns the shared Gameplay event tags and identifier prefixes used by event publishers and ability subscribers.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `MOVEMENT_HAZARD_TAG` | `"Gameplay.Movement.Hazard"` |
| `BATTLE_RULES_EVENT` | `"Event.Combat.ResolveBattleRules"` |
| `MOVEMENT_STEP_EVENT` | `"Event.Movement.Step"` |
| `MOVEMENT_QUERY_HAZARD_EVENT` | `"Event.Movement.QueryHazard"` |
| `MOVEMENT_QUERY_HAZARD_BOUNDS_EVENT` | `"Event.Movement.QueryHazardBounds"` |
| `COMBAT_RESOLVE_ATTACK_EVENT` | `"Event.Combat.ResolveAttack"` |
| `COMBAT_RESOLVE_DEFENSE_EVENT` | `"Event.Combat.ResolveDefense"` |
| `COMBAT_RESOLVE_HIT_COUNT_EVENT` | `"Event.Combat.ResolveHitCount"` |
| `COMBAT_RESOLVE_DAMAGE_EVENT` | `"Event.Combat.ResolveDamage"` |
| `COMBAT_RESOLVE_INCOMING_DAMAGE_EVENT` | `"Event.Combat.ResolveIncomingDamage"` |
| `EQUIPMENT_EQUIP_EVENT` | `"Event.Equipment.Equip"` |
| `SPECIAL_PREFIX` | `"Special."` |
| `STATE_PREFIX` | `"State."` |
| `EQUIPMENT_PREFIX` | `"Equipment."` |

## SpecialAbilities

**Module:** `Source.Gameplay.SpecialAbilities`

Concrete ability classes can also be loaded from `Source.Gameplay.SpecialAbilities.<ClassName>`, for example `require("Source.Gameplay.SpecialAbilities.MultiHitAbility").new(magnitude)`.

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateEffect` | `specialID: string`, `magnitude: any` | `GlobalCore.GameplayEffect` | Creates one Infinite `Special.<id>` effect, tag and ability. |
| `CreatePoisonedAbility` | — | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbility` | Creates the State Poisoned incoming-damage ability. |
| `GetMagnitude` | `abilitySystem: GlobalCore.AbilitySystemComponent`, `specialID: string` | `any` | Reads the magnitude stored on the active special effect. |

Compete, Hard, Magic, MultiHit and Poisoned use their combat resolution events. `GameplayConstants.BATTLE_RULES_EVENT` gathers Vampire healing, First damage and FixDmg. Numeric FixDmg applies directly, while string FixDmg substitutes the player's and enemy's current numeric attributes before evaluation. Domain, Flank and Blockade handle `Event.Movement.QueryHazard` and grant `Gameplay.Movement.Hazard`. Other IDs grant queryable passive tags.

## MovementSpecials and movement danger

**Module:** `Source.Utils.MovementSpecials`

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreatePreviewContext` | `enemies`, `player` | `PreviewContext` | Validates hazard coverage and caches combat damage and coverage radii for one unchanged player/enemy snapshot. |
| `Preview` | `enemies`, `player`, `playerPosition: sf.Vector2i`, `ignoredEnemies?`, `previewContext?` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Resolves movement-hazard damage and contributing sources. |
| `Commit` | `player`, `pathPositions: sf.Vector2i[]` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Reuses `Preview` for every traversed cell, applies total damage and performs Blockade retreat. |
| `NotifyPlayerMovementFinished` | `player`, `pathPositions?: sf.Vector2i[]` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Commits a completed movement path or the current cell. |

Load `local MovementResultCode = require("Enums.MovementResultCode")` for movement results: `HAZARD_BOUNDS = "MovementHazardBounds"`, `HAZARD = "MovementHazard"`, `NO_HAZARD = "NoMovementHazard"` and `HAZARD_COMMITTED = "MovementHazardCommitted"`.

`Preview` owns movement-hazard geometry. It dispatches `Event.Movement.QueryHazard`, resolves Flank and ignored enemies, and returns ordered sources and total damage. Domain activates when Manhattan distance is `<= max(1, magnitude)`, including the range boundary, and uses `MotaBattleAbility.CalculateDamagePerRound` with combat specials such as Magic. Ignored Flank enemies are included in geometry but not in damage.

Pass movement-hazard enemies, such as those returned by `CollectEnemies`, to `CreatePreviewContext`. Every granted ability subscribed to `Event.Movement.QueryHazard` must also handle `Event.Movement.QueryHazardBounds`. The bounds event uses the enemy as `instigator`, the player as `target` and an empty payload.

Each bounds handler must successfully return `GameplayAbilityResult.Success(MovementResultCode.HAZARD_BOUNDS, { radius = n })`, where `n` is a non-negative integer. The inclusive square from `(enemy.x - n, enemy.y - n)` to `(enemy.x + n, enemy.y + n)` must contain every cell where that ability can contribute damage. Domain declares `max(1, magnitude)`; Blockade and Flank declare `1`. Missing subscriptions, rejected queries and malformed results raise errors, including when another ability on the same enemy supplies valid bounds. Bounds and damage previews must not mutate gameplay state.

`PreviewContext` contains `player`, `damageByEnemy` and `radiusByEnemy`; the radius is the largest declared by that enemy's abilities. Recreate it when enemy membership, visibility, positions or player/enemy ability state changes. Danger grids filter by `Gameplay.Movement.Hazard` and materialise on demand. They clip coverage to the requested area, run `Preview` only for candidate cells and relevant enemies, and preserve source and row-major entry order. Coverage is conservative: per-cell events and Flank resolution determine the exact damage. Unchanged overlapping cells, including zero-damage cells, are reused when the area changes.

## Generated GeneralDataTypes

**Module:** `Source.Configs.GeneralDataTypes`

The General Data generator owns this module and its stub. `Types` and named fields expose each generated `<TypeName>AttributeSet`. Type keys come from `Enums.GeneralDataKey`; member keys come from the matching `Enums.GeneralData.<TypeName>` module.

`Create(typeName, memberID, memberData)` returns `GlobalCore.AttributeSet`, deep-copying schema fields and setting `ID`. Use `Source.Data.CreateGeneralAttributeSet(typeName, memberID)` when starting from IDs.

## Lua runtime API

| `InitPlayer` | `playerPath: string`, `applyInitialEquipment?: bool = true` | `Source.MapActors.Player` | Static. Constructs a Player from a Blueprint class path and optionally applies Class initial equipment. |
| `FromDict` | `data: table` | `Source.MapActors.Player` | Static. Restores Bases, inventory abilities, equipment Effects and State Effects without applying Class initial equipment or executing member graphs. |
| `asDict` | — | `SaveData` | Serialises stable state, excluding runtime Effect handles. |
| `activateItem` | `itemID: string` | `GlobalCore.GameplayAbilityResult` | Activates `GeneralData.Item.<id>.onUse`. |

A runtime equip or unequip changes the Infinite Effect before the corresponding graph runs. Movement completion sends `Event.Movement.Step`.

HP Current is constrained to `0..MAXHP`. Permanent MAXHP and LEVEL growth uses Base deltas. Effect and Constraint changes never alter progression Bases.

`setName` trims Unicode whitespace and accepts between 1 and `Player.MAX_NAME_GRAPHEMES` grapheme clusters. `Enums.PlayerNameValidationError.EMPTY` is `"empty"`; `TOO_LONG` is `"tooLong"`. # Source.Scenes.SceneMap

`SceneMap` is the map Scene controller and public gameplay entry point for Default Gameplay. It manages the active map, primary Player, dialogue and menu windows, environment state and persistence records.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/Source/Scenes/SceneMap_meta.lua`

## Scene

**Inherits:** `Source.Gameplay.GameplayScene` (see the [GameplayScene contract](<Gameplay.md#gameplayscene>)).

`SceneMap` is the public gameplay entry point and owns the current `inst` and `player`. `getGameInstance()`, `getPlayer()` and `getGameMap()` read the current objects. The Scene coordinates lifecycle and frame order, map input blocking, Game Over requests, tutorials and locale refresh. It creates HUD and Region Title directly; optional windows follow [Windows, Menus, Input and Controls](<../Default Gameplay/Windows Menus Input and Controls.md>).

Each Scene owns separate instances of these modules under `Source.Scenes.SceneMap`:

| Module | State and responsibility |
|---|---|
| `MapSession` | Loaded map, map path, region, builder and pending transfers; map replacement, destination resolution, floor previews and persistence commands. |
| `Dialogue` | Message window, active operation, voice, movement restoration and dialogue locale snapshots. |
| `Windows` | Other optional windows, focus groups, window operations, movement restoration and deferred menu/save requests. |
| `Environment` | Map audio and panorama settings, return-to-scene restoration and world ambient-light transitions. |

The Scene passes current objects to components or exposes them through getters and commands. Components keep their private state separate; gameplay scripts use the Scene entry points.

Ordinary map loading binds the Scene and current map identity, restores terrain and Actor records, then binds the Player and runs surviving Actors' `onCreate`. Map replacement and Scene destruction release the departing map's ConditionalActor subscriptions without dispatching Actor destruction or altering persistent records.

### Functions and events

Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.Scenes.SceneMap`, metadata class `Scene`), which Blueprint nodes expose as the first target pin.

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getGameMap` | — | `gameMap: Global.GameMap` | Pure. Returns the loaded `GameMap` or compatible `WorldGameMap`. |
| `openPlayerName` | — | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `Closed` (`true`). Opens the player rename window. |
| `showMessage` | `name: string`, `message: string`, `refActor: Engine.Actor`, `localeArgs: Dict[string, any] = {}` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branch: `FinishedDialogue` (`true`). |
| `showSelection` | `name: string`, `options: string[]`, `refActor: Engine.Actor`, `allowCancel: bool = true`, `localeArgs: Dict[string, any] = {}` | `Engine.AsyncOperation` | Latent. Branches: `Selected0` (`0`), `Selected1` (`1`), `Selected2` (`2`), `Selected3` (`3`), `Cancelled` (`-1`). |
| `applyLoadedGame` | `inst: Source.GameInstance` | — | Rebinds player, HUD and windows from `inst` and forces a map reload. Default execution output. |
| `showEnemyBook` | — | — | Opens the monster handbook window. Default execution output. |
| `showFloorTeleporter` | — | — | Opens the floor-teleporter window. Default execution output. |
| `showShopRecords` | — | — | Opens the visited-shop list (Lua callers receive a boolean indicating whether it opened). Default execution output. |
| `openMenu` | — | — | Opens the in-game menu. Default execution output. |
| `recordAddedActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records an added Actor in map persistence. Default execution output. |
| `recordActorPosition` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `position: sf.Vector2i = nil` | — | Records the Actor's current position, or explicit `position` when supplied. Default execution output. |
| `recordDestroyedActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Records a destroyed Actor in map persistence. Default execution output. |

### Script operations and lifetime

`showShopRecords()` opens the [visited-shop list](<../Default Gameplay/Windows Menus Input and Controls.md#visited-shops>) under the same conditions as `V` and returns a Lua boolean indicating whether it opened. `openShop(buyItemIDs, canSell, actor?)` accepts an optional shop Actor for recording; direct Scene calls supply that Actor explicitly.

`showMessage`, `showSelection`, `openPlayerName`, `openShop` and `openAttrShop` return `Engine.AsyncOperation`. Results and window replacement rules match the [Scene nodes](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#lua-waiting-and-results>).

`showVoiceMessage(name, message, voiceFileName, refActor, minDistance, spatial)` is also available to Lua. With `spatial = true`, it positions the voice at `refActor` and passes `minDistance` to the audio manager; with `false`, the voice is non-spatial. Even with `spatial = false`, `refActor` positions the message window.

Lua wrappers that supply node-local formatting values can call `showMessageWithContext`, `showSelectionWithContext` or `showVoiceMessageWithContext`. Each takes its corresponding ordinary method's arguments followed by `localVars: table<string, any>`, copied when the dialogue starts, and returns the same `Engine.AsyncOperation`. The ordinary Scene methods and Scene nodes capture their active node context before delegating. The `WithContext` methods have no Blueprint nodes.

Scene exit, destruction and map replacement cancel unfinished tutorials, dialogues, shops, player-name windows and scene timers, dismissing windows and releasing input blocks. They also close the shop-record list and release its remote shop Actor. Registered operations on departing map Actors, including movement and doors, are also cancelled. Waiting Lua tasks and Blueprint events stop without running subsequent statements or completion outputs.

Scene exit and destruction also discard deferred menu, Save/Load and quick-save requests and queued map transfers. Cancelling a queued transfer releases its frozen background and restores movement for the player captured by that request. `applyLoadedGame(inst)` and `applyPrimaryPlayer()` cancel outgoing interactions and pending requests before rebinding the player, HUD and existing windows, then force a map reload. Movement restoration therefore targets the outgoing player rather than changing the newly bound player's movement state.

Pushing another Scene stops map BGM/BGS and clears weather and panorama. On `SceneManager.popScene()`, the departing Scene's BGM/BGS and weather are cleared, then the map's configured audio and panorama are reapplied. Ordinary maps use settings captured at load; worlds follow the [composite-world environment rules](<../Default Gameplay/Resources Audio Video and Effects.md#composite-world-environment>). Music restarts with the map filter's offset and loop-point settings rather than its previous playback position. Temporary script changes to music, filters, weather and panorama are not restored.

The map, Actors, fog and ambient-light transitions remain alive. Returning neither reloads the map nor repeats Actor `onCreate`.

### Composite-world behaviour

`getGameMap` returns `Global.GameMap` or a compatible `WorldGameMap`. `gotoMapAndPos` accepts either world coordinates for a manifest or local coordinates for a placed child, and stores the manifest as the primary player's map. `blockTransition` skips the mask, but not the target readiness checks.

World Actor records use the manifest. Terrain uses child paths and local cells. `recordActorPosition` updates moved-root ownership. Its optional `position` input defaults to `nil`, which records the Actor's current position; an explicit `sf.Vector2i` records that position instead. `recordDestroyedActorTag` releases a resident match's condition subscriptions and suppresses its tree without destruction events or child I/O. `recordDestroyedActor` is record-only.

# Source.MapActors.Teleporter

`Teleporter` is a conditionally visible map Actor for stairs and direct map transfers. It declares stair direction, arrival offset, sound effect, transition and timing properties alongside stair-transfer and chosen-map Blueprint methods.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/Source/MapActors/Teleporter_meta.lua`

## Teleporter

**Inherits:** `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor` (see [Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor](<ConditionalActor.md>) for inherited visibility conditions).

`goUpstairs` and `goDownstairs` record the `getTeleportPosition()` of the triggering stair (including `Offset`) and its raw `getMapTag()` after the transfer request is accepted. Arrival records the destination stair. For discovery and display rules, see [Windows, Menus, Input and Controls](<../Default Gameplay/Windows Menus Input and Controls.md>).

`stairDirection` uses the standalone `Enums.StairDirection` enum module and offers `None` (ordinary teleporter, the default), `Up` and `Down`, storing the matching string value. Configure every stair Blueprint, including custom variants, with its direction. Lua code loads `local StairDirection = require("Enums.StairDirection")` and uses `StairDirection.None`, `StairDirection.Up` or `StairDirection.Down`.

Going up selects the nearest visible, surviving `Down` stair on the next map; going down selects an `Up` stair. Distance is measured from the source stair's offset position to each candidate's map position using squared Euclidean distance. Equal distances keep Actor order, and arrival applies the selected stair's `Offset`. A missing counterpart follows the standard cancellation path, restores movement and releases the transition freeze; it does not select another direction or an ordinary teleporter.

`FindNearestTeleporter(actors, position, stairDirection?)` accepts the same enum. Omitting the argument searches all teleporters; passing `None` filters ordinary teleporters. `IsAsideOrOverlapping` and general nearest-teleporter transfers search all directions.

`goToMap(mapPath, position, record = true)` exposes a map and tile selector in Blueprint. It transfers directly to `position` without searching for a destination Teleporter. With recording enabled, the source stores this Actor's `getTeleportPosition()` and raw tag; the destination stores the chosen tile with an empty tag. Passing `false` adds neither endpoint and preserves existing records. Child-map destinations resolve to their world manifest and world coordinates.

Each endpoint is stored under its own map path. The source and destination maps belong to their respective configured regions, and the floor-teleporter window lists only visited maps in the current region. Stair transfers resolve the source map's region; map loading resolves the destination region. A map outside all configured regions clears the current region and shows no floor entries.

Transfer requests use [GameplayScene.requestFloorStep and requestMapTransfer](<Gameplay.md#gameplayscene>). Rejected requests do not change movement or records.

### Properties

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Offset` | `sf.Vector2i` | `sf.Vector2i(0, 0)` | Arrival tile offset applied on transfer. |
| `stairDirection` | `Enums.StairDirection` | `"None"` | String enum selector (`None`, `Up`, `Down`). |
| `stairSE` | `string` | `""` | Path: `/Game/Assets/Sounds`; config fallback: `Audio.stairSE`. |
| `transitionName` | `string` | `""` | Path: `/Game/Assets/Transitions`. |
| `transitionTime` | `float` | `0.5` | Transition duration in seconds. |

### Functions and events

Instance methods omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Source.MapActors.Teleporter`), which Blueprint nodes expose as the first target pin. Leave the target pin unset to use the current Teleporter Blueprint owner, or connect another Teleporter instance.

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goUpstairs` | — | — | Transfers to the next floor up and records both endpoints on acceptance. Default execution output. |
| `goDownstairs` | — | — | Transfers to the next floor down and records both endpoints on acceptance. Default execution output. |
| `goToMap` | `mapPath: string`, `position: sf.Vector2i`, `record: bool = true` | — | Transfers directly to `position` on `mapPath`. `Transfer` metadata links `position` to `mapPath`. Default execution output. |

# Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor

`ConditionalActor` is a map Actor base class that controls visibility from a game-variable condition. Configure its variable name, operator and comparison value to show or hide an Actor dynamically at runtime.

**Metadata source:** `Scripts/Source/MapActors/ConditionalActor_meta.lua`

**Inherits:** `Engine.Actor`

## Properties

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conditionVariable` | `string` | `""` | `InstVar` selector restricted to `int`, `float`, `bool` and `string`. |
| `conditionOperator` | `string` | `"=="` | Drop-down: `==`, `~=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`. |
| `conditionValue` | `any` | `0` | `InstVarValue = "conditionVariable"`; runtime accepts `number`, `bool` or `string`. |

An empty variable name leaves the authored `visible` value unchanged. Otherwise, the current variable and comparison value must have matching scalar types. Numbers support all six operators; booleans and strings support only equality and inequality. Missing variables, unsupported operators and mismatched or unsupported types raise errors without implicit conversion.

The condition continuously controls `setVisible(result, false)`: a `false` result hides the Actor again. Child Actors keep their own visibility settings and follow their ancestors' effective visibility. Hidden Actors keep their instances and subscriptions, and Tick stays governed by `tickable` and world streaming.

`applyConditionVisibility(variables)` evaluates the same condition against the supplied game-variable table and applies visibility once. It requires no owning Scene, registers no subscription and dispatches no lifecycle events. An empty condition preserves the Actor's current visibility.

Live Actors and floor previews share the scalar evaluator `Source.Utils.ActorVisibility.Evaluate(variable, operator, comparison, authoredVisible, variables)`. Previews apply its result to static display records after restoring map records, without creating Actors or subscriptions. A hidden record stays cached for later re-evaluation, and a child's effective visibility also requires its ancestors to be visible.

## Lifecycle

`onCreate()` subscribes to `GameInstance:getVariables()` and immediately evaluates the condition. A subscription uses the current map path and a non-empty `getMapTag()`. Multiple Actors may watch the same field independently. A failed initial evaluation releases the subscription before propagating the error.

`onDestroy()` and `onWorldSleep()` unsubscribe. `onWorldWake(elapsedSeconds)` subscribes again and re-evaluates current variables. Overrides in Lua or Script Mixins must call `super()`. Blueprint lifecycle graphs must continue the parent event; the Game project's empty lifecycle graphs inherit this automatically.

`releaseConditionMonitor()` performs repeatable subscription cleanup without changing visibility or persistent destruction records. `ConditionalActor.ReleaseMapMonitors(gameMap)` releases all condition subscriptions belonging to a departing map. `SceneMap` uses it before map replacement and destruction, and releases a suppressed world Actor tree before removing its identity. Temporarily covering a Scene preserves its subscriptions for re-entry.

No subscription or derived visibility state is saved. Variables keep their current logical values in the save snapshot. Map restoration removes destroyed placements before `onCreate`, so collected pickups do not reappear.

## Inheritance

`Enemy`, `Item`, `Equip`, `DoorBase` and `Teleporter` inherit this class. `Bottle`, `Gem` and the Game project's other direct map-Actor Blueprints use `Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor.ConditionalActor` as their parent. `EnemyDamageText` inherits `Engine.Actor` and uses its own damage-hint logic.

# Global and Core Modules Overview

This section documents the three native Lua modules (`Engine`, `GlobalCore` and `GlobalFunctions`) and the shared `Global.*` modules provided by Default Gameplay.

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Engine` | Actors, components, input, graphics, data and UI controls. |
| `GlobalCore` | Scenes, maps, cameras, resource managers and the ability system. |
| `GlobalFunctions` | Native Lua helpers grouped into `Components`, `Manager`, `NodeGraph` and `UI`. |
| `Global.*` | Shared Game project modules, such as `Global.GameMap`. |

Load native modules by root name (`require("Engine")`) and project modules by their full dotted path (`require("Global.GameMap")`). [Lua node libraries](<../Node Functions/Overview.md>) such as `GlobalFunctions.Math` load as separate modules and are not members of the native `GlobalFunctions` root table. See [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md>) for startup loading order.

## Topic reference

| Topic | Documentation |
|---|---|
| Remote Lua snapshot proxies, void RPCs, online events and connection probes (`Global.Net`, `Global.NetProxy`, Storage, `GlobalCore.Server.CheckConnectionAsync`) | [Simple Server client API](<../../Simple Server/Native Client API.md>) |

# Global.GameMap

`Global.GameMap` declares the project map-level API for Player and Actor lookup, Actor creation and destruction, passability, camera binding, tilemaps, terrain tiles and the map environment. Instance method tables on this page omit the implicit `self` receiver (`Global.GameMap.GameMap`), which Blueprint nodes expose as the first target pin.

Metadata source: `Scripts/Global/GameMap_meta.lua`

## Map data and region builders

Shared map data declarations belong to `Global.GameMap.*` and `Global.WorldGameMap.*` in their matching stubs. These are Lua annotation types; they add no constructors and do not change the map file format.

| Namespace | Types |
|---|---|
| `Global.GameMap` | `MapDataBase`, `SerializedMapData`, `MapData`, `MapLayerData`, `MapEnvironmentData`, `SerializedMapFogSettings` |
| `Global.GameMap` | `SerializedTileCell`, `SerializedAutoTileCell`, `SerializedTileRow`, `SerializedAutoTileRow` |
| `Global.WorldGameMap` | `WorldMapData`, `WorldRegionData`, `WorldRegionEnvironmentData` |

`SerializedMapData` describes loaded map records, whereas `MapData` describes normalised Actor data and native environment values. The project module `Source.SceneComponents.MapBuilder.MapDataParser` provides shared parsing operations for ordinary maps and streamed child maps:

- `ValidateMapData(data)` checks a `Global.GameMap.SerializedMapData` record against the [map layer-order rules](<../../../Editor User Guide/Tilesets Autotiles and Maps.md#tilesets-and-autotiles>). It raises an error for invalid data without modifying the record.
- `NormaliseActorData(actorData)` returns a new `Global.Data.ActorData` record that preserves `bp` and `tag` and converts `position` to native unsigned cell coordinates (`sf.Vector2u`). Missing positions or coordinates default to zero.

`NormaliseMap` applies both operations to an ordinary map. A streamed region validates its map data when construction starts, then normalises each authored Actor incrementally rather than in one initial pass.

The world facade receives `WorldMapData` and an injected factory matching this signature:

```lua
---@param region Global.WorldGameMap.WorldRegionData
---@param data Global.GameMap.SerializedMapData
---@param priorityRect Global.WorldGeometry.CellRect | nil
---@return Global.WorldGameMap.RegionBuildState
```

`RegionBuildState` exposes build progress, the region payload, and `step`, `prepareActors`, `prepareRect`, `areActorsReady`, `isCellReady` and `isRectReady`. `Global` consumes this interface without importing the project's builder. `Source.SceneComponents.MapBuilder.WorldRegionBuildState.State` extends it with `layerBuildStates` (elements of type `Source.SceneComponents.WorldLayerBuildState`). Project Actor descriptors, persistence records, layer construction state and floor-preview caches stay in `Source`.

Region builders also implement the resource-lifetime contract:

| Member | Contract |
|---|---|
| `waitingForResources` | `true` when the last build step returned because requested resources were pending. A later step can retry; waiting does not mark the region ready. |
| `setResourcePriority(priority)` | Updates current pending subscriptions and the priority for dependencies discovered later. The world supplies `1` for Active or explicitly forced regions and `0` for Prepared regions. |
| `resolvePendingResources()` | Synchronously finishes already-discovered pending resource loads for an explicit drain. It does not advance layer construction, Actors or publication; those proceed through normal builder steps. |
| `cancel()` | Releases resource subscriptions and closes the construction coroutine. Safe to call repeatedly when publication is cancelled, the region is evicted or the world is disposed. A cancelled builder cannot advance again. |

Texture loading during map and region construction follows these rules:

- **Ordinary maps** queue distinct tileset and autotile textures across all layers before resolving them for layer construction.
- **Streamed regions** request tileset and autotile textures as dependency scanning discovers them, including autotiles introduced by saved terrain changes. The default builder collects dependencies across layers before constructing those layers, reuses duplicate requests and reads autotile frame counts only after the textures are ready. [TextureManager](<../Core Modules/GlobalCore/Resource Managers.md#texturemanager>) owns the request, error and memory semantics.
- **Background streaming budgets:** A resource wait ends the current builder step, and a waiting region is attempted at most once per logic update so other regions retain budget. Required texture failures propagate rather than producing a partial layer.
- **Synchronous drains:** `ensureRegionLoadedAt` and explicit viewport preparation resolve pending resources while draining the builder, whereas background preparation uses its normal time budget.

## GameMap

**Inherits:** `GlobalCore.GameMapBase`

A `getGameMap` output connects to parameters declared as `GlobalCore.GameMapBase`, including `Camera.setMap`. `setTerrainTile` and `setTerrainTiles` expose Blueprint execution pins because they modify terrain, and their result pins report the changes.

### Properties

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HideDisconnectedRegions` | `bool` | `false` | — |
| `DefaultCoverAlpha` | `int` | — | — |
| `MapViewRect` | `sf.IntRect` | `[192, 32, 416, 416]` | — |

### Composite-world facade

For world manifests, `WorldGameMap` exposes world coordinates backed by a native sparse-region index that supplies passability, Dir4, materials and terrain for placed children. Holes are passable, and queries do not load distant children.

- `getTilemap()` returns sparse backing storage rather than a flattened world.
- `getActorByTag` performs no I/O and searches Active or previously activated resident roots.
- `getGameplayCellRect()` returns a copied cell rectangle without loading regions: full bounds for an ordinary map, or Active bounds for a world map (falling back to visible bounds until the Active area exists).
- `prepareViewportAt` queues the required camera neighbourhood's cold child maps together, reuses reads already in flight, completes their Actors and publication, and renders the destination before returning. Surrounding placements continue streaming asynchronously; failures in a required child, Actor or publication propagate.

### Rendering and fog

Ordinary maps, composite worlds and floor previews delegate map content to the shared native `MapRenderer`. The game adapter preserves Actor callbacks, particles, billboards, layer effects and ordinary-map player cover. World regions draw in global layer order, and their Actor lights and tile blockers share world coordinates so lighting crosses placement boundaries.

Map lights come from `Actor.lightComp`, while ambient light uses `getAmbientLight` and `setAmbientLight`.

Each `GameMap` owns a separate fog controller. The runtime Lua methods `getFogSettings()` and `setFogSettings(settings)` read a copy of or replace its `Engine.MapFogSettings`. `getRegionFogSettings(path)` returns a world child's settings, or `nil` when it has no resident configuration.

> **Note:** Mutating a settings value returned by `getFogSettings()` does not modify the map. Pass the updated value to `setFogSettings(settings)`.

### Actor visibility

`getAllActors` and tag lookups include hidden instances. Position and range queries, collision, overlap and pathfinding exclude Actors hidden by their own `visible` flag or by an ancestor's. Rendering also excludes their attached lights and light blocking.

The Game project filters hidden Actors from enemy lists and movement hazards. Visibility changes refresh cached danger before the next query without waiting for a Tick.

### Disconnected regions

`GameMap.HideDisconnectedRegions` enables native region hiding for ordinary finite maps. Configure its startup value with [`hideDisconnectedRegions` in Gameplay](<../../Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#shared-gameplay-configuration>), set the module default before constructing maps, or call `setHideDisconnectedRegions(enabled)` on an existing map. `GameMap` skips this default for `sparseWorldConfig`; calling the native setter with `true` on a sparse world raises an error.

Tile connectivity and replacement follow these rules:

- **Connectivity:** Regions use four-way connectivity based solely on tile passability, determined by the topmost visible layer with tile content in each cell. Map edges bound connectivity; doors and other Actors do not divide regions.
- **Hidden-cell replacement:** The player's region stays visible, while other passable cells display the tile layers of the nearest impassable cell using Manhattan distance (ties break top to bottom, then left to right), preserving source-cell texture, autotile shape and animation. Impassable cells keep their own display.
- **Missing observer:** Without a valid observer (no player, an out-of-bounds position or an impassable observer cell), all passable cells and all Actors are hidden while walls stay visible. Previews supply an explicit observer cell.

Actor visibility follows these geometric rules:

- **Passable anchors:** Actors anchored on passable cells follow their anchor cell's region.
- **Impassable anchors:** The Actor's local image rectangle is transformed by its position, translation, origin, rotation and scale; the resulting quadrilateral must overlap a visible passable cell with positive area (touching an edge is insufficient). Images entirely inside walls or with zero area stay hidden. This allows wall-mounted torches to follow the room their graphics enter.
- **Hierarchy and extent:** The test is geometric rather than per-pixel alpha, and an image spanning multiple regions draws in full whenever it overlaps the visible region. Every ancestor must independently pass the rule and its own `visible` flag; a hidden parent hides all descendants.

Entering a region reveals it and leaving hides it again without storing exploration state in saves. Rendering suppresses hidden-region Actors, their descendants, attached particles and lights, and damage text in hidden cells, without altering Actor `visible` flags, terrain data, collision, pathfinding or events. Enemy Book filters through `isActorVisibleOnMap(actor)` before grouping enemies.

Visibility queries refresh after terrain edits or observer movement without waiting for drawing. For the native observer and visibility APIs, see [GameMapBase](<../Core Modules/GlobalCore/Map and Fog.md#gamemapbase>).

### Functions and events

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getPlayer` | — | `player: Engine.Actor` | Pure. |
| `setPlayer` | `player: Engine.Actor` | — | Exec (`default`). |
| `getAllActors` | — | `actors: Engine.Actor[]` | Pure. |
| `getActorsByPosition` | `position: sf.Vector2i` | `actors: Engine.Actor[]` | Pure. |
| `getActorByLayerAndPosition` | `layer: string`, `position: sf.Vector2i` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | Pure. |
| `getActorsByRange` | `position: sf.Vector2i`, `radius: int` | `actors: Engine.Actor[]` | Pure. |
| `getActorByTag` | `tag: string` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | Pure. |
| `isPassable` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `targetPosition: sf.Vector2i` | `passable: bool` | Pure. |
| `spawnActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `layer: string`, `emitCreateEvent: bool = true` | — | Exec (`default`). |
| `createActor` | `actorClass: Engine.Actor`, `layer: string`, `kwargs: any`, `emitCreateEvent: bool = true` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | Exec (`default`). |
| `destroyActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor` | — | Exec (`default`). |
| `getCamera` | — | `camera: GlobalCore.Camera` | Pure. |
| `setCamera` | `camera: GlobalCore.Camera` | — | Exec (`default`). |
| `getTilemap` | — | `tilemap: Engine.Tilemap` | Pure. |
| `getTerrainTile` | `layerName: string`, `position: sf.Vector2i` | `tileID: any` | Pure. |
| `getTerrainTilePositions` | `layerName: string`, `tileID: any` | `positions: sf.Vector2i[]` | Pure. |
| `setTerrainTile` | `layerName: string`, `position: sf.Vector2i`, `tileID: any` | `success: bool` | Exec (`default`). |
| `setTerrainTiles` | `layerName: string`, `positions: sf.Vector2i[]`, `tileID: any` | `positions: sf.Vector2i[]` | Exec (`default`). |
| `getAmbientLight` | — | `ambientLight: sf.Color` | Pure. |
| `setAmbientLight` | `ambientLight: sf.Color` | — | Exec (`default`). |
| `getSize` | — | `size: sf.Vector2u` | Pure. |
| `getTopMaterial` | `pos: sf.Vector2i` | `topMaterial: string?` | Pure. |
| `findPath` | `start: sf.Vector2i`, `goal: sf.Vector2i`, `actor: Engine.Actor`, `excludedAnchors: sf.Vector2i[] = {}` | `path: sf.Vector2i[]` | Pure. |
| `isPathfindingPassable` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `targetPosition: sf.Vector2i` | `passable: bool` | Pure. |
| `hasPathBlockingOverlapActor` | `actor: Engine.Actor`, `targetPosition: sf.Vector2i` | `hasActor: bool` | Pure. |
| `getScene` | — | `scene: GlobalCore.SceneBase` | Pure. |
| `addCommonTip` | `text: string` | — | Exec (`default`). |
| `addDamageText` | `text: string`, `position: sf.Vector2f` | — | Exec (`default`). |
