# UI, Actor, Particle and Subtitle Previews

Each asset editor uses PreviewHost to display live appearance and timing within the [preview/gameplay boundary](<Overview.md#preview-and-gameplay>). For host availability, rebuilds and errors, see [Build, Publish and Troubleshooting](<Build Publish and Troubleshooting.md>).

## UI previews

The [UI Asset Editor](<../Editor User Guide/UI Asset Editor.md>) renders the authored asset without running its Lua Controller. Select **Refresh Preview** to display pending edits; after modifying native controls, rebuild the project before checking the result.

Provide representative placeholder content for model-dependent areas. Use `previewText`—part of the node's design-only `editor` data—for runtime strings, and supply representative `#TAB` and `#ITEM` entries alongside Game visuals so tabs, lists and character displays stay readable during authoring.

Placeholders are not fallback game data: business code must supply localised labels and populate dynamic collections before display. See [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>) for runtime ownership.

Select an animation in the Timeline, then use play, pause, stop and scrubbing to inspect it without modifying the saved Slot layout. With no animation selected, the Designer shows the authored UI appearance. See [UI Timeline](<../Editor User Guide/UI Asset Editor.md#timeline>) for animation definitions, inherited Global animations and instance overrides.

For nested-asset and repeated-template editing, see [UI Asset Editor](<../Editor User Guide/UI Asset Editor.md>); control properties, children and Slot rules are documented in [UI Controls in the Palette](<../Editor User Guide/UI Controls in the Palette.md>).

## Actor previews

Selecting a Blueprint JSON file in a file selector previews its current appearance and animation, including unsaved changes. A missing appearance or texture displays the file icon.

**File Explorer** thumbnails and Blueprint editing surfaces display resolved Actor appearances: texture regions, character frame animation, `material` and `materialParameters` come from current Blueprint values, with map instances applying their instance overrides. Updating inherited defaults (including Undo/Redo) refreshes affected visuals.

See [Actor placement and Actor Info](<../Editor User Guide/Blueprints Common Functions and Actors.md#actor-placement-and-actor-info>) for selecting Blueprints and editing instances, and [Map and World Previews](<Map and World Previews.md>) for map lighting, selection aids and Live Debug display.

## Material previews

Material, Actor, map and UI previews receive unsaved material snapshots. The native host compiles them in memory without modifying the game's runtime material cache. An invalid preview displays an error instead of showing a stale successful image. See [Preview and diagnose](<../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#preview-and-diagnose>) for the shared compiler, preview controls, error navigation and GLSL view.

## Particle previews

Open a particle from **Database → Common Particle Overview** (`F6`) or **File Explorer**. The preview can isolate the selected track and provides Play/Pause, Stop, Restart, single simulation step, time entry, seeking, playback speed and zoom controls.

A step advances `1 / simulationRate` seconds. Seeking pauses playback and can take longer for later times. These controls do not modify the saved resource; track and property edits follow the normal Save and Undo workflow. A fixed resource seed supports repeatable authoring on the same runtime and GPU, not cross-device deterministic simulation.

Missing resources or unsupported GPU capabilities report an error; particle preview uses the native GPU implementation with no CPU fallback. See [Common Particles](<../Editor User Guide/Common Particles.md>) for resource fields, emission and ownership rules, GPU requirements and feature limits.

## Subtitle previews

Open a document under `Data/Subtitles` in the [Subtitle Editor](<../Editor User Guide/Video Subtitles.md>). Use Play/Pause, Stop, current time, timeline playhead and preview language to check timing. Without a reference video, playback uses a plain background and stops at the last section's end time. An empty subtitle document is editable.

Select a project video for temporary reference, or clear it to return to the plain background. The video preserves its aspect ratio and plays synchronised audio with a mute toggle; seeking pauses audio and restores the previous playback state once positioning finishes. Preview duration is the longer of the video and subtitle durations, and any subtitles after the video ends appear over the plain background.

Selecting a video in a project without FFmpeg reports that it is not an FFmpeg project, while subtitle editing and plain-background preview work normally. Reference video, preview language, playhead and mute are window-session state and are not saved to the subtitle document.

Native preview and runtime playback share subtitle layout. Subtitle data, language editing, font, wrapping and layout rules are documented in [Video Subtitles](<../Editor User Guide/Video Subtitles.md>).

documents.title: Architecture and Data Flow
documents.content:
# Architecture and Data Flow

PreviewHost renders editor content with the project's native implementation: the editor owns authoring, input and overlays, while PreviewHost owns native preview sessions and pixel transport. See [Map and World Previews](<Map and World Previews.md>) and [UI, Actor, Particle and Subtitle Previews](<UI Actor Particle and Subtitle Previews.md>) for view-level operation.

## Shared renderer and module boundary

- **Shared map renderer (`Engine/Source/Core/include/Graphics/MapRenderer.hpp`):** Engine and `PreviewHostRuntime` compile the same Core Graphics renderer. `Scene` holds ordered layers, tilemap regions, sprites, lights, ambient light, panorama and fog; `View` and `Options` supply camera, output size, time and display flags. It outputs an `sf::RenderTexture` without parsing editor requests or reading pixels to the CPU.
- **Map and world layers:** Ordinary maps use one region; worlds draw regions within each authoritative layer, preserving placement priority and cross-region lighting and occlusion. `GlobalCore.GameMapRenderer` adapts gameplay state and supplies emitter, billboard, layer-effect and ordinary-map player-cover hooks.
- **Tile updates and animation:** `TileLayer::updateBlock` rebuilds affected chunks and autotile neighbours while invalidating material and occlusion caches; streaming uses `writeBlock` and its normal build stages, and animation uses the explicit frame time.
- **Host isolation (`Engine/PreviewHost`):** `Engine/PreviewHost` owns request parsing, editor sessions, IPC, BGRA readback and temporary frame transport outside Core's recursive source collection. Game modules never include it or link `PreviewHostRuntime`, and `LudorkRuntime` keeps its downward dependency boundary without depending on map gameplay objects. See [native module layout](<../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md>) and [Build, Publish and Troubleshooting](<Build Publish and Troubleshooting.md>).

## Scene updates

- **Live in-memory snapshots:** The editor sends live in-memory map data—including unsaved edits, Blueprint instance overrides, referenced particle resources with resolved curves and material-document snapshots—within the [preview/gameplay boundary](<Overview.md#preview-and-gameplay>). Lights and Emitter effects preview even when their Actor has no texture. The native registry supplies the material node and parameter schema; the editor maintains no separate shader model.
- **Map material revisions:** Map requests carry a `materialRevision`. A complete `materials` snapshot accompanies the first request, material edits, undo, renames, deletions and resource refreshes; other frames and map switches reuse that snapshot and its parsed resources (a missing snapshot for the requested revision is an error). Material overrides apply only within their own preview request and never affect other preview types.
- **Material-window requests (`renderMaterial`):** Each request carries a `materialRevision` for the active material. The first request, content or path changes, and new connections send that material's `asset` and `materialPath` (excluding graph layout and unrelated materials); subsequent frames send only time and preview settings.
- **Material-window caching:** The session caches the parsed material, generated GLSL and compilation errors, updating the scene when preview settings or source textures change. Resending the same revision and path returns cached sources and diagnostics without recompiling, while detecting texture file changes between frames.
- **Material diagnostics (`diagnosticsRevision`):** Texture and frame-rectangle errors can appear or clear independently of material edits. Ordinary frames include diagnostics only on change (an empty array clears earlier errors), whereas snapshot responses always include diagnostics and generated sources.
- **Diagnostics retention and error recovery:** The client preserves diagnostics even when a newer edit invalidates the accompanying image. A failed material shows its error image instead of a previous valid render; fixing the graph or missing texture restores the preview.
- **Incremental map updates:** A full map scene initialises a session; later edits update scene fields, regions and identified sprite/light records, while camera and animation frames reuse the installed scene. Actor-only edits refresh cached visuals and lighting without rescanning terrain or rebuilding Tilemaps; structural changes and resource refreshes rebuild required state across ordinary maps, worlds and thumbnails.

### Renderer caching and statistics

- **Static light caching:** The Core renderer reuses render targets and light caches between frames. Static light results key on position, colour, radius, intensity and texture dimensions regardless of distance sorting; static occlusion changes invalidate affected cache entries while preserving reusable texture storage.
- **Dynamic occupancy and transmission:** Dynamic transmission and occupancy textures cache separately by exact dimensions, preserving lighting resolution and sampling coordinates. Static and dynamic occupancy share one reusable CPU pixel buffer; unchanged dimensions receive pixel updates, and dynamic occlusion redraws and uploads current pixels each frame.
- **Dynamic pool budget:** Each dynamic texture pool holds at most the shader light limit (64 in the shipped configuration), and pools share a 64 MiB RGBA pixel budget per renderer with least-recently-used eviction. Active-light textures stay alive until drawing finishes; over-budget requests allocate temporary storage reclaimed afterwards.
- **Static caches and CPU buffer:** The 64 MiB dynamic budget excludes driver and framebuffer overhead, static light caches and the CPU buffer. Static light caches cap at the shader light limit, and the CPU buffer preserves its peak capacity; working sets fitting within both limits are reused after warm-up, whereas larger sets may reallocate.

`MapRenderer::statistics()` and preview responses report these frame metrics:

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `renderTextureAllocations` | Render targets created during the latest frame. |
| `occupancyTextureAllocations` | Static or dynamic occupancy textures created during the latest frame. |
| `occupancyBufferGrowths` | CPU occupancy buffer capacity growths during the latest frame. |
| `staticLightRedraws` | Static light redraws performed during the latest frame. |
| `residentRenderTextures` | Resident render targets held at frame end, including cached lighting targets. |
| `dynamicLightingCacheBytes` | Estimated RGBA pixel bytes held by dynamic lighting pools at frame end. |

Map switches and scene closure keep reusable textures, CPU buffer capacity, shaders and material programs while invalidating scene-dependent occlusion and lighting (`MapRenderer::invalidateScene()`; call `reset()` to release all renderer resources). Resource refreshes and connection shutdown release preview resources. Surface masks render only when a visible material needs reflections.

The renderer consumes plain scene, region, sprite, light and view records with no Actor or Lua dependencies. View mode, fog and panorama options operate independently (see [Map and World Previews](<Map and World Previews.md>)); runtime fog configuration and static floor-preview APIs are documented in [GlobalCore: Map and Fog](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Map and Fog.md>).

## Scheduling and frame ownership

- **Host processes:** The project map preview service starts separate PreviewHost processes as needed for map/world viewports and for serialised thumbnail rendering; other preview surfaces may open their own connections. On macOS, host processes run without Dock icons and leave keyboard focus with the active application. Thumbnail count never spawns additional processes.
- **Foreground coalescing:** At most one foreground request runs at a time, keeping only the latest pending state with animation capped at 30 FPS. A newly selected map's first frame bypasses the animation interval once the connection is free, though an in-flight request completes before the pending map is submitted.
- **Hidden views and thumbnails:** Hidden views stop refreshing, and active interactions pause new thumbnail tasks. Thumbnails render at time `0` and cache by scene/resources, size and display options.
- **Progressive map publication:** Compatible completed map frames may publish during continuous edits so newer pending edits do not starve the display, while scene-identity, resource and display changes invalidate incompatible results. Each published bitmap carries its frame's camera transform, and the final edit renders once interaction ends.
- **Material-window scheduling:** The material window schedules a `640 × 300` preview every 100 ms with at most one request in flight; hidden, minimised or disabled windows do not submit frames. Its `generation` identifies the active material and preview settings so obsolete images are discarded independently of the cached `materialRevision`, and layout-only graph changes do not replace the material snapshot.
- **Shared-memory pixel transport:** Each connection owns two reusable file mappings for BGRA frames, growing them only when capacity is insufficient. The host writes into mapped storage and holds pixels until the client copies all pages (including Actor batches); the editor reuses mapped views. Closing or rebuilding a connection releases its mappings and temporary files.
- **Thread ownership:** The UI captures an independent map request on the UI thread, runs serialisation, IPC, pixel reads and bitmap creation off-thread (background work never reads the editable scene) and publishes an immutable bitmap with its camera transform. These responsibilities belong exclusively to PreviewHost and the editor, never the game runtime.

## Capabilities and timing

The editor validates the host protocol and advertised capabilities before submitting requests:

| Surface | Required capabilities |
|---|---|
| All previews (transport) | `persistentFrames` |
| Map editing | `map`, `mapActorChanges`, `mapEmitters`, `mapMaterialSnapshots` |
| Material window | `material`, `materialSnapshots` |

An incompatible host must be rebuilt or updated; map previews have no Avalonia fallback renderer. See [Build, Publish and Troubleshooting](<Build Publish and Troubleshooting.md#troubleshooting>).

`MapPreviewLease.LastFrameTiming` exposes change-to-publication latency alongside per-stage timings: scene update, serialisation, native scene application, rendering, readback, transfer, client pixel read and bitmap creation. Its nullable `SelectionToPublishMilliseconds` measures from map selection (before document preparation) to the first compatible published frame; discarded frames do not consume it, and later animation frames leave it unset.

Both publication timings end when the editor publishes the frame rather than when the display presents it. Compare stages at identical scene, camera and output dimensions before attributing latency to native drawing: a `3840 × 2160` frame carries over 33 MB of BGRA pixel data before transport overhead, regardless of map tile dimensions.

documents.content:
# Build, Publish and Troubleshooting

PreviewHost belongs to the editable project. Keep its executable, dedicated runtime library and UI control registry aligned with the project's native controls and the editor protocol.

## Preparing Source and Standalone projects

For a **C++ Source** project, **Construct** builds the Debug game and preview runtime without launching gameplay; a full desktop `tools/build_cpp` build also produces the preview artefacts. **Standalone** projects use the matching preview runtime bundled in `Binaries`. Map edits preview immediately after each change without **Play** or **Export**.

Windows x64 previews support the same MSVC, MinGW-w64 and LLVM Clang toolchains as game builds. Follow [Build the project](<../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md#build-the-project>) for toolchain setup and the runtime DLLs carried by editable projects and packages.

Build only the preview host on Windows with:

```text
tools\build_preview_host.bat Game Debug
```

On macOS:

```sh
sh tools/build_preview_host.sh Game Debug
```

The underlying command family is `ludork-build preview`. Validate published project artefacts with `ludork-build preview validate Game`, replacing `Game` with the project root when necessary.

Native UI control changes require rebuilding the project and publishing its updated registry. See [Native UI Adapters](<../Native C++ Development/Native UI Adapters.md>) for control registration and [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>) for asset and generated-code ownership.

## Build configurations

| Build | `LUDORK_BUILD_PREVIEW_HOST` | `LUDORK_BUILD_GAME_APPLICATION` | UI validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full desktop development | `ON` | `ON` | Matching desktop registry |
| Preview only | `ON` | `OFF` | Host publishes the project registry |
| Game only | `OFF` | `ON` | Supply `LUDORK_UI_REGISTRY_PATH` with the matching desktop registry |

Mobile cross-builds require an explicitly supplied desktop UI registry. Native builds do not generate UI Lua Views or declarations; use the separate [UI export workflow](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>). See [Run, Debug and Package](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for the build and export records required by **Play** and **Pack**.

## Published artefacts and rebuilding

A desktop native build produces:

| Artefact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `PreviewHost` | Native preview process for maps, Actors, particles, subtitles and UI |
| `PreviewHostRuntime` | Dedicated preview runtime library |
| `EditorCache/Preview.json` | Manifest describing the matching binaries and registry |
| `EditorCache/UiPreview.registry.json` | UI-specific control registry |
| `EditorCache/Preview.building` | Temporary marker suspending connections during a rebuild |

- **Binary layout and reconnection:** **C++ Source** preview and game binaries share `bin/<configuration>`, whereas **Standalone** projects use `Binaries`. The editor reconnects once updated artefacts are published.
- **Build failures and UI validation:** Compilation, linking, description or publication failures leave preview unavailable until the next successful publication clears `EditorCache/Preview.building`. Full UI asset validation runs afterwards, so an asset error can fail the build while leaving the newly published preview usable for editing.
- **Runtime identifiers:** Generic preview services use `PreviewRuntimeService` and `PreviewRuntimeSnapshot`; UI-specific components use `UiPreviewClient`, `UiPreviewSession` and `UiPreview.registry.json`.

Missing, damaged or mismatched **Standalone** preview JSON regenerates from the current `Binaries/PreviewHost` during preview preparation, **Save**, **Export** or `ludork-build preview ensure <project-root>`. Recovery replaces only the two preview JSON files and preserves other cache files.

An active `Preview.building` marker blocks recovery, and missing host binaries or dependencies produce errors. **C++ Source** projects require a build whenever their selected preview metadata is unavailable.

## Editable templates and final packages

[Source-to-Standalone conversion](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#convert-source-to-a-standalone-project>) builds and publishes the matching Release preview alongside the editable project. On macOS, signing refreshes the preview build identity and validates the host before publishing. Only preview metadata is written to `EditorCache`; the source project's Export record is not copied.

Both **C++ Source** and **Standalone** editable projects and templates include preview support. Final game packaging uses the valid project UI registry for asset validation, then excludes preview executables, dedicated runtime libraries (including versioned libraries), manifests, build markers, temporary frame files and the `Engine/PreviewHost` source tree. Game executables and runtime libraries never link `PreviewHostRuntime`.

This exclusion applies to both loose and `.ldpak` layouts and to platform binary/resource directories, including macOS application bundles. Packaging operates on a staging copy without removing preview support from the editable project. See [Run, Debug and Package](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>) for distribution, encryption and signing options.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Action |
|---|---|
| Host, manifest or registry is missing | **Construct** the **C++ Source** project. For **Standalone**, regenerate its preview metadata; update the matching runtime if binaries or dependencies are missing. Then validate the published artefacts. |
| Protocol or capability is incompatible | Rebuild or update the host to supply the [required preview capabilities](<Architecture and Data Flow.md#capabilities-and-timing>). There is no fallback map renderer. |
| Preview pauses during a build | Wait for publication and reconnection. If the build failed, fix the build error and rebuild before retrying preview. |
| Windows build reports that runtime files are in use | Close the processes listed in the build log (including any externally launched game or test process), then rebuild. The log includes process IDs when Windows can identify the owners. |
| A newly added native control is unavailable | Rebuild its adapter and registry together; adding an editor Palette entry alone does not register a native control. |
| Packaging rejects UI assets or a registry | Fix the reported asset/registry mismatch using the matching desktop build; never replace the registry with one from an unrelated project. |
| Map dragging or animation is delayed | Inspect the timing stages in [Architecture and Data Flow](<Architecture and Data Flow.md#capabilities-and-timing>) at the actual output size. Native drawing, GPU readback, pixel copying and UI publication carry separate costs. |

View-specific placeholders and unsupported content are documented in [UI, Actor, Particle and Subtitle Previews](<UI Actor Particle and Subtitle Previews.md>); map display controls are in [Map and World Previews](<Map and World Previews.md>).

documents.content:
# Installing and Managing Plug-ins

Create, import, update or uninstall C# source plug-ins globally across all projects or scoped to the current project. Plug-ins can add editor commands, text hints and operation hooks through the [public registration API](<Registration and Hook Reference.md>); to extend the game runtime itself, use [native C++](<../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md>).

> **Warning:** Editor plug-ins are trusted in-process code running with the full permissions of the editor process and are not sandboxed. Inspect the source, manifest and origin of any third-party plug-in directory and import only code you trust.

Each plug-in owns its source, windows, labels, settings, retained data and third-party notices. The editor host owns registration, lifecycle, command contexts, restricted host bridges (map, Blueprint and resource cleanup) and operation sequencing. Longer creation, import, status-refresh and uninstall tasks display a progress dialog during which related windows cannot start another operation or close; trust confirmation is a separate step before import.

## Create a plug-in

1. Open **Plug-ins → Manage Plug-ins** and select **New Plug-in...**.
2. Enter a display name and a unique plug-in ID, then choose **With a Window** (default) or **Logic Only**.
3. Choose **Global Plug-ins** or **Current Project Plug-ins**. With a project open, **Current Project Plug-ins** is selected by default; on the start page, only **Global Plug-ins** is available.
4. Confirm creation. The editor generates and compiles the template, validates its entry type, then installs and registers it. If an error occurs, no partial plug-in is left behind and no existing directory is overwritten.
5. The source directory opens automatically. Edit the generated files, then restart Ludork to load your changes.

Neither template registers commands or opens a window automatically; see [Generated template](<Manifest and Minimal Plug-in.md#generated-template>) for the generated files and entry class.

## Import a third-party plug-in

1. Close any sensitive work that must not be exposed to unverified code, and inspect the plug-in's source, `plugin.json` manifest and origin.
2. Select **Plug-ins → Import Plug-in...** or **Import Plug-in...** in the **Plug-in Manager**. When a project is open, choose **Global Plug-ins** or **Current Project Plug-ins** (default: current project; the start page always imports globally), select the complete source directory and confirm the trust prompt.
3. Review the import result and resolve any manifest or compilation errors before continuing.
4. Restart Ludork (imported source is never hot-loaded).
5. Open **Plug-ins → Manage Plug-ins** and confirm the plug-in reports **Loaded** in its scope (open the target project first for a project plug-in).

![Import Plug-in source-directory selection](../../../images/plugins/import-plugin.png)

*Select the directory containing `plugin.json`, not an individual source file or build output.*

### Import validation rules

- **Directory name and collisions:** The imported directory keeps its name. Invalid manifests, compilation failures, duplicate IDs within the effective global-plus-current-project set and existing target directories block installation. `__ProjectPlugins` is reserved for project plug-in storage and cannot be imported as a plug-in directory.
- **Required and rejected files:** The directory must contain `plugin.json` and at least one participating `.cs` file. Inaccessible paths, symbolic or broken links, reparse points, embedded `.data`, host-shared DLLs, F# or VB projects, and loose Avalonia XAML files are rejected before installation.
- **Ignored build and IDE files:** A `.csproj` file may remain for IDE diagnostics, though the plug-in compiler never executes it. Sources beneath `bin`, `obj`, `.git` and `.vs` are ignored.

## Global and project storage

On Windows and macOS, newly created and imported global plug-ins install to `~/Ludork/Plugins` with registrations in `~/Ludork/plugins.json` (`~` is the user's home directory, typically `C:\Users\<user>` on Windows). Writable retained plug-in data always lives under this user directory.

### Discovery and priority

- **Working directory vs user directory:** At startup, the editor reads both the working directory's `plugins.json` (and sibling `Plugins` directory) and the user installation. Development builds launched from another directory without a registry fall back to the repository identified by the build's development marker.
- **Conflict resolution:** Within each scope, working-directory registrations take priority: a matching plug-in ID loads only from the working directory, while unique IDs from either location load normally. Load failures on the selected copy are reported without substituting the other copy. A missing registry contributes no plug-ins; an invalid registry reports a diagnostic while the other location loads. Directories must be registered explicitly — scanning never auto-registers directories.
- **Manager routing:** The **Plug-in Manager** shows each plug-in's active source and routes unregistration or deletion to that source's registry and directory. Importing an unregistered immediate child of the working directory's plug-in root registers it in place; all other imports and new plug-ins go to the user directory. Removing a working-directory registration activates a remaining user copy on the next restart.
- **Repository and portable packages:** Official plug-ins load directly from a repository checkout. Windows development archives ship `Plugins` and `plugins.json` beside `Ludork.exe` (which sets the working directory to the archive root), loading bundled plug-ins without copying to the user directory. Windows release packages keep `BuildTools/OfficialPlugins` as an installation input and never overwrite user plug-ins at startup. See [User data directory](<../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#user-data-directory>) for other editor data and manual migration.

### Project plug-in layout

Project plug-ins follow this layout under either scanned root with the same working-directory priority, while writable `.data` stays under the user root:

```text
Plugins/__ProjectPlugins/<project-key>/
├── plugins.json
├── .data/<plugin-id>/
└── <plugin-directory>/
    ├── plugin.json
    └── Plugin.cs
```

`<project-key>` identifies each project by its absolute path, so projects sharing a directory name at different paths stay independent. Newly created plug-in directories use `<plugin-id>`, whereas imported directories keep their original name.

Each project scope has its own registry and data, and the **Plug-in Manager** separates **Global Plug-ins** and **Current Project Plug-ins** with their respective statuses and diagnostics. Project plug-ins apply only to that project's menus, map context menus, text hints and operation hooks. Moving or renaming a project directory creates a new scope with no automatic migration; re-import its plug-ins into the new scope.

## Official release plug-ins

[Official Blueprint AI](<Official Plug-ins/Blueprint AI.md>), [Official Locale Tools](<Official Plug-ins/Locale Tools.md>), [Official Random Map](<Official Plug-ins/Random Map.md>), [Official Mota Map Fill](<Official Plug-ins/Mota Map Fill.md>) and [Official Resource Cleanup](<Official Plug-ins/Resource Cleanup.md>) ship as global plug-ins with a generated `plugins.json`. Once installed, they load on the next editor start without the third-party trust dialog. Official distributions include no project plug-ins.

> **Warning:** Quit Ludork and back up anything you need before installing official plug-ins. Installation replaces the entire `~/Ludork/Plugins` directory and `~/Ludork/plugins.json` — it does not merge them. Existing third-party source, registrations, `Plugins/.data` and all project plug-ins, registries and data under `Plugins/__ProjectPlugins` are permanently removed. Other editor settings and template caches are preserved.

An ordinary installation failure rolls back to the previous installation; if rollback cannot finish, follow the reported recovery instructions. Successful replacement deletes the temporary backup, reporting cleanup failure separately if it cannot be removed.

### Windows installers (EXE and MSI)

- **Opt-out:** Both Windows installers install official plug-ins by default for the user who started setup. Clear **Install Official Plug-ins** in the EXE wizard or pass `INSTALL_OFFICIAL_PLUGINS=0` to the MSI to skip without modifying existing plug-ins.
- **User identity:** Launch setup normally as your own account so plug-ins install to your profile even when another administrator provides UAC credentials. Explicitly starting setup as another user targets that user instead; service-account installations must skip user plug-ins.
- **Repair, upgrade and uninstall:** Repair preserves user plug-ins, whereas an upgrade that installs official plug-ins replaces them again. Editor uninstall deletes user data (including plug-ins) by default; clear **Delete user data** to keep it. See [User data directory](<../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#user-data-directory>) for deletion scope, identity rules and silent flags.

### macOS DMG

The macOS DMG keeps plug-ins outside `Ludork.app`: Finder displays `Ludork.app`, an `Applications` link and **Install Official Plugins** (its `.command` extension and the plug-in payload are hidden).

1. Drag `Ludork.app` to `Applications` — do not drag plug-in files to `Applications`.
2. Ensure Ludork is closed, then double-click **Install Official Plugins**.
3. Review the replacement warning and select **Replace and Install** to validate the hidden payload and transactionally replace `~/Ludork/Plugins` and `~/Ludork/plugins.json`.

### Repository and portable installation

Repository checkouts load registered plug-ins directly. To install a separate user copy outside the checkout, build Toolchain, quit Ludork and run:

```sh
.tools/Toolchain/ludork-editor editor-official-plugins prepare Plugins obj/official-plugins
.tools/Toolchain/ludork-editor editor-official-plugins install-current-user obj/official-plugins
```

On Windows, use `.tools\Toolchain\ludork-editor.exe`. To retry a failed installation from an installed Windows release editor directory:

```bat
BuildTools\Toolchain\ludork-editor.exe editor-official-plugins install-current-user BuildTools\OfficialPlugins
```

Run these commands as your normal user without **Run as administrator** or `sudo`; the same full-replacement rules apply. Windows installer operations and `install-current-user` write their latest log to `~/Ludork/Log/OfficialPluginInstall.log` when writable. If an EXE setup reports that plug-in installation failed, the editor itself remains installed — inspect the log and installer output (or installer output alone if identity resolution failed before resolving the user directory) before retrying. The macOS DMG installer displays its own status and recovery details.

## Restart and status

Creation and import compile source before registration. Global plug-ins compile and load at editor startup. Each project's plug-ins compile and load once before its first project window opens in that session (shown in the project-opening progress dialog), and that result is reused when switching or reopening projects.

After creating, importing, uninstalling or editing a plug-in, choose **Quit Ludork** and launch the editor again. Closing every window can leave the editor and its plug-ins running under the [background preference](<../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#start-page>). Plug-ins have no hot enable or disable switch. **Loaded** identifies a plug-in active in the current session.

Open **Plug-ins → Manage Plug-ins** to inspect plug-in diagnostics and states (**Loaded**, **Invalid Manifest**, **Compilation Failed**, **Initialisation Failed**, **Pending Restart**, **Unregistered; Active Until Restart** and **Pending Deletion**) before replacing or deleting installed source.

## Data and uninstall

- **Writable plug-in data:** Global plug-ins store writable state in `~/Ludork/Plugins/.data/<plugin-id>` (supplied via `PluginDataDirectory`; for example, `~/Ludork/Plugins/.data/Ludork.OfficialBlueprintAI`). Project plug-ins use `~/Ludork/Plugins/__ProjectPlugins/<project-key>/.data/<plugin-id>`, keeping the same plug-in ID isolated per project. Always write settings and history under `PluginDataDirectory` rather than the read-only plug-in source directory.
- **Uninstalling:** Uninstalling through the **Plug-in Manager** unregisters the plug-in and optionally schedules safe deletion of its installed source files (a loaded assembly's directory may remain until the next restart). Unregistering without deletion lets you re-register the same immediate child directory under that scope's plug-in root later. Both modes preserve plug-in data, which must be removed in a separate explicit action. Never edit `plugins.json` by hand while the editor is running.
- **Project-owned keep lists:** Official Resource Cleanup stores project-specific keep-list additions in `EditorCache/ResourceCleanupKeep.list` through its host bridge, separate from both plug-in source and `PluginDataDirectory`.

## Compilation references

Source plug-in compilation can reference the .NET runtime, `Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions`, `Ludork.Plugin.Avalonia` and the editor's shared Avalonia assemblies. Plug-ins cannot reference internal editor implementation assemblies.

documents.content:
# Manifest and Minimal Plug-in

Generate a C# 13 plug-in template directly from the editor, or author a minimal source plug-in from scratch that adds one Help menu command for Ludork 1.0.0 and newer.

## Requirements

- .NET 9 SDK (optional; required only if you use an IDE `.csproj` file for diagnostics and local builds).
- Access to `Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions` from the Ludork repository or editor development kit.
- A plug-in ID unique within its effective scope and a matching CLR namespace.

## Generated template

Open **Plug-ins → Manage Plug-ins** and select **New Plug-in...** to create a ready-to-edit plug-in directory in the chosen global or current-project scope:

```text
<plugin-id>/
├── plugin.json
├── Plugin.cs
└── PluginWindow.cs   (With a Window only)
```

The generated manifest sets `version` to `1.0.0`, `minimumEditorVersion` to the current editor version and `entryType` to `Ludork.UserPlugins.Plugin`. Because each plug-in compiles into its own assembly, generated templates can share that CLR type name:

```csharp
using Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions;

namespace Ludork.UserPlugins;

public sealed class Plugin : IEditorPlugin
{
    public void Register(IPluginRegistrar registrar)
    {
    }
}
```

**With a Window** (default) adds an independent `PluginWindow : Window` styled with the host theme; **Logic Only** generates only `plugin.json` and `Plugin.cs`. Neither template registers commands, opens a window automatically, or generates XAML or a `.csproj` file. Add your registrations and logic, then restart Ludork to load the updated source.

## Hand-written command example

The example below creates a complete source plug-in that adds one **Help** menu command, with an optional `.csproj` for IDE analysis.

### Source directory

```text
MyPlugin/
├── plugin.json
├── MyPlugin.cs
└── MyPlugin.csproj
```

Ludork supports one source-directory plug-in format. The editor compiles `.cs` files in relative-path order using C# 13 with nullable reference types enabled, `unsafe` allowed and Release optimisation. The host never restores NuGet packages or loads a prebuilt entry assembly.

### Write `plugin.json`

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "Example.MyPlugin",
  "name": "My Plug-in",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "minimumEditorVersion": "1.0.0",
  "entryType": "Example.MyPlugin.Plugin"
}
```

| Field | Contract |
|---|---|
| `schemaVersion` | Manifest schema version; must equal `1` |
| `id` | Identifier containing only ASCII letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores |
| `name` | Non-empty display name |
| `version` | Version string accepted by .NET `Version` parsing |
| `minimumEditorVersion` | Minimum editor version parsed as a .NET `Version` |
| `entryType` | Namespace-qualified CLR type name, matched case-sensitively |

All JSON property names are case-sensitive.

### Add the entry type

```csharp
using Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions;
using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

namespace Example.MyPlugin;

public sealed class Plugin : IEditorPlugin
{
    public void Register(IPluginRegistrar registrar)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(registrar);
        PluginMenuCommand command = new(
            "Example.MyPlugin.About",
            PluginMenuLocation.Help,
            500,
            "My Plug-in",
            ShowMessageAsync);
        registrar.RegisterMenuCommand(command);
    }

    private static async Task<PluginResult> ShowMessageAsync(
        PluginMenuContext context)
    {
        await context.UserInterface.ShowMessageAsync(
            "My Plug-in",
            "The plug-in is loaded.",
            PluginMessageKind.Information,
            context.CancellationToken);
        return PluginResult.Completed();
    }
}
```

The entry type must be `public`, non-abstract, implement `IEditorPlugin` and expose a public parameterless constructor. Plug-in IDs and command IDs must be unique within the effective global-plus-current-project set; separate project scopes may reuse IDs.

### Add an optional IDE project

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
    <LangVersion>13.0</LangVersion>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>disable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\..\Editor\Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions\Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions.csproj">
      <Private>false</Private>
    </ProjectReference>
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Adjust the relative path to match your checkout layout (official plug-ins under `Plugins/` reach `Editor/Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions` with `..\..`). This project file is strictly for IDE diagnostics: every runtime `.cs` source must stay inside the imported plug-in directory and rely only on host-provided references.

### Import and restart

[Import the complete `MyPlugin` directory and restart Ludork](<Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#import-a-third-party-plug-in>).

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Plug-in Development and Installation/Avalonia UI Secrets and Localisation.md
documents.content:
# Avalonia UI, Secrets and Localisation

Open a plug-in-owned Avalonia window, store credentials in the host secret store and present localised UI strings in the editor's active language without depending on internal editor types. Start from the [With a Window template](<Manifest and Minimal Plug-in.md#generated-template>) referencing `Ludork.Plugin.Avalonia` and the host-shared Avalonia assemblies, and register a menu or map context-menu command to open your window.

## Set the window owner

Cast `context.UserInterface` to `IAvaloniaPluginUserInterface` to pass the editor's owner window to `ShowDialog`:

```csharp
if (context.UserInterface is not IAvaloniaPluginUserInterface avaloniaUi)
{
    return PluginResult.Failed("Avalonia UI is unavailable.");
}

MyPluginWindow window = new();
await window.ShowDialog(avaloniaUi.Owner);
return PluginResult.Completed();
```

Set `WindowStartupLocation` to `CenterOwner` where appropriate. The plug-in owns its window, controls, view state, cancellation and disposal of bitmaps or other native resources. Never search `Application.Current` for an editor window or inject controls into editor-owned views.

### Host theme and shared UI utilities

- **Theme resources (`Ludork.Plugin.Avalonia.PluginTheme`):** Read semantic colours with `Brush("Surface")` or `Color("Accent")`, and access the UI font (with Chinese fallback) through `FontFamily`. Available keys: `Background`, `Surface`, `Input`, `Hover`, `Border`, `Text`, `TextMuted`, `TextDisabled`, `Accent`, `AccentMuted`, `AccentHover`, `AccentPressed`, `TextOnAccent`, `Error`, `Warning` and `Success`. Read these resources only after the editor application has initialised, and let standard controls inherit the host theme.
- **Hue normalisation (`Ludork.Plugin.Avalonia.EditorBitmapEffects`):** `NormalizeHue(double)` wraps degrees into `[0, 360)` and treats non-finite values or offsets within `0.0001` degrees of a full turn as zero (`IsNeutralHue(double)` applies the same rule).
- **Bitmap and BGRA hue shifting:** `CreateHueShiftedBitmap(Bitmap, double, CancellationToken)` returns a new bitmap matching source size and DPI even for a neutral offset (caller owns disposal). `ApplyHueShiftBgra(Span<byte>, int width, int height, int stride, double hue, CancellationToken)` modifies an unpremultiplied BGRA buffer in place, preserving alpha, fully transparent pixels and row padding. Both accept an optional cancellation token and use Avalonia's double-precision HSV conversion with nearest-integer RGB rounding (matching the colour picker, which preserves its last hue for greyscale colours).
- **Zoom anchoring (`EditorZoomInput` / `EditorZoomAnchor`):** `EditorZoomInput.PrimaryModifier` and `HasPrimaryModifier` map to Command on macOS and Control on other platforms. `EditorZoomAnchor.Capture(contentPoint, viewportPoint, origin, scale)` records the pointer anchor in content coordinates, and `Apply(scrollViewer, origin, scale)` consumes it after layout while clamping the offset to the viewport (`scale` must be positive and finite). Callers own coordinate conversion, layout subscriptions and viewport resets; `IsPending` and `Clear()` expose pending state.
- **Markdown syntax parsing (`MarkdownSyntax`):** `GetLines`, `GetInlineMatches` and `ReadTable` share parsing without loading resources or opening links. Pass `Profile.Documentation` for documentation images, strikethrough and table escaping, or `Profile.Assistant` for assistant messages and preserved non-pipe escapes. `ReadTable` returns `null` if no table begins on that line; otherwise `MarkdownTable` returns `Header`, `Alignments`, padded/truncated `Rows` and `ConsumedLines`. Rendering controls, styling, resource validation and link handling remain the plug-in's responsibility.

## Separate program and data paths

Treat `PluginDirectory` (imported program content) as read-only and write all settings, caches and history under `PluginDataDirectory`. Both paths reflect the plug-in's active installation scope (global shared data vs project-isolated data); never derive either path from the process working directory.

- **Atomic file helpers (`Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions.FilePersistence`):** `WriteAllTextAtomic` and `WriteAllTextAtomicAsync` write UTF-8 without BOM; `WriteAtomic` and `WriteAtomicAsync` handle stream-based formats. Each writes a same-directory temporary file, flushes to storage and replaces the target, cleaning up on failure. Async overloads check cancellation before replacement, and the synchronous `beforeCommit` callback runs after closing the temporary file. Validation, multi-file transactions and rollbacks remain the caller's responsibility.
- **Custom transaction primitives:** `CreateTemporaryPath`, `WriteDurable` (creates a new file and flushes to storage), `MoveFile`, `DeleteFile` and `MoveDirectory` support custom atomic workflows. Move and delete helpers retry transient Windows sharing or access failures for up to 10 seconds, clear read-only destination attributes before overwrite or deletion, and propagate errors to the caller.

## Store secrets

Use the plug-in-scoped `SecretStore` from the command context:

```csharp
await context.SecretStore.WriteAsync(
    "api-key",
    apiKey,
    context.CancellationToken);
string? stored = await context.SecretStore.ReadAsync(
    "api-key",
    context.CancellationToken);
```

- **Platform backends:** `ContainsAsync`, `ReadAsync`, `WriteAsync` and `DeleteAsync` store credentials in Windows Credential Manager or macOS Keychain with no plaintext-file fallback. On Linux, reads use environment variables while writes and deletes throw an exception naming the required variable (`LUDORK_PLUGIN_SECRET_<hash>` for global plug-ins; `LUDORK_PROJECT_PLUGIN_SECRET_<hash>` for project plug-ins).
- **Scoping:** Global credentials are scoped by plug-in ID; project credentials include the project scope so identical plug-in IDs and secret names across different projects never collide.
- **Handling rules:** Keep logical key names stable and scoped to one purpose. Never copy a retrieved secret into settings files, diagnostics, URLs or conversation logs.

## Localise plug-in UI

Read `IPluginRegistrar.EditorLanguage` during `Register` and load matching string resources shipped inside your plug-in directory, with an explicit fallback such as `en_GB`. Both `PluginMenuCommand.Label` and `PluginMapContextMenuCommand.Label` must be localised before registration, and window titles, buttons, validation messages and diagnostics must be localised inside the plug-in — the host never translates plug-in strings.

- **`Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions.PluginLocalizer`:** `LoadDirectory(pluginDirectory, language)` reads `locales/<language>.json` and falls back to the entire `en_GB.json` file only when the requested file is missing. `LoadCatalog(localePath, language)` reads one language-keyed JSON object and falls back to `en_GB` per key. `Text(key)` returns the key itself when missing, and `Format(key, arguments)` uses the current culture.
- **Separation from game catalogues:** Game localisation is a separate project data workflow; never reuse a plug-in's UI locale files as the game's runtime text catalogue.
- **Generated Lua strings (`Ludork.Plugin.Abstractions.LuaStringLiteral`):** Use `Quote(string)` or `Append(StringBuilder, string)` to emit complete double-quoted Lua literals that escape quotes, backslashes and ASCII control characters while preserving Unicode text (including C1 control characters) as UTF-8. Because decimal Lua escapes encode bytes rather than Unicode codepoints, never convert non-ASCII codepoints directly into decimal escapes.

> **Note:** `IAvaloniaPluginUserInterface` exposes only the owner window — never editor controls, services or styles. The plug-in importer rejects loose XAML files, and the host does not support live language switching for already-loaded plug-ins.

documents.content:
# Distribution

Package a third-party plug-in as a single self-contained source directory that recipients can import into either the global or current-project scope.

## Directory contents

- **Include:** `plugin.json` (with `minimumEditorVersion` set to at least `1.0.0`), all required `.cs` source files, plug-in resources (such as locale JSON files) and licence notices. Document the supported editor versions and any post-import setup required.
- **Exclude:** Build outputs (`bin/`, `obj/`), local settings, credentials, `.data`, and any enclosing `__ProjectPlugins` tree or `plugins.json` registry. Recipients select their own scope during import; official editor distributions never bundle project plug-ins.

For source compilation rules and the role of an optional `.csproj` file, see [Source directory](<Manifest and Minimal Plug-in.md#source-directory>).

## Installation

Recipients import the complete source directory and restart Ludork. See [Installing and Managing Plug-ins](<Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md>) for scope selection, updates and retained data behaviour.

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Plug-in Development and Installation/Registration and Hook Reference.md
documents.content:
# Registration and Hook Reference

Reference for every registration method, command context, host bridge and lifecycle hook exposed on `IPluginRegistrar`. All registrations occur exclusively inside `IEditorPlugin.Register`; an empty `Register` method (as generated by the creation templates) is valid.

## Scope and execution order

- **Active scope:** The start page loads global plug-ins only. A project window combines global plug-ins with that project's plug-ins across menus, map context menus, text hints, Export/Run/Pack hooks and export-participant fingerprints. Each window resolves these registrations against its own project, even when another project window has focus.
- **Source precedence:** Within each scope, working-directory and user registrations merge by plug-in ID with the working-directory copy winning; only the selected copy contributes commands, providers and hooks.
- **Ordering and uniqueness:** Global plug-ins run before project plug-ins for providers and hooks. Menu items sort by menu location and `Order` (global commands win ties). Plug-in IDs and command IDs must be unique within the effective global-plus-current-project set — ordinary menu commands and map context-menu commands share one command-ID namespace. Conflicting registrations fail rather than overwriting earlier ones. Independent project scopes may reuse IDs, and one project's load failure never blocks global or other-project plug-ins.

## Menu commands

`RegisterMenuCommand(PluginMenuCommand)` adds a command to `File`, `Edit`, `Game`, `Database`, `Help` or `Plugins`. Command IDs must be non-empty and unique in the effective set, and `Order` determines placement within the menu.

| `PluginMenuCommand` field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Id` | Non-empty command ID, unique in the effective set |
| `Location` | One of the six supported menu locations |
| `Order` | Numeric sort key within the menu |
| `Label` | Already-localised displayed text |
| `Handler` | Asynchronous `PluginMenuHandler` |

The `PluginMenuContext` passed to `Handler` supplies the optional project path, editor language, read-only plug-in directory, writable plug-in data directory, message UI, text-hint invalidation, plug-in-scoped secret store, optional Blueprint assistant and resource-cleanup host bridges, and a `CancellationToken`. Avalonia source plug-ins referencing `Ludork.Plugin.Avalonia` can cast `UserInterface` to `IAvaloniaPluginUserInterface` to obtain the real owner window. Return `PluginResult.Completed()` on success or `PluginResult.Failed(error)` on a handled failure.

## Map item context-menu commands

`RegisterMapContextMenuCommand(PluginMapContextMenuCommand)` appends a command after built-in actions when the user right-clicks a map item (never when right-clicking empty space in the map list). Command IDs share the unique namespace with ordinary menu commands, `Order` sorts plug-in commands, and `Label` is the already-localised displayed text.

| `PluginMapContextMenuCommand` field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Id` | Non-empty command ID, unique in the effective set |
| `Order` | Numeric sort key |
| `Label` | Already-localised displayed text |
| `Handler` | Asynchronous `PluginMapContextMenuHandler` |

`PluginMapContextMenuContext` provides `MapKey` (the right-clicked map), the project path, editor language, plug-in directories, message UI, text-hint invalidation, secret store, `CancellationToken` and `MapEditorHost`, returning `PluginResult` like an ordinary menu command.

### `IMapEditorHost` contract

`IMapEditorHost` is a narrow read/write boundary — plug-ins never receive `ProjectDataStore`, editor view models, `MapPanel`, host controls or mutable editor JSON.

| `IMapEditorHost` member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ProjectPath` | Open project root |
| `CellSize` | Read-only source cell size from the compiled engine declaration, independent of preview zoom |
| `SuggestedMapKey` | Map that opened the plug-in, when available |
| `ListMaps()` | Ordered map summaries containing key and display name |
| `ReadMap(mapKey)` | Immutable snapshot of the current in-memory map |
| `ReadTileset(tilesetKey)` | Immutable tileset snapshot |
| `ListActorBlueprints()` | Actor Blueprint summaries (`Key` is the canonical class reference; `DisplayName` is the project Blueprint key) |
| `ReadActorBlueprintPreview(blueprintReference)` | Resolved default Actor appearance at cell `(0, 0)` for an existing Actor Blueprint |
| `AcquireActorPreview(snapshot)` | Native material preview handle (`IPluginActorPreview`) for a resolved Actor snapshot |
| `ResolveAssetFile(assetPath)` | Resolve a logical path at final editor file I/O; empty if unavailable |
| `GetSaveDirectoryAsync(cancellationToken)` | Return the project's absolute user save directory without creating it |
| `ReplaceLayerAndSaveAsync(request, cancellationToken)` | Revision-checked layer replacement and direct single-map save |
| `ReplaceActorsInRegionAndSaveAsync(request, cancellationToken)` | Revision-checked replacement of Actor placements in one layer's rectangular region |
| `RunProjectScriptAsync(scriptPath, request, cancellationToken)` | Execute a Lua entry with the current project's game runtime and return its JSON object result |

`GetSaveDirectoryAsync` reads the static `APP_NAME` from the saved `Scripts/Entry.lua` and follows the [desktop game directory rules](<../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#game-configuration>). It never executes Lua or creates directories; unreadable or invalid names, unavailable home directories or cancellation fail the call.

### Map, tileset and Actor snapshots

- **Map and passage snapshots (`PluginMapSnapshot`):** Exposes identity, dimensions, an opaque `Revision` (copy unchanged into write requests), ordered layers with `Visible`, rectangular `Tiles` and `AutoTiles`, and a map-sized `Passage` matrix. Each `PluginMapPassage` gives terrain `Passable` plus resolved `Up`, `Right`, `Down` and `Left` movement permissions across visible terrain layers, AutoTiles, map edges and both ends' directional flags; Actor occupancy is separate.
- **Tilesets and asset paths:** Tileset snapshots include tile dimensions, count and passability. Tileset and Actor `AssetPath` values stay exact-case `/Game/Assets/...` paths — call `ResolveAssetFile` only at final native file I/O, never for snapshots or intermediate caches.
- **Actor snapshots (`PluginMapActorSnapshot`):** Each layer exposes immutable Actor snapshots carrying `Tag`, `BlueprintReference` and visuals resolved via the map editor's own Blueprint/script and instance-override resolver. `SourceRect` is the resolved static texture rectangle (including the character direction's first frame — do not re-derive character sheet layouts).
- **Actor transforms and placeholders:** Translation, scale, origin, rotation, `Material`, `MaterialParameters` and `PreviewOpacity` (`0.25` for invisible Actors, `1.0` for visible) are pre-resolved. Missing visuals have an empty `AssetPath` and null `SourceRect` for cell placeholders. Scale rendering by `CellSize`, not tileset tile dimensions.
- **Native Actor material preview:** Call `IMapEditorHost.AcquireActorPreview(snapshot)` for native material rendering of the resolved source frame. The returned `IPluginActorPreview` exposes `Changed` and a `Frame` with premultiplied BGRA pixels, dimensions, `OffsetX`/`OffsetY` and any material error. Apply `OffsetX`/`OffsetY` relative to the source-frame origin before the Actor transform (displaced materials can expand the frame). Set `IsActive = false` while hidden and dispose the handle when finished; source-frame animation remains the plug-in's responsibility.

### Layer and Actor-region writes

- **Tile layer replacement (`PluginMapLayerWriteRequest`):** Identifies the map and layer, echoes `BaseRevision` and `ExpectedTilesetKey`, and provides full `Height × Width` `Tiles` and `AutoTiles` matrices. For regional tile edits, copy the snapshot matrices and modify only the target rectangle (there is no separate regional tile write API). `PluginMapWriteResult` distinguishes success, revision/tileset conflict and error, and returns the current revision. Validation or write failures leave editor memory, Undo history and UI untouched.
- **Actor region replacement (`PluginMapActorRegionWriteRequest`):** Identifies `MapKey`, `LayerName`, `BaseRevision`, a zero-based `PluginMapRegion(X, Y, Width, Height)`, a required `PreserveBaseClassReference`, and a non-empty list of `PluginMapActorPlacement(BlueprintReference, X, Y)`. The host preserves Actors outside the rectangle and Actors inside whose resolved class derives from `PreserveBaseClassReference`, removing other inside Actors and their instance overrides while keeping preserved records intact.
- **Actor placement validation:** New placements must reference valid Actor Blueprints on distinct passable cells inside the rectangle without colliding with preserved Actors or Actors on other layers; the host assigns map-unique tags. Hidden layers, invalid bounds, unresolved classes, invalid or duplicate existing tags, empty placement lists and revision conflicts fail before writing. Tiles and AutoTiles are untouched.
- **Direct save and Undo semantics:** Either successful write updates the in-memory map, atomically saves only `Data/Maps/<mapKey>.json`, pushes one Undo step onto that map's history, advances its revision and refreshes the target map and layer. Any existing unsaved edits on that same map are included in this save; other maps and project documents are neither saved nor cleared of their dirty state. Undo restores the pre-write in-memory state and marks the map dirty without auto-saving.
- **Pending path-change guard:** Writes are refused while the target map has an unsaved related path change; complete a global Save first.

### Project script execution

`RunProjectScriptAsync` launches the project's own game executable against an existing absolute `.lua` or `.luac` entry file and an independent `JsonObject` request, using the project root as working directory (without invoking normal `Entry` or saving project documents).

- **Preconditions:** Unsaved non-map project documents are rejected, and C++ Source projects require a current native build. Execution also fails if `APP_NAME` cannot be resolved from `Scripts/Entry.lua`.
- **Arguments and initialisation:** The entry receives the temporary request JSON path in `arg[1]`, the required output JSON path in `arg[2]`, and the resolved `APP_NAME` in `arg[3]`. Call `Engine.setAppName(arg[3])` before loading project modules so user data and resource overrides resolve properly. Scripts creating Actors or material-dependent graphics must also run [material cache preparation](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Maps and Materials.md#material-cache-preparation>) first.
- **Result contract and limits:** Write one JSON object to `arg[2]` before exiting. `PluginProjectScriptResult.Success` confirms clean execution and decoding, `Data` holds the JSON object and `Error` describes host failures (plug-in payload fields are the plug-in's responsibility). Results exceeding 32 MiB, missing or invalid JSON objects, non-zero exit codes and detected project input changes during execution all fail the request.
- **Process lifecycle:** The host captures stdout and stderr, terminates the process on cancellation or after 60 seconds, and removes the temporary request/result directory. Because the script runs as a full child process rather than a restricted sandbox, it controls what it loads; [Official Mota Map Fill](<Official Plug-ins/Mota Map Fill.md>) uses this entry point to decode saves and compute battle previews without starting a scene.

## Text hints

`RegisterTextHintProvider(ITextHintProvider)` registers synchronous text-hint resolution. `TextHintContext` supplies the project path, editor language and current field text. Providers run in plug-in order and the first non-empty result wins; thrown exceptions are recorded as plug-in diagnostics.

## Before Export, Before Run and Before Pack

- **Before Export (`RegisterBeforeExportHook`):** Accepts `IProjectExportHook` (extending `IProjectOperationHook` with `ProjectExportFiles GetFiles(string projectPath)`). `GetFiles` inspects without modifying files and returns concrete project-relative `InputPaths` and `OutputPaths` with no duplicates or input/output overlap (declare missing input files too so later creation is detected); `ExecuteAsync` performs the work.
- **Export sequencing and fingerprinting:** Export saves and validates the project, runs Export hooks sequentially, generates UI runtime files and records success. The editor fingerprints declared files plus export plug-in identity (including project scope for project plug-ins) to decide whether another Export is needed. Export hooks run for **Export**, confirmed **Export and Play**, and every editor **Pack**; a before-Run hook modifying export inputs forces another Export before launch. See [Construct, Export and Play](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#construct-export-and-play>).
- **Before Run and Before Pack (`RegisterBeforeRunHook`, `RegisterBeforePackHook`):** Accept `IProjectOperationHook` and run sequentially prior to their operation. Editor game packaging runs a complete Export before running before-Pack hooks. [Standalone project conversion](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#convert-source-to-a-standalone-project>) runs Export hooks only — it skips before-Pack hooks and their packaging exclusions. Any failed result or exception aborts subsequent hooks and blocks the operation. Honour `CancellationToken` and report progress via `IPluginOutput`.

| Operation context field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ProjectPath` | Open project root |
| `EditorLanguage` | Current editor language key |
| `Operation` | `ProjectOperationKind.Export`, `Run` or `Pack` |
| `Packaging` | Non-null only during before-Pack hooks; null during Export and before-Run |
| `Output` | Append-only operation output |
| `TextHints` | Request text-hint refresh |
| `CancellationToken` | Cancellation token for the current operation |

When `Packaging` is non-null, `IProjectPackaging` exposes the following controls:

| `IProjectPackaging` member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `UseLuac` | Whether Pack compiles supported Lua sources |
| `UseLdPak` | Whether Pack writes complete `Assets`, `Data` and pruned `Scripts` trees into root `Assets.ldpak`, `Data.ldpak` and `Scripts.ldpak` |
| `CompileLuaDirectory(relativePath)` | Include a project-relative Lua directory in Pack compilation |
| `ExcludeFile(relativePath)` | Omit a project-relative file from the final package |

For example, Official Locale Tools calls `ExcludeFile("Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx")` in its before-Pack hook to omit the authoring workbook from final game packages while keeping it in Standalone conversions; its Export hook writes the Lua language catalogues separately.

## Blueprint assistants

A Blueprint assistant registers an ordinary `PluginMenuCommand` and owns its UI, settings and conversation history (the host supplies no assistant window or controls; `IAvaloniaPluginUserInterface` provides only an optional owner window). Inside a project window, `PluginMenuContext.BlueprintAssistantHost` provides the project path, suggested current Blueprint, available Blueprint keys and `CreateSession`.

- **Session and workspace boundaries:** `IBlueprintAssistantSession` binds to one existing Blueprint, exposing its base revision and an `IBlueprintAssistantWorkspace`. The workspace can list and read Blueprints, query the API catalogue, search or read allowlisted project source, query official documentation, validate candidates and stage proposals — it cannot mutate Blueprints directly or access arbitrary editor services.
- **Approval and apply:** The plug-in retains the session and calls apply or discard explicitly after user approval. Apply rechecks the base revision and candidate validity, records one Undo snapshot, marks project data dirty and refreshes open editors for that Blueprint without saving to disk.
- **Secrets:** Store API keys in the scoped `PluginMenuContext.SecretStore`; see [Store secrets](<Avalonia UI Secrets and Localisation.md#store-secrets>).

### Official documentation queries

| Documentation member | Result |
|---|---|
| `SearchDocumentationAsync(query, maxResults, cancellationToken)` | Keyword matches across titles, paths and full Markdown with document keys, excerpts and official page URLs |
| `ReadDocumentationAsync(documentKey, startLine, lineCount, cancellationToken)` | Numbered Markdown lines from a document key and one-based line range, with its official page URL |

These methods fetch the fixed website's search index on demand for the editor-selected documentation version and language (matching [online documentation](<../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#online-documentation>)), sharing one cached snapshot per request workspace. They accept queries and document keys only (never project paths or arbitrary URLs). Missing or invalid indexes and network failures return tool errors without switching version or language.

Documentation results are capped at 12,000 characters: continue reads from `nextLine` when present, and inspect `truncatedLine` when an oversized line's tail was omitted (continuation resumes at the following line). API catalogue metadata remains authoritative for concrete Blueprint APIs; see [Official Blueprint AI](<Official Plug-ins/Blueprint AI.md#official-documentation>).

## Resource cleanup

Inside a project window, `PluginMenuContext.ResourceCleanupHost` exposes `IResourceCleanupHost`. The plug-in owns its scan UI, built-in native keep list and final confirmation; the host owns static reference analysis, report validation, project keep-list storage and system Trash recycling.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ProjectPath` | Open project root |
| `ReadKeepPathsAsync` / `SaveKeepPathsAsync` | Read or replace project additions in `EditorCache/ResourceCleanupKeep.list` (an empty list deletes the file) |
| `ScanAsync(nativeKeepPaths, userKeepPaths, progress, cancellationToken)` | Analyse static references and return an immutable report of candidates, categories, sizes and issues |
| `TrashAsync(reportId, progress, cancellationToken)` | Revalidate and recycle all candidates in the report, returning moved paths, remaining paths and any error |

`ResourceCleanupProgress` reports stage, completed/total counts and current path. Reports containing scan issues cannot be recycled, and modified project inputs invalidate existing reports. The host never falls back to permanent deletion when the system Recycle Bin or Trash is unavailable. See [Official Resource Cleanup](<Official Plug-ins/Resource Cleanup.md>) for scan boundaries and the review workflow.

## Unsupported extension points

There are no public hooks for host-docked panels, toolbars, arbitrary context menus, custom data types or editor events. `RegisterMapContextMenuCommand` is the sole context-menu extension point. Plug-ins may open their own Avalonia windows from a command, but cannot inject controls into editor-owned views.

documents.title: Overview
documents.content:
# Official Plug-ins Overview

Ludork ships five official C# plug-ins covering localisation, procedural map layout, Mota Actor placement, Blueprint AI assistance and resource cleanup. Their source directories under `Plugins/` also serve as reference implementations of the public plug-in API.

## Included plug-ins

| Plug-in | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Official Locale Tools](<Locale Tools.md>) | Opens the translation workbook, provides editor text hints and exports Lua language catalogues |
| [Official Random Map](<Random Map.md>) | Generates procedural terrain regions and saves one layer under revision protection |
| [Official Mota Map Fill](<Mota Map Fill.md>) | Populates map regions with doors, enemies and rewards using a saved player's battle damage |
| [Official Blueprint AI](<Blueprint AI.md>) | Discusses one existing Blueprint and applies a validated, reviewable proposal as a single Undo step |
| [Official Resource Cleanup](<Resource Cleanup.md>) | Finds statically unreferenced resources, protects keep-listed paths and moves confirmed candidates to the system Trash |

For workbook authoring, Export integration and runtime `{ID}` resolution with Official Locale Tools, see [Game Localisation Workflow](<Game Localisation Workflow.md>).

## Installation and management

See [Installing and Managing Plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md>) for installer options, command-line installation, restart requirements, status diagnostics and retained data.

> **Warning:** Installing the official plug-ins replaces all existing global and project plug-ins, their registries and their data on every platform. Close Ludork and back up anything you need before installing.

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Locale Tools.md
documents.content:
# Official Locale Tools

`Plugins/OfficialLocaleTools` is the official plug-in for game translation workbooks and serves as the reference implementation for an ordinary menu command, a text-hint provider, an Export hook and a before-Pack exclusion hook (it registers no map-item context-menu command).

Install it through [Official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>) and confirm it reports **Loaded** in the **Plug-in Manager**.

## Registration

The entry type loads the plug-in's own `locale.json`, then registers four components:

- A **Database** menu command (order `900`) that opens `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx`
- `LocaleTextHintProvider` for `{ID}` editor hints
- `LocaleExportHook` via `RegisterBeforeExportHook`
- A before-Pack hook that excludes the authoring workbook from final game packages (skipped during Standalone project conversion so the workbook stays intact)

`LocaleExportHook` declares `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx` as its input and the generated Lua language files as outputs for Export change detection, refreshing its internal cache and editor text hints after every export attempt.

See [Game Localisation Workflow](<Game Localisation Workflow.md>) for workbook rules, generated Lua files and runtime usage.

## Menu behaviour

The menu handler requires an open project, verifies that `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx` exists and asks the operating system to open it with the default spreadsheet application, reporting handled warnings and errors through `IPluginUserInterface`.

## Plug-in and game languages

`Plugins/OfficialLocaleTools/locale.json` localises the plug-in's own menu label and diagnostic messages using `EditorLanguage`. It is completely separate from the project's game language catalogues.

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md
documents.content:
# Game Localisation Workflow

Author game strings in an Excel workbook (`Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx`) and use Official Locale Tools to export Lua language catalogues for editor hints and gameplay runtime formatting.

## Workflow

Ensure your project contains `Scripts/Source/Locale/Core.lua` and normal locale initialisation in `Scripts/Entry.lua`, and use a spreadsheet application that preserves cached formula values if your workbook uses formulas.

1. Install Official Locale Tools via [Official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>).
2. Add string IDs and translations to `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx`.
3. Select **Export** before running or packaging the project.
4. Format strings in scripts and data with `LOC("ID")` or `{ID}`.

## Workbook

Create `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx` following these structure rules:

- **Headers:** Every worksheet uses row 1 as its header row. Column A must be `ID` (case-insensitive), and columns B onwards name target languages such as `en_GB` and `zh_CN`. Blank language headers are ignored, and at least one language column is required.
- **Rows and merging:** Rows with a blank ID are skipped. IDs are trimmed and case-sensitive. Multiple worksheets merge into one catalogue: duplicate IDs are reported with both the first and duplicate cell coordinates, and a non-empty later value overwrites the earlier value for that language.
- **Formulas and leading equals signs:** Formula cells export their cached value when present; without a cached value, the exported text is the formula minus its leading `=`. Enter `'=` or `'==` to export a literal `=` or `==`.

## Export

During unified editor **Export**, Official Locale Tools generates one UTF-8 Lua table per language at `Scripts/Source/Locale/<language>.lua`:

```lua
return {
    ["TITLE_START"] = "Start",
    ["TITLE_EXIT"] = "Exit",
}
```

- **Validation:** Language names must be non-empty, non-rooted and free of path separators or invalid filename characters. A missing workbook skips export without error; a malformed workbook stops Export.
- **Encoding:** Export preserves Unicode text (including C1 control characters) as UTF-8 and escapes quotes, backslashes and ASCII control characters with Lua escapes, ensuring editor hints and the runtime read identical strings.
- **Change detection and packaging:** The workbook and generated language files participate in [Export change detection](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#construct-export-and-play>). Game packaging exports and excludes `Locale.xlsx`, whereas [Standalone conversion](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#convert-source-to-a-standalone-project>) keeps both the workbook and generated catalogues. Command-line run or pack requires running Export first. Generated language files are git-ignored and omitted from project templates while handwritten `Core.lua` is preserved.

## Editor hints

Any editor field whose trimmed text is a single `{TITLE_START}` token can display a live hint. The provider reads `Scripts/Source/Locale/<EditorLanguage>.lua` and falls back to `en_GB.lua`. Spaces or nested braces invalidate the token.

## Runtime

`Scripts/Entry.lua` calls `Source.Locale.Core.Init()` to load language catalogues before reading the active language via `Source.Configs.Main.LoadOrCreate()` (requiring `Core` alone does not load catalogues). Bind a local `LOC` formatter in gameplay modules:

```lua
local Locale = require("Source.Locale.Core")

local LOC = Locale.ApplyStringLocaleFormat

local buttonText = LOC("TITLE_START")
local tabLabels = Locale.ApplyListLocaleFormat({ "MENU_LOAD", "MENU_SAVE" })
local message = LOC(
    "{ITEM_NEW}: {ITEM_NAME}"
)
```

- **String formatting (`ApplyStringLocaleFormat`):** Resolves either a bare key or every `{ID}` placeholder in a string. Missing keys stay unchanged, unavailable languages fall back to `en_GB` where available, and doubled `{{` / `}}` produce literal braces. General Data strings are not auto-translated — pass them through `LOC` when displaying them.
- **List formatting (`ApplyListLocaleFormat`):** `Locale.ApplyListLocaleFormat(values: string[]): string[]` formats each element in order and returns a new array without mutating the input. Use it for tab labels and option lists, and call it again on language change.
- **Language switching:** `Locale.SetLanguage` switches the active language and synchronously broadcasts `LocaleChanged`, and the Config window persists the selection. Subscribed UI refreshes text from its original locale keys without resetting selection, focus or an active dialogue.
- **Initial language and packaging:** A new game configuration selects the platform language if it exactly matches an available catalogue, otherwise `en_GB`, while preserving existing saved settings; see [Runtime configuration](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#configuration>). Lua compilation and **Archive Assets, Data and Scripts (.ldpak)** process `Core.lua` and generated language tables along with the rest of `Scripts`.
- **Reloading:** Restart the game after exporting updated translations. [Lua hot reload](<../../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>) preserves already-loaded language tables.

> **Note:** `Data/Locale/Locale.xlsx` is a project authoring source rather than a runtime database or save format. Plug-in UI localisation is independent of game language catalogues.
