documents.content:
# Official Random Map

Official Random Map (`Plugins/OfficialRandomMap`) generates procedural terrain inside a selected map region and saves one layer under revision protection. It also serves as the reference implementation for a map-item context-menu command with a plug-in-owned Avalonia window.

## Requirements

- Install [Official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>) and confirm Official Random Map reports **Loaded**.
- Open a project with at least one map, layer and valid tileset.
- Save any unsaved edits in the target map, or accept that a successful plug-in write includes them in its direct save of that map.

## Registration contract

`OfficialRandomMapPlugin` registers one `PluginMapContextMenuCommand` shown when right-clicking a map item. Its handler receives `PluginMapContextMenuContext`, casts `UserInterface` to `IAvaloniaPluginUserInterface` and opens `RandomMapWindow` with the host-supplied owner window. The window interacts solely through `IMapEditorHost` — never with editor view models, controls or mutable JSON.

## Workflow

1. Right-click a map item and select **Random Map Designer**.
2. Choose the target map and layer (read from immutable `PluginMapSnapshot` and `PluginTilesetSnapshot` objects).
3. Pick a wall tile. The preview defaults to the full map; select **Select region** and drag between two cells for a rectangle (both endpoints inclusive, clamped to map bounds, zero-based origin), or select **Full map** to reset.
4. Select **Next**, choose a layout mode and target wall density, and optionally switch to **Place markers** to toggle required open cells inside the region. Markers are temporary and never saved; shrinking the region drops markers outside it, switching layers preserves the region and markers, and switching maps resets to the full map.
5. Select **Generate and Save** to overwrite Tiles and clear AutoTiles inside the selected rectangle on that layer. Cells outside the rectangle, other layers and all Actors stay unchanged; local generation does not inspect or connect to terrain outside the rectangle.
6. Inspect the result (reported density covers the selected region). Select **Generate Again** to roll another layout for the same region. Controls lock with a status animation while generating; a revision conflict reloads the map and resets the workflow.

## Actor preview

The preview renders resolved [Actor snapshots](<../Registration and Hook Reference.md#map-item-context-menu-commands>) combining Blueprint/script classes and instance overrides, showing placeholders for missing assets and following the reference transform, opacity and `CellSize` scaling rules.

Actor positions are visual guides only — place a marker on any Actor cell that must stay open. Character sprites show the first frame of their resolved direction, and native material previews evaluate time-dependent graph inputs and vertex displacement without running Actor gameplay.

## Layouts and density

Both layout algorithms keep all empty cells four-way connected, leave markers open and forbid solid 2 × 2 wall blocks. Outermost cells of the region remain open to paths and rooms — generation does not enforce a closed perimeter ring.

- **Lattice:** Scatters single-cell walls and 2–3 cell straight segments with varied positions, orientations and spacing so separate wall components never touch orthogonally. Reserves single-cell gateways (walls on two opposite sides, open cells front and back) for doors or blocking Actors, protecting their supporting cells while filling towards the target density. Gateways block local passages while alternate routes may still bypass them. Lattice never carves rooms or room rings and rejects empty 4 × 4 areas. Minimum region size: **7 × 7 cells**.
- **Rooms:** Combines small rooms (interiors up to 9 cells, such as 2 × 2, 2 × 3, 2 × 4 and 3 × 3; adjacent rooms may share a one-cell wall), one-cell doorways and branching corridors. An 11 × 11 region produces 4–7 rooms and 1–2 loops for alternate routes, scaling up in larger regions. At least half of the rooms have a single entrance whose blockage disconnects the room from the main route; wide room interiors and wider corridors do not count as alternate routes. Minimum region size: **short side ≥ 7 cells and area ≥ 81 cells**.

Smaller rectangles can be selected in the UI but cannot be generated.

| Layout | Target wall density | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Lattice | 20–35% | 30% |
| Rooms | 30–45% | 36% |

Switching layouts updates the slider bounds and restores that layout's default. Target wall count equals the region cell count multiplied by the percentage (rounded to the nearest whole cell), with an allowed tolerance of 2% of region cells rounded up (minimum 1 cell). Density guides layout generation and the saved result reports the achieved wall percentage.

If the target density, markers and layout constraints cannot be met together, generation fails without saving. Identical dimensions, markers, layout mode, target density and seed reproduce the exact same layout. `RandomMapGenerator.GetDensityProfile(mode)` returns the min/max/default density values, and the `Generate` overload omitting density uses the mode's default.

## Saving contract

Generated layers are submitted through `PluginMapLayerWriteRequest`, rejecting conflicting edits and never applying partial writes on failure. See [Map item context-menu commands](<../Registration and Hook Reference.md#map-item-context-menu-commands>) for complete save and Undo semantics.

> **Note:** `IMapEditorHost` cannot create maps, resize maps, inject editor UI or bypass revision checks. Official Random Map edits terrain only (use [Official Mota Map Fill](<Mota Map Fill.md>) to populate Actors) and has no packaging responsibility, so it never registers a Pack hook.

documents.content:
# Official Mota Map Fill

Official Mota Map Fill (`Plugins/OfficialMotaMapFill`) populates an existing map region with doors, enemies and rewards by analysing current terrain connectivity and ranking enemy battle damage against a saved player state. Install it via [Official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>).

The project must keep the Default Gameplay `Player`, `Enemy`, `DoorBase`, `Teleporter` and `MotaBattleAbility` contracts. The plug-in launches the project's game executable to restore the player, prepares the project's user material cache automatically (reporting any errors in the status area) and computes battle damage. Save Blueprint, script and other non-map edits before opening a reference save — C++ Source projects also require an up-to-date **Construct**. The plug-in does not save those documents.

## Choose the region and reference player

1. Right-click a map in the map list and select **Mota Actor Fill**.
2. Choose a visible layer, then drag across the map preview to select a rectangle or choose **Full map**. Coordinates are zero-based and include both dragged endpoint cells.
3. Choose a `.json` or `.ldc` game save. The file picker opens in the previously chosen directory or, initially, in the project's user save directory `~/<APP_NAME>/Save` (falling back to the nearest existing parent without creating directories; errors resolving `APP_NAME` from `Scripts/Entry.lua` appear in the status area).
4. Pick a player from the **Reference player** drop-down (listed in `playerKeys` order, defaulting to the first player). Displayed HP, ATK and DEF include restored equipment, item abilities and states. Switching players recalculates enemy damage; **Reload** re-reads the save and project definitions.

The reference save supplies player state only — terrain always comes from the map currently open in the editor, and map edits stored inside the save are ignored.

## Choose Actor Blueprints

Select **Next**, then **Choose Blueprints…** to pick one or more `.json` Blueprint files under `Data/Blueprints`. The list starts empty; subsequent picks append new entries without duplicates, and cancelling leaves the list unchanged. If any file in a batch is invalid or uses an unsupported Actor type, the entire batch is rejected and the previous selection stays intact.

The **Doors**, **Enemies** and **Items** tabs display only your selected Blueprints, with a preview shown below when selecting or hovering over an entry. Right-click an entry and select **Remove**, or highlight it and press **Delete** or **Backspace**, to exclude it. Damage evaluation covers both the selected Blueprints and existing Actor references on the map:

- **Doors:** Display their inherited key ID and required count. Yellow doors (`KEY_Y`) and blue doors (`KEY_B`) are supported; other door types are not placed.
- **Enemies:** Display single-battle damage calculated by the project's `MotaBattleAbility` (including combat specials). Enemies that cannot be defeated or cost more than half of the reference player's current HP are marked for the largest-room guardian role. An enemy that deals zero damage may legitimately display `0`, while an undefeatable enemy stays marked as undefeatable even when its damage field is `0`.
- **Items:** Include Item and Equip Blueprints, consumables (such as gems and bottles) and other Actor Blueprints that are neither players, doors, enemies nor teleporters. Select only pickups intended as rewards; teleporters and their subclasses are excluded.

## Placement rules

### Terrain and room analysis

The plug-in reads terrain passability across visible layers, including AutoTiles and directional movement flags. It analyses the full map so selection edges do not act as artificial walls, while restricting placement strictly to the chosen layer and region. Existing Actors on other layers and preserved teleporters reserve their cells.

Wide room interiors consist of cells belonging to at least one fully traversable 2 × 2 block, grouped via four-way traversable connections. Single-cell straight passages, bends and junctions do not count towards wide room area.

### Room guards and doors

- **One enemy per room:** Given suitable enemies and free cells, each room receives one enemy across its interior and direct entrances (preferring an interior cell near an entrance). An enemy already guarding a shared entrance covers both adjacent rooms without adding a second enemy, while independent main corridors outside those entrances may receive their own guards. Rooms with no usable doorway can still receive an ordinary enemy on a free interior cell.
- **Independent doors:** Doors are placed at usable entrances independently and do not count towards a room's one-enemy limit.
- **Room size and enemy tiers:** Large rooms (at least 9 interior cells) favour blue doors and stronger enemies; smaller rooms favour yellow doors and weaker enemies. Among defeatable enemies costing at most half the player's HP, the lower half sorted by damage (rounded up) supplies weaker guards and the upper half supplies stronger guards. When only one eligible enemy is selected, it serves both roles.

### High-risk guardian

At most one high-risk enemy is placed per generation, guarding one of the largest large rooms wholly inside the selection that has a usable entrance (ties break randomly). High-risk candidates include enemies costing more than half the player's HP, undefeatable enemies and enemies whose counterattack would be lethal. High-risk enemies are never placed into ordinary rooms, pockets or unguarded corridors.

### Terminal pockets

- **Definition:** A terminal pocket contains 1–8 cells separated from the main route by a single narrow entrance (L-shaped and T-shaped interiors are supported), contains no wide room or teleporter, and connects externally to a wide room, teleporter or junction. Pockets do not contribute to large-room area.
- **Guards, doors and rewards:** Pockets follow the same one-enemy rule across interior and entrance, reusing an existing entrance guard when present. With enough free interior space, a pocket favours a weaker enemy inside plus a reward, and may place a yellow door at its entrance. When only one interior cell is available for a reward, its guard may stand at the entrance. Ordinary corridors receive no items.

### Rewards and fallbacks

- **Minimum and target count:** Rooms and pockets prioritise at least one reward whenever item candidates and a legal cell exist (a retained item satisfies this minimum; otherwise one reward cell is reserved before placing guards, with a pocket's first reward favouring deeper interior cells). New rewards target 40% of the remaining free interior cells, rounded up.
- **Spatial pattern:** Placement prefers a randomly chosen checkerboard parity (such as `1010` / `0101`) and rejects any horizontal or vertical run of three consecutive item cells (counting retained and already-reserved rewards), which can reduce the final count.
- **Missing candidates and reporting:** Missing candidate categories skip independently (for example, omitting blue doors still allows strong guards). Generation reports rooms or pockets that could not receive an enemy, guard or reward without violating occupied cells, selection bounds or high-risk rules. Results list placed counts, combined room/pocket count and the random seed; **Generate Again** rolls a new layout with the same selections.

## Replace and save

> **Warning:** **Generate and Save** removes every existing Actor inside the selected layer and region except `Source.MapActors.Teleporter` instances and subclasses — including events, decorations, doors, enemies and items — along with their instance overrides. Preserved teleporters keep their tags and overrides, and Tiles, AutoTiles, other layers and Actors outside the rectangle remain untouched. If no placements can be generated, the map is neither cleared nor saved.

Saving performs one revision-checked direct map save and pushes one Undo step (including any existing unsaved edits on that map). A conflicting edit, unresolved Actor class or failed save leaves the map untouched; a revision conflict reloads the map and requires reloading the reference save. See [Map item context-menu commands](<../Registration and Hook Reference.md#map-item-context-menu-commands>) for full write and Undo rules.

> **Note:** Damage values are single-battle estimates at the chosen save state. Generation does not simulate collecting rewards, spending keys, multi-battle attrition or spatial movement damage (such as Domain and Flank), and does not guarantee map solvability.

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Blueprint AI.md
documents.content:
# Official Blueprint AI

Configure the official Blueprint AI plug-in (`Ludork.OfficialBlueprintAI`, source in `Plugins/OfficialBlueprintAI`) to inspect your project, discuss changes to one existing Blueprint and review a validated diff before applying it. Open the assistant from **Game → Blueprint AI**.

## Workflow

1. Install the official plug-ins as described in [Official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>).
2. Open a project and select **Game → Blueprint AI**.
3. Open **Settings** to configure your provider, model, endpoint and API key.
4. Select **New** to create a conversation bound to one existing Blueprint, then review any staged proposal and generated diff.
5. Select **Apply** after validation succeeds, then use the normal project Save command when ready to write the change to disk.

## Local data

Settings and conversation history are stored under `~/Ludork/Plugins/.data/Ludork.OfficialBlueprintAI`. Uninstalling the plug-in retains this directory; see [Data and uninstall](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#data-and-uninstall>) for storage paths and explicit removal.

## Scope and permissions

- **Read scope:** Each conversation binds to one project and one existing Blueprint. The assistant can inspect other Blueprints, Lua metadata, allowlisted Lua/C/C++ source files and official Ludork documentation to understand available APIs.
- **Write boundaries:** The assistant cannot create, rename or delete Blueprints, edit multiple Blueprints, modify source code, run shell commands or start processes.
- **Review and Apply:** The model can only stage a Blueprint proposal; the editor validates the candidate and renders a generated diff, changing nothing until you select **Apply**. Applying re-reads the editor's working copy, verifies its base revision, records one normal Undo step, marks the project dirty and refreshes all open editors for that Blueprint without saving to disk.

> **Note:** Plug-ins run as trusted in-process code rather than inside an operating-system sandbox. The restrictions above are enforced by the official assistant's model-facing tool surface together with the editor's session and Apply boundaries.

## Provider settings and credentials

Open **Settings** in the Blueprint AI window to configure a provider profile, model and endpoint:

- **Supported profiles:** OpenAI uses the Responses API; DeepSeek, Google OpenAI-compatible and Custom profiles use an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint. Model and endpoint fields remain editable so new model releases need no plug-in update.
- **Endpoint validation:** Endpoints must be absolute `https://` URLs without embedded credentials, query strings or fragments. Plain `http://` is permitted only for loopback addresses during local development.
- **API keys:** Keys are stored in the [host secret store](<../Avalonia UI Secrets and Localisation.md#store-secrets>) and never written to `settings.json`. The UI shows only the first three and last three characters separated by a fixed mask (short keys are completely hidden), and updates a stored credential only when you enter a new value or explicitly remove it. Provider availability is outside Ludork's control.

## Local conversations and provider state

The local index and append-only JSONL files in the plug-in data directory are the authoritative conversation history. They store messages, model snapshots, compact tool activity and proposal decisions, and never record API keys or full source-file reads.

OpenAI Responses requests set `store:false`, avoiding reliance on provider-side conversation state. For long conversations, only a rolling summary and recent messages are sent in subsequent requests; this context compaction never deletes or alters the complete local history.

An interrupted request is recorded as interrupted: completed local entries survive restart, while the in-flight network request is never resumed automatically.

## Project source inspection

Project search and file reads accept only project-relative paths under the configured runtime and API source roots with supported text extensions. Build outputs, logs, version-control metadata, INI/plist configs, plug-in data, credentials and out-of-project paths are rejected, as are symbolic links, broken links and reparse points anywhere in the path (including the project root). Filesystem failures return tool errors, and file contents are treated strictly as data rather than instructions that can expand permissions.

## Official documentation

The assistant searches and reads the development or release documentation selected by the editor in the editor's active language, matching the [online documentation](<../../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#online-documentation>) version rules and returning links to the source pages.

If the matching documentation index is unavailable, the assistant reports the failure without falling back to another version or language. The current project's API catalogue and metadata remain authoritative for concrete nodes, types, serialised names and pins. See [Blueprint assistants](<../Registration and Hook Reference.md#blueprint-assistants>) for the underlying host API.

## Troubleshooting

- **Blueprint AI is missing from Game:** Install the [official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>), restart Ludork and inspect **Plug-ins → Manage Plug-ins** for registration or load diagnostics.
- **No project or Blueprint is available:** Open a project containing at least one existing Blueprint (the host bridge is unavailable outside a project window). Opening the window does not select a target automatically; click **New** to choose one.
- **The target was renamed or deleted:** The existing conversation stays readable, but its target cannot be reassigned silently. Start a new conversation for an existing Blueprint.
- **Missing API key or HTTP 401:** Re-enter the API key in **Settings** and confirm it matches the chosen provider, endpoint and any OpenAI **Organisation** or **Project** values. The UI never displays the full stored key.
- **Connection or endpoint errors:** Supply an absolute `https://` base URL without embedded credentials, query parameters or fragments, and check DNS, proxy, firewall and TLS settings (plain `http://` works only for loopback endpoints).
- **Apply reports a revision conflict:** The Blueprint changed after the proposal captured its base revision. Discard the proposal, inspect the updated Blueprint and start a new request or conversation.
- **History shows interrupted:** The request, window or editor stopped before completion. Local history remains intact; send a new request rather than expecting the previous stream to resume.

documents.content:
# Official Resource Cleanup

Official Resource Cleanup (`Plugins/OfficialResourceCleanup`) scans a saved project for resources with no detected static references, lets you protect dynamically loaded paths and moves confirmed candidates to the operating-system Recycle Bin or Trash.

## Workflow

Install Official Resource Cleanup via [Official release plug-ins](<../Installing and Managing Plug-ins.md#official-release-plug-ins>), then open a project, stop the game and save all pending edits before scanning.

1. Select **Plug-ins → Resource Cleanup**. The window separates the read-only built-in protected list from the project's additional keep paths.
2. Review the built-in protected list, which includes the editor's [fixed resource directories](<../../Editor User Guide/Project Settings and Asset Layout.md#fixed-resource-directories>) plus plug-in entries for UI defaults, application icons and asset licences. Assets referenced by files in protected directories are also kept.
3. Add project-relative files or directories loaded via dynamic Lua paths to the additional keep list, one per line (for example, `Assets/Characters/Dynamic` or `Data/Animations/GeneratedEffect.json`). Listing a directory protects everything inside it.
4. Select **Scan**. Scanning runs in the background displaying stage, progress and current path; **Cancel** stops scanning without recycling anything.
5. Inspect the **Data** and **Assets** tabs, each showing per-file project-relative paths, sizes, counts and totals. Listing a candidate means no supported static reference was found — not that runtime usage has been disproved.
6. To protect a listed file, select its row and choose **Keep selected and rescan**, or edit the keep list and rescan. Modifying the keep list invalidates the previous report, and any scan issues must be resolved before recycling unlocks.
7. Select **Move to Trash**, confirm the final file count and total size, and proceed. Recycling applies to every candidate in the current report after the host revalidates it against current project files.
8. Review moved files, any error and unprocessed files. Cancellation or errors stop further moves while already-moved files stay in the system Trash; run a fresh scan before cleaning up again.

Additional keep paths are saved to `EditorCache/ResourceCleanupKeep.list` when scanning, saving the list or closing the window. Opening with an empty list creates no file, clearing and saving deletes the file, and built-in entries are never copied into it. If saving fails, the window stays open and displays the error.

## Scan boundaries

> **Important:** Resource Cleanup performs static analysis only — it never executes Lua, traces gameplay or infers concatenated or runtime-computed paths. Add dynamic resource paths to the keep list and review every candidate even when scanning reports zero issues.

- **Scanned sources:** Reads every ordinary map and world child map, all Lua sources and all supported structured Data files. Data dependencies are traced before evaluating Assets, so an unreferenced Data file does not keep its own Asset dependencies alive. Blueprint fields and map-instance overrides are traversed recursively using metadata, including resource references inside components and typed containers.
- **Protected vs candidate types:** Maps, `Data/General`, `Data/UI`, `Data/Configs`, `Data/Locale` and their supported references stay protected. Data candidates are restricted to Materials, Tilesets, AutoTiles, Blueprints, CommonFunctions, Animations, Particles, Curves and TextConfigs (unknown Data formats are never candidates). Lua scripts are scanned for references but never deleted, generated UI mirrors and declaration stubs do not count as independent usage, and material caches live in the user data directory managed by [runtime generation](<../../Editor User Guide/Materials.md#runtime-generation>).
- **Lua expression support:** Recognises string literals, parentheses, constant aliases and `and`/`or` conditional branches in known resource API arguments, conservatively retaining constant paths from every branch and following their Data dependencies.
- **Filesystem safety checks:** Symbolic links, broken links, reparse points and inaccessible paths (including the project root) produce scan issues and block recycling; checks repeat before moving files. Keep entries may name paths that do not exist yet, but cannot bypass safety checks on existing ancestor directories.

## Recycling and editor state

Recycling follows the same Trash, failure and recovery rules as [resource deletion in the editor](<../../Editor User Guide/Start Page Workspace and Shortcuts.md#file-explorer-and-reference-tree>). The project must be saved before scanning, reports cannot be reused after recycling, and any modified project input invalidates the current report.

## Plug-in contract

Official Resource Cleanup registers one ordinary menu command and owns its Avalonia window, built-in protected list and translations. `PluginMenuContext.ResourceCleanupHost` supplies the narrow `IResourceCleanupHost` bridge for reading/saving project keep paths, scanning with progress and cancellation, and recycling a report by ID without exposing mutable editor documents or arbitrary file deletion.
